For n > 393, m(n) = F(n) = C(n-1,2) + 1 - floor((n-1)/2) (Elliott 1967, corrected by Purdy-Smith; Balintova-Balint 1994). For n <= 393 it is open. Forum (mzn, 2026-08-18): m(5)=5, m(6)=8, m(7)=11, m(8)=17, with exact-arithmetic configurations (versus F = 5, 9, 13, 19), and m(9) <= 25 = F(9), with no way found to beat it. Forum (Peysakhov, 2026-06-11): 18 circles at n=8.
targets.success_criterion: Confirmed: (A) exact coordinates for n >= 9 points, not all collinear and not all concyclic (exact nondegeneracy as in 506.lean), determining strictly fewer than F(n) = C(n-1,2) + 1 - floor((n-1)/2) circles (F(9)=25, F(10)=33, F(11)=41, F(12)=51) AND strictly fewer (direction: min) than the best value posted on the forum thread for that n AT VERIFICATION TIME. Or (B) a complete proof that m(n) = F(n) for every 9 <= n <= 393.

partial_wins.statement: A rigorous lower-bound proof establishing m(n) exactly for some n in {6, 7, 8} (matching the forum configuration), provided no matching lower-bound proof was already posted on the forum.
A complete proof that m(9) = 25.
A complete proof that the formula m(n) = F(n) holds for all n > N0 with an explicit N0 < 393 (lowering the Elliott/Balintova-Balint threshold), with every constant recomputed exactly.

targets.verification_method: (A) For every non-collinear triple, compute the exact circumcircle (centre and r^2 as rationals or exact field elements), deduplicate and count. Independent re-implementation: union-find on triples using the exact 4-point concyclicity determinant. Confirm the configuration is neither all collinear nor all concyclic, then compare with F(n). (B) Line-by-line refereeing of the constants in the Elliott-type argument; recompute every numeric inequality exactly.
angles: Lift to the sphere by inverse stereographic projection. Circles correspond to planes not through the pole and lines to planes through the pole. So minimise (#planes containing >= 3 points) - (#those through the pole). Search orbit configurations of finite rotation groups (prisms, antiprisms, cuboctahedron, Johnson solids, two parallel regular polygons plus poles) and choose the pole on as many plane sections as possible. Use rational points on S^2 for exact arithmetic.

Extend mzn's n=8 cube and Peysakhov's two-squares configurations by adding points lying on many existing circles, or by moving to 3-fold or 4-fold symmetric families with many concyclic 4-sets and collinear triples. Collinear triples are 'free' because they determine no circle.

For (B): revisit Elliott's argument with modern tools. Lin-Makhul-Mojarrad-Schicho-Swanepoel-de Zeeuw ('On sets defining few ordinary circles') handles sufficiently large n. Make their constants explicit, and use inversion to turn Melchior/Csima-Sawyer-type ordinary-line inequalities into circle bounds.
pitfalls: Counting lines as circles.
Floating-point concyclicity.
n <= 9 data is already on the forum.
The F(n) formula is proved only for n > 393, so beating it at n <= 8 is already known.
Nondegeneracy convention: the Lean statement uses 'not all collinear and not all concyclic'; do not switch to 'no three collinear' silently.
The forum's small-n 'exact' values may be upper bounds only; check whether a matching lower-bound proof was posted before citing them as m(n).
Degenerate configurations (all concyclic, or all but one collinear) are excluded by the Lean statement; check the exact nondegeneracy in 506.lean.

targets.name: Erdos #617 (Erdos-Gyarfas): balanced 5-colouring of K_26
targets.statement: Is there a 5-colouring of the edges of K_26 in which every 6-vertex set sees all 5 colours? Equivalently: can E(K_26) be partitioned into 5 graphs G_1..G_5, each with independence number alpha(G_c) <= 5? Erdos-Gyarfas conjecture that for every r >= 3 no balanced r-colouring of K_{r^2+1} exists. Per erdosproblems.com/617 (last edited 2026-04-01): proved for r = 3 and r = 4 (credited there to Erdos-Gyarfas); false for r = 2. On r^2 vertices balanced colourings exist for infinitely many r (affine planes). r = 5 is the first open case; the forum (42things, 2026-07-15) says r = 5 'appears to be open' and reports no computational results.
targets.success_criterion: (A) An explicit symmetric 26x26 matrix with off-diagonal entries in {0..4} in which every one of the 230,230 six-sets sees all 5 colours. This disproves #617 for r=5 and is a full success. (B) A complete impossibility proof for r=5: an UNSAT result on an encoding regenerated by the verifier, with a DRAT/LRAT proof checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr, and every symmetry-breaking or structural lemma proved in writing and refereed. The same pipeline must first reproduce r=3 (K_10) and r=4 (K_17) UNSAT. Solving only a symmetric sub-family (Cayley colourings, etc.) is a partial win. Under (B), state explicitly that the conjecture stays open for r >= 6.

partial_wins.statement: A DRAT/LRAT-checked impossibility proof (CNF regenerated by the verifier, pipeline also reproducing r = 3 and r = 4 UNSAT) that no balanced 5-colouring of K_26 is a Cayley colouring on Z_26, i.e. colour depends only on the difference class (all 5^13 assignments excluded).

The same kind of checked impossibility for another named symmetric family stated in advance: Cayley colourings on Z_13 x Z_2 or D_13, or colourings by orbits of a named subgroup of PGammaL(2,25) acting on pairs of PG(1,25).

targets.verification_method: (A) Exhaustive loop over all six-sets with a colour bitmask check, plus an independent check that every colour class has independence number <=5 (exact max-clique of its complement) and >=55 edges. (B) Fresh encoding by the verifier; independent solver run; proof checking; manual audit of symmetry breaking (vertex lex-leader composed with colour permutation must be shown sound jointly); r=3 and r=4 sanity reproductions.
angles: Turan counting gives rigid structure. Each G_c has alpha <= 5, so its complement is K_6-free with at most t_5(26) = 270 edges, so |E(G_c)| >= 55. That totals 275 of the 325 edges, leaving only 50 'surplus' edges. By Erdos-Simonovits stability, each colour class is close to a disjoint union of cliques of sizes 6,5,5,5,5. Enumerate these clique-partition 'skeletons' plus the surplus edges; this may give a human-readable impossibility proof (probably how r=3 and r=4 were done by hand).

Algebraic ansatz: 26 = |PG(1,25)|. Colour edges by orbits of subgroups of PGammaL(2,25) on unordered pairs. Also try Cayley colourings on Z_26, Z_13 x Z_2 and D_13, where the colour depends only on the difference class (13 classes, 5^13 ~ 1.2e9 assignments, pruned by exact alpha checks with numba; exhaustive search is feasible).

Affine-plane extension: AG(2,5) (6 parallel classes merged into 5 colours) gives balanced colourings of K_25. Analyse exactly why adding a 26th point fails, and whether twisted or non-Desarguesian-like structures on 25+1 points escape.

SAT with 1,625 variables and about 1.15M length-15 clauses: lex-leader symmetry breaking on S_26 (vertex order) and S_5 (colours), cube-and-conquer on 10 cores. In parallel, run MaxSAT or tabu search minimising the number of colour-deficient 6-sets, to hunt for (A).
pitfalls: Confusing K_{r^2} (where balanced colourings do exist via affine planes) with K_{r^2+1}.
Reversing the quantifier: the conjecture says some 6-set MISSES a colour.
Unsound composition of vertex and colour symmetry breaking in an UNSAT claim.
Reporting a solver timeout as UNSAT.
Estimating alpha heuristically instead of exactly.
Attributions: the problem page credits r=3,4 to Erdos-Gyarfas; do not cite Chung-Liu without opening the source.
Restricted-family UNSAT (e.g. no Z_26-Cayley colouring works) says nothing about general colourings.

targets.name: Erdos #699: a prime p >= i dividing gcd(C(n,i), C(n,j)), for a full proof
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (proof work plus exhaustive residual check)
targets.statement: For every n and every 1 <= i < j <= n/2, is there a prime p >= i dividing gcd(C(n,i), C(n,j))? Erdos-Szekeres 1978. FALSIFIABLE/OPEN. Proved for j <= 3i/2 or n=2j (GPT 5.6 via L. Price, Jul 2026). Del Pin (2026-07-25) extends the range slightly past floor(3i/2). MaxDKaos (2026-07-25) gives j <= C i log^2 i unconditionally. Exhaustively checked for n <= 10^7 (Cong, 2026-01-06), with targeted extensions to about 1.34e8. No full proof is claimed. Only finitely many n are possible for each fixed (i,j). Bloom highlighted the identity C(n,i)C(n-i,j-i) = C(n,j)C(j,i) and calls the problem possibly very deep in general.
targets.success_criterion: (A) An explicit counterexample (n,i,j), 1<=i<j<=n/2, with no prime p>=i dividing both C(n,i) and C(n,j), verified by Kummer valuations and by direct factorisation. (B) A complete proof for all (n,i,j): every step elementary or citing a theorem with its exact published statement, any finite residual range closed by reproducible exhaustive code. The forum's partial cases (j <= 3i/2, n = 2j, Del Pin's interval, j <= C i log^2 i) may be used only after the verifier re-proves or checks them.

partial_wins.statement: A rigorous, refereed proof covering a new infinite region strictly beyond j <= C i log^2 i (e.g. all j <= i^{1+delta} for an explicit delta > 0).
A rigorous proof of the statement for ALL (n, j) whenever i <= B, for an explicit bound B larger than any i-range already settled on the forum, with any finite residue closed by reproducible code.

An exhaustive verification for all n <= 10^9 and all valid pairs (i,j), beyond Cong's n <= 10^7 and the targeted ~1.34e8 checks, reproduced by an independent implementation (e.g. Lucas-theorem bitsets versus direct gcd factorisation on a random sample of n plus full Kummer scan).

targets.verification_method: (A) For every prime p in [i, n], compute v_p(C(n,i)) and v_p(C(n,j)) by Kummer (count carries of i + (n-i) in base p), and confirm that no prime has both valuations positive. Cross-check with sympy.factorint on the gcd for moderate n. (B) Line-by-line refereeing. Rerun the residual computation with independent code (e.g., a Lucas-theorem bitset method versus direct gcd factorisation). Check edge cases i = 1, 2 and the p >= i versus p > i distinction.
angles: Combine the identity C(n,i)C(n-i,j-i) = C(n,j)C(j,i) with Kummer carries. A prime p > j dividing C(n,i) must divide C(n,j) unless it is absorbed by C(n-i,j-i). Split into cases on the base-p digit pattern of n.
Use Sylvester-Schur strengthenings (a prime > c*i divides C(n,i) for n >= 2i, Ecklund-Eggleton-Erdos-Selfridge style) to push past the j ~ 1.5i magnitude ceiling that Del Pin identified.

Make MaxDKaos's bound n <= j^{i/(i-pi(i-1))} uniform in i via explicit prime-counting (Dusart bounds), reducing to a finite region. Close that region with a fast exhaustive search: for each n, bitsets D_p(n) = {i : p | C(n,i)} from Lucas' theorem, and for each i the union over p >= i.
Hunt counterexamples near the known exceptions of the stronger p > i variant, e.g. (28,5,14), and among n that are prime powers, or prime powers plus or minus 1, which minimise carries.
Make Del Pin's interval endpoint J_1(i) explicit and attempt to bridge it to MaxDKaos's C i log^2 i range.
pitfalls: The p >= i and p > i versions differ: the stronger version has genuine exceptions such as gcd(C(28,5), C(28,14)) = 2^3*3^3*5.
Checking special families of n is not a proof.
Forum AI proofs need independent re-checking.
Off-by-one errors in j <= n/2.
Exhaustive range claims below 10^7 duplicate Cong (forum 2026-01-06).
Del Pin's interval result already extends 3i/2 slightly; re-proving it is not new.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Erdos #7 / Selfridge: a covering system with distinct odd moduli
targets.compute_profile: needs cluster (for search); pure thought for impossibility
targets.statement: Is there a finite set of congruences a_i mod n_i, with distinct odd moduli n_i > 1, covering every integer? Erdos offered $25; Selfridge later offered $2000 for an explicit example. Known: impossible with odd squarefree moduli (BBMST 2022). Some modulus must be divisible by 3 (Hough-Nielsen 2019). The lcm L is divisible by 9 or 15. Forum (2026, needs re-verification): L is abundant (>= 945), L >= 11,486,475, L has >= 9 distinct prime factors, and some modulus has >= 4 distinct prime factors.
targets.success_criterion: An explicit finite list of (a_i, n_i) with distinct odd n_i > 1 that covers Z, verified by two independent exact checkers. Alternatively, a complete axiom-free proof of impossibility.

partial_wins.statement: A rigorous proof, checked line by line or in Lean without extra axioms, that L = lcm(n_i) of any odd distinct-moduli covering has at least 10 distinct prime factors (the forum claims >= 9, unrefereed).
A rigorous proof raising the lower bound on L strictly above 11,486,475 (Egeozturk, forum Aug 2026), rechecked by independent code.

An axiom-free Lean formalisation of one of the forum's unrefereed necessary conditions (e.g. Schroeder's >= 9 distinct primes in L, or a modulus with >= 4 distinct primes), checked with #print axioms.

targets.verification_method: Let L = lcm(n_i). If L <= ~2e9, sieve a bitset of residues mod L. Otherwise use a recursive CRT check: process the prime-power factors of L layer by layer, tracking uncovered residue classes, as in Nielsen/Krukenberg-style verifiers. Use two independent implementations, and also check distinctness and oddness.
angles: Run the BBMST distortion/sieve LP numerically to map which prime-exponent profiles of L are not excluded, then search only there.
Nielsen-style tree search (the method that found a covering with minimum modulus 40) adapted to odd moduli: residue trees over primes 3, 5, 7, 11, ... with exact-cover/ILP at each level.
Prove the strongest rigorous necessary conditions (e.g., >= 10 distinct primes in L) as a publishable partial result.
pitfalls: The forum already has a retracted Lean 'proof' that relied on an impossible axiom.
Moduli must be distinct.
Odd squarefree moduli are already impossible.
Covering 'almost all' integers is not covering all of them.
Schroeder's prime-count papers are forum postings, not refereed; re-verify before building on them.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Erdos #723: a projective plane of order 12 (fallback: 6 MOLS of order 12)
targets.statement: Must every finite projective plane have prime-power order? Orders 6 and 14 are ruled out by Bruck-Ryser-Chowla, order 10 by Lam's computer search, and the conjecture is proved for n <= 11. Order 12 is the smallest open case. A plane of order 12 is equivalent to 11 MOLS of order 12. The best known count of MOLS of order 12 is N(12) >= 5 per the Handbook table (not live-verified by the auditor; the verifier must confirm against the current Colbourn-Dinitz tables).
targets.success_criterion: MOONSHOT: an incidence structure of 157 points and 157 lines, each line of size 13, with N N^T = 12I + J (disproves the prime power conjecture). FALLBACK RECORD: k mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 12 (equivalently a TD(k+2,12)) with k STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the order-12 entry of the current Colbourn-Dinitz/Handbook MOLS table AT VERIFICATION TIME, which the verifier must open (5 as of the researcher's reading on 2026-10-03, i.e. 6 MOLS needed).

partial_wins.statement: A DRAT/LRAT-checked proof (CNF regenerated by the verifier) that no (12,8,1) difference matrix exists over one of Z_2 x Z_6, A_4 or D_6 (i.e. 6 MOLS cannot arise that way from that group), provided this is not already in the literature.
A rigorous, independently rerun computation excluding a specific collineation group (or group order) for a projective plane of order 12 that is not already excluded in the published literature.

targets.verification_method: Plane: build the 157x157 incidence matrix N and check N N^T = 12I + J, all row and column sums 13, entries 0/1. MOLS: each square is Latin (rows and columns are permutations of 0..11), and for every pair of squares all 144 ordered symbol pairs are distinct.
angles: Difference matrices over groups of order 12 with non-cyclic Sylow 2-subgroup ONLY (Z_2 x Z_6, A_4, D_6; Z_12 and Dic_3 admit no (12,k,1) DM for k >= 3): extend known 7-row matrices (giving 5 MOLS) to 8 rows (giving 6 MOLS) with SAT or exact cover, imposing group regularity.

Plane search restricted to collineation groups not yet excluded by the literature (Janko-van Trung-type restrictions on automorphisms of a putative plane of order 12). Use orbit-SAT on the remaining small groups.
Transversal design TD(8,12) via a large-neighbourhood search seeded from the known TD(7,12).
pitfalls: Partial-orthogonality claims.
Using order-10 nonexistence techniques as if they applied to 12.
Mis-recording the current MOLS(12) record; check the Handbook of Combinatorial Designs table.
Groups with a cyclic Sylow 2-subgroup (Z_12, Dic_3) admit no (12,k,1) difference matrix for k >= 3; search only Z_2×Z_6, A_4 and D_6.
Do not confuse 'k-1 MOLS' with 'k rows of a difference matrix': a (12,8,1) DM gives 6 MOLS.

targets.name: Erdos #835: (k+1)-colouring of J(2k,k), equivalently large sets of Steiner systems S(k-1,k,2k)
targets.compute_profile: pure thought + laptop-minutes (literature, design-theory proofs, small exhaustive checks)
targets.statement: Does some k > 2 admit a colouring of the k-subsets of [2k] with k+1 colours such that every (k+1)-set sees all k+1 colours, i.e. chi(J(2k,k)) = k+1? A (k+1)-set has exactly k+1 k-subsets, so each colour class meets every (k+1)-set exactly once; taking complements, each colour class is a Steiner system S(k-1,k,2k), so the property is equivalent to a large set LS(k-1,k,2k) (athvedt, forum 2026-05-21). OPEN. Settled negatively for k=3..8 (computation), for all k with k+1 composite (Ma-Tang), and for k=10 and k=12 (athvedt, forum 2026-05-21, via the nonexistence of S(4,5,15) [Mendelsohn-Hung] and S(4,5,17) [Ostergard-Pottonen]). The smallest open case is k=16 (veljjanoski, forum 2026-09-21; partial Kramer-Mesner searches). Then k=18, 22, 28, ... KentaKitamura (2026-05-30): every k-set must share its colour with its complement. The answer is widely expected to be NO.
targets.success_criterion: FULL: a complete proof that chi(J(2k,k)) != k+1 for every k>=16 with k+1 prime, or an explicit colouring for some k. Partial win: a fully verified settlement of k=16 (the smallest open case per the forum), with every cited nonexistence theorem quoted with its exact hypotheses. Re-deriving k=10 or k=12 is NOT a result. At verification time, re-read the forum thread to confirm the claimed case is still listed as open.

partial_wins.statement: A fully verified settlement of k = 16 (no LS(15,16,32), equivalently no (k+1)-colouring of J(32,16) as required), with every cited nonexistence theorem opened and quoted with exact hypotheses and any computation rerun independently, provided k = 16 is still listed as open on the forum at verification time.
A fully verified settlement of a single other open case (k = 18, 22, 28, ...; k+1 prime), with the same citation and rerun standards, provided it is not already settled on the forum.
A rigorous, refereed obstruction (e.g. spectral/Delsarte-type or block-intersection integrality) that rules out an explicitly described infinite subfamily of the open k.

targets.verification_method: YES case: brute force over all (k+1)-subsets for distinct colours. NO case: (1) re-derive the colour class to S(k-1,k,2k) reduction and the derived-design chain; (2) for k=16 the chain reaches S(4,5,21), S(5,6,22), etc. Confirm from the literature which of these are known not to exist and which are admissible but open; chains ending in admissible-but-open or existing designs (e.g. S(4,5,23) for k=18) do not kill the case; (3) any computer search (Kramer-Mesner under group G) proves nothing in general unless combined with a proof that every solution has such a symmetry; (4) independent rerun of the code.
angles: k = 16: follow the derived-design chain from S(15,16,32) down through S(5,6,22) and S(4,5,21); confirm from the literature which of these are known not to exist and which are admissible but open. Also derive the large-set chain (blocks through a point across all systems form a large set of S(k-2,k-1,2k-1)), which is a stronger hypothesis than a single system.

Attack the large-set condition rather than single Steiner systems. The colour classes are perfect 'clique-hitting' codes in the Johnson scheme J(2k,k). Apply Delsarte's theory (design-orthogonal-to-clique / Roos-type identities, Lloyd-type theorems for perfect codes in Johnson graphs, eigenvalue integrality) for a uniform obstruction killing all k at once.

Derived large sets: the blocks through a fixed point, across all k+1 systems, form a large set of S(k-2,k-1,2k-1). Iterate to small parameters where exhaustive nonexistence is checkable (LS of S(3,4,v) or S(4,5,v) for small v) and look for a pattern.

Use intersection-number constraints: in S(t,t+1,2t+2) with v = 2(t+1) the Tits bound holds with equality. Exploit the equality case (block complements, self-complementarity of the whole large set) to derive integrality conditions via block-intersection polynomials (Cameron/Mendelsohn style).
Use KentaKitamura's lemma (every k-set shares its colour with its complement) to halve the variables in any SAT/Kramer-Mesner encoding and to derive further parity/integrality constraints.
Extend veljjanoski's Kramer-Mesner searches for S(15,16,32) to further automorphism groups, but treat results as heuristic unless paired with a proof that any large set must have that symmetry.
pitfalls: Cameron's 2014 blog asserts that S(9,10,20) does not exist without giving a citation.
Keevash-type existence results apply only to large v and are irrelevant here.
Notation varies: S(2k,k,k-1) versus S(k-1,k,2k).
A large set needs k+1 pairwise disjoint systems covering ALL k-subsets; disjointness alone is weaker.
k=10 is already settled on the forum; do not claim it.
k=12 is ALREADY settled on the forum (athvedt, 2026-05-21, via S(4,5,17) nonexistence); do not claim it.
Kramer-Mesner searches restricted to specific automorphism groups do not prove nonexistence.
AlphaProof's J(18,9) result concerns k=9 (composite k+1), not k=18.

targets.name: Erdos #993: a tree (or forest) with non-unimodal independent-set sequence
targets.statement: For every tree or forest T, is the sequence i_k(T) (number of independent sets of size k) unimodal? This is the Alavi-Malde-Schwenk-Erdos conjecture. It is false for general graphs. Log-concavity fails for trees from n = 26 (Kadrawi-Levit 2023). The n = 32 check covered all 109,972,410,221 trees (forum 2026-08-09) and the 3-branch-vertex lemma has a Lean formalisation (BrettRey2, 2026-08-21).
targets.success_criterion: An explicit tree or forest (edge list) whose exactly computed sequence (i_0, i_1, ...) has indices a < b < c with i_a > i_b < i_c. Plateaus do not count.

partial_wins.statement: An exhaustive, reproducible verification that every tree on 33 vertices has a unimodal independent-set sequence, with the enumerated tree count matching the known number of unlabeled trees on 33 vertices (OEIS A000055) and the code rerun by the verifier.
A rigorous (refereed or Lean-checked) proof that any counterexample tree must have at least 4 vertices of degree >= 3, strengthening the known 3.

targets.verification_method: Confirm the graph is a forest (acyclic; for a tree, connected with n-1 edges). Compute the independence polynomial exactly with Python big integers by the rooted-tree DP I(T) = I(T-v) + x*I(T-N[v]), done twice: two different roots, or DP versus brute force for n <= 40. Then scan for a strict valley.
angles: Mixture design: I(T) = I(T-v) + x*I(T-N[v]). Engineer the two summands to be log-concave with well-separated modes and comparable mass, e.g. attach many pendant stars K_{1,m} (factors (1+x)^m shift modes) on one side versus long paths on the other. Optimise the parameters analytically.
Amplify the known 'multiple breaks of log-concavity' trees (arXiv 2511.00334, 2502.10654) by gluing or iterating them; search for a dip.
Evolutionary / RL search over trees with 50-300 vertices. Fitness: min over b of i_b / min(i_{b-1}, i_{b+1}) approaching 1 from above. Use mutations preserving >= 3 branch vertices.
Forest route: by Hoggar, a forest counterexample needs a non-LC component. Build disjoint unions of non-LC trees whose convolution creates a valley.
pitfalls: Plateaus are allowed in unimodality.
Float overflow; use exact integers.
Confirm the object is a tree or forest (a cycle gives an invalid graph).
Already exhaustively checked to n = 32.

targets.name: Gyarmati-Hennecart-Ruzsa sum-difference constant C_3a: beat 1.19519192 (finite-certified record 1.19102809)
targets.statement: C_3a is the largest constant such that there are arbitrarily large integer sets A, B with |A+B| << |A| and |A-B| >> |A+B|^{C_3a}. Upper bound 4/3 (GHR 2007). Per the teorth 3a page, a finite set U of nonnegative integers containing 0 gives C_3a >= 1 + log(|U-U|/|U+U|)/log(2·max(U)+1). Lower-bound records rose fast in 2025-2026: Gerbicz 1.173050, Griego 1.1740744, Mosaic 1.1835129324, Numaro 1.18733* (limit), Kleinwaks 1.19102809 (finite-certified, base 34065 masked digits), Kleinwaks 2026b 1.19519192* (Lean-formalised limit construction, base 27022).
targets.success_criterion: A construction certified at finite depth (explicit U, or a masked-digit construction with an exact counting certificate) whose value under the 3a page's formula is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the best lower bound listed on https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/blob/main/constants/3a.md itself (not the README table) AT VERIFICATION TIME, including asterisked limit values, by at least 1e-7, after the verifier re-reads the exact hypotheses of the formula on the 3a page (e.g. 0 in U, nonnegativity, |U-U| < 2max(U)+1). As of 2026-10-03 that value is 1.19519192* (Kleinwaks 2026b).

partial_wins.statement: A finite-certified construction whose value lies strictly above the best finite-certified value on the 3a page (1.19102809 as of 2026-10-03) but does not beat the limit record, verified with directed rounding and the formula's hypotheses checked.

A limit (asterisked-type) construction, with an exact derivation rechecked by independent code or Lean, whose limiting value strictly exceeds the best value on the 3a page at verification time, but without a finite-depth certificate.

targets.verification_method: For an explicit U: compute |U+U| and |U-U| exactly (bitset or numpy convolution of indicator vectors), check that U contains 0 and is nonnegative, and check the hypotheses. Evaluate the formula with 50-digit mpmath using directed rounding (round the lower bound down). For digit constructions: re-derive the counting formula independently, recompute the counts with separate code, and reproduce Kleinwaks's 1.19102809 with the same pipeline first.
angles: Reproduce Kleinwaks's masked-digit construction, then search mask families (sets of forbidden digit patterns) in other bases with simulated annealing on the exact counting formula.
Carry-controlled multi-level digits: combine two different bases or digit alphabets in a product construction and optimise the joint mask.
Local search directly on finite U (|U| up to 1e5) with incremental sumset/difference-set counts via FFT.
Analyse why the limit and finite-depth values differ (1.19519 vs 1.19103) and design constructions whose finite-depth certificate approaches the limit.
pitfalls: Asterisked limit values are not finite certificates; state which kind you beat.
The formula's hypotheses (0 in U, nonnegativity, the |U-U| < 2max(U)+1 condition) are easy to violate silently.
Floating-point log ratios; use directed rounding.
Confusing C_3a with the single-set constants 3d/3e.

targets.name: Erdos-Szemeredi 3-sunflower-free capacity: beat the 1997 lower bound 1.551 (optimization constant C_49)
targets.statement: Let f(n) be the largest family of subsets of [n] with no 3-sunflower, i.e. no three distinct sets with pairwise equal intersections (three pairwise disjoint sets count, with empty core). mu = lim f(n)^{1/n}. Published lower bound: >1.551 (Deuber-Erdos-Gunderson-Kostochka-Meyer 1997, numerical value as stated in FPP2024/TZ2025). An unpublished >= 1.554 is cited in Naslund-Sawin. Upper bound: 3/2^{2/3} ~ 1.88988 (Naslund-Sawin 2017). By the tensor-product lemma proved on the C_49 page, any explicit r-uniform sunflower-free family F in C([n],r) gives mu >= |F|^{1/n}. The lower bound is about 30 years old.
targets.success_criterion: An explicit (n, r, F) with F a subset of C([n],r), all members distinct and of size exactly r, F 3-sunflower-free (including no three pairwise-disjoint sets), whose rate |F|^{1/n} is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than both the best lower bound listed at https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/blob/main/constants/49a.md AT VERIFICATION TIME and the unpublished 1.554 bound, with margin: |F| > 1.5545^n under exact comparison (integer comparison |F|*10^(4n) > 15545^n). As of 2026-10-03 the page lists >1.551 (DEGKM 1997) and >=1.554 (unpublished); for context the 1.5545 thresholds are n=16: >=1163, n=20: >=6790, n=24: >=39644 (recompute with exact integers, do not hand-copy). If the 49a page lists a bound above 1.5545 at verification time, the bar becomes strictly above that value. Product claims list each uniform base family explicitly, and the verifier checks each base.

partial_wins.statement: An explicit uniform 3-sunflower-free family (verified as in the success criterion) whose rate |F|^{1/n} strictly exceeds DEGKM's exact published 1997 value, after the verifier reconstructs that exact value from the 1997 paper, but does not exceed 1.5545.

An exact value of g(n, r) (the maximum r-uniform 3-sunflower-free family on [n]) for some (n, r) not previously published: an explicit family of size g plus a DRAT/LRAT-checked UNSAT proof that size g+1 is impossible, with the CNF regenerated by the verifier.

targets.verification_method: (1) Size, range, distinctness and uniformity. (2) Sunflower check by two independent implementations (numpy bitmask over pairs × third sets; C/numba triple loop): for every pair {A,B} with I=A∩B, no third C with C∩A=C∩B=I. (3) Exact integer rate comparison as above. (4) For products: verify each factor separately and confirm all factors are uniform.
angles: Get exact small values g(n) = max r-uniform sunflower-free family for n <= 10-12 via OR-tools CP-SAT (pip install ortools). Inspect the extremal families for algebraic structure, then tensor them.
Reconstruct the DEGKM 1997 construction first, then parameter-sweep and generalise it (it is probably a product of a small base family).
Invariant ansatz: take F as a union of orbits of Z_n, AGL(1,p) or PSL(2,q) acting on [n]; this shrinks the search space by orders of magnitude for n = 16-30.

Tabu search / simulated annealing with incremental conflict counting (maintain, for each pair, the count of 'third sets' that complete a sunflower). Seed with the best products found so far, like Edel-style cap-set records.

Cross-field mapping: try encoding cap-set-like objects (3-AP-free sets in F_3^m) as set families. A pair-of-coordinates map can turn 'no three in a line' into 'no three sets with equal pairwise intersections' on suitable layers. Prove the embedding before scaling it.
pitfalls: Non-uniform families do NOT tensor: the lemma needs uniform layers, so f(n) >= |F| for a single n does not bound mu.
Forgetting that three pairwise-disjoint sets are a sunflower.
Floating-point rounding when comparing |F|^{1/n}.
Confusing this with odd-sunflowers (FPP2024) or with k-sunflowers for k > 3.
Off-by-one in the threshold: compute ceil(1.5545^n + tiny) with exact integers, do not hand-copy.
Comparing against 1.551 when the unpublished 1.554 is the real bar for novelty.

targets.name: Smaller (k,g)-graph than the cage record
targets.statement: n(k,g) is the order of a smallest k-regular graph of girth g. Construct a k-regular graph of girth at least g with fewer vertices than the best known upper bound for some open (k,g), e.g. (3,13) (lower bound 202) or (4,10) (record 320 since arXiv 2511.07247).
targets.success_criterion: (1) Explicit adjacency list on N vertices. (2) Simple graph, every vertex of degree exactly k. (3) Girth computed exactly is >= g. (4) N STRICTLY LESS than the best known upper bound for n(k,g) at verification time, taken as the minimum over DS16 (https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/DS16/pdf/), the latest version of arXiv 2511.07247, and every newer source found by a fresh arXiv/Scholar search for '(k,g)-cage'. (5) N >= Moore bound for (k,g). Girth-diameter cages and mixed cages do not count.

partial_wins.statement: A k-regular girth-g graph whose order equals the live best known upper bound for an open (k,g) but which is non-isomorphic (nauty/pynauty canonical form) to every published record graph for that (k,g) that can be downloaded (House of Graphs, the 2511.07247 data, or the record authors); not claimable if no record graph is obtainable for comparison.

A graph strictly beating a live entry of the separate girth-diameter cage table (arXiv 2511.21144) or the mixed-cage table (arXiv 2506.20003), verified exactly against that table's own definition; logged as a partial win, never as a cage record.

targets.verification_method: In networkx, check that all degrees equal k. Compute the girth with an independent BFS-from-every-vertex shortest-cycle routine and cross-check against networkx.girth (networkx >= 3.1). Assert girth >= g. Assert the Moore bound <= N < the record. Search arXiv and Google Scholar for '(k,g)-cage' newer than the survey before claiming.
angles: Excision from generalized polygons: delete carefully chosen vertex sets from incidence graphs of generalized quadrangles and hexagons (g = 8, 12) to get g = 7, 9, 11, 13 graphs. Search excision sets with SA.

Voltage lifts with girth constraints: base graph plus a voltage assignment in Z_n or a small nonabelian group. Girth equals the minimum length of a closed walk with net voltage zero, which is computable on the quotient. Enumerate cheaply and exhaustively for small base graphs.

Cayley graphs of PSL(2,q), PGL(2,q) and their subgroups and extensions with generators of order 2 or 3 (the 272 record is a Cayley graph of AGL(1,17)). Do an exhaustive generator search for q up to about 50.
Exoo-style edge-swap local search starting from the record graph with a few vertices deleted and 'deficient' vertices repaired, as in arXiv 2511.07247.
Mixed-integer or CP-SAT completion: fix a large symmetric skeleton and let CP-SAT add edges subject to no short cycles.
pitfalls: Using a stale record. The 2025-2026 paper changed eleven entries, and others may have changed since.
A graph whose girth is exactly g but which is not regular. Biregular and 'record mixed' graphs do not count.
A girth computed on the quotient or voltage graph instead of the lift.
Confusing girth-diameter cages or (k,g)-graphs with excess with ordinary cages.
The attribution of rec(3,13)=272 and its 'Cayley graph of AGL(1,17)' structure was not verified. Do not rely on it, and read DS16 Table 1 directly.
Girth-diameter cages (arXiv 2511.21144) and mixed cages (2506.20003) have separate record tables and do not count.
The researcher's angle that the 272 record is a Cayley graph of AGL(1,17) is unverified; use it only as a search idea.

targets.name: Conway's 99-graph, srg(99,14,1,2)
targets.statement: Does a strongly regular graph with parameters (99,14,1,2) exist? Equivalently: is there a 99-vertex graph in which every edge lies in exactly one triangle and every non-adjacent pair has exactly two common neighbours? Conway offered $1000 for an answer.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for an explicit 99 x 99 symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix with zero diagonal satisfying A^2 = 14I + A + 2(J - I - A), checked exactly in integers. Non-existence requires a formal (Lean/Isabelle) proof or a fully reproducible exhaustive computation with UNSAT certificates checked by drat-trim/cake_lpr and an independently re-derived encoding; never a confirmed claim without that. Near misses (any fraction of constraints satisfied) are never results.

partial_wins.statement: A DRAT/LRAT-checked (independently re-encoded) proof that no srg(99,14,1,2) admits a specified automorphism (stated prime order and fixed-point/cycle structure) that is not already excluded by arXiv 2308.02978, its refinements, or arXiv 2608.11211 (literature check at verification time).
An independent machine-checked re-derivation (Lean/Isabelle, or SAT with DRAT-checked proofs from an independent encoding) of the forced-structure reduction of arXiv 2608.11211.

targets.verification_method: Exact integer matrix identity check in numpy (int32). For non-existence or UNSAT claims, require DRAT/LRAT proofs checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr, together with an independent re-derivation of the encoding.
angles: Prescribe automorphism groups not yet excluded by the 2308.02978 analysis (orders 3 and 11 actions) and solve the orbit-matrix SAT problem.

Local structure: each vertex neighbourhood is 7 disjoint edges, and the graph contains 693 triangles that form a partial geometry or linear space. Search for the corresponding pg(2,6,1)-like geometry with exact cover.
Use the 2608.11211 forced-structure reduction as a starting point with a different SAT encoding (pysat with cadical, cube-and-conquer over 10 cores).
pitfalls: Many repos claim 'near misses'. A near miss is not a result.
Do not confuse it with Conway's other $1000 problems or with srg(99,...) relatives.

targets.name: First Costas array of order 32 or 33
targets.statement: A Costas array of order n is an n x n permutation matrix in which all n(n-1)/2 displacement vectors between pairs of dots are distinct. Costas arrays are conjectured to exist for all n, but no array of order 32 or 33 is known. Orders 32 and 33 are the smallest open cases.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for a permutation pi of {0..n-1} with n = 32 or 33 such that all n(n-1)/2 displacement vectors (j-i, pi(j)-pi(i)), i<j, are distinct, checked exhaustively by two independent methods (vector set size and difference-triangle rows), and no Costas array of that order is listed at verification time on the live primary page https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costas_array (direction: none; existence target), in Beard's database of known arrays, or in a fresh arXiv/literature search. 'Almost Costas' arrays are never results.

partial_wins.statement: A complete enumeration of main-diagonal-symmetric Costas arrays at order 43 (one past the 37-42 census of arXiv 2608.28690), reproduced by an independent solver, with the list of arrays found (or the certified empty list) and each array checked exactly.

A complete enumeration, at order 32 or 33, of a symmetry class other than main-diagonal symmetry (stated precisely) with an independently reproduced search or DRAT-checked UNSAT proof, where no published census covers that class at that order.

An exhaustive, independently reproduced proof that no order-32 Costas array arises from a precisely stated perturbation family of algebraic arrays (e.g. Welch or Golomb/Lempel arrays of orders 30-34 with at most r rows/columns changed or corner dots added/removed, r stated).

targets.verification_method: Python: build the set of the n(n-1)/2 vectors (j-i, π[j]-π[i]) and assert its size is n(n-1)/2. Also check the equivalent difference-triangle condition (distinct entries in each row of the difference triangle) as an independent second check.
angles: Modify algebraic constructions: take Welch (p=31, 37) and Golomb/Lempel (q=31, 32 as 2^5, 37) arrays of nearby orders, remove or add corner dots, and search for 'repairs' with SAT over small row/column perturbations.

Symmetric search: require main-diagonal or other symmetry (the 2608.28690 census shows symmetric families are fully enumerable to order 42). Try other symmetry types at order 32 with a SAT plus symmetry-breaking encoding (pysat).
Exploit the order-32 field: GF(32) Golomb constructions give order 30. Search for two-dot extensions under every primitive-element pair systematically.
Annealing on permutations with an exact incremental collision count, plus restarts seeded from near-Costas arrays. Known to plateau at a few collisions, but it is cheap to run in the background.

Avoid main-diagonal symmetry (ruled out by 2608.28690). Explore other dihedral-type symmetric classes or near-algebraic arrays, e.g. Welch W_1(37) arrays with 4-5 corner dots removed plus repair by local search.

Do backtracking with difference-triangle constraints and bitset pruning (Drakakis/Rickard methods), run on 10 cores over randomized row orders. It is unlikely to finish but can sample deep partial arrays.
Use SAT with pysat: one-hot permutation encoding plus at-most-one constraints per displacement vector. Use cube-and-conquer seeded by fixing the first 3-4 columns.
Partial win: 'near-Costas' arrays of order 32 with the fewest repeated vectors, compared against published deficiency studies (Jedwab-Wodlinger).
pitfalls: 'Almost Costas' arrays with 1-2 repeated vectors are not results.
Off-by-one errors in order (an order-31 Welch array is already known).
Exhaustive enumeration of order 32 was estimated at about a year on tens of thousands of CPUs, so do not try it.
Mistaking a Golomb-ruler-like partial array or a non-permutation for a Costas array.
Main-diagonal symmetric searches at these orders are proven fruitless.
Experts estimate exhaustive enumeration of order 32 needs massive compute, so the realistic outcome is a partial or negative result.

targets.name: New largest known (Delta,D) graph in the degree-diameter table
targets.statement: For maximum degree Δ and diameter D, find a graph with more vertices than the current entry in the Comellas degree-diameter table. The table covers degree up to 20 and diameter up to 10.
targets.success_criterion: (1) Explicit adjacency list of a simple undirected graph G on N vertices. (2) Maximum degree <= Delta. (3) G connected with diameter <= D, checked by all-pairs BFS, or by one BFS plus a machine-checked vertex-transitivity proof (explicit Cayley group and generators regenerating exactly the submitted edge set). (4) N STRICTLY GREATER than the (Delta,D) entry of the live Comellas general-graph table at https://web.mat.upc.edu/francesc.comellas/delta-d/table_degree_diameter.html, re-fetched immediately before claiming (the table changes daily). (5) N <= Moore bound; boldface (proven-optimal) entries cannot be beaten, so beating one signals a bug.

partial_wins.statement: A graph satisfying (1)-(3) with N strictly greater than the (Delta,D) entry in a table snapshot whose fetch time and SHA-256 were recorded BEFORE the search started, but which was overtaken by another group's update logged on the live table after that snapshot (independent collision); the skeptic checks the graph, the snapshot hash and the update-log date.

A graph strictly beating the live entry of a separately maintained special-class degree-diameter table (bipartite, Cayley or circulant), verified with the same exact degree/diameter checker plus the class property (bipartition, or Cayley group and generators reproducing the edge set), compared against that table's live page.

targets.verification_method: Load the graph with scipy.sparse. Assert it is symmetric with no loops and no multi-edges, and check the degree array. Run BFS from every vertex: multi-source frontier bitsets in numpy work up to about 2e5 vertices. For Cayley graphs, regenerate the edge set from the stated group and generators, check it equals the submitted list, and then run one BFS. Compare N with the live HTML table. Also confirm N is at most the Moore bound.
angles: Voltage-graph lifts: choose a small base graph (Petersen, Hoffman-Singleton, or the record graphs for (Δ, D-1)) and anneal voltage assignments over Z_n, Z_n x Z_m, or metacyclic groups, scoring by the number of vertex pairs at distance greater than D in the lift. Base graph plus group gives a fast BFS on the quotient.
Cayley graphs of semidirect products Z_m ⋊_r Z_n with generator sets chosen by SA. Many of the 2026 entries are Cayley graphs, marked with an asterisk in the table.
Polarity-quotient and Kronecker-product constructions (arXiv 2608.27253): apply them systematically to every table entry to propagate the recent improvements to neighbouring (Δ,D).
Gómez-style compound graphs: replace vertices of a large diameter-(D-2) graph with copies of a small graph and rewire. Use the fresh 2026 records as seeds.
Target the entries updated least recently. Large-D, small-Δ entries got fewer 2026 updates than (Δ,3), (Δ,4), (Δ,5).
Seed voltage-lift and Kronecker/polarity searches with the partial-flag graphs H_{k,q} of arXiv 2608.03965, after checking whether they already appear in the table.
pitfalls: The table is updated almost daily. A claim must beat the value shown at verification time, not the value at search start.
Diameter computed on the quotient or base graph instead of the actual lift.
Multi-edges or loops in voltage lifts silently reduce the true degree count.
Degree-diameter problems for special classes (bipartite, Cayley-only, circulant) have separate tables. Only the general-graph table counts here.
Boldface entries such as (3,2), (3,3), (3,4) and (4,2) are proven optimal. Beating one means there is a bug.
More than 15 independent groups updated the table in August to October 2026. Timestamp claims and re-fetch the table just before claiming.
arXiv 2608.03965 (partial-flag graphs H_{k,q}, asymptotically attaining the Moore bound) is a new seed family. Its graphs may already be in the table.

targets.name: Unmarked polyform with Heesch number 5 or more
targets.statement: Find an unmarked polyomino, polyhex or polyiamond that does not tile the plane but admits 5 or more coronas, with Heesch number Hc >= 5 under Kaplan's hole-free-corona definition. Separately, any planar figure with Heesch number >= 7 would beat Bašić's record of 6 for general figures.
targets.success_criterion: (1) A cell list defining a connected polyform on the stated grid. (2) Explicit tile placements for coronas 1..5 with no overlaps; each corona surrounds the previous patch completely and is hole-free, matching Kaplan's Hc definition. Each placement must be a genuine grid isometry. (3) A proof that the shape is a non-tiler: a machine-checked UNSAT proof (DRAT or LRAT, checked by drat-trim, lrat-check or cake_lpr) that no (m+1)-corona exists for some m >= 5. That bounds the Heesch number, so the shape cannot tile. (4) Hc STRICTLY GREATER than the best polyform Hc recorded at verification time in the Layr-Labs/heesch challenge (live, including open PRs) and the literature (4 as of 2026-10-03). (5) The Layr-Labs/heesch verifier accepts the submission. For the Hc >= 7 general-figure variant, the same structure is needed, with explicit exact geometry (rational or algebraic coordinates) and an independent overlap check. Hyperbolic-plane results do not count.

partial_wins.statement: A new polyform (polyomino, polyhex or polyiamond) larger than Kaplan's exhaustive census sizes (more than 19 cells, 17 hexes or 24 iamonds) with Hc = 4 certified exactly: explicit hole-free coronas 1..4 plus a DRAT/LRAT-checked UNSAT proof that no 5-corona exists and a checked non-tiler proof, reproduced by isohedral/heesch-sat.

A polykite or polydrafter with certified Hc strictly greater than the largest Hc reported for that grid in the literature at verification time (literature check required), with explicit coronas and a checked non-tiler proof.

A polyform with certified Hh (holes allowed) strictly greater than the largest Hh reported in Kaplan's census (arXiv 2105.09438) and any newer source, clearly labelled as Hh, with explicit coronas and a checked non-tiler proof.

targets.verification_method: Clone Layr-Labs/heesch and run its verifier, which rebuilds coronas from placements and gates on non-tilerhood with checked UNSAT proofs. Independently, build isohedral/heesch-sat (needs cryptominisat; it builds on macOS with brew), recompute the Heesch number, and require agreement. Re-check the DRAT/LRAT proof with drat-trim.
angles: Go beyond the exhaustive sizes: mutate the seven known Hc=4 shapes (add or remove boundary cells, keep them non-tiling) and hill-climb on 'deepest corona reached', using incremental SAT. Hc=4 shapes cluster near 'almost tilers'.

Engineer 'locally forced' boundaries: design edge words (Wang-style bumps and nicks) on the hex grid so that the first corona is nearly unique and errors propagate only at radius 5 or 6, mimicking Bašić's construction on a lattice.
Polykites and polydrafters (other heesch-sat grids) are outside the Hc=4 census. A first record there is a meaningful partial result, but check the literature for those grids first.
Filter candidates quickly with Kaplan's isohedral SAT check (arXiv 2406.16407) to discard tilers, then spend SAT time only on non-tilers with Hc >= 3.
Allow holes in coronas (Hh) as a separate, clearly labelled partial result. Do not mix it with the Hc record.
pitfalls: Hc (hole-free coronas) and Hh (holes allowed) are different records. Label which one is meant.
A shape that actually tiles anisohedrally or aperiodically has an infinite Heesch number. Non-tilerhood must be proven, not assumed.
Coronas that are not simply connected, or that overlap by floating-point slivers in general-figure variants.
Polyform sizes at or below 19-omino, 17-hex or 24-iamond were already exhaustively searched. A claimed Hc=5 there implies a bug.
Autonomous bots are submitting to the Layr-Labs challenge. Check its open PRs before claiming.
Hyperbolic-plane Heesch results (arXiv 2603.27827, unbounded Heesch numbers) are unrelated to the Euclidean record. Do not cite them as progress.

targets.name: Langton's ant highway conjecture
targets.statement: Conjecture: from every finite initial configuration of black cells, Langton's ant eventually builds the period-104 diagonal highway. It is proven that the ant's trajectory is always unbounded (Cohen-Kong), but not that it always reaches the highway.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for (a) a finite initial configuration of black cells together with a machine-checkable proof that the ant never produces the highway (e.g. a proven different eventual behaviour verified by exact simulation to a provably repeating state), or (b) a formal (Lean/Isabelle) proof of the conjecture. Long transients without the highway are never counterexamples.

partial_wins.statement: Exhaustive verification of all initial configurations in a 6x6 (or larger) box under a stated symmetry reduction, each with a highway-capture certificate (window at t equals window at t+104 shifted by (+-2,+-2), ant beyond all black cells, and no initial black cell anywhere in the future sweep of the highway) re-checked by an independent simulator on a random 1% sample plus all hard cases.

A rigorous highway-capture lemma (formal proof, or proof reduced to an exhaustively checked finite case analysis re-run independently) stating exactly when a highway, once formed with a given local pattern and no black cells in its future sweep, persists forever.

targets.verification_method: Exact integer simulation by an independent implementation. For highway detection, verify that the ant's local window at time t equals the window at time t+104 shifted by (+-2,+-2), and that the ant is beyond all initial black cells in the drift direction, so the future is provably periodic. For exhaustive claims, re-run a random 1% sample plus all hard cases with the independent simulator.
angles: Prove a rigorous 'highway capture lemma': once the ant is beyond the convex hull of the debris in the highway direction with a specific local pattern, it is locked in forever. This turns finite simulation into proof for bounded boxes.
Exhaustive 6x6 (2^36, about 6.9e10, reduced by 8-fold symmetry) with bit-parallel simulation on 10 cores using the capture lemma.
Study the generalized ants of arXiv 2505.05426 and look for an obstruction mechanism that could appear in LR (Langton) rules from engineered initial patterns, for example highway-colliding 'eaters'.
pitfalls: Simulation without a proven capture lemma is not a proof that the highway persists.
Claims of counterexamples based only on long transients (the ant's chaotic phase can last 10^4 or more steps).
The highway-capture certificate must also show that no initial black cell lies anywhere in the future sweep of the highway, not only ahead of the ant at the moment of detection.

targets.name: Game of Life orphan with a smaller bounding box
targets.statement: An orphan is a finite rectangular pattern, every cell specified on or off, with no predecessor under Conway's Life (B3/S23). Find an orphan whose bounding-box area is below that of the smallest known orphan (8x12 = 96, Eker 2016), or certify by UNSAT proof that no orphan fits in a box size (height >= 5) not previously ruled out.
targets.success_criterion: (1) An m x n pattern with 5 <= min(m,n) and m*n STRICTLY LESS than the smallest orphan area listed on LifeWiki's Garden of Eden page as confirmed by a human in a browser at verification time (96 as of 2026-10-03 per Wikipedia). (2) Two independently written CNF encodings of 'there exists an (m+2) x (n+2) predecessor' are both UNSAT under CaDiCaL and kissat, and at least one DRAT/LRAT proof is checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr. (3) Sanity: the encoders return SAT with simulation-verified predecessors on 100 random non-orphans and on Eker's 8x12 with one cell flipped where applicable. (4) A human confirms on LifeWiki's Garden of Eden page that no orphan of area <= m*n is already listed. Do not bypass Cloudflare; the human gate is mandatory.

partial_wins.statement: A DRAT/LRAT-certified proof (two independent encodings, checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr) that no orphan exists in some h x w box with h >= 5 that is not already ruled out in the literature (human LifeWiki/forum check required; height <= 4 is already known).

An orphan of height h in {5, 6, 7} strictly narrower than the narrowest height-h orphan listed on LifeWiki at verification time (human-checked; 2016 values for context: widths 83, 21, 15), certified as in (2)-(3).

targets.verification_method: Write an independent CNF encoder: each inner cell's next state is a function of its 3x3 neighbourhood, encoded with totalizer or cardinality clauses or directly as a 512-row truth table. Solve with cadical153 and kissat (pip install python-sat). Emit DRAT and check it with drat-trim. Cross-check the encoder on random SAT instances by simulating the predecessor it finds with a numpy Life step. A human then checks LifeWiki's Garden of Eden page in a browser.
angles: Start from Eker's 8x12 and its symmetric relatives. Delete a row or column and run a MaxSAT/CEGAR loop: find the cells to flip so that the shrunken pattern has no predecessor. Each SAT counterexample (a found predecessor) becomes a blocking constraint.

Search directly for 9x10 (area 90) and 8x11 (area 88) orphans with a 2-QBF formulation: there exists a pattern such that for all predecessors the image differs. Solve by CEGAR with incremental SAT and run the 10 cores on different symmetry restrictions (mirror, 180-degree, none).
Tile-based composition: orphans often contain small 'unexplainable' sub-motifs. Mine the minimal unsatisfiable cores of known orphans and pack them more tightly.
Lower-bound direction: prove 'no orphan fits in 7x7' or another unknown small box via cube-and-conquer over all patterns modulo symmetry. A DRAT-certified negative result counts as a partial win.
pitfalls: Orphan and Garden of Eden are different notions. A GoE is a whole configuration; an orphan is a finite patch with all cells, including off cells, specified.
The predecessor region must be the full (m+2) x (n+2) border-extended box.
The record status could not be verified on LifeWiki because of Cloudflare. A human must confirm before claiming.
SAT encodings with an off-by-one in birth or survival rules (B3/S23).
Wade (2023) already proved that 4-high orphans do not exist. Re-proving height <= 4 impossibility is not new.
Achim's orphan page is outdated (2004 record). Do not use it as the current record.
Do not try to bypass the Cloudflare challenge. The human gate is mandatory.

targets.name: The missing Moore graph (degree 57, diameter 2)
targets.statement: Does a 57-regular graph on 3250 vertices with diameter 2 and girth 5 exist? This is srg(3250,57,0,1), the last open case of the Hoffman-Singleton theorem.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for an explicit adjacency list on 3250 vertices that is 57-regular with A^2 + A - 56I = J, checked exactly in integers. A non-existence argument is NOT a confirmed claim unless fully formalized in Lean or Isabelle and checked. Partial wins are logged, not claimed.

partial_wins.statement: A computer-verified exclusion (reproducible code, exact arithmetic; formal proof preferred) of automorphisms of a specific odd prime order p, or of a specific automorphism-group order, that is not already excluded in the literature (arXiv 2606.29183 and its references, checked fresh); if it relies on 2606.29183 (unrefereed), the dependency must be stated.
An independent machine-checked (Lean/Isabelle) or fully reproducible exact-computation verification of the arXiv 2606.29183 theorem that a Moore graph of degree 57 has no involutory automorphisms.

targets.verification_method: Load the adjacency matrix as a 3250 x 3250 int8 array. Check symmetry, zero diagonal and all row sums equal to 57. Compute A@A + A in int32 and compare with 56I + J exactly. For partial results, independently re-run the eigenvalue and character-table or fixed-point arguments, for example with GAP or sympy, in exact arithmetic.
angles: Build on the 'no involutions' result: push the fixed-subgraph analysis to elements of order 3, 5, 7 and 11, using eigenvalue multiplicity (1729/1520) and trace constraints. A computer-checked exclusion of a prime order is a partial win.
Search for constructions with large odd-order groups acting semiregularly (orbit matrices or quotient matrices over Z_{2·5^3·13} subgroups), using CP-SAT on orbit matrices.
Mine 'potential subgraphs' work (MDPI Symmetry 16(12):1563) for forbidden configurations, and encode them as SAT on small neighbourhood structures.
pitfalls: Long history of incorrect non-existence claims. Treat any 'proof' with extreme suspicion.
Floating-point eigenvalue checks are not proofs.
2606.29183 is a recent single-author preprint and has not been refereed. Partial results that build on it inherit that risk, so state the dependency explicitly.

targets.name: No-three-in-line: 150 points on the 75x75 grid (smallest open n)
targets.statement: Place 2n points on the n x n integer grid with no three collinear, for n = 75. n = 75 is the only n <= 76 with no known solution. Also, any 2n-point configuration for n >= 77 would be a new largest-known record. This is Ben Green's open problem #72 (formal-conjectures GreensOpenProblems/72.lean), which asks whether 2n is impossible for all large n. Guy and Kelly (1968) conjectured that only about c*n points are possible for large n, with c = (2*pi^2/3)^(1/3) ~ 1.874, later corrected by Guy to c = pi/sqrt(3) ~ 1.814. Both are below 2, so the expected answer to Green's question is yes (2n eventually becomes impossible); this says nothing definite about n = 75.
targets.success_criterion: (1) Exactly 150 distinct integer points (x,y) with 0 <= x,y <= 74 (which forces exactly 2 per row and per column). (2) Zero collinear triples, checked exactly with integer arithmetic by two independent methods. (3) At claim time, a fresh fetch of the live primary table https://wwwhomes.uni-bielefeld.de/achim/no3in/readme.html (and its tabular summary) shows no n=75 entry, and the readme's 'last update' timestamp is recorded in the report (2026-09-11 13:40 UTC+2 on 2026-10-03). (4) The live EinsteinArena 75x75 leaderboard (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/no-three-in-line-75; best 148 points on 2026-10-03), the OssaBellator issues and a fresh search at verification time show no 150-point solution. If an n=75 solution was posted by anyone before the claim, the result is downgraded to 'independent solution' and not claimed. Variant, under the same rules (direction: max over n): 2n points in [0,n-1]^2 with no three collinear for some n STRICTLY GREATER than the largest n with a solution on the live readme at verification time (76 on 2026-10-03, so n = 77 or more). Near-misses, solutions for n already listed, and UNSAT results within a single symmetry class are not a success.

partial_wins.statement: A DRAT/LRAT-certified UNSAT proof (checked by drat-trim or cake_lpr, encoding re-derived independently) that n = 75 has no 150-point solution within a stated symmetry class not previously ruled out in Flammenkamp's notes, arXiv 2602.07751, arXiv 2609.25133 or the OssaBellator issues.
A 2n-point no-three-in-line solution for some n <= 76 in a symmetry class that Flammenkamp's live page does not list for that n, verified exactly.

A 150-point configuration in [0,74]^2 with strictly fewer collinear triples than the best reported in OssaBellator issues #42/#43 (or any newer public report) at verification time, not obtained by cropping or perturbing the n=76 solution; counted exactly.

A 149-point no-three-in-line set in [0,74]^2, verified exhaustively by two methods, strictly larger than the live EinsteinArena 75x75 best at verification time (148 points, Prellberg, on 2026-10-03), and not already posted on the arena, the Bielefeld page or the OssaBellator issues.

targets.verification_method: For each point P, compute the reduced direction (dx/g, dy/g) with sign normalization to every other point. If any direction repeats for the same P, three points are collinear. That is O(N^2) with exact integer arithmetic. Cross-check with a brute-force O(N^3) determinant test (N=150 gives about 551k triples, which is trivial). Assert there are no duplicate points and all coordinates are in range. Re-fetch the Bielefeld readme and its table and the EinsteinArena 75x75 leaderboard, and record the readme 'last update' timestamp and the arena best with fetch times.
angles: Enumerate which symmetry classes are even possible for odd n = 75 (center point and center lines). The listed odd-n solutions are in class 'rct4'. Run a SAT encoding (pysat with cadical153 or kissat via pip) restricted to every class, including the low-symmetry ones Heule may have skipped, with at-most-2-per-line cardinality constraints (sequential-counter or totalizer encodings).

Local repair from neighbours: crop or descend the n=76 rot4 solution and the n=74 and n=73 solutions. Formulate repair as an exact max-SAT over a growing window. Exactly 2 points are needed in every row and column, which is a strong propagation constraint.
Cube-and-conquer on 10 cores: split on the row-pair patterns of the first few rows under symmetry, then solve the cubes in parallel.
Learn a generative prior from the 431k stored configurations (row-gap statistics and slope usage), and use it as a branching heuristic in a custom bitset DFS.
Algebraic seeds: modular-parabola constructions (points (x, x^2 mod p)) give about 1.5n points. Use them as partial assignments and complete with SAT.

SAT on symmetry-orbit variables, using the symmetry class Heule used for odd n = 71 and 73 ('rct4' per the DB; check Flammenkamp's class definitions for which classes odd n allows). Encode exactly-2 per row and column plus at-most-2 on every grid line with >= 3 lattice points. Use pysat (pip install python-sat, bundles CaDiCaL), or compile kissat/CaDiCaL from source with clang.
Cube-and-conquer across 10 cores: split on the placements in the middle rows and columns, and run a portfolio of symmetry classes (rot2, rot4, rct4, dia2) with different seeds.

Pattern transfer: download the n=73, 74 and 76 solutions from the DB, study their orbit structure (e.g., closeness to conic-arc constructions like Hall et al.'s modular conics), and feed them as phase hints or soft assumptions for n=75.
Large-neighbourhood search: tabu/min-conflicts over orbit representatives with incremental collinear-triple counts. Freeze most of a near-solution and hand the remaining window to SAT.

Precompute every line through >= 3 grid points (primitive directions with |a|,|b| <= 37) once. Reduce the lines modulo the symmetry group so each orbit of lines becomes a single cardinality constraint.
Before starting, re-fetch the Bielefeld readme; Heule posts monthly and may already have n = 75.

Copy the symmetry class that worked for odd n. The 2026 odd solutions (71, 73) are in class rct4, so impose it on n=75, which divides the variables by about 4. Encode as SAT with pysat/CaDiCaL: one variable per orbit, exactly-2 per row and column, at-most-2 per line. Use cardinality encodings (sequential counters) and lines grouped by slope.
Line pruning: only lines through at least 3 grid points matter, so precompute them and drop symmetric duplicates.
Use cube-and-conquer on the 10 cores. Split on the placements in the first few rows (or orbit representatives) and run parallel CaDiCaL instances.
Warm-start by local search (WalkSAT-style on constraint violations) from n=73 or 76 solutions embedded or trimmed, then hand the near-solution to SAT with assumptions.
pitfalls: Floating-point collinearity tests. Use exact integers only.
Grid-size off-by-one: n = 75 means coordinates 0..74.
Only lines with 3+ grid points matter, but all slopes must be checked, including steep rational ones.
Others, including Heule, Prellberg and several AI-agent repositories, are actively attacking n=75. Re-check the database immediately before claiming.
Boards cropped or perturbed from n=76 are provably maximal at 148 points, so local single-point repair cannot succeed. Issue #43 documents this dead end.
n=75 is on Epoch AI's FrontierMath open-problem list, so many AI-agent attempts are underway. Duplicate discovery on the same day is plausible.
Claiming an n that is already in the DB (74 and 76 are solved).
Off-by-one between 0-based and 1-based coordinates.
Checking only small slopes, or using floating-point slopes.
Picking a symmetry class that is invalid for odd n (centre-point issues), which wastes the whole run.
Reporting a solver timeout as evidence of nonexistence.
Heule may post n=75 any day; a solution found after the DB lists 75 is not a record.

Using a symmetry class (e.g. rot4 with a fixed centre cell) that forces a centre point or an odd row count incompatible with exactly-2-per-row for odd n; check Flammenkamp's class table before encoding.
Only checking horizontal, vertical and diagonal lines. All rational slopes must be checked.
Heule needed substantial SAT compute for these cases, so a one-day laptop attempt may well fail. Report partial progress (e.g. 149 points) as a partial result only.
Odd-n symmetry classes differ from even ones (center point issues).
Mis-crediting: the readme credits n = 70, 71, 72, 73 and 76 to Heule (SAT, Jun-Aug 2026) and n = 74 to Prellberg (Jul 2026). Do not repeat older claims that Prellberg's GPU runs covered n = 49-76.

targets.name: Polyomino of order 6, or of odd order 5 or more
targets.statement: The order of a polyomino is the minimum number of congruent copies (rotations and reflections allowed) that tile some rectangle. No (connected) polyomino of odd order greater than 1 is known; order 3 is impossible (Stewart-Wormstein 1992). The smallest even order with no known example is 6. Find a connected, simply connected polyomino of order 6 or of odd order >= 5.
targets.success_criterion: (1) A connected, simply connected, non-rectangular polyomino P given as a cell set, with edge-connectivity checked. (2) An explicit tiling of an a x b rectangle by N copies, each an exact grid isometry of P (rotations and reflections allowed), with N = 6 or N odd and >= 5. (3) An exhaustive proof that no rectangle is tiled by k copies for any k < N, k >= 2, covering every factorization of k|P| with both sides >= P's minimal width. Two independent methods (DLX and SAT with DRAT-checked UNSAT) must agree. (4) A literature check (Handbook DCG chapter 14, Reid's rectifiable-polyomino pages, Friedman's Math Magic polyomino-order pages) finds no prior example.

partial_wins.statement: A connected polyomino of a known sporadic order (10, 18, 24 or 28) or any other even order not of Golomb's multiple-of-4 type, not appearing on Reid's rectifiable-polyomino pages or in the Handbook, with the explicit tiling and the minimality proof for all smaller counts (DLX plus DRAT-checked SAT, as in criterion (3)).

A connected polyomino whose minimum odd tiling count (smallest odd number of copies tiling some rectangle) is strictly smaller than every value recorded on Reid's and Friedman's live pages, with the explicit odd tiling and a two-method exhaustive proof that no smaller odd count works.

An exhaustive, two-method (DLX + DRAT-checked SAT) census showing that no connected polyomino with at most m cells has order 6 or odd order, for an m strictly larger than any size covered by a published census (literature check required).

targets.verification_method: Verify the tiling by checking that the cell multiset equals the rectangle, that each placed copy is an isometric image of P, and that there are no overlaps. For minimality, enumerate all rectangles of area k|P| for k < N with sides at least P's minimum width. Run DLX (an independent Python implementation of Knuth's Algorithm X) and a CNF with pysat, and check DRAT proofs. Both must agree on infeasibility.
angles: Inverse search: enumerate dissections of small rectangles into 6 congruent pieces via SAT (cell-to-piece variables plus congruence-witness variables per piece pair). Then reject pieces that also tile with 2 or 4 copies, which is a cheap DLX check.
Lift Reid's order-6 heptabolo: refine its triangle grid into squares at scale s and search nearby polyominoes for which the 6-copy tiling survives and 2- and 4-copy tilings die.
For odd orders: Reid built polyominoes whose smallest odd tiling count is 3(p+2). Search these families for members whose even-count tilings are killed by notches, so the overall minimum becomes odd.
Use coloring and invariant arguments (Conway-Lagarias tiling groups) as fast filters to prove '2 and 4 copies impossible' before exact cover.
pitfalls: Confusing 'odd-order' (the smallest odd number of copies tiling a rectangle) with 'order' (the overall minimum). Reid's 3(p+2) results are about the former.
Forgetting that reflections are allowed.
Missing rectangles in the minimality proof, for example very long thin ones or rectangles that need copies in many orientations.
The status source is a 2017 handbook. Confirm against Reid's and Friedman's pages.
Friedman's mathmagic/0299 page concerns 1D disconnected polyominoes, where order 6 and odd orders exist. Those do not count.
The shape must be connected (edge-adjacent cells). Disconnected or corner-touching shapes are not polyominoes.

targets.name: Rectilinear crossing number of K_n: resolve n=28 (7233 vs 7234) or beat a best-known drawing
targets.statement: The rectilinear crossing number cr(K_n) is the minimum, over n points in general position in the plane, of the number of 4-point subsets in convex position (each one gives exactly one crossing of straight-line edges). Exact values are known for n<=27 and n=30. For n=28 the value is 7233 or 7234, and for n=29 and n=31..99 there are gaps between the lower and upper bounds. The goal is a point set with fewer crossings than the best known for some n; a 28-point set with 7233 crossings would settle cr(K_28).
targets.success_criterion: (A) Upper bound: (1) n distinct points with integer coordinates and no three collinear, checked exactly. (2) The exact number of convex-position 4-subsets (= crossings) is STRICTLY LESS than the best known upper bound for that n at verification time: the minimum of Aichholzer's table (http://www.ist.tugraz.at/aichholzer/research/rp/triangulations/crossing/), OEIS A014540, and any newer paper found by a fresh search. (3) The count is at least the table's lower bound (below it means a bug). For n=28, a set with 7233 crossings resolves cr(K_28). (B) A rigorous proof that cr(K_28) = 7234 also resolves n=28, but only if formally verified or machine-certified (e.g. DRAT-checked) with an independently re-derived encoding. Abstract/pseudo-line order types never count for (A).

partial_wins.statement: A machine-certified (exhaustive arrangement-cell enumeration in exact arithmetic, independently reproduced, or DRAT-checked) proof that no 28-point set obtained by adding one point to a specified published optimal 27-point set (bestNNN.asc) has 7233 crossings, or the same for a precisely stated symmetric class.

An abstract order type (pseudo-configuration / CC-system) on n points, axioms checked exactly, whose crossing count is strictly below the live best upper bound for that n, with a documented realizability attempt; logged as a stepping stone only, never as a record.

targets.verification_method: Use exact integer orientation tests in Python (arbitrary-precision ints). Assert there are no collinear triples (O(n^3)). Count convex 4-subsets: a 4-set is convex exactly when no point lies inside the triangle of the other three. Brute force is C(n,4), at most 3.9M for n=100, which is trivial. Cross-check with an independent method that counts crossing segment pairs directly, and confirm the checker reproduces the exact counts of downloaded bestNNN.asc files.
angles: Start from Aichholzer's bestNNN.asc sets. Do local moves (single-point relocation over the arrangement cells of the other points' lines) and simulated annealing on the exact crossing count with O(n^2) incremental updates.

Halving-line/k-edge-guided construction: the crossing count is determined by the k-edge vector. Optimize the <=k-edge profile directly, which also matches the lower-bound proof technique, then realize it geometrically.
Recursive 'double-chain' or 3-fold-symmetric constructions (the records for large n use 3-fold rotational symmetry). Search symmetric configurations, which divides the variables by 3.
For n=28: start from the n=27 and n=30 optimal sets. Delete or add points and run exhaustive arrangement-cell placement for the last 1-2 points.
Order-type space search: work combinatorially with abstract order types (CC-systems), then realize them. A non-realizable abstract order type is not a solution.
pitfalls: Collinear triples or floating-point orientation tests. Use exact integers only.
Counting crossings of K_n in a non-straight-line (topological) drawing. The topological crossing number is a different problem.
Abstract or pseudo-line order types that are not realizable do not count; an explicit coordinate set is required.
The table was last modified in 2015. Search the literature for later improvements before claiming.

targets.name: Tighten God's number bounds for the 4x4x4 cube (OBTM)
targets.statement: Improve either bound on God's number for the 4x4x4 Rubik's Revenge in the outer block turn metric (OBTM). Upper bound 54 OBTM (ananasclassic, 2026-07-21, 18+16+20); confirmed counting lower bound 32 (2015 thread). No exact value is known.
targets.success_criterion: Lower bound: a rigorous counting proof that the number of distinct OBTM move sequences of length <= d, under a canonical form that only identifies sequences proven equal as permutations, is smaller than the exact number of distinct 4x4x4 positions (identical centers indistinguishable, ~7.4e45, recomputed exactly), giving G > d with d STRICTLY ABOVE the best published OBTM lower bound found in the speedsolving thread (latest page) and a fresh search at verification time. Upper bound: a multi-phase solve where each phase's worst case is an exact coset-BFS diameter the verifier reproduces, with the sum STRICTLY BELOW the best published OBTM upper bound at verification time (54 as of 2026-10-03). Both counts must be exact integers recomputed by independent code.

partial_wins.statement: An independent exact reproduction of ananasclassic's phase 1+2 bound of 18 OBTM (and of the 16 and 20 phase diameters) by symmetry-reduced coset BFS with code independent of the original, matching per-depth counts if published.

A rigorous upper or lower bound in another stated metric (SSTM, BTM, STM or QTM) strictly better than the best value for that same metric found in the speedsolving thread and a fresh search at verification time, verified exactly as in the success criterion.

targets.verification_method: Lower bound: an independent transfer-matrix count of canonical sequences in Python with big integers. Check every quotienting relation used (same-axis commutation, any length-k identities) by applying both sides to a permutation representation of the cube. Recompute the exact position count. Upper bound: rerun the phase BFS (symmetry-reduced) and compare per-depth counts.
angles: Sharpen counting lower bounds: beyond the same-axis commutation used in 2015, enumerate short relations of the 4x4x4 move group by computer (BFS to depth 6-8 in the permutation group, looking for collisions). Feed them into a canonical-sequence automaton (as Rokicki did for 3x3x3) and recount.
Exploit the indistinguishable centers: positions are counted modulo center permutations, but sequences that differ only by center-permuting tails collide too. Quantify this rigorously.
Upper bound: try alternative phase decompositions (a different first-phase subgroup or merged phases 2 and 3) and compute exact coset diameters with symmetry and bitset BFS on 10 cores.
State the metric clearly and do the work in one metric (OBTM) to avoid apples-to-oranges claims.
pitfalls: Metric confusion (OBTM, SSTM, BTM, STM, QTM). Records are per metric.
Counting sequences as positions without proving the canonicalization only merges truly equal sequences.
Treating the supercube (oriented centers) count as if it were the normal-cube count.
An upper bound from heuristic 'never saw worse than' solving is not a bound.

The 35 OBTM lower bound comes from a secondary source and was not found in the thread. Treat 32 as the confirmed baseline, but check the latest posts and metric before claiming an improvement to 33 or more.

targets.name: Raise the lower bound on Schur numbers S(6) / S(7) or weak Schur WS(6)
targets.statement: S(k) is the largest N such that {1..N} can be partitioned into k sum-free sets (no x+y=z within a part, x=y allowed); WS(k) is the weak variant (x != y). Exact values are known only for k <= 5 (S(5)=160, Heule 2017). Find an explicit partition beating the best known lower bound for S(6), S(7), WS(6) or WS(7).
targets.success_criterion: (1) An explicit assignment color: {1..N} -> {1..k}, k in {6, 7}. (2) No monochromatic solution of x+y=z, with x=y allowed for Schur and x != y required for weak Schur, checked exhaustively in O(N^2) by two independent implementations. (3) N STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the best known lower bound in the largest-N convention at verification time, taken from the live tables https://oeis.org/A045652 (Schur) or https://oeis.org/A118771 (weak Schur, converting its smallest-failing convention by subtracting 1), arXiv:2607.15034 and a fresh arXiv search (2026-10-03 context: S(6) 536, S(7) 1696, WS(6) 582, WS(7) 1740). (4) Bounds obtained only by plugging into recurrences are not records.
