partial_wins.statement: An explicit, directly verified k-coloring for some k >= 8 (Schur or weak Schur) whose N strictly exceeds the best value at verification time in arXiv 2607.15034, OEIS A045652/A118771 and a fresh search (recurrence-only bounds excluded).

A DRAT/LRAT-checked UNSAT proof (independent encoding) that no sum-free 6-partition of {1..537} exists within a precisely stated template or symmetry class (e.g. the Fredricksen-Sweet symmetric structure or a Rowley-style S-template) not previously ruled out in the literature.

targets.verification_method: Independent Python check: for each color class C (as a set), assert that no x,y in C have x+y in C (for weak Schur, require x<y). This is O(N^2), under 3M operations for N=1700. Check the version convention explicitly: A045652 (S(5)=160) versus A030126 (S(5)=161).
angles: Template and symmetry search in the style of Rowley's S-templates and 2607.15034's shifted S-templates. Search for template colorings that extend a good S(4) or S(5) coloring, using SAT for the special label cells.

Symmetric sum-free partitions (Fredricksen-Sweet: color(x) = color(N+1-x) structure). Encode them as SAT with symmetry, which roughly halves the variables, and use cube-and-conquer over 10 cores for N=537 with 6 colors.
Incremental SAT growth: take the best known 536-coloring, extend N by 1, and repair with local search (WalkSAT or probSAT) over a sliding window of recolorable elements.
For weak Schur, start from the Ahmed et al. 2023 constructions and use SAT on the tail.
Use symmetric colourings: impose c(x) relations with c(N+1-x) (or the Abbott-Hanson/template structure used in 2607.15034) to shrink the SAT instance, then solve with CaDiCaL/kissat.
Extend Fredricksen-Sweet's 536 colouring: run SAT with assumptions fixing most of the colouring and freeing a window near the end, then search for 537.
Use cube-and-conquer on 10 cores with symmetry breaking (colour order fixed by first occurrence).
Use template- or modular-based constructions (colouring determined by x mod m with exceptions) and exhaustive search over small templates.
pitfalls: Off-by-one between conventions: largest partitionable N versus smallest failing N (S(5)=160 vs 161).
Schur requires x=y to be forbidden as well (2x in the same part as x); weak Schur does not. Do not mix the two.
Bounds obtained from recurrences, such as S(k+2) >= 10S(k)+2, are not new direct colorings for k=6 or 7.
Forgetting the x=y case (x+x=z), which weak Schur numbers omit. Do not confuse S(6) with WS(6).
S(6) >= 536 has resisted 26 years of SAT attempts, so expect failure and report partial results honestly.
An off-by-one in N: a colouring of {1..536} only matches the record.

targets.name: Tighten God's number bounds for the 24-puzzle (5x5 sliding tiles, STM)
targets.statement: God's number G for the 5x5 sliding-tile puzzle (single-tile metric) satisfies 152 <= G; the best upper bound is 182 (de Ruiter, 2020 forum claim, not refereed; OEIS still lists 205). Raise the lower bound to >= 154 (parity forces even steps) by certifying that some position needs at least 154 moves, or rigorously lower the upper bound below de Ruiter's 182.
targets.success_criterion: Lower bound: a solvable position P with a certificate that its optimal length is >= 154, STRICTLY ABOVE the best lower bound in the cubeman threads, OEIS A087725 and a fresh search at verification time: either (a) h(P) >= 154 from a provably admissible heuristic recomputed independently (disjoint additive PDBs, walking distance, or max of these), or (b) a complete IDA* to threshold 152 with no solution, reproduced by an independent solver with matching per-iteration node counts. Upper bound: a phase decomposition with phase-shift offsets, every phase diameter and offset table recomputed by full BFS, giving a rigorous bound STRICTLY BELOW the best claimed upper bound at verification time (de Ruiter's 182 as of 2026-10-03, i.e. <= 180). A result of 182 or more is not a record.

partial_wins.statement: A rigorous, independently reproduced verification of de Ruiter's 182 upper bound (cubeman node/view/559): every phase diameter, phase-shift offset and combination recomputed by full BFS from scratch with code independent of his, reproducing exactly 182.

A solvable position P with a provably admissible heuristic value h(P) >= 152 (recomputed independently by the skeptic's own PDB/walking-distance code), giving a seconds-checkable certificate of the current lower bound in place of Rokicki's 10-day IDA* search.

targets.verification_method: Recompute the PDBs from scratch with the verifier's own BFS code, look up h(P), and check the additivity partition is disjoint. For IDA* claims, rerun with an independent solver and compare per-iteration node counts. Confirm P's solvability parity. For upper bounds, rerun each phase BFS and check the maximum depth table.
angles: Search over positions rather than over moves: hill-climb or anneal to find positions maximizing max(additive 6-6-6-6 PDB with reflection, walking distance) in milliseconds per evaluation. If any position scores >= 154, that alone is the certificate. The 180-degree position only scores 140 with WD, but no systematic adversarial search over positions is reported in the sources found.
Stronger admissible heuristics: 7-7-5-5 or 8-8-8 partitions (with 64 GB RAM limits in mind, using compressed or modular PDBs), plus the maximum over symmetric lookups (transpose and conjugation).
Finish Rokicki's ply-152 IDA* on the 180-degree position with modern PDBs and 10-core parallel IDA*. If it completes with no solution, the bound becomes 154. Log node counts for verification.
Upper bound: re-split the three-phase method (which solves 7 tiles, then 9, then the last 8-puzzle) to balance phase diameters. Compute exact phase diameters with disk-based BFS.
pitfalls: Inadmissible heuristics, such as the linear-conflict variants combined incorrectly with additive PDBs.
Parity: a position needing 'at least 153' automatically needs 154. Make sure the statement is about the correct parity class.
The forum's metric ambiguity (single-tile STM vs multi-tile MTM). The 152/205 bounds are STM.
A bound claimed from an IDA* run that was interrupted or that used a buggy goal test.
The upper bound is 182 (de Ruiter 2020), not 205. Any upper bound from 183 to 204 is old news.
The ply-152 IDA* on the 180-degree position costs roughly 4-5 times Rokicki's ten-day 2011 run. It is not feasible in one day without much stronger PDBs.
Forum upper-bound claims are phrased 'I believe'; reproduce before relying on them.

targets.name: Herculaneum papyri: first legible letters in one of the 21 still-unread Vesuvius Challenge First Letters scrolls (official credit only)
targets.statement: The Vesuvius Challenge First Letters Prizes ($50,000 per scroll, at most 10 scrolls, deadline 2027-06-25 23:59 PT; scrollprize.org/prizes fetched 2026-10-08, HTTP 200) pay the first team to produce a programmatically generated image of a virtually unwrapped segment showing at least 10 visible, legible letters within a single 4 cm2 area of an eligible scroll volume, with tifxyz meshes, a 1 cm scale bar, letter sizes in px and mm, text rows annotated without obscuring letters, no manual character annotations (including annotations used as training data), ink outputs that do not overlap any training region, and open-sourcing of code, data, weights and results after winning. Status 2026-10-08: the prizes page still lists 22 eligible volumes, but the substack post of 2026-10-08 ('$50K First Letters Prize awarded for PHerc. 343') credits Erwin Nieuwlaar for PHerc. 343 (windings w047/w048 of the 8.64 um / 116 keV scan; spiral fitter + ink_9um seeds 42/43 + Hecate + his dense_native fine-tune; reproduction repo github.com/Nieuwlaar/pherc343-first-letters with the meshes, image, sidecar JSON and SHA256SUMS), so 21 volumes and 9 prizes remain: PHerc0125, 0175A, 0175B, 0191, 0211, 0257, 0268, 0306B, 0358, 0483A, 0483B, 0490A, 0490B, 0800, 0813, 0826, 0846A, 0846B, 1203, 1218, 1545 (volume ids on the prizes page). PHerc. 1667 was fully read (prize retired Dec 2025); ink was found in PHerc. 1447 (Grand Prize set); a published null attempt exists for PHerc. 0826 (winners page, Aug 2026 progress prize). Official recipe (substack 2026-08-18): VC3D -> spiral fit (GPU) or GrowPatch -> optional Lasagna flatten (GPU) -> vc_render_tifxyz -> ink_9um inference -> conservative iterative labelling. Data: CC BY-NC 4.0 plus EduceLab terms, streamed from the public S3 bucket vesuvius-challenge-open-data (OME-Zarr; PHerc0343 level 0 is 1.33 TB, level 2 about 21 GB); published surface (m7) and Lasagna predictions exist for PHerc0343 under PHerc0343/representations/predictions/.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED (CONFIRMED_SOLUTION) exists ONLY when https://scrollprize.org/prizes or https://scrollprize.org/winners, re-fetched live immediately before claiming, publicly credits a First Letters award to a submission made by the human for a scroll that was on the eligible list and unclaimed at submission time. Nothing produced by an agent alone can be CONFIRMED: every reading of unread text, however convincing, is capped at PROMISING, no partial win may be awarded for a reading of unread text, and no reading leaves local files (no artifact, post, gallery page or upload; the EduceLab terms and the prize terms forbid publicising discoveries). Internal PROMISING requires all of: (a) the scroll is on the eligible list and unclaimed on scrollprize.org/prizes, /winners and the substack archive at verification time; (b) the image is rendered programmatically from the public CT volume and a submitted tifxyz mesh with a 1 cm scale bar, and contains no manual annotation of characters or text, none of the ink labels used anywhere in training were drawn on this scroll, and no pseudo-labels from the claimed region were used (no training/prediction overlap, checked by leak_audit over every labelling iteration); (c) blind reading: at least 2 independent readers who see only the unannotated image each identify at least 10 Greek letters, agreeing in identity and position, within one 4 cm2 window; (d) model-prior null: the same weights on a blank or non-papyrus region of the same scroll and on a z-shuffled render of the claimed region produce no letter-like structures (component statistics reported); (e) a second ink model of a different family shows the same strokes in the same window; (f) fiber continuity across the window is shown in the render (no sheet switch).

partial_wins.statement: Positive control, mechanical and about already-credited text: from the published PHerc. 343 meshes (github.com/Nieuwlaar/pherc343-first-letters outputs/, sha256 per SHA256SUMS) and the public PHerc0343 8.64 um volume streamed from S3, re-render the credited w047/w048 segment on this Mac, run the four named public 9 um models (ink_9um seeds 42 and 43, Hecate 9.6 um, Nieuwlaar/ink9um-dense-native), ensemble as in the repo, and obtain Pearson r >= 0.9 between the agent's ensemble map and the ink channel of the published award image within the credited 4 cm2 window, with the same leak_audit rules; this validates the local render + inference pipeline before any unread scroll is attempted.

targets.verification_method: Verifier re-renders the claimed window from the public zarr volume (streamed at the declared level) and the submitted tifxyz mesh with vc_render_tifxyz or an equivalent pinned script, re-runs the submitted weights on the rendered stack (MPS/CPU, minutes for a 4 cm2 window), checks correlation > 0.99 with the submitted image, runs leak_audit on the training manifest and labelling history, runs the blank-region and z-shuffle nulls and the second-model check, performs the blind letter count with 2 readers who see only the image, and re-fetches scrollprize.org/prizes, /winners and the substack archive to confirm eligibility and non-claim. For p1 the verifier checks the mesh sha256 against the repo's SHA256SUMS and recomputes the correlation.
angles: Do p1 first: the published PHerc. 343 meshes make the GPU-bound spiral-fit and Lasagna steps unnecessary; VC3D renders on macOS (CPU) and the four 9 um models run on MPS/CPU.

For unread scrolls use published m7 surface and Lasagna predictions from S3 (PHerc0343 shows the pattern; check <scroll>/representations/predictions/ for each eligible id) so only rendering and inference run locally; stream level-2 volumes.
Prioritise eligible scrolls with 2.4 um or 8-9 um scans and outer, well-separated wraps where sheet switches are rare.
Average forward and reverse z-order predictions and two model families; require agreement before any human looks, to suppress single-model hallucinations.
Rank windings by a mechanical crackle/ink heatmap statistic (fraction of pixels above a fixed probability in 2x2 cm tiles) before any reading attempt.
pitfalls: Ink models trained on Greek text hallucinate Greek letterforms; blind readers, the blank-region / z-shuffle nulls and the second-model check are mandatory, and a single-model image is never evidence.

Pseudo-labels or fine-tuning on the claimed region, or any hand-drawn letter labels on the target scroll, violate the no-overlap / no-manual-annotation rules; leak_audit must cover every labelling iteration.
Sheet switches splice strokes from two wraps into plausible letters; fiber continuity across the window must be shown.
Publishing or posting a reading before the official announcement breaks the prize terms and the EduceLab terms; readings stay on the contributor's machine for the human.

Full-resolution volumes are 1-3 TB per scroll and spiral fitting / Lasagna need CUDA; attempts that ignore the streamed-level and published-prediction route exhaust disk and time with nothing checkable.
The prizes page lags announcements (it still listed PHerc0343 on 2026-10-08); check the substack archive too.

targets.name: Herculaneum fragment ink detection: beat the 2023 Kaggle winners' own weights on the released hidden-test Fragment 4 (PHercParis1Fr39) under one pinned full-fragment F0.5 protocol, with a model that never saw Fragment 4
targets.statement: The 2023 Kaggle 'Vesuvius Challenge - Ink Detection' ($100K, closed 2023-06-14) trained on Fragments 1-3 and scored pixel F0.5 on a hidden fragment split into two pieces; the hidden fragment was released in Aug 2023 as Fragment 4 = PHercParis1Fr39 (substack '4th fragment released'). Verified live 2026-10-08 with plain curl (HTTP 200, no auth): dl.ash2txt.org/fragments/Frag4/PHercParis1Fr39.volpkg/working/54keV_exposed_surface/ holds PHercParis1Fr39_54keV_inklabels.png (6064 x 9791 px, values {0,1}, 7.76% ink, sha256 a6f39eb59422a4507313ec912185eb92b44e3dd9e2e8e6a97e7b571462ce18fc, last-modified 2023-03-01), PHercParis1Fr39_54keV_mask.png (74.8% valid, sha256 5d437887925ecd6a0f5b943c5b318a6a15c85e9fc97c95d442ada2255b4f51c7), extras/ (IR photo, mesh) and a 65-layer 3.24 um / 54 keV surface volume (65 x ~119 MB TIFF). Ink fraction inside the mask is 10.4% and differs between halves (left 9.0%, right 11.7%), so half-fragment scores are not interchangeable. scrollprize.org/winners (200) lists the Kaggle winners 1st ryches, 2nd RTX23090, 3rd wuyu; the leaderboard page is a JS shell under plain curl (the researcher's figures 0.682693 / 0.682443 / 0.681137 are UNVERIFIED by curl and, because Kaggle scored only the private piece of Frag4 while this target scores the whole masked fragment, they are context, never the bar). No public table reports full-Frag4 F0.5 for any model (searched 2026-10-08). Public weights that are DISQUALIFIED as initialisation because their cards list frag4 in training: scrollprize/resnet50_7.9um_scroll1_frags and scrollprize/resnet50_3um_01122024 (both 'frag1..frag6'). Public weights with no fragment training (clean): scrollprize/timesformer_GP_scroll1 (Scroll 1 segments), timesformer_large_scroll1_01122024, ink_9um (0139/1667/Paris4/0814), hecate (ink bucket), ink_detection_pipeline (GP model); the HF bucket scrollprize/datasets tree 'ink' (0009b, 0139, 0500p2, 1667, 814, 841, man5, phercparis4, unused) contains no fragment data. The open question: a reproducible model trained without any Fragment 4 bytes whose frozen full-Frag4 prediction beats the actual 2023 winning models run under the same protocol.
targets.success_criterion: Protocol (pinned, 'full-Frag4'): a frozen probability map over the whole of PHercParis1Fr39_54keV_inklabels.png's grid (6064 x 9791, resampled by the scout's pinned score_f05.py if the model works at lower resolution), scored as pixel F0.5 (beta 0.5) against inklabels > 0 only where mask > 0, at ONE binarisation threshold written into the attempt manifest (sha256 of weights + threshold) BEFORE the first Frag4 inference of that attempt. Gate A (comparability): the scout has run the human-fetched 2023 1st-place weights (and any other fetched winner) on Frag4 under this identical protocol with their published inference recipe (TTA and all), and recorded the threshold-optimal F0.5 per model in a hash-locked BASELINES.json file with the weights' sha256; the baseline B = max over fetched winners. Gate B (leakage): leak_audit.py hashes every file in the training manifest and every pretrained initialisation; any PHercParis1Fr39 path/hash, any Frag4 IR use, any unsupervised/transductive use of Frag4 bytes, or initialisation from weights whose documented training includes frag4 (resnet50_7.9um_scroll1_frags, resnet50_3um_01122024 or any card listing fragments beyond Frag1-3) fails the attempt. Gate C (selection): model and threshold selection must be justified by a logged Frag1-3 validation split score recorded before Frag4 scoring; every Frag4 scoring in the campaign is appended to FRAG4_EVALS.log and the claim reports the total count. Gate D (model-prior null): the same weights on the z-shuffled 65-layer Frag4 stack (pinned seed) must score F0.5 at most 0.5 x the claimed F0.5, and on the mask region with zero ink labels the predicted-ink fraction must not exceed the baseline model's. Success: F0.5 >= B + 0.02 on the whole masked fragment AND >= B + 0.01 on each of the two halves split at mask-bbox column 3031 (left/right) AND F0.5 >= the top private score shown live on the Kaggle leaderboard URL (direction max; read in a browser by the skeptic since the page is JS). This is an internal full-Frag4 benchmark: it never claims Kaggle leaderboard parity, and it is credited officially only if scrollprize.org/winners credits a Progress Prize submission made by the human.

partial_wins.statement: Scroll-to-fragment transfer, no winners' weights needed: a model trained ONLY on sealed-scroll labels from the HF bucket scrollprize/datasets (trees ink/ and ink_9um/; no fragment labels, no Frag1-4 bytes at all; initialisation only from weights with no fragment training) reaching F0.5 >= 0.55 on the whole masked Frag4 under the pinned protocol, with gates B, C and D satisfied and the threshold declared before Frag4 inference.
Matching the winners on this Mac: with gate A done, a model trained on Fragments 1-3 only (gates B-D) whose full-Frag4 F0.5 is within 0.02 of B and wins on at least one of the two halves.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the two PNGs (150 KB; sha256 must match the statement), loads the claimed frozen map plus the manifest threshold, runs score_f05.py (minutes) for the whole fragment and both halves, and recomputes the baseline numbers from the scout's stored baseline maps with the same script (BASELINES.json must match within 1e-6). Runs leak_audit.py on the training manifest and initialisation weights. Spot-check: downloads 16 central layers of the Frag4 surface volume (1.9 GB), re-runs the submitted weights on 8 random 512 x 512 tiles (seeded) and requires Pearson r > 0.99 with the frozen map on those tiles. Re-runs the z-shuffle null on 8 tiles. Re-reads the Kaggle leaderboard page and scrollprize.org/data_datasets, /2026_open_problems and /winners before any claim.
angles: Fine-tune the released GP TimeSformer-small (villa/ink-detection/optimized_inference supports MPS) on Frag1-3 only; pick epochs/thresholds on a Frag1-3 split, never on Frag4.

p1: run ink_9um (seeds 42/43), Hecate 9.6 um and dense pseudo-label retrains on Frag4 pooled to ~9.7 um (3x XY, z mean-pooling), forward+reverse averaged, upsample the map to the label grid; calibrate the threshold on Frag1-3 pooled the same way.

Reproduce the 2023 2.5D U-Net recipes (central 16-24 layers, large tiles, TTA; 3rd-place training code is on GitHub) on Frag1-3 with MPS, adding scroll pseudo-labels from the HF ink bucket as extra data.
Depth-jittered training (random z-window within the 65 layers) to stop depth-locking, then average forward and reverse z-order predictions.
Topology-aware post-processing calibrated on Frag1-3 (remove components smaller than a stroke, close gaps along the fiber direction) to raise precision, which F0.5 weights 4x over recall.
pitfalls: Kaggle's private score was computed on one hidden piece of Frag4 (public LB on the other, and the two differ a lot), so 'beating 0.68 on the whole fragment' proves nothing; only the winners' weights re-run under the pinned protocol define the bar.

Any peek at Frag4 (threshold sweep, epoch choice, visual checks, repeated attempts picking the best Frag4 score) is leakage; thresholds are declared before inference and the FRAG4_EVALS.log count is reported.
resnet50_3um_01122024 and resnet50_7.9um_scroll1_frags were trained on frag4; fine-tuning from them is disqualifying.
Scoring outside mask.png or at the wrong resolution inflates or deflates F0.5; resample the map to the label grid and score only masked pixels.
Blurry high-recall maps collapse precision; letter-shaped hallucinations from Greek-text priors must be caught by the z-shuffle and blank-region nulls.
Access gate: no download until the human has accepted the EduceLab-Scrolls terms; agents never run vesuvius.accept_terms, never logs in to Kaggle, never redistributes data.

targets.name: Herculaneum optical-profilometry ink segmentation: beat the Sci. Rep. 2026 nnU-Net held-out Dice on the shipped 5-fold splits of scrollprize/profilometer, topography only
targets.statement: Angelotti, Nicolardi, Henderson and Seales, 'Ink detection from surface topography of the Herculaneum papyri', Scientific Reports 16, 27835 (published 2026-06-18, version of record 2026-09-07, doi 10.1038/s41598-026-58467-1; arXiv:2603.27698v1, 2026-03-29) trained default 2D nnU-Net on height maps from optical profilometry of mechanically opened papyri (14 samples / 16 letters from PHerc. 248, 250, 500P2) with five sample-level cross-validation folds, so every sample is held out exactly once (n = 14). Verified live 2026-10-08 (nature.com tables, plain curl): Table 1 primary native height maps median Dice 0.890 [Q1 0.864, Q3 0.905] (plane-detrended 0.891 [0.867, 0.911]); Table 3 at the native row: matched-resolution 0.890 / mean 0.881 +- 0.039, and the native model on the degraded-input pipeline 0.899 (the highest native-row figure); Table 4 leave-one-papyrus-out: 248 held out 0.757 [0.733, 0.812], 250 held out 0.817 [0.755, 0.822], 500P2 held out 0.475 [0.454, 0.482], pooled mean 0.691. The dataset is public: huggingface.co/datasets/scrollprize/profilometer (CC BY-NC 4.0, 14 samples x {calibrated XYZ .txt, normalised uint16 height map _z.tif, brightfield _stack.tif, _label.png with nonzero = ink}, manifest.csv, configs/experiment.json (nnUNetv2 2.5.1 commit 834b80f, trainer nnUNetTrainer, 2d, plans nnUNetResEncUNetPlans_24G, 1000 epochs x 250 iterations, SGD), configs/nnunet/plans for resolution factors 1,2,3,4,6,8,10,16,32, folds/splits_final.json with folds 0-4 (val sizes 3,3,3,3,2) and LOPO folds 5-7). RESOLUTION DISCREPANCY (live): the paper calls the native sampling 0.34 um while the dataset's sampling.json and manifest record 0.68793625 um/px and the README carries a 2026-09-03 NOTICE that the authors are investigating; the factor-k rows of the paper correspond to the dataset's resolution factors k regardless of the physical label (0.34 x 32 = 10.88 um matches the paper's coarsest row). Therefore the released factor-1 data IS the paper's native-row data and the native-row numbers (0.890 / 0.899), not the 0.68 um row (0.817), are the baseline. No code was released. Open: higher held-out Dice on the shipped folds using topography only.
targets.success_criterion: Using exactly folds 0-4 of folds/splits_final.json (sha256 recorded), train one model per fold on that fold's train cases only, with inputs derived solely from the height data (_z.tif or the .txt XYZ, plus any functions of them); _stack.tif brightfield must not be read at any stage (training, pre-training, pseudo-labelling, selection), declared in the manifest and audited. Threshold and checkpoint selection use only the fold's train cases (an inner split), declared before predicting the held-out cases; seeds are fixed and recorded. Freeze binary masks for all 14 held-out cases at native resolution. Skeptic computes per-case Dice against _label.png (nonzero = ink; empty-empty = 1, else standard) with score_dice.py. Gate (calibration): the scout's reproduction of the paper's recipe from configs/experiment.json (nnUNetv2 2d, nnUNetResEncUNetPlans_24G plans shipped in configs/nnunet, same folds; a shortened schedule is allowed if logged) must reach a median >= 0.880 across the 14 held-out cases, with per-case scores stored in a hash-locked BASELINE.json file; without this gate no win is accepted. Success (all): median Dice over the 14 held-out cases >= 0.919 (= highest native-row median 0.899 + 0.02) AND mean >= 0.909 (= 0.889 + 0.02) AND per-case wins over the reproduced baseline on >= 10 of 14 cases AND the live-reread paper tables show no higher factor-1 figure (if they do, the bar moves to that figure + 0.02). Internal benchmark; official only if a journal/arXiv version or scrollprize.org credits a submission made by the human.

partial_wins.statement: Cross-papyrus generalisation on the shipped leave-one-papyrus-out folds 5-7 (train on two papyri, predict all cases of the third; same input, brightfield and selection rules): pooled mean Dice over the 14 held-out cases >= 0.741 (= Table 4 pooled mean 0.691 + 0.05) AND median Dice on the PHerc. 500P2 held-out cases >= 0.575 (= 0.475 + 0.10), with the calibration gate passed on folds 0-4.

Resolution robustness: with every input first block-averaged by the dataset's factor 2 (nonoverlapping 2x2 mean on the continuous height as in configs/experiment.json) and nothing finer ever read, median held-out Dice on folds 0-4 at native label resolution >= 0.901 (= Table 3 factor-2 best figure 0.881 + 0.02), same rules otherwise.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads folds/splits_final.json, configs/, the 14 _label.png (about 1.5 MB) and the 14 _z.tif (about 0.57 GB; the .txt files are optional), checks the submitted masks cover exactly the held-out cases of each fold, computes per-case Dice and the median/mean with score_dice.py (seconds), compares per case with BASELINE.json, and reads the training manifest for brightfield access (every opened path is logged by the pinned data loader). Retrains one fold with the submitted config and seed on MPS when the logged training time is <= 2 h per fold and requires that fold's per-case Dice within 0.03 of the claim; if the recipe exceeds 2 h per fold the claim is capped at PROMISING until a human reruns it.
angles: Reproduce the shipped nnU-Net 2D recipe on MPS (shortened schedule logged) to pass the calibration gate, then add topography-derived channels (gradient magnitude, Laplacian, local roughness, multi-scale detrending) which the paper's detrending ablation suggests help slightly.
Pretrained 2D encoders (timm) on height-map pseudo-RGB with heavy augmentation; small data favours strong priors; test-time flips/rotations.
Thin-stroke losses (clDice / skeleton recall) and boundary refinement, since Dice on ink strokes is boundary-dominated.
p1: domain-robust normalisation (per-sample percentile scaling, roughness equalisation) to lift the PHerc. 500P2 held-out fold, the paper's worst case (0.475).
Leave-one-papyrus-out and per-papyrus reporting on every claim to show gains are not a single-papyrus artefact.
pitfalls: Using the 0.68 um row (0.817) as the baseline because the dataset says 0.69 um/px fabricates a win; the released factor-1 data is the paper's native-row data (0.890 / 0.899).
n = 14 held-out cases: medians move by 0.01-0.02 from seeds alone; fixed seeds, the paired 10-of-14 rule and the skeptic's fold retrain are mandatory.
Brightfield (_stack.tif) makes the task trivial; any read of it, even for pre-training or label QA, voids the attempt.
Re-splitting or selecting on held-out cases is leakage; use the shipped folds unchanged and inner splits for selection.
Label polarity (nonzero = ink) and the empty-empty Dice convention must follow score_dice.py.
The authors' sampling notice may lead to a revised Table; re-read the tables before any claim, and never lower the bar.

targets.name: Papyrus surface detection: beat the released Kaggle-2026 1st-place nnU-Net (surface_m7_nnunet) on a frozen 88-volume holdout of the open 320^3 training mirror under a pinned open topology-aware composite metric
targets.statement: Kaggle 'Vesuvius Challenge - Surface Detection' (2025-11-13 to 2026-02-13, $200K; scrollprize.org/winners: 1st 'Vesuvius Team', 2nd 'risk of overfitting', 3rd 'W & A') scored recto-surface segmentation of 320^3 CT chunks with a composite of TopoScore (Betti matching), SurfaceDice@2 voxels and a VOI-based score; the hidden test labels were never released and the exact metric code lives in the login-gated Kaggle dataset sohier/vesuvius-metric-resources. Verified live 2026-10-08 (plain curl, no login): the TRAIN set is mirrored in the HF bucket scrollprize/datasets at surfaces/kaggle/images and surfaces/kaggle/labels (892 files each, ids sample_00001..sample_00916 with gaps; labels 15.9 GB total; one label inspected = 320x320x320 uint8). Label values are {0 background, 1 surface, 2 ignore} (surface_m7_nnunet model card) and the ignore class is large: 45-88% of voxels in four inspected labels (sample_00007: 84.8%), so the ignore convention decides the score. The 1st-place single model is public: huggingface.co/scrollprize/surface_m7_nnunet (nnU-Net v2 ResEnc-L, 3d_fullres 192^3, fold_0 checkpoint_best ~783 MB, permissive open-source licence, trained on all 786 'Dataset100_VesuviusSurface' volumes, i.e. contaminated for any mirror holdout). Betti-Matching-3D (MIT, github.com/nstucki/Betti-Matching-3D) builds on this Mac at master commit db623be7456ae451beb422af3bbcea94e9863a8f (cmake + pybind11) and took 174 s on a worst-case speckled synthetic 320^3 pair, so per-volume runtime caps are part of the protocol. Frozen holdout: every mirror sample whose numeric id satisfies id % 10 == 7 (88 volumes). Open problem #2 on scrollprize.org/2026_open_problems (surface topology). No public post-competition leaderboard exists.
targets.success_criterion: Metric (pinned, open): score_surface.py, written by the scout on day 1 and frozen by sha256 in a hash-locked METRIC.sha256 file before the baseline run; it (1) sets every voxel with label == 2 to 0 in BOTH label and prediction, (2) binarises the label as == 1 and the prediction at the threshold declared in the attempt manifest (default > 0 for binary masks), (3) computes TopoScore = weighted topological F1 from Betti matching with github.com/nstucki/Betti-Matching-3D at commit db623be7456ae451beb422af3bbcea94e9863a8f (dims 0/1/2 weighted .34/.33/.33, inactive dims skipped, wall-clock cap 10 min per volume, a cap hit = TopoScore 0 for that mask), SurfaceDice at tolerance 2 voxels, and VOI score = 1 / (1 + VOI) with 26-connectivity components, and (4) composite = 0.30 x TopoScore + 0.35 x SurfaceDice + 0.35 x VOI score. Any change to the script resets every stored score. Success: binary 320^3 masks for ALL 88 holdout volumes (id % 10 == 7), from a model whose training manifest (leak_audit.py) lists only mirror ids with id % 10 != 7 plus optional other open data, with NO pretrained weights unless their documented training data provably excludes every holdout id (scrollprize surface checkpoints incl. surface_m7_nnunet, surface_recto*, fiber_* are presumed contaminated and are disallowed as initialisation or ensemble members); mean composite >= baseline mean + 0.02 AND per-volume wins on >= 53 of 88 volumes AND mean SurfaceDice not more than 0.01 below the baseline's. Internal benchmark: the Kaggle URL is re-read for context only, no leaderboard parity is claimed, and official credit exists only if scrollprize.org/winners credits a Progress Prize submission made by the human.

partial_wins.statement: Post-processing only: a deterministic function (hole filling, merger cutting, component pruning, distance-based thinning) applied to surface_m7_nnunet's own softmax probabilities on the 88 holdout volumes (produced and stored by the scout), with parameters chosen on non-holdout volumes only, raising the mean composite by >= 0.02 and winning on >= 53 of 88 volumes; the skeptic re-applies the code to the stored probabilities.

From scratch on this Mac: a model with no pretrained weights, trained <= 12 logged wall-clock hours on non-holdout mirror volumes, whose holdout mean composite is within 0.05 of the contaminated baseline and whose mean SurfaceDice is within 0.05 of it.

Topology at constant overlap: under the full-win training rules, mean TopoScore >= baseline + 0.05 while mean SurfaceDice is not more than 0.01 below the baseline's, with TopoScore wins on >= 53 of 88 volumes.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic fetches the 88 holdout labels from the HF resolve URLs (about 60 MB), checks METRIC.sha256 against the script, builds Betti-Matching-3D once at the pinned commit (minutes), verifies sha256 of all 88 submitted masks and of the stored baseline masks, then re-scores a seeded random subset of 20 holdout volumes (seed 0 over the sorted id list) for both submission and baseline within one hour (<= 3 min per volume at the cap) and requires |recomputed - stored| < 1e-6 for every one of them; the 88-volume means are then taken from the hash-locked stored tables. leak_audit.py checks the training manifest for holdout ids and disallowed initialisations. Label ignore handling is checked by asserting the script zeroes label==2 voxels.
angles: Day 1: install nnunetv2 + torch (MPS), run surface_m7_nnunet with nnUNetv2_predict -device mps on the 88 holdout volumes (store softmax and masks), freeze score_surface.py and BASELINE.json.
p1: topology-aware post-processing of the stored m7 probabilities (cut thin bridges between sheets, fill small holes along the sheet, prune components below a size chosen on non-holdout data).
Train a small 3D U-Net (128^3 patches, MPS) with clDice / skeleton-recall losses on non-holdout volumes; distance-transform regression thresholded to a 1-2 voxel sheet (open problem #2 suggestion).
Fiber-direction priors derived on the fly from the CT (structure tensor) to cut mergers between adjacent wraps; no fiber_* checkpoints.
Report TopoScore, SurfaceDice and VOI separately per volume so p3 can be checked.
pitfalls: Label value 2 is ignore and covers most voxels; binarising labels at > 0 would count ignore as surface and wreck every score. The pinned script zeroes label==2 in both arrays.
The open metric is not Kaggle's exact code (login-gated); pin the script by sha256, never claim leaderboard parity, and never edit the script after the baseline run.
The baseline trained on the holdout, so a loss means nothing and the holdout rule (id % 10 == 7) must never be 'fixed' after seeing results.

Betti matching can take minutes on noisy masks (174 s measured on a speckled synthetic); the 10-minute cap and the 20-volume skeptic subset are part of the protocol, and submitting noisy masks to time out the baseline is impossible because baseline scores are stored and hash-locked.
Label noise (approximate recto labels) caps achievable scores; gains under 0.02 are inside label noise, hence the margin.
Access gate: data only after the human accepted the terms; never redistribute the mirror.

targets.name: RobustBench CIFAR-10 L2 (eps 0.5): lower a listed model's robust accuracy below the leaderboard value with a stronger L2 attack
targets.statement: The RobustBench CIFAR-10 L2 eps=0.5 leaderboard (model_info/cifar10/L2, 21 JSON files as of 2026-10-09; the website table is JS-rendered, the GitHub JSONs are the primary machine-readable record) lists 20 robust open-weight models plus the undefended 'Standard' baseline, each evaluated with standard AutoAttack (L2 APGD-CE, APGD-T, FAB-T, Square). Only ONE entry carries an 'external' (adaptive-attack) value, Amini2024MeanSparse_S-WRN-70-16 (autoattack_acc 87.28, external 84.33); for the other 19 robust models the single-seed AutoAttack number is the best known. The last change to the L2 model_info files was 2023-03-03 (Wang2023Better). The L2 threat model has had far less adaptive-attack scrutiny than Linf: A3 and MALT are Linf-only; the strongest recent published L2 effort, Adversarial Frontiers (arXiv:2607.19855, Jul 2026, minimum-norm ensembles incl. FMN/ALMA/DDN-style solvers/APGDmin) matched but did NOT lower AutoAttack's value on the L2-trained CIFAR-10 models it tested (Augustin, Engstrom, Rade, Sehwag) on 1000-sample subsets, while it did lower AA on Linf-trained models evaluated under L2. Beating the table on a genuinely L2-trained model on the full 10,000-image test set is therefore open and non-trivial. CPU-realistic entries: Rade2021Helper_R18_ddpm (76.15), Rebuffi2021Fixing_R18_cutmix_ddpm (75.86), Sehwag2021Proxy_R18 (74.41), Rice2020Overfitting PreActRN18 (67.68), Ding2020MMA WRN-28-4 (66.09); WRN-28-10 / WRN-34-10 entries overnight. (Numbers quoted are the 2026-10-09 snapshot; the live JSON is authoritative.)
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved float32 tensor x_adv of shape 10000x3x32x32 of adversarial inputs for the FULL standard CIFAR-10 test set (torchvision test split, ToTensor only, pixel range [0,1], no normalisation outside the model) against ONE model loaded unmodified via robustbench.utils.load_model(model_name, dataset='cifar10', threat_model='L2') in eval mode, such that (a) for every image the single float64 L2 norm of the flattened 3072-dim perturbation satisfies ||x_adv - x||_2 <= 0.5 + 1e-6 and 0 <= x_adv <= 1; (b) the robust accuracy recomputed by the skeptic's OWN forward pass (fraction of the 10,000 images whose clean prediction is correct AND whose adversarial argmax is still correct; ties count as not fooled) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the model's best-known value min(autoattack_acc, external) in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobustBench/robustbench/master/model_info/cifar10/L2/<Model>.json, re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 20 images (0.20 percentage points; AutoAttack's own single-seed variance is of order 0.1 points and a multi-seed union of standard AutoAttack alone can shave ~10 images, so 10 images is noise); and (c) the value is also strictly lower (by >= 20 images) than any FULL-test-set robust accuracy already published for the same model under L2 eps=0.5 in arXiv papers of the last 24 months found by the NOVELTY skeptic (minimum-norm / FMN / ALMA / DDN / APGDmin evaluations included). Values published on subsets (e.g. the 1000-sample numbers in arXiv:2607.19855 Table 6) are not full-test-set values and do not replace the table, but the author must cite them. Only models present in the live model_info/cifar10/L2 directory count; the undefended 'Standard' entry (0.00) is excluded.

partial_wins.statement: The same full-test-set result (strictly lower by >= 20 images than live min(autoattack_acc, external), under the L2-norm, range, shape and dtype checks) for a model whose live L2 model_info JSON has NO 'external' value AND for which the NOVELTY skeptic finds no published full-test-set L2 eps=0.5 robust accuracy below the autoattack_acc; i.e. clause (c) is vacuous for that model. Must be re-fetched live. 'Standard' excluded.

For a model whose live L2 model_info JSON carries an 'external' value (today only Amini2024MeanSparse_S-WRN-70-16), a full-test-set robust accuracy strictly lower by >= 20 images than BOTH the live autoattack_acc and the live 'external' value (re-fetched), under the same checks.

A reproducible per-image attack-strength finding: at least 50 CIFAR-10 test images (indices listed), for one RN18/PreActRN18 L2 model, on which the skeptic's OWN run of standard AutoAttack (autoattack package, version='standard', norm='L2', eps=0.5, seed 0, full 4-attack ensemble, run on exactly those indices) finds no adversarial example but the attacker's saved perturbations (checked for L2 norm <= 0.5 + 1e-6, range, and misclassification by the skeptic's forward pass) do. This is NOT a leaderboard change and must be reported as such; it does not count if the attacker's x_adv merely reproduce AutoAttack with other seeds (the attacker must disclose the method and seeds).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic writes their OWN checker (never runs the author's): pip install robustbench autoattack torch torchvision; model = robustbench.utils.load_model(<Model>, dataset='cifar10', threat_model='L2').eval; record sha256 of the downloaded weight file and the robustbench version; load the torchvision CIFAR-10 test set (10,000 images, ToTensor only) in canonical order; load the author's x_adv tensor and manifest (sha256 of the tensor file must match the manifest frozen in REPRODUCE.md); assert shape 10000x3x32x32 and dtype float32; in float64 compute per-image d = ||(x_adv - x).reshape(10000, -1)||_2 and assert d.max <= 0.5 + 1e-6 (one norm over all 3072 pixels per image, never per channel/row) and x_adv.min >= 0, x_adv.max <= 1; compute clean and adversarial predictions in batches on CPU in eval mode (RN18 ~5-10 min, WRN-28-10 ~30-60 min); robust_acc = mean(clean_correct & adv_correct) with argmax ties counted as not fooled. Re-fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobustBench/robustbench/master/model_info/cifar10/L2/<Model>.json live (plain curl, default UA, no retries through 403/429), quote value and fetch time, compare against min(autoattack_acc, external) with the 20-image margin. The NOVELTY skeptic searches arXiv (last 24 months) for full-test-set L2 eps=0.5 values for the same model (FMN, ALMA, DDN, APGDmin, Adversarial Frontiers arXiv:2607.19855, HO-FMN arXiv:2407.08806 which is Linf-only) and fails the claim if any is lower. For p3: run autoattack.AutoAttack(model, norm='L2', eps=0.5, version='standard', seed=0) on exactly the listed indices and confirm it finds no adversarial example on >= 50 of them while the author's perturbations misclassify under the skeptic's own forward pass. If the GitHub JSON cannot be fetched today, the comparison is PENDING TABLE CHECK and no meets_* may be true.
angles: Minimum-norm attacks as a complement to fixed-eps APGD: run FMN-L2 / DDN / ALMA to find the smallest fooling perturbation per image, then keep those with norm <= 0.5; minimum-norm methods often beat fixed-budget projected methods on exactly the borderline images AutoAttack misses.
APGD-L2 with many restarts and long schedules on the residual robust set of an RN18 model, with targeted versions against all 9 classes and per-image loss selection (CE, DLR, CW-margin).
Transfer-seeded starts from other L2 robust models and from the same model's Linf adversarial examples rescaled to the L2 ball.

Boundary polishing: after any success, binary-search the perturbation scale toward the clean image to free budget, then re-run a few APGD steps from the boundary point; also try Linf-to-L2 'corner' starts (sign patterns scaled to norm 0.5).
Square Attack L2 with large query budgets on the residual images of a small model.
pitfalls: Computing the L2 norm per channel or per row, or in float32 where rounding masks violations; always a single float64 norm over all 3072 pixels per image.
Loading the Linf-trained variant of a model name instead of the L2 variant (threat_model argument), or attacking in normalised input space.
Clipping to [0,1] after the norm check (clipping can only shrink the norm, but the saved tensor must itself be checked).
Seed variance and tiny margins; fewer than 10 images is noise. Also compare with the live JSON, not the website or a cached copy.
Novelty: minimum-norm attack papers (FMN, ALMA, DDN) report L2 robust accuracies for several RobustBench models; the NOVELTY skeptic must search for them.

Prior art: Adversarial Frontiers (arXiv:2607.19855, Jul 2026) Table 6 reports L2 eps=0.5 robust accuracy on 1000-sample subsets for Augustin, Engstrom, Rade and Sehwag L2 models and did NOT beat AutoAttack on them (equal or +0.1); it did beat AA on Linf-trained models under L2, which are NOT on the L2 leaderboard. Do not confuse the two, and do not compare a 10k-image number against a 1k-subset number.

Cheap non-wins: re-running standard AutoAttack with several seeds and taking the per-image union, or adding restarts, gains a handful of images; that is why the margin is 20 images, and the author must disclose the method and seeds. A multi-seed AA union by itself is not a 'stronger attack' finding.
Shape/dtype: the saved tensor must be the full 10,000 images in canonical torchvision order (not a subset, not shuffled); a per-image index map is not acceptable for the full criterion or p1/p2.

Compute: FMN/DDN-style attacks on an RN18 over 10k images are CPU-hours; APGD-L2 with many restarts or the full standard AutoAttack on the whole test set is CPU-days on a WRN; do not claim a full-set result from a partial run.

targets.name: RobustBench CIFAR-10 Linf (eps 8/255): a stronger attack that lowers a listed model's robust accuracy below the leaderboard value
targets.statement: RobustBench (robustbench.github.io) is the standard leaderboard for adversarially robust CIFAR-10 classifiers under Linf eps=8/255. Each of the 99 listed models (open weights, loaded with robustbench.utils.load_model) carries an 'autoattack_acc' (standard AutoAttack: APGD-CE, APGD-T, FAB-T, Square, full 10k test set) and, for 17 of them (verified 2026-10-09), an 'external' value from a stronger evaluation: the original authors' hybrid AutoAttack+MultiTargeted runs (Gowal2020/2021, Rebuffi2021 WRNs), APGD with BPDA for the two Amini2024MeanSparse models (non-differentiable operator), Adaptive AutoAttack for Bai2024MixedNUTS, transfer APGD for Kang2021Stable (unreliable: true) and 30-restart Square for Xiao2020Enhancing (unreliable: true). The leaderboard's own policy (README section 'Adding a new evaluation') is that any evaluation yielding a LOWER robust accuracy than AutoAttack gets added; the last such batch was the 'adaptive-eval' PR merged 2025-02-05, repo last pushed 2026-04-14. The open question for each model is whether its best-known robust accuracy can be lowered further by an adaptive or better-optimised attack. Known headroom is small: Adaptive Auto Attack (A3, Liu et al., CVPR 2022, arXiv:2203.05154, Table 1: 35 CIFAR-10 models) lowers AutoAttack by 0.04-0.16 points on adversarially trained models (avg 0.1), AutoAE (arXiv:2211.12713, Table: 20 CIFAR-10 Linf models) by 0.01-0.17 (median 0.05), PMA+ (arXiv:2411.15210, CVPR 2025, Tables 3/6: 10 top CIFAR-10 models) by 0.02-0.15, and MALT (arXiv:2407.02240, NeurIPS 2024) by 0.00-0.07 on CIFAR-100 only (no CIFAR-10 results). NONE of these published lower numbers has been copied into the model_info 'external' fields, so for roughly 30 models the literature already sits below the leaderboard value; a claim must beat the literature, not just the JSON. arXiv:2402.17018 (TMLR 2025) shows AutoAttack badly overestimating a randomized ensemble (90.8% -> 18.2%), but randomized defenses are not on this leaderboard. On this Mac (CPU only) the realistic targets are the ResNet-18 / PreActResNet-18 entries (Rade2021Helper_R18_ddpm 57.09, Rade2021Helper_R18_extra 57.67 [AutoAE: 57.63], Rebuffi2021Fixing_R18_ddpm 56.66, Sehwag2021Proxy_R18 55.54 [A3 lists a 'Proxy ResNet-18' at AA 54.43 -> 54.35, apparently a different checkpoint], Addepalli2022Efficient_RN18 52.48, Addepalli2021Towards_RN18 51.06 [A3: 51.02], Gowal2021Improving_R18_ddpm_100m 58.63 with external 58.50); a full 10k-image adaptive attack on an RN18 is laptop-hours (standard AutoAttack alone is several CPU-hours on an RN18). The result object is a tensor of 10,000 perturbed images.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved set of adversarial inputs for the FULL standard CIFAR-10 test set (10,000 images, the torchvision test split in its canonical order, pixel range [0,1], no normalisation outside the model) against one CIFAR-10 Linf model loaded unmodified via robustbench.utils.load_model(model_name, dataset='cifar10', threat_model='Linf') in eval mode, with weights downloaded fresh by the skeptic (never attacker-supplied), such that (a) every perturbation satisfies max|x_adv - x| <= 8/255 (checked in float64 with tolerance 1e-6) and 0 <= x_adv <= 1, (b) the robust accuracy, computed by the skeptic's own forward pass as the fraction of the 10,000 images whose clean prediction is correct AND whose adversarial prediction (argmax of logits; ties count as not fooled) is still correct, is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the model's best-known value min(autoattack_acc, external) in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobustBench/robustbench/master/model_info/cifar10/Linf/<Model>.json, re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 10 images (0.10 percentage points, to exceed AutoAttack seed variance), and (c) the value is also strictly lower (by at least 1 image) than every robust accuracy already published for the same model name and threat model by Adaptive Auto Attack (arXiv:2203.05154 Table 1), AutoAE (arXiv:2211.12713, CIFAR-10 Linf table), PMA / PMA+ (arXiv:2411.15210 Tables 3 and 6), MALT (arXiv:2407.02240), and any arXiv paper of the last 24 months found by the NOVELTY skeptic; a published row counts as covering the model when its AutoAttack column matches the JSON autoattack_acc within 0.05. Models with footnotes changing eps (0.031 instead of 8/255) must be attacked at 8/255 exactly as RobustBench evaluates them. How x_adv was produced is irrelevant to the check (BPDA/transfer/anything is allowed): only the skeptic's plain forward pass on the unmodified deterministic model counts. Any 'robust accuracy' inferred from attack logs, per-image flags, subsets, or a different test order does not count.

partial_wins.statement: The same full-test-set result (perturbation, prediction and live re-fetch checks identical to the main criterion) for a model that NO published adaptive evaluation covers (not in A3 Table 1, not in the AutoAE CIFAR-10 Linf table, not in PMA/PMA+ Tables 3/6, not in MALT, and nothing found by the NOVELTY skeptic for the last 24 months; e.g. as of 2026-10-09 Rade2021Helper_R18_ddpm, Rebuffi2021Fixing_R18_ddpm, Addepalli2022Efficient_RN18, Gowal2021Improving_R18_ddpm_100m appear uncovered), with robust accuracy strictly lower than live min(autoattack_acc, external) by at least 20 images (0.20 points: above the 0.04-0.17 point gain that A3/AutoAE/PMA+ routinely obtain on adversarially trained models, so it is not merely re-running a known attack).

For a model whose live model_info has 'unreliable': true (as of 2026-10-09: Kang2021Stable autoattack 71.28 / external 64.20; Xiao2020Enhancing autoattack 18.50 / external 7.40, which must be attacked at 8/255), a full-test-set robust accuracy strictly lower by >= 10 images than BOTH the autoattack_acc and the external value, under the same checks (a)-(c).

A reproducible per-image result: at least 50 CIFAR-10 test images (indices listed), for one RN18/PreActRN18 model, on which the skeptic's own run of standard AutoAttack (autoattack package, version='standard', seed 0, full 4-attack ensemble, run on exactly those indices) finds no adversarial example but the attacker's saved perturbations (checked for eps, box and misclassification by the skeptic's forward pass) do. This is an attack-strength finding, not a leaderboard change, and must be reported as such; it never triggers a record claim.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic writes their own checker: pip install robustbench autoattack torch torchvision; load the model by name via robustbench.utils.load_model into a fresh cache (never accept attacker-supplied weights or model code), model.eval; load the torchvision CIFAR-10 test set (train=False, ToTensor only, canonical order) and confirm its sha256 against the attacker's manifest; load the attacker's x_adv tensor (shape 10000x3x32x32, dtype float32) and manifest; assert in float64 that (x_adv - x).abs.max <= 8/255 + 1e-6 and 0 <= x_adv <= 1; compute clean and adversarial predictions in batches on CPU (RN18: ~5 min; WRN-28-10: ~30 min); robust_acc = mean(clean_correct & adv_correct), reported as an integer count out of 10000. Re-fetch the live model_info JSON (quote URL and fetch time) and compare to min(autoattack_acc, external) * 100 images; then open A3 Table 1 (ar5iv 2203.05154), the AutoAE CIFAR-10 table (ar5iv 2211.12713) and PMA Tables 3/6 (arxiv.org/html/2411.15210) and compare against every row whose AutoAttack column matches the JSON autoattack_acc within 0.05. For p3 run AutoAttack standard (seed 0) on the listed indices and confirm it fails on each while the attacker's x_adv succeeds. If GitHub is unreachable the comparison is PENDING TABLE CHECK.
angles: Start from AutoAttack's own robust set: run APGD-CE/APGD-T once on an RN18 model, keep only the images it fails on (~5,700), and spend the whole budget there with many random restarts, longer schedules (500-1000 steps), margin/DLR/CW losses with per-image loss selection, and targeted attacks against all 9 classes (AutoAttack's APGD-T uses only the top-3 non-true classes).

Re-implement Adaptive Auto Attack (A3) ideas: adaptive initialisation from directions that fooled neighbouring images, online statistics-based discarding, plus a final 'minimum-margin' polishing pass; A3's own numbers for the covered models are the bar to beat.

Composite/transfer seeding: generate adversarial examples from several other robust RobustBench models (transfer), then use them as starting points for APGD on the target; robust models share adversarial directions, and transfer starts often succeed where random starts do not.

Gradient quality: attack in float64, use exact (not detached) BN statistics in eval mode, try input-space line search along the final APGD direction, and test boundary points at exactly +-8/255 corners (sign patterns) with coordinate-wise flips (a cheap 'bit-flip' local search over the hypercube vertices).

Cheap full-set black-box top-up: Square Attack with 20k+ queries on the remaining unbroken images of an RN18 model is CPU-feasible and is exactly the signal AutoAttack's flags doc says indicates overestimation.

Pick the model with the largest gap between 'reported' and 'autoattack_acc' or with large gaps between APGD-CE and APGD-T results (available from a local AutoAttack run), which indicates loss-landscape pathologies to exploit.
pitfalls: Wrong model or wrong mode: not using robustbench.utils.load_model with the exact model_name, loading in train mode (BatchNorm uses batch statistics and makes the model look weaker), or using a different test split/order. Skeptic must check weights sha256 and eval mode.

Perturbation bound violations hidden by float32 rounding, by saving to uint8 PNG, or by clipping after the eps check; always check in float64 on the saved tensor and reject any pixel over 8/255 by more than 1e-6.

Counting images that are already misclassified on clean inputs as 'new' adversarial successes, or counting a prediction flip on an image whose clean prediction was wrong; robust accuracy must be recomputed from scratch, not inferred from AutoAttack's per-image logs.

Seed noise: AutoAttack numbers differ by a few hundredths of a point between runs; a difference below 10 images is not a record. Also the website table and model_info JSON can lag each other: use the JSON (the website is generated from it) and quote fetch time.

Novelty trap: A3 (2022) already reports lower numbers than AutoAttack for many RobustBench models; matching A3's number is not new. The NOVELTY skeptic must open A3 Table 1 and the model's 'external'/footnote fields.
Changing the threat model (eps 0.031 vs 8/255, L2 instead of Linf, perturbing after normalisation) or attacking a logit-scaled/softmax wrapper instead of the leaderboard model.

Published adaptive tables (A3, AutoAE, PMA) sometimes evaluate a different checkpoint under the same author/year: match rows by RobustBench model name AND an AutoAttack column within 0.05 of the JSON autoattack_acc (e.g. A3's 'Proxy ResNet-18' shows AA 54.43 while RobustBench Sehwag2021Proxy_R18 is 55.54). A row that does not match does not excuse ignoring it: the NOVELTY skeptic must say which checkpoint it is.

The model_info 'external' fields do NOT include the A3 / AutoAE / PMA+ literature; roughly 30 models already have published numbers below the leaderboard value. Beating only the JSON number on such a model is NOT a record.

Compute underestimation: standard AutoAttack on an RN18 over 10k images is several CPU-hours (APGD-T alone is 9 targets x 100 steps on ~5.7k images); a full adaptive campaign that only finishes on a subset cannot be scored. Partial coverage must be reported as p3 at most.

targets.name: RobustBench CIFAR-100 Linf (eps 8/255): lower a listed model's robust accuracy below the best published value with a stronger attack
targets.statement: The RobustBench CIFAR-100 Linf eps=8/255 leaderboard lists 38 open-weight models (model_info/cifar100/Linf, verified 2026-10-09 via the GitHub API). Only 4 carry an 'external' value: Wang2023Better_WRN-70-16 42.67->42.66 and Wang2023Better_WRN-28-10 38.83->38.77 (both MALT, Melamed et al. 2024), Bai2024MixedNUTS 41.91->41.80 (the paper's own adaptive AutoAttack), and Amini2024MeanSparse_S-WRN-70-16 44.78->42.25 (APGD with BPDA through the MeanSparse operator; a 2.5-point drop showing post-hoc 'robustness enhancers' can be strongly over-estimated by AutoAttack). Beyond the leaderboard, four papers have published lower-than-AutoAttack numbers for CIFAR-100 models that were NOT folded into the table: Adaptive Auto Attack / A3 (arXiv:2203.05154, Table 1: 12 models, e.g. Gowal2020Uncovering_extra 36.86, Rebuffi2021Fixing_70_16 34.55, Rebuffi 28_10 32.00, Addepalli2021Towards_WRN34 30.31, Addepalli2021Towards_PARN18 27.09, Wu2020 28.78, Hendrycks2019 28.31, Sitawarin2020 24.51, Rice2020Overfitting 18.90, Gowal2020Uncovering 29.99, LBGAT 34-20 30.12 and 34-10 29.18 at eps 0.031), AutoAE (arXiv:2211.12713, Table 1: Gowal_extra 36.86, Rebuffi 70_16 34.62, Rebuffi 28_10 32.02, LBGAT 34-20 30.13, Gowal 30.00), MALT (arXiv:2407.02240, Table 1: Gowal_extra 36.81, Cui2023Decoupled_WRN-28-10 39.18 unchanged), and PMA/PMA+ (arXiv:2411.15210, Tables 3 and 6: Wang 70-16 42.63, Cui2023Decoupled 28-10 39.17, Wang 28-10 38.77, Gowal_extra 36.85, XCiT-L12 34.95, Rebuffi 70_16 34.63, XCiT-M12 34.13, Pang2022 WRN70_16 33.00). The bar for any model is therefore the minimum over the live table and all of these. Headroom argument: standard AutoAttack's APGD-T and FAB-T attack only the 9 highest-scoring wrong classes (autoattack.py set_version: n_target_classes = 9), i.e. 9 of 99 on CIFAR-100, and MALT also stops at 9, so wider targeted sweeps, per-image loss selection and BPDA-style attacks on the post-hoc defenses have real room. As of 2026-10-09 about 18 of the 38 models have NO published stronger-than-AutoAttack number at all (see partial win p1). CPU-realistic entries: Rade2021Helper_R18_ddpm (28.88, no published adaptive number), Rebuffi2021Fixing_R18_ddpm (28.50, none), Addepalli2022Efficient_RN18 (27.67, none), Addepalli2021Towards_PARN18 (27.14; A3 27.09), Rice2020Overfitting PreActRN18 (18.95; A3 18.90), and the WRN-28-10 / WRN-34-10 entries overnight.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved tensor of adversarial inputs for the FULL standard CIFAR-100 test set (all 10,000 torchvision CIFAR100(train=False) images in their standard order, fine labels, [0,1] range, no normalisation applied before the model) against one model loaded unmodified via robustbench.utils.load_model(model_name, dataset='cifar100', threat_model='Linf') in eval mode, with (a) every perturbation satisfying max|x_adv - x| <= 8/255 (float64 check, tolerance 1e-6) and 0 <= x_adv <= 1; (b) skeptic-recomputed robust accuracy (fraction of the 10,000 images whose adversarial argmax equals the label; clean-misclassified images count as non-robust; argmax ties count as not fooled) that is LOWER by at least 10 images (0.10 points) than the BAR, where BAR = min over: min(autoattack_acc, external) in the live https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobustBench/robustbench/master/model_info/cifar100/Linf/<Model>.json re-fetched immediately before claiming (direction: min); every robust accuracy published for the same model and threat model in A3 (arXiv:2203.05154, Table 1), AutoAE (arXiv:2211.12713, Table 1), MALT (arXiv:2407.02240, Table 1) and PMA/PMA+ (arXiv:2411.15210, Tables 3 and 6); and every value for that model found by the NOVELTY skeptic in arXiv papers of the last 24 months and in open RobustBench issues/PRs; and (c) the skeptic's recomputed clean accuracy matches the model_info clean_acc to within 0.05 points, proving the right model, test set and label set were used. Fewer than 10 images below the BAR is seed noise, not a win.

partial_wins.statement: The full-test-set result of the success criterion (>= 10 images below live min(autoattack_acc, external), same perturbation, prediction and clean-accuracy checks) for a CIFAR-100 Linf model with NO published stronger-than-AutoAttack evaluation: no 'external' field, not in A3 Table 1, not in AutoAE Table 1, not in MALT Table 1, not in PMA Tables 3/6, and nothing found by the NOVELTY skeptic's 24-month sweep. As of 2026-10-09 that set is: Bai2023Improving_edm, Bai2023Improving_trades, Cui2023Decoupled_WRN-34-10, Cui2023Decoupled_WRN-34-10_autoaug, Debenedetti2022Light_XCiT-S12, Pang2022Robustness_WRN28_10, Jia2022LAS-AT_34_10, Jia2022LAS-AT_34_20, Addepalli2022Efficient_RN18, Addepalli2022Efficient_WRN_34_10, Cui2020Learnable_34_10_LBGAT9_eps_8_255, Cui2020Learnable_34_10_LBGAT0, Sehwag2021Proxy, Chen2024Data_WRN_34_10, Chen2021LTD_WRN34_10, Rade2021Helper_R18_ddpm, Rebuffi2021Fixing_R18_ddpm, Chen2020Efficient; the skeptic must re-derive this set live, not trust the list.

For one of the post-hoc / ensemble defenses Amini2024MeanSparse_S-WRN-70-16 (live autoattack 44.78, external 42.25), Bai2024MixedNUTS (41.91, external 41.80), Bai2023Improving_edm (38.72, no external) or Bai2023Improving_trades (35.15, no external): a full-test-set robust accuracy at least 10 images below BOTH the live min(autoattack_acc, external) and every value for that model published in the papers enumerated in the success criterion or found by the NOVELTY skeptic, passing the same perturbation, prediction and clean-accuracy checks. These are the defenses AutoAttack is known to over-estimate, so the attack must be run on the exact robustbench-loaded model (the operator / mixing network included), not on a surrogate.

Attack-strength finding, not a leaderboard change: for one RN18/PreActRN18 CIFAR-100 Linf model, at least 50 test images that are still correctly classified after the skeptic's own standard AutoAttack run (version='standard', seed 0, on the same robustbench-loaded model) but are misclassified by the attacker's saved perturbations (eps and range checks as in the success criterion). The attacker's method must be a single disclosed procedure with a stated compute budget; a union over many AutoAttack seeds, restarts or random-start reruns of the standard attacks does not qualify, and the skeptic reports how many of the 50 standard AutoAttack with seed 1 also finds.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic's own script, on CPU: (1) pip-install robustbench from GitHub at a pinned commit and load the model with robustbench.utils.load_model(model_name, dataset='cifar100', threat_model='Linf'); record the sha256 of the downloaded weights file and confirm it matches a fresh download; model.eval. (2) Load torchvision CIFAR100(train=False) with ToTensor only, fine labels, standard order; recompute clean accuracy and require |clean - model_info clean_acc| <= 0.05. (3) Load the attacker's x_adv tensor; check shape (10000,3,32,32), dtype, then in float64: max|x_adv - x| <= 8/255 + 1e-6 and 0 <= x_adv <= 1 for every image. (4) Recompute adversarial argmax in eval mode in batches; robust_acc = mean(argmax(model(x_adv)) == y), with ties counted as correct (not fooled). (5) Re-fetch the live model_info JSON for the model, compute BAR as in the success criterion (also reading the four enumerated papers' tables and the NOVELTY skeptic's sweep), and require BAR - robust_acc >= 0.10. (6) For p3 run AutoAttack(version='standard', seed=0) from fra31/auto-attack on the same model and count images AutoAttack leaves correct that the attacker's x_adv fools. Every number quoted with URL and fetch time.
angles: Wide targeted APGD: for each image unbroken by APGD-CE, run targeted DLR attacks against many more than the 9 wrong classes standard AutoAttack and MALT try (all 99 ranked by clean logit on an RN18 is cheap); this is the most obvious headroom on a 100-class problem.

Restart-heavy APGD on the robust subset only, transfer-seeded starts from other CIFAR-100 robust models, hypercube-vertex local search, float64 gradients; target the RN18/PreActRN18 entries first, then WRN-28-10.

Exploit the post-hoc defenses: for MeanSparse, attack the underlying model's features through the sparsification operator with a straight-through or smoothed surrogate (BPDA-style; the 42.25 external already came from APGD+BPDA, so beat that) and verify on the exact model; for MixedNUTS / Bai2023Improving adaptive-smoothing ensembles attack the mixing network's confidence pathway so the non-robust branch is selected.
Square Attack with a large query budget (20k-50k) on the residual unbroken images of a small model; black-box success where white-box fails is the flagged over-estimation signal.

Loss diversity per image: keep the best of CE, DLR, CW-margin, probability-margin (PMA) and a logit-difference-to-second-class loss with adaptive step sizes, selecting per image rather than per attack run.
Prefer the ~18 models with no published stronger evaluation (p1 list): there the bar is the plain AutoAttack number and nobody has tried harder yet.
pitfalls: Mixing up CIFAR-100 fine labels with coarse labels, applying normalisation before the robustbench model (it normalises internally), or using a differently ordered test set; recompute clean accuracy first and compare with the model_info clean_acc (must match to within 0.05 points) before trusting anything.
Eps or range violations hidden by float32 saving or image formats; check in float64 on the saved tensor.

Treating the leaderboard value or the 'external' value as the thing to beat is not enough: A3 Table 1 (12 CIFAR-100 models), AutoAE Table 1 (5), MALT Table 1 (4) and PMA/PMA+ Tables 3/6 (8) publish lower numbers that were never folded into the table (e.g. Gowal2020Uncovering_extra 36.88 listed vs 36.81 MALT; XCiT-L12 35.08 listed vs 34.95 PMA+). The NOVELTY skeptic must check all four plus 24 months of arXiv.

Evaluation drift: PMA's own AutoAttack reruns differ from the RobustBench values by up to 0.13 points (XCiT-L12 35.04 vs 35.08), and A3 used eps 0.031 for the LBGAT models; differences under 10 images are noise, and a mismatch in clean accuracy means a different pipeline, not a stronger attack.
Attacking a wrapper (softmax outputs, temperature scaling, different normalisation) instead of the robustbench-loaded model in eval mode, or counting clean-misclassified images as successes.
For p3, a union over many AutoAttack seeds trivially produces extra broken images; that is seed variance, not attack strength.

targets.name: VNN-COMP 2026: a validated counterexample for a benchmark instance that no participating verifier solved
targets.statement: VNN-COMP 2026 (results published in https://github.com/VNN-COMP/vnncomp2026_results, last pushed 2026-08-03; 13 tools: act, agate, alpha_beta_crown, bright, cora, n2v, neuralsat, nnenum, nnv, pyrat, sobolbox, super_simple_vnn_comp, vibecheck; 3,618 scored instance rows over 30 benchmarks, independently re-parsed by the vetter on 2026-10-09) left 127 instances that NO tool resolved: every tool returned timeout/unknown/error, and no validated counterexample exists. Parsed from SCORING/results.txt on 2026-10-09 they are: cifar100_2024 (40: CIFAR100_resnet_medium/large local robustness at eps 0.0039 = 1/255), tinyimagenet_2024 (22: TinyImageNet_resnet_medium, eps 1/255), challenging_certified_training_2026 (21: cifar10_eps2/eps8 cnn7 and wide_cnn7, tinyimagenet_eps1 cnn7), cora_2024 (27: mostly mnist-trades img0-19, plus cifar10 set/point/trades), traffic_signs_recognition_2023 (9: quantised QConv GTSRB nets, eps 1 and 3 in 0-255 pixel units), yolo_2023 (6: TinyYOLO eps 1/255), metaroom_2023 (1), ml4acopf_2024 (1). Each instance is an ONNX network plus a VNN-LIB property (input box + output constraints). Whether each is SAT (a counterexample exists) or UNSAT is open. Finding a counterexample is pure attack work (PGD and its variants on a small ONNX network, CPU-trivial per instance) and the competition's own validator (SCORING/cex_checks.py: replay with onnxruntime CPU, inputs within the box with atol 1e-4, replayed outputs authoritative) makes checking mechanical. Participating tools already ran cheap PGD before verification, so the easy cases are gone; what remains needs stronger search, which is exactly what this target asks for. The 2025 edition (VNN-COMP/vnncomp2025_results, SCORING-ZERO-TOL/results.txt) had 177 all-tool-unsolved instances, many of which (vit_2023, relusplitter) were later resolved as 'holds' in 2026, so 2025-only sets are stale and the 2026 table is the primary frontier. SEMANTICS (verified against SCORING/counterexamples_v2.py validate_vnnlib2_counterexample): a VNN-LIB file encodes the violation condition; the official validator declares a witness 'correct' iff EVERY assertion in the .vnnlib file holds at zero tolerance on the assignment (inputs as given, outputs replayed by onnxruntime CPU), 'correct_up_to_tolerance' iff they hold with input tolerance Settings.COUNTEREXAMPLE_ATOL = 1e-4, else 'spec_not_violated'. A 'counterexample' here means an assignment making all assertions true.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved counterexample input vector (plain text, one value per line, VNN-COMP witness format) for one instance (ONNX file + .vnnlib file taken unmodified from https://github.com/VNN-COMP/vnncomp2026_benchmarks at the version directory (1.0 or 2.0) that a participating tool's results.csv in the live results repo names for that benchmark, sha256 of both files recorded) such that ALL of the following hold: (a) in the live SCORING/results.txt of https://github.com/VNN-COMP/vnncomp2026_results (re-fetched live immediately before claiming, never a cached copy) NO tool's cell for that instance's 'Row:' line contains '(h)' or '(v)' (the instance is in the all-tool-unsolved set computed by the skeptic's OWN parse of the live file), and no *.counterexample.check.json for it in any tool directory has result 'correct' or 'correct_up_to_tolerance'; (b) every input coordinate lies STRICTLY inside its vnnlib input bounds (lo < x_i < hi, zero tolerance), and when the ONNX model is run on the input with onnxruntime CPUExecutionProvider in float32, EVERY assertion in the .vnnlib file evaluates to true exactly as written under VNN-COMP semantics (i.e. the official validator's zero-tolerance check `_assertions_hold(query, assignment, 0.0, 0.0)` is satisfied), and on the satisfied branch of each output assertion every atomic comparison holds with a strict margin >= 1e-6 (|lhs - rhs| >= 1e-6 in the required direction); (c) the same holds after rounding the input to float32 and re-running, AND in a second runtime that is not onnxruntime (onnx2pytorch/torch or onnx.reference.ReferenceEvaluator), AND the competition's own SCORING/counterexamples_v2.py (run unmodified from the live results repo against the live benchmark files) returns 'correct' (not merely 'correct_up_to_tolerance'); (d) the instance is not from soundnessbench_2026 or test; (e) a live web search finds no previously published counterexample for that exact ONNX+vnnlib pair (if one exists the result is a replication, not a win). A 'holds'/UNSAT claim for an unsolved instance is never a success under this target.

partial_wins.statement: A counterexample for an all-tool-unsolved 2026 instance (same set as criterion (a), criteria (d)-(e) also required) that satisfies all vnnlib assertions only with the competition's official input tolerance (inputs within the box up to atol 1e-4, outputs replayed by onnxruntime CPU), i.e. the unmodified SCORING/counterexamples_v2.py returns 'correct_up_to_tolerance' but not 'correct'; confirmed in a second non-onnxruntime runtime.

A strict counterexample (criteria (b)-(e) of the full criterion) for an instance in the VNN-COMP 2025 all-tool-unsolved set (parsed by the skeptic from the live https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VNN-COMP/vnncomp2025_results/main/SCORING-ZERO-TOL/results.txt: no '(h)'/'(v)' in any cell of its 'Row:' line; 177 such rows on 2026-10-09 in cora_2024, ml4acopf_2024, relusplitter, tinyimagenet_2024, traffic_signs_recognition_2023, vit_2023) whose identical ONNX+vnnlib pair (same sha256 of both files) is either NOT present anywhere in the live vnncomp2026_benchmarks repo, or is present and still all-tool-unsolved in the live 2026 results.txt.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic writes their own checker without reading the attacker's code: download the named ONNX (.onnx.gz) and .vnnlib files from the vnncomp2026_benchmarks repo at the named version directory, verify sha256 against the attacker's manifest; parse the vnnlib (SMT-LIB subset: declare-const, assert, <=, >=, and, or) with their own parser; check every input coordinate strictly within its bounds; run onnxruntime (CPU, float32) on the input; evaluate EVERY assertion exactly as written and require all of them true (VNN-COMP semantics: the file encodes the violation; the witness must satisfy it) with margin >= 1e-6 on each output comparison of the satisfied branch; repeat in a non-onnxruntime runtime; then run the unmodified SCORING/counterexamples_v2.py from the live results repo and require 'correct'. Re-parse the live results.txt ('Row:' lines, no '(h)'/'(v)' in any cell) and grep the tool directories' *.check.json to confirm the instance is still all-tool-unsolved. Web-search the instance name for prior published counterexamples. Total time: minutes per instance.
angles: Massive-restart PGD/APGD directly on the ONNX graph (convert with onnx2pytorch or run gradients through onnxruntime-training/torch export), with margin losses targeting each output disjunct of the vnnlib property separately; the tools' built-in attacks use small restart counts under a time limit, this run can use hours per instance.

Exploit the box structure: the cifar100/tinyimagenet/certified-training instances are eps=1/255 or 2/255 local-robustness boxes around a test image; search the box vertices (sign patterns) with coordinate-wise flipping and simulated annealing, since ReLU networks' extremes on a box are often at vertices; combine with gradient-free CMA-ES in the few hundred most sensitive pixels.

Branch-and-attack: use interval/CROWN bounds (auto_LiRPA on CPU) to split the input box, discard sub-boxes proven safe, and concentrate PGD on the surviving sub-boxes where the lower bound on the margin is most negative; a counterexample found in a tiny sub-box is still a counterexample for the instance.

For traffic_signs_recognition (quantised QConv nets, integer-valued pixel eps 1/3) search integer perturbations exhaustively over the highest-gradient pixels and use the network's quantisation to exploit threshold flips; for TinyYOLO (eps 1/255, 6 instances) target the specific output constraints in the vnnlib (bounding-box/objectness) with a margin loss rather than classification loss.

cora_2024 mnist-trades img0-19 (27 unsolved out of the TRADES-trained MNIST set): these are small MLP/CNNs where exact MILP (Gurobi-free: use OR-Tools CP-SAT or SCIP via pyscipopt) on the ReLU network with the box constraints is CPU-feasible and either produces a counterexample or an exact proof; the counterexample part is the claimed object.

Cross-check candidate counterexamples with float64 replay and with the competition's counterexamples_v2.py before claiming; prefer inputs with margin >> 1e-6 (push further inside the violated region along the gradient after finding one).
pitfalls: INVERTED SEMANTICS TRAP: do not look for inputs that make the vnnlib assertions FALSE. The official validator (counterexamples_v2.py) declares 'correct' iff all assertions in the file HOLD on inputs + replayed outputs; the file already encodes the unsafe region. Evaluate the file literally.
Counterexample valid only in one runtime or only in float32/float64 but not both; rounding at ReLU thresholds can flip tiny-margin violations. Require strict margin and two runtimes.

Input coordinates on or outside the box boundary (equality with bound is allowed by the vnnlib semantics but keep strictly inside for the full criterion), or using the wrong ONNX input shape/order (NCHW vs flattened) or the wrong version directory (1.0 vs 2.0 vnnlib spelling) of the benchmark.

Misreading the vnnlib: VNN-LIB properties are 'violation conditions' (the assertion describes the unsafe output region) in some benchmarks and 'safety conditions' in others; the skeptic must evaluate the file exactly as written using the competition's semantics (counterexamples_v2.py), not an informal reading.

The instance was not actually unsolved: a tool may have a validated counterexample in its directory (check *.counterexample.check.json) even if the aggregate line is unclear; re-parse the live results.txt and the tool directories, not a cached copy.
soundnessbench_2026 instances have planted counterexamples that may be public (SoundnessBench HF dataset); they are excluded. Likewise 'test' benchmark.

Claiming 'holds' (UNSAT) for an unsolved instance: that is a verification claim, not an attack result, and is not checkable by a skeptic in under an hour unless an independently reproducible exact method (e.g. MILP with a certificate) is provided; it is not part of this target's criteria.

The only 2026 rows where a '(v)' claim was rejected by the validator and no tool returned '(h)' are in soundnessbench_2026 (excluded); every other rejected claim (agate 'malformed_ce', neuralsat/nnenum 'spec_not_violated') sits on a row another tool resolved. There is therefore no 'rejected-claim-only' partial win on the live table; do not invent one.

targets.name: VNN-COMP verifier soundness: a validated counterexample for an instance that a participating tool certified as 'holds'
targets.statement: In VNN-COMP, when one tool says 'holds' (UNSAT) and another produces a validated counterexample, the 'holds' tool is scored as incorrect (PENALTY_INCORRECT = -150 in SCORING/settings.py).
