The 2026 scoring log (SCORING/results.txt, re-parsed by the vetter on 2026-10-09) records incorrect 'holds' verdicts for act (7, dist_shift_2023), super_simple_vnn_comp (14, sat_relu), neuralsat (8, soundnessbench_2026), sobolbox (2, cgan2026) and cora (1, sat_relu), so unsound 'holds' answers happen in practice; SoundnessBench (arXiv:2412.03154, TMLR 12/2025) found soundness bugs in alpha-beta-CROWN, NeuralSAT and Marabou-2023 with planted counterexamples, and arXiv:2605.17153 (May 2026) reports an implementation bug and numeric-tolerance concerns in popular verifiers. The open question: among the VNN-COMP 2026 instances for which at least one tool returned 'holds' and NO tool's counterexample was validated (True Result 'unsat' in the log; 2,152 instances on 2026-10-09, of which 2,127 have no 'violated' cell at all; 2,138 / 2,113 after excluding soundnessbench_2026), is any one OUTSIDE the soundnessbench_2026 and test benchmarks actually SAT? A single strict counterexample for such an instance is a new soundness finding about a named verifier, mechanically checkable by replaying the ONNX model on the input (onnxruntime CPU) against the vnnlib property. soundnessbench_2026 is excluded because every instance there is SAT by construction with ground truth held privately by the benchmark authors (a hit there is subsumed). The analogous 2025 set (holds-only instances under SCORING-ZERO-TOL in VNN-COMP/vnncomp2025_results, 2,505 on 2026-10-09, of which 2,074 have no 'violated' cell) is a secondary table (partial win p1). Hottest hunting grounds: the 25 2026 instances where some tool returned 'violated' but every submitted witness failed validation (21 malformed_ce, 3 spec_not_violated, 1 correct_up_to_tolerance) while another tool said 'holds'; the 77 instances where act is the ONLY tool saying 'holds' (and 20 where alpha_beta_crown is the only one, 1 bright); and remaining 'holds' answers from tools with incorrect verdicts elsewhere (act, super_simple_vnn_comp, neuralsat, sobolbox, cora).
targets.success_criterion: Success means a saved counterexample input (in the competition witness text format) for ONE VNN-COMP 2026 instance such that ALL of the following hold. (a) INSTANCE: ONNX and vnnlib are unmodified files from https://github.com/VNN-COMP/vnncomp2026_benchmarks at the exact benchmarks/<category>/<version>/ paths named in the contradicted tool's per-benchmark results.csv (<tool>/2026_<category>/results.csv in the live results repo; sha256 of both files recorded); the category is neither 'test' nor 'soundnessbench_2026'. (b) CONTRADICTED VERDICT: in the live https://github.com/VNN-COMP/vnncomp2026_results, re-fetched immediately before claiming, at least one tool's per-benchmark results.csv row for that exact (network path, property path) has result 'holds' or 'unsat' with run_time <= the timeout for that instance in the same version's instances.csv (a 'holds' reported after the timeout is scored as a timeout by the organisers and does NOT count), AND no tool directory contains a witness for that instance whose .counterexample.check.json has result 'correct' or 'correct_up_to_tolerance' (equivalently classification 'correct' or 'correct_with_tolerance'); if the live log shows the instance's True Result as 'sat', the finding is already known and fails. (c) STRICT VIOLATION: every input coordinate lies strictly inside the vnnlib input bounds (lb < x < ub, checked in float64 on the float32-rounded values actually fed to the network) and running the ONNX model on it with onnxruntime CPUExecutionProvider in float32 makes some disjunct of the vnnlib output assertion true with margin >= 1e-6 on every constraint of that disjunct, evaluated by the competition validator for the instance's VNN-LIB version (SCORING/counterexamples.py for 1.0, SCORING/counterexamples_v2.py for 2.0) with input_tol = 0 and output_tol = 0 returning CORRECT. (d) SECOND RUNTIME: the same input violates the property (same disjunct, margin >= 1e-6) under an independent ONNX executor (onnx2pytorch or onnx reference evaluator) in float32 AND float64. (e) WRITE-UP: names every tool whose 'holds' is contradicted, quotes their results.csv rows, and records the attack script and random seeds. Nothing is reported to the organisers or tool authors by the agent; the human decides.

partial_wins.statement: The same as the full criterion (a)-(e), with the 2025 repositories substituted: ONNX + vnnlib unmodified from https://github.com/VNN-COMP/vnncomp2025_benchmarks; a 'holds'/'unsat' row within timeout in some tool's results in https://github.com/VNN-COMP/vnncomp2025_results; the instance's True Result is 'unsat' in SCORING-ZERO-TOL/results.txt AND no tool's witness for it was classified 'correct' or 'correct_up_to_tolerance' in EITHER 2025 scoring run (zero-tolerance or small-tolerance), since tightening an existing within-tolerance witness into the box is trivial; the category is not soundnessbench or test; and, if the identical ONNX+vnnlib pair (same sha256) was reused in 2026, it must also satisfy (b) in the 2026 repo. Strictness check (c)-(d) as in the full criterion.

A soundness bug demonstrated on a NEW property (not a VNN-COMP instance) over an unmodified VNN-COMP 2026 ONNX network: a vnnlib file for which a named open-source VNN-COMP 2026 participant (alpha_beta_crown, neuralsat, pyrat, nnenum, cora, nnv, act, super_simple_vnn_comp, n2v, bright, agate, vibecheck, sobolbox), installed at the commit it submitted to VNN-COMP 2026 and run with its official 2026 configuration for that benchmark (only the device may differ, e.g. CPU instead of GPU, and this must be stated), returns 'holds'/'unsat', while a counterexample satisfying (c)-(d) exists. The property file, tool commit, full command line and config must be frozen in the attempt with sha256; the skeptic must be able to re-run the tool on the property in under one hour; and the write-up must show the bug is not a reproduction of one already reported in SoundnessBench (arXiv:2412.03154), arXiv:2605.17153, or the tool's public issue tracker (search terms and dates recorded). A 'holds' that disappears when the tool is run twice (non-determinism) still counts; a 'holds' caused by the tool silently skipping an unsupported operator counts only if the tool did not warn.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic's own checker, written from the vnnlib grammar before reading the attacker's code: (1) download ONNX + vnnlib from the benchmarks repo at the version directory named in the contradicted tool's results.csv row and verify both sha256 values; (2) parse the vnnlib independently and check every input coordinate is strictly inside its bounds; (3) replay the input with onnxruntime CPUExecutionProvider (float32) and with a second executor (onnx2pytorch or onnx.reference) in float32 and float64; require the same disjunct violated with margin >= 1e-6 in all runs; (4) run the competition's own validator for the instance's VNN-LIB version (counterexamples.py for 1.0, counterexamples_v2.py for 2.0) with zero tolerance and require CORRECT; (5) fetch the live results repo, open the per-benchmark results.csv of every tool for that category, confirm at least one 'holds'/'unsat' row for the exact network+property paths with run_time <= the instances.csv timeout, and confirm that no <tool>/2026_<category>/<instance>.counterexample.check.json has result correct or correct_up_to_tolerance; also confirm the instance's True Result is 'unsat' in SCORING/results.txt; (6) confirm the category is not test or soundnessbench_2026. For p1 repeat with the 2025 repos and both scoring runs. For p2 install the named tool at the frozen commit, run the frozen command on the frozen property, and require the 'holds' output to reproduce. Minutes to one hour.
angles: Start with the 25 instances (2026-10-09 parse) where a tool returned 'violated' but its witness was rejected (malformed_ce / spec_not_violated / tolerance-only) while another tool said 'holds': re-run a strong attack there, since a verifier already believed the property was violable.

Rank the remaining holds-only instances by suspicion: 'holds' from a tool with incorrect verdicts elsewhere (act, super_simple_vnn_comp, neuralsat, sobolbox, cora), 'holds' where that tool is the ONLY one saying holds (act 77, alpha_beta_crown 20, bright 1), 'holds' returned in under 1 second on a large network, 'holds' where other complete tools timed out, and 'holds' on benchmarks with non-ReLU activations or unusual ops (cgan2026, ml4acopf_2024, smart_turn_multimodal_2026, adaptive_cruise_control_non_linear_2026, dist_shift_2023 concat nets, vit_2023); attack those with heavy PGD, random restarts, vertex and boundary search.

Numerical-tolerance hunting: tools reason in float64 or with loosened constraints; look for instances where the vnnlib output threshold is within ~1e-4 of the network's maximum over the box (estimate with gradient ascent) and try to produce a float32 counterexample that a float64 reasoner would miss, then push the margin past 1e-6.

Operator-semantics bugs (p2): for networks with ops verifiers approximate (Reshape/Transpose/Flatten orders, average pooling, BatchNorm folding, Sigmoid/Tanh, Softmax, Gather, residual adds, Concat), build small new properties that stress each op and compare the tool's 'holds' against onnxruntime sampling; SoundnessBench's planted-counterexample recipe (train so attacks miss the counterexample) can be reproduced locally on a tiny network, but the resulting bug must be new.

Replay official 2026 tool configurations locally for the open-source tools and compare verdicts on perturbed properties (shrink/shift the input box slightly around a known violated instance): a tool that flips to 'holds' while a counterexample still exists in the shrunk box exhibits a reproducible bug (p2).

Exhaustive methods on tiny instances: for acasxu_2023 / isomorphic_acasxu_2026 / monotonic_acasxu_2026 / lsnc_relu / sat_relu (5-input or small MLPs) run an exact MILP/SMT (OR-Tools CP-SAT, SCIP, or Z3 on the exact piecewise-linear encoding in rational arithmetic) on the instances a suspicious tool marked 'holds'; any SAT answer gives a candidate to validate in float32.
pitfalls: Counterexample that violates the property only by floating-point noise (< 1e-6), only in one runtime, or only with inputs on or outside the box boundary. Require strict interior membership, margin >= 1e-6 and two runtimes; the organisers' 1e-4 input tolerance (COUNTEREXAMPLE_ATOL) does not apply here.

Misattributing a verdict: read the per-benchmark <tool>/2026_<category>/results.csv in the live repo, not the aggregate log columns; the flat per-tool results.csv has multi-network (python-list-like) network fields for isomorphic/monotonic acasxu that break naive CSV parsing. Confirm no validated witness exists in ANY tool directory (check.json result correct / correct_up_to_tolerance), otherwise the finding is already known (subsumed).

check.json vocabulary: the 'result' field uses correct / correct_up_to_tolerance / malformed_ce / spec_not_violated / unsupported / no_ce, while the 'classification' field uses correct / correct_with_tolerance / malformed / incorrect / unsupported / missing. Use the right field.

Scoring timeouts: a 'holds' row whose run_time exceeds the instance timeout in instances.csv was scored as a timeout, not as holds; it does not count. Likewise 'unknown'/'timeout'/'error' never count as 'holds'.

VNN-LIB 1.0 vs 2.0: the same benchmark exists in two version directories and the two validators differ (counterexamples.py vs counterexamples_v2.py; 1.0 checks bounds in Python float, 2.0 in the declared dtype, see results-repo issue #1). Use the version directory the contradicted tool actually ran, and the matching validator.

Property semantics: the vnnlib assertion describes the violation region as a disjunction of conjunctions; a point outside the informal SAFE region may not satisfy any disjunct as written. Use the competition evaluator, and read sat_relu / lsnc_relu encodings carefully.

Vacuous 'holds': adaptive_cruise_control_non_linear_2026 has 18/50 instances with an empty input region (benchmarks issue #11, open) and isomorphic_acasxu_2026 had a contradictory output spec (issue #6); no counterexample can exist there. Skip them.

soundnessbench_2026 (and 2025 soundnessbench) are excluded from the full criterion and p1: all instances are SAT by construction and the benchmark authors hold the planted counterexamples, so any hit is subsumed. cifar100_2024 deliberately retains ~18% instances with known adversarial examples (2025 report, section 4.10) 'for potentially identifying unsound results'; a hit there is admissible only if the panel confirms the adversarial example is not published in the benchmark's source repo.

p2 claims where the tool was run with a non-competition configuration, a later commit, or with an unsupported op silently skipped; freeze commit, config and full command line, and state the device. Bugs already reported in SoundnessBench, arXiv:2605.17153 or the tool's issue tracker are not new.
Hard-coding counts: the 2,152 / 2,138 / 25 / 77 figures are the vetter's 2026-10-09 parse of the log; re-derive them live, since the organisers may re-score (the 2025 repo was re-scored twice).

targets.name: New high-quality abc triples (q >= 1.4, c > 10^20) or beat Reyssat's 1.6299
targets.statement: An abc triple is coprime positive a + b = c with rad(abc) < c; its quality is q = log c / log rad(abc). Bart de Smit's list has 241 known triples with q >= 1.4 (last updated 2019-03-02) and states the list of good triples is COMPLETE up to 20 digits (Demeyer, June 2007), so new ones can only have c > 10^20. The record is q = 1.6299 (Reyssat: 2 + 3^10*109 = 23^5). Target: a new record q, or new q >= 1.4 triples with c > 10^20.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED for coprime positive integers a + b = c with complete prime factorizations of a, b and c (every factor proven prime: BPSW plus ECPP/Pocklington above 2^64) and quality q = log c / log rad(abc), computed at 50 digits, STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the highest quality on https://pub.math.leidenuniv.nl/~desmit/abc/index.php?set=2 AT VERIFICATION TIME (1.6299, Reyssat, on 2026-10-03, context only) and than any higher value found in a same-day literature check. New q >= 1.4 triples below the record are partial wins (partial win). Any 'new' triple with c <= 10^20 is a BUG (that range is complete).

partial_wins.statement: New good triple (partial win): coprime a + b = c with c > 10^20, complete proven factorizations, q >= 1.4 at 50 digits, and the sorted (min(a,b), c) pair absent from the de Smit q >= 1.4 list at verification time; labelled 'new relative to the de Smit list' unless also absent from ABC@Home and Rubin's results.
New top-20 triple: a triple as in p1 whose quality exceeds the 20th-highest quality on the de Smit list at verification time (about 1.55 per the researcher).

targets.verification_method: Recompute the sum and gcd, re-factor a, b and c independently (sympy.factorint, plus ECPP via PARI isprime(...,2) for large factors), check c > 10^20, compute rad and q with mpmath at 50 digits, and string-diff against the freshly scraped de Smit list (and ranking for p2).
angles: LLL on polynomial identities (Dokchitser / Browkin-Brzezinski style): find polynomials f, g, h with f + g = h and small radical degree, specialize at rational points, and LLL-reduce to make the parts smooth/powerful.

Continued fractions of n-th roots: a triple like 2 + 3^10*109 = 23^5 comes from near-equalities x^n ≈ y^m. Scan convergents of log(p)/log(q) for small primes p, q and test the error term for smoothness.
Mason-Stothers extremal polynomial families (Davenport-Zannier pairs, Belyi maps / dessins d'enfants) specialized at integers. Search over the catalog of genus-0 dessins with few edges.
Search S-unit equations x + y = z with x, y, z supported on the first ~12 primes with high exponents (de Weger's method). Solve with LLL and keep near-powerful solutions.
Aim every construction at c > 10^20; anything smaller is already enumerated completely.
pitfalls: Incomplete factorization: a large composite cofactor treated as prime inflates rad and lowers q wrongly, or a missed square factor lowers rad and fakes high q.
Duplicates up to swapping a and b.
The list being stale since 2019 means a 'new' triple may be in ABC@Home or Frank Rubin's results; label carefully.
The list is complete for c up to 20 digits (Demeyer 2007), so 'new' small triples are bugs.
Infinite polynomial families (e.g., 1 + (x^n - 1) = x^n with smooth x^n-1) almost always give q < 1.4.

targets.name: Antihydra (BB(6) Cryptid): prove non-halting (Collatz-like / Mahler 3/2 problem)
targets.statement: Antihydra (1RB1RA_0LC1LE_1LD1LC_1LA0LB_1LF1RE_---0RA) halts iff an iterated map halts: per the bbchallenge wiki, iterate H(n) = floor(3n/2) starting from 8, halting iff the number of odd iterates exceeds twice the number of even ones (exact definition and start state must be quoted from the wiki). Proving non-halting requires showing the parities of the iterates are never too odd-heavy, closely related to Mahler's 3/2 problem. Simulated to 2^38 rule steps without halting; heuristic halting probability about 2.884e-28,723,042,565. Public AI autoresearch repos (mfornet/antihydra-autoresearch; golirt1/antihydra-notes, which states 'not a proof') exist; no 2026 proof is known.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only with a complete proof of non-halting (or an explicit halting step count) that is (a) formalized in Lean or Rocq with no sorry/admit and an axiom audit showing only standard axioms, with the formal statement shown to match the Turing machine semantics or the wiki's proven-equivalent reformulation (equivalence proof included or cited from the Rocq repo); or (b) for halting, an exact step count reproduced by two independent accelerated simulators AND a naive spot-check of the rule translation. Heuristic, probabilistic or 'verified up to N' arguments never count. Any proof that would also resolve Mahler's 3/2 problem gets extra scrutiny.

partial_wins.statement: Simulation frontier: an independently reproducible simulation of the Antihydra map strictly beyond the depth stated on https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Antihydra at verification time (2^38 rule steps as context), with no halt, publishing checkpoint values (iterate hash and counter) at fixed step indices that a second, independently written simulator reproduces exactly.

Formal reduction: a Lean/Rocq-checked theorem (no sorry, clean axiom audit) reducing Antihydra non-halting to a strictly different explicit statement (e.g. about the binary/3-adic digits of the orbit, or a specific automatic/morphic sequence), where the reduction is not already stated on the wiki page or in the mfornet/golirt1 repos at verification time.

targets.verification_method: The verifier runs lake build / coqc in a clean environment, prints axioms, and diffs the top-level theorem statement against the wiki's formal definition. For p1 it reruns the published checkpoints with its own simulator.
angles: Look for a proof of a weaker but sufficient statement: Antihydra only needs the running count (2*#even - #odd) to stay ≥ 0 from a SPECIFIC start, not equidistribution. Explore 2-adic structure: the parity sequence of floor((3/2)^n * x) is determined by binary digits of x * 3^n. Seek a combinatorial invariant on 3-adic/2-adic expansions for that one orbit.

Automaton approach: test whether the parity sequence from this start is (provably) a morphic/automatic sequence on some subsequence, which would give a closed-form count. Searching for this computationally is fast; finding it would be a new idea.

Transfer from known results: Dubickas/Flatto-Lagarias-Pollington bounds on fractional parts of ξ(3/2)^n give partial distribution results. Check whether any known bound on lim sup/lim inf of the parity density already suffices for a tail version, leaving a finite check.
Read the existing autoresearch repos first and document their negative results to avoid repeating dead ends.
pitfalls: Confusing simulation depth with proof.
Subtle off-by-one in the counter or start state when reformulating.
A purported proof that would also prove Mahler's 3/2 conjecture outright is almost certainly wrong.

targets.name: BB(3,3) non-Bigfoot holdouts and BB(2,5) non-Hydra holdouts
targets.statement: BB(3,3) has 6 holdouts (4 up to equivalence): Bigfoot, #397 ('similar to Wily Coyote'), the equivalent pair #153/#758 (flagged as a potential Cryptid) and the Wily Coyote pair #531/#532 (BB(3,3) page last edited 2026-09-17; the three Rocq formalizations of 2026-03-15, machines 650, 412, 279, are not among the 6). BB(2,5) has 60 formal holdouts after mxdys' Rocq deciders (2026-09-08) and an informal list of 38 (2026-10-02), including Hydra 1RB3RB---3LA1RA_2LA3RA4LB0LB0LA and the Bonus Cryptid 1RB3RB---3LA1RA_2LA3RA4LB0LB1LB; the 22-machine difference is covered by pending, not yet independently verified GPT6/Aristotle Lean proofs. Target: decide a non-Bigfoot BB(3,3) holdout or a BB(2,5) machine on the 38-list other than Hydra and the Bonus Cryptid, with a formal or independently checked certificate.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED under the same certificate rules as bb6-holdout-certificates (newest holdout file linked from https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Holdouts_lists AT VERIFICATION TIME, normal-form match with file sha256, whole-language closure check by an independent checker or Lean/Rocq proof with no admits and a clean axiom audit, two-simulator step count for halting, not marked decided on the wiki/sheet/Discord, else 'NEW, PENDING COMMUNITY CHECK'), applied to BB(3,3) #397, #153/#758 or #531/#532, or to a BB(2,5) machine on the newest informal list other than Hydra and the Bonus Cryptid and not covered by the pending AI Lean proofs. Deciding one member of an equivalent pair counts once. Progress on Bigfoot, Hydra or the Bonus Cryptid does NOT count here.

partial_wins.statement: Independent audit of a pending AI proof: for one of the 22 BB(2,5) machines covered by the pending GPT6/Aristotle Lean proofs, either an independent confirmation (clean build, #print axioms showing only standard axioms, top-level statement diffed against Coq-BB5-style semantics, plus a cross-check by a certificate checker sharing no code) or a concrete defect (a sorry/axiom, a statement mismatch, or a failing step), where the wiki does not already record that machine's proof as independently verified at verification time. This is not a new decision.

Verified reduction: for BB(3,3) #397, #153/#758 or #531/#532, a mechanically checked proof (symbolic checker or Lean/Rocq) that the machine halts if and only if an explicitly stated arithmetic map/condition holds, where the machine's wiki page does not already give an equivalent proven reduction at verification time.

targets.verification_method: Independent certificate checker (whole-language inclusion test) plus a 1e9-step naive simulation for consistency; Lean/Rocq compile in a clean project with an axiom audit and statement diff. For the audit partial win, the verifier rebuilds the pending proof itself and reruns the independent cross-check.
angles: Extract each holdout's macro rules with an accelerated simulator. Many 'almost-Cryptids' reduce to a map with one parity split plus an exploitable invariant mod 2^k or mod 3^k (a finite automaton on residues), giving a proof by finite residue-class closure.
2-adic/3-adic invariants: show the orbit never enters the halting residue class by exhibiting a set of residues mod M closed under the map. Search M up to 2^20 x 3^10.
Search for a Lyapunov/potential function as an integer linear combination of tape-block counters that strictly increases, using LP/ILP over symbolic rule effects.
Cross-check with the Rocq repository's existing proof patterns and reuse their certificate format to make formal adoption easy.
Auditing the pending AI Lean proofs is cheap and useful; finding a statement mismatch matters as much as confirming one.
pitfalls: Bigfoot/Hydra are Collatz-hard; heuristic 'probviously' arguments do not count.
Duplicating the active AI Lean campaign on BB(2,5).
Equivalence classes: deciding one member may already be implied by a decided twin.
153/758 is flagged as a potential Cryptid, so expect Collatz-hardness.
The 22 AI Lean proofs on BB(2,5) are unverified. Independently checking one is a useful contribution but is NOT a new decision.

targets.name: Decide official BB(6) holdout machines with independently checkable certificates
targets.statement: The bbchallenge collaboration keeps lists of 6-state 2-symbol Turing machines whose halting status from a blank tape is undecided. BB(6) has 815 holdouts up to equivalence and 1674 without (wiki, late Sept 2026; informal count about 998). The newest count on Holdouts_lists is 797 machines (@mxdys, 2026-09-30; announced on Discord, file 'To be done' on 2026-10-03, so the newest posted file is BB6_holdouts_815.txt from 2026-09-24), after FAR and other deciders removed about 113 machines, so what remains is the hard residue. Target: prove that one or more machines on the newest official BB(6) list never halts (or halts), with a machine-checkable certificate. (BB(2,5) and BB(3,3) holdouts are handled by the separate target bb33-bb25-cryptid-adjacent; Cryptids such as Antihydra by antihydra-collatz-cryptid.)
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED requires all of the following, checked against the live primary table https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Holdouts_lists at verification time (direction: min; each newly decided holdout lowers the live count). (1) The machine's standard-format string, or its bbchallenge lexical normal form after state/symbol permutation and mirror normalization, appears in the NEWEST BB(6) holdout file linked from https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Holdouts_lists AT VERIFICATION TIME (the 2026-09-30 797-machine @mxdys count is context only; on 2026-10-03 it had no posted file, so the newest linked file was BB6_holdouts_815.txt of 2026-09-24, and 815 - 797 = 18 machines in that file had already been decided by 2026-09-30, which makes check (4) essential). Record the file name, its date and its sha256. The claim must name which list it targets (informal or formal holdout list). (2) Non-halting: a finite certificate, such as a CTL/FAR automaton, inductive symbolic templates, or a Lean/Rocq proof with no sorry/admit/new axioms. For a Lean/Rocq proof, the formal TM model must be shown equal to the bbchallenge semantics (start state A, blank tape of 0s, the bbchallenge head-move convention, halting exactly when an undefined transition is read) and must be tested on known machines: under the formal model the BB(5) champion must halt at step 47,176,870. Any use of native_decide (which adds the Lean.ofReduceBool axiom) must be flagged in the report together with the #print axioms / Print Assumptions output. A checker that shares no code with the search must verify three things over the WHOLE certificate language, not only over configurations seen in simulation: (a) the blank-tape start configuration is in the language; (b) the language is closed under one TM step, checked as a language inclusion with automata operations or symbolic case analysis covering every template instance; (c) no configuration in the language reads a halting (undefined) transition. (3) Halting: an exact step count reproduced by two independent simulators, at least one of them a published accelerated simulator, plus a naive single-step simulator if the count is <= 1e10. (4) The machine is not marked decided on the BB(6) wiki page, the linked sheet, or the bbchallenge Discord #bb6 channel when it can be checked. If decided status cannot be confirmed, report 'NEW, PENDING COMMUNITY CHECK', not a record. Heuristic ('probviously') arguments never count.

partial_wins.statement: Verified macro-rule reduction: for a machine in the newest BB(6) holdout file whose wiki/holdout notes give no accelerated rule set, an explicit set of parametric rules (e.g. A(n) -> A(f(n))) proven for ALL parameter values by a symbolic checker or Lean/Rocq (no sorry), with every rule application also matching a naive simulation for the first 1e8 steps.

Cryptid-style reduction: for such a machine, a mechanically checked proof that it halts if and only if an explicitly stated arithmetic (Collatz-like) condition holds, where the wiki has no equivalent reduction for that machine (or any machine equivalent to it under normal form) at verification time.

targets.verification_method: Download the newest holdout file, compute the canonical normal form of the claimed machine, and grep for it. Run an independent checker (about 100 lines of Python) for the certificate class. For automaton certificates it checks closure as an inclusion test with automata operations (product/complement emptiness), not by sampling. Simulate 1e8 naive steps as a sanity check. For Lean/Rocq, build in a clean project, run #print axioms / Print Assumptions, and diff the top-level statement against the Coq-BB5-style TM semantics (start state A, blank 0 tape, head-move convention, halt on an undefined transition). Run the formal model on the BB(5) champion (must halt at step 47,176,870) and on a known non-halting machine before trusting it, and flag native_decide. For partial wins, re-derive each macro rule symbolically and replay it against a naive simulator.
angles: Pull the BB(6) holdout list and cluster machines by behavior signatures: tape-growth exponent, repeated macro-symbols, counter-like Collatz rules. Attack the largest cluster of 'translated cycler with growing counter' machines with one parametric certificate generator instead of one machine at a time.

Implement a weighted-automaton or 'regular language + linear counter' certificate class (a Presburger-closed tape language). It strictly generalizes CTL, and existing FAR deciders miss counter-dependent invariants.

Run accelerated simulation to extract the inductive rules (A(n) -> A(f(n))). For machines whose rule is affine with no parity split, derive the non-halting proof mechanically by solving a linear recurrence, then emit a symbolic certificate.

Use the bbchallenge 'Collatz-level' taxonomy: target machines whose extracted map is Collatz-like but with a contracting drift that is provably monotone (a 2-adic Lyapunov function), which avoids the Antihydra-type parity problem.

Do not rebuild FAR: the remaining 797 survived FAR, CTL and loop deciders. Spend effort on certificate classes that strictly generalize them (counter-augmented regular languages, Presburger-closed tape languages).
Check the bbchallenge Discord and wiki for same-day AI-agent (GPT6/Aristotle) activity on the chosen machine before investing in it.

Run the cheap deciders on every holdout first (cyclers, translated cyclers, bouncers, FAR with growing DFA size via SAT/pysat). Then cluster the residue by behaviour, such as counters, bouncers with growing gaps, and Collatz-like rules.

Symbolic rule extraction: compress the tape into run-length macro blocks, infer affine 'shift rules' (block^n patterns maps to block^{an+b}), and prove the inferred rule system non-halting by induction with Z3 (pip install z3-solver). Then emit a Lean proof skeleton.
Weighted or counter automata certificates (WFAR) found by an ILP search over weights. These catch machines with unbalanced counters that plain DFAs miss.

Translate a holdout's macro-dynamics into a Fractran program or Collatz-like map. Where the map has an obvious invariant, such as mod-2^k drift or a monotone potential, that proves non-halting. Where it is Hydra-like, mark it as a cryptid and move on.
BB(3,3) and BB(2,5) residues are tiny. Aim the full ten-core budget at one machine for a whole day rather than many.
pitfalls: Machines decided on Discord or the Google Sheet but not yet removed from the file. Report these as 'pending community check'.
Off-by-one or normalization errors: a machine equivalent under symbol/state permutation may already be decided.
Certificates that check closure only for reachable configurations seen in simulation, not for all configurations in the language.
'Probviously' heuristic arguments (random-walk estimates) are NOT proofs.
Cryptids (Antihydra, Hydra, Bigfoot, Space Needle, Lucy's Moonlight) encode Collatz-like problems. Do not count heuristic progress on them here.
The remaining 797 survived FAR, CTL and loop deciders. A 'new' decider that only reproduces FAR will find nothing.
AI agents (GPT6/Aristotle) are already active on bbchallenge holdouts, so check for duplication the same day.
A machine may be solved between list updates. Check the wiki and Discord-mirrored lists at claim time.
Equivalence: proving the mirror image of an already-decided machine is not new.
Lean proofs using sorry, axiom, or unchecked native_decide. The wiki notes some 'proofs in Lean using GPT6' are pending verification.
Cryptids (Antihydra, Hydra, Bigfoot) encode open Collatz-like problems. Heuristic or probabilistic arguments do not count.
Simulation-only 'non-halting' evidence.
A Lean proof of the wrong statement, where the TM encoding or semantics differs from bbchallenge's (start state, tape conventions, an off-by-one step count). Test the formal model on known machines.
The informal and formal holdout lists differ. Say which one the claim targets.
Many AI agents (Aristotle, GPT6-based) are attacking the same lists. Re-check the wiki and Discord-mirrored lists at claim time.

Newest-list confusion: the 797 count (2026-09-30) had no posted file on 2026-10-03; the newest posted file (BB6_holdouts_815.txt, 2026-09-24) still contains 18 machines decided since. Membership in a file is not proof that a machine is still undecided.
A formal model that has not been run on the BB(5) champion (halts at step 47,176,870) may encode the wrong semantics; native_decide is a trusted-compiler axiom and must be reported, not hidden.

targets.name: Improve the Erdős-Moser equation lower bound (beyond the 2026 claim m > 8.213e1,800,000,044)
targets.statement: The Erdős-Moser equation 1^k + 2^k + ... + (m-1)^k = m^k is conjectured to have only the solution 1 + 2 = 3. Gallot-Moree-Zudilin (Math. Comp. 80, 2011; arXiv 0907.1356) proved m > 2.7139 x 10^1,667,658,416 via their Theorem 2: 2k/(2m-3) must be a convergent of log 2, checked with a large continued-fraction computation of log2/(2N). An unreviewed 2026 GitHub note (twentyseventhllc-lgtm/erdos-moser-bound, written with Claude Code) claims m > 2^5,979,470,720 > 8.213 x 10^1,800,000,044 from 3,493,054,981 certified partial quotients. arXiv 2608.03375 (Aug 2026) treats only an arithmetic-progression variant. Target: a rigorously larger lower bound.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED ('NEW RECORD') for an explicit lower bound B such that every solution other than 1+2=3 has m > B, with B STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the largest bound, reviewed or not, stated at https://github.com/twentyseventhllc-lgtm/erdos-moser-bound and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Moser_equation AT VERIFICATION TIME (8.213e1,800,000,044 on 2026-10-03, context only). The proof must follow GMZ Theorem 2 exactly (theorem number cited); log 2 comes from interval endpoints computed by two independent formulas; partial quotients of log2/(2N) are computed by exact rational arithmetic on both certified endpoints, which must give identical quotients; the GMZ threshold (180N-2) is checked at every index. Beating only GMZ's 2011 bound is NOT new. Unproven heuristics never count.

partial_wins.statement: INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION (partial win): with code sharing nothing with the 2026 repo, certify the first K = 3,493,054,981 partial quotients of log2/(2N) from both certified endpoints, confirm none reaches the GMZ Theorem 2 threshold, recompute q_{K-1}, and match the claimed exponent 5,979,470,720, with block hashes of the partial-quotient stream published for comparison.

Discrepancy: an index i <= 3,493,054,981 at which the certified partial quotient (identical from both endpoints) differs from the 2026 repo's value or reaches the threshold, demonstrated so that a verifier can recompute that block independently.

Structural restriction: a new necessary condition on solutions (e.g. a congruence condition on m from higher prime powers, or a sharpened Moser/Moree divisibility condition) with a complete written proof checked line by line by the verifier, ideally in Lean, and absent from GMZ, Moree's survey literature and the 2026 note at verification time.

targets.verification_method: First, a regression: reproduce GMZ's published bound and the 2026 repo's small-size validation values. Then recompute the continued-fraction prefix with python-flint/gmpy2 half-gcd on both certified endpoints and require identical partial quotients. Check the threshold condition at every index, and hash the partial-quotient stream in blocks for comparison against the 2026 repo's logs. Structural claims get a line-by-line proof check (or Lean build with axiom audit).
angles: Reproduce GMZ at smaller scale first (regression), then scale. Python-flint arb can compute log 2 to ~10^9-10^10 bits on a laptop with enough RAM. Use a divide-and-conquer (half-gcd) continued fraction on the certified rational.

Strengthen the criterion: GMZ need m-1, m+1, 2m-1, 2m+1 to satisfy prime-divisibility conditions (Moser's congruences). Adding conditions from more primes (via Moree's 'lcm of p-1' condition on k) would let a given CF length imply a bigger m bound.

Replace log 2 by a simultaneous approximation: the equation also forces near-relations with other constants (Bernoulli/zeta asymptotics). A 2D lattice (LLL) criterion could rule out ranges without extending the CF.
Purely algebraic route: study the equation mod higher prime powers p^2 to get new 'm ≡ ... mod M' conditions that shrink the convergent set exponentially.
Start by independently reproducing the 2026 claim (partial win p1); only then push K beyond 3,493,054,981.
pitfalls: Uncertified floating-point continued fractions: one wrong partial quotient invalidates everything.
Misreading the GMZ criterion (which N, which convergents).
Bound improvements via unproven heuristics.
Beating only the 2011 GMZ bound is NOT new. The 2026 claim is higher.
Memory: about 3.6e9 decimal digits of log 2 means half-gcd on numbers of roughly 1.5 GB. Check the RAM budget before starting.

targets.name: Computationally decidable open number-theory Erdős problems (erdosproblems.com)
targets.statement: erdosproblems.com lists about 652 open problems. Some number-theoretic ones are decidable by a finite certificate: an explicit counterexample, a finite exceptional set, or an explicit construction disproving a quantitative conjecture. FrontierMath Erdős (Adamczewski-Bloom, arXiv 2609.25050, 2026-09-06) selected 68 open problems, on which the best model (GPT-6 Astra) scored 3%. The teorth/erdosproblems wiki tracks AI contributions (e.g. #396, #513, #650 in Feb-Apr 2026). Target: pick an open problem whose resolution, or a clearly stated sub-question, is a finite checkable object, and produce it.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if: (1) the problem's page on https://www.erdosproblems.com/ shows status OPEN on the day of the claim, its comment/forum thread reports no resolution, and the teorth AI-contributions wiki has no entry resolving it; (2) the claimed result is a finite object (counterexample/construction/certificate) plus a short reduction proving that this object resolves the problem AS STATED on the site (exact quantifiers and constants; statements containing 'for sufficiently large n' or other asymptotic quantifiers cannot be resolved by a finite counterexample); (3) an independent re-implementation verifies the object. A proof-style resolution needs a Lean proof (elan/lake install allowed) that compiles without sorry and with a clean axiom audit. Otherwise it is reported as 'CLAIM, UNVERIFIED', with no claim.

partial_wins.statement: Explicit sub-question: a finite, independently re-verified object that settles a specific sub-question or special case that the problem's erdosproblems.com page (or its cited source) explicitly states as open at verification time, with the reduction to that exact sub-question written out.

Bound improvement: an explicit construction, independently re-verified, that strictly improves a numeric bound or constant the problem's page cites as the best known at verification time (direction as stated on the page), without resolving the problem.

targets.verification_method: The verifier fetches the problem page and re-reads the exact statement, checks that the reduction lemma matches it, and re-implements the certificate check from scratch in a separate script (no shared code). For Lean, it runs lake build and #print axioms. It also checks the comment thread, the AI-contributions wiki and the 68-problem FrontierMath Erdős list for prior or parallel work.
angles: Triage: scrape erdosproblems.com tags for number theory + 'open' and filter for statements with explicit finite parameters or 'is it true that for all n ≥ ...' forms that a counterexample could falsify.
Use OEIS cross-referencing: many Erdős number theory problems relate to sequences. Extend the sequence far beyond the OEIS b-file and look for a pattern break that disproves the conjecture.

Use SAT/ILP (pip install python-sat or OR-Tools) for problems about sets of integers with additive/multiplicative restrictions (Sidon-type, primitive sets, covering systems) to find explicit extremal constructions beating conjectured bounds.
Covering systems: search for coverings with prescribed moduli properties via exact cover + CRT, and verify coverage by enumerating residues mod lcm.
pitfalls: The #1 failure is that the problem was already solved in the literature or the site's statement differs subtly from the folklore version. The teorth wiki documents many such 'confused with another problem' cases.
Erdős problems with 'infinitely many' or asymptotic quantifiers cannot be settled by finite data.
Check this repository's results first to avoid repeating already-attacked items.
Site status can lag. Also read the problem's comment/forum thread and the 68 FrontierMath Erdős problems list to avoid duplicating benchmarked items.
An 'explicit counterexample' to a conjecture whose site statement includes 'for sufficiently large n' resolves nothing.

targets.name: A fifth primitive solution to a^5 + b^5 + c^5 + d^5 = e^5 (or a third all-positive one)
targets.statement: Only four primitive solutions of x1^5 + x2^5 + x3^5 + x4^5 = x5^5 in nonzero integers are known: Lander-Parkin 1966 (144^5 = 27^5+84^5+110^5+133^5), Scher-Seidl 1996 (14132^5 = (-220)^5+5027^5+6237^5+14068^5), Frye 2004 (85359^5 = 55^5+3183^5+28969^5+85282^5), and Braun 2026 (1956878^5 = 719115^5+1331622^5+(-1340632)^5+1956213^5; all four verified in Python). Target: a fifth primitive solution, or a third solution with all terms positive. J. M. Braun found the fourth (arXiv 2603.05549, 2026-03-05, revised 2026-08-21) with an optimized meet-in-the-middle search and makes no completeness claim below e = 1956878.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED for nonzero integers x1..x5 with x1^5+x2^5+x3^5+x4^5+x5^5 = 0 exactly (the 5.1.4 equation with signs moved across), gcd = 1, no pair x_i = -x_j, and the 5-tuple not equal, up to permutation and global sign, to any primitive solution listed on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler%27s_sum_of_powers_conjecture or in arXiv 2603.05549 AT VERIFICATION TIME (four on 2026-10-03: 144, 14132, 85359, 1956878 as the largest absolute terms). Flag additionally if a, b, c, d are all positive (only the third such solution).

partial_wins.statement: Certified completeness bound: an exhaustive search, independently reimplemented by the verifier, proving that the known primitive solutions are the only ones with largest absolute term up to a bound B strictly greater than the largest exhaustive-search bound stated in the literature (Braun 2026 and references therein) at verification time, with hashed logs and sampled windows rerun.

All-positive completeness bound: as p1 restricted to all-positive a, b, c, d (only 144 and 85359 known), with B strictly greater than the largest published exhaustive bound for the all-positive case at verification time.

targets.verification_method: Python big integers: evaluate the sum of fifth powers, gcd, the trivial-pair check, and a multiset comparison (with both global signs) against the four hard-coded known tuples. Under 1 second. For completeness partial wins, the verifier reimplements the meet-in-the-middle kernel with the mod-30/11-adic/5-adic filters, reruns sampled windows and audits the coverage argument.
angles: Reproduce Braun's meet-in-the-middle with the classical filters (x ≡ x^5 mod 30 gives a+b+c+d ≡ e mod 30; 11-adic and 5-adic constraints) and extend e beyond 1956878 in a different residue class partition, coordinating on regions his paper says it covered.

Signed-term specialization: two of the four known solutions have one negative term. Search the 2+2 split (a^5+b^5 = e^5 - c^5 + ... ) form with sorted-sum merging of a^5+b^5 and e^5-c^5-d^5 tables, which needs much less memory.
Structural pattern: Braun notes structural regularities across known counterexamples. Test whether they predict residue or ratio constraints that shrink the search by large factors.
Elkies-style: look for rational curves or elliptic fibrations on the 5.1.4 threefold through known points (e.g., planes x1 + x2 = λ(x3 + x4)), and search fibers with positive rank.
pitfalls: Permutations, global sign flips and rearrangements across the equals sign of the four known solutions are not new.
Non-primitive multiples.
Trivial solutions with cancelling pairs (x, -x).
Brute force below e ≈ 2e6 likely repeats Braun's searched space.

targets.name: Hall's conjecture: new good examples beyond 10^29 or beat Elkies' ratio 46.6
targets.statement: A good example for Hall's conjecture is a pair of positive integers (x, y) with 0 < |x^3 - y^2| < sqrt(x); its Hall ratio is r = sqrt(x)/|x^3 - y^2|. Aanderaa-Kristiansen-Ruud (Math. Comp. 87 (2018)) found 9 new examples and verified that ALL good examples with x < 10^29 are known. The record ratio is Elkies' x = 5853886516781223, |x^3 - y^2| = 1641843, r = 46.600... (recomputed). OEIS A078933 (good-example x values) was edited 2026-10-03. Target: a new record ratio, or new good examples with x > 10^29.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED for positive integers x, y with d = x^3 - y^2 != 0 and Hall ratio r = sqrt(x)/|d| STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the largest ratio among all examples listed in OEIS A078933, its b-file and the AKR 2018 table AT VERIFICATION TIME (46.600..., Elkies, on 2026-10-03, context only), compared exactly as rationals: x/d^2 must exceed max(x_i/d_i^2) over the listed examples; x must also be absent from those lists. A 'new' example with x < 10^29 is a BUG (that range is complete). Members of the Danilov-Elkies Fermat-Pell family (r about 1.03) never count as new.

partial_wins.statement: New good example (partial win): positive x > 10^29 and y with 0 < (x^3-y^2)^2 < x (exact), x absent from OEIS A078933, its b-file and the AKR 2018 table at verification time, and not a member of the Danilov-Elkies Fermat-Pell family.

Completeness extension: an exhaustive search, independently reimplemented by the verifier (AKR continued-fraction method or Elkies lattice method), certifying the complete list of good examples for 10^29 <= x < 10^30 (or a larger strictly-beyond-published range), with logs whose sampled windows the verifier reruns.

targets.verification_method: Python big integers: compute d = x^3 - y^2, check d ≠ 0 and d^2 < x, and compute r with mpmath at 50 digits. Diff x against the downloaded A078933 b-file and the AKR table. For the family check, test whether (x, y) satisfies the Danilov-Elkies parametrization (listed in AKR §table notes / Elkies 2000).
angles: Elkies' lattice-reduction method (rational points near the curve y^2 = x^3) applied in windows x ∈ [10^29, 10^33]. It is sub-linear in x and was designed for this.
Extend AKR's continued-fraction algorithm for sqrt(x) ('good septuples') beyond 10^29 with parallel windows on the 10 cores.
Search specializations of polynomial identities f^3 - g^2 = h with deg h small (Davenport bound extremals) at rational parameters, then LLL-adjust to integers.

Use Mordell-curve integral points: for each small k, integral points on y^2 = x^3 + k with huge x give good examples. Use known rank/height data (e.g., Gebel-Pethő-Zimmer style) to find large integral points for |k| up to 1e6.
pitfalls: The Danilov-Elkies infinite family gives infinitely many good examples with r just above 1. These are not interesting.
Floating-point sqrt for y; use isqrt and check both y and y+1.
Examples with x < 10^29 are already complete per AKR.

targets.name: Lehmer's totient problem: composite n with phi(n) | n - 1
targets.statement: Is there a composite n with phi(n) dividing n - 1? Any such n is odd and squarefree. Known computational bounds: omega(N) >= 15 and N > 10^26 (Renze, computational notebook, cited in Yamada arXiv 2303.16853); Pinch claims N > 10^30. If 3 | N: omega(N) >= 4*10^7 and N > 10^(3.6*10^8) (Burcsi-Czirbusz-Farkas 2011). A 2025 preprints.org paper claiming elimination of 14-prime composites and a 'GRH-density resolution' is unreviewed and treated as unverified.
targets.success_criterion: Full resolution CONFIRMED only with a Lean-formalized proof (no sorry, clean axiom audit), or an explicit composite n with phi(n) | n-1 verified via a complete prime factorization (every factor proven prime). Computational bound improvements are partial wins, judged against the best bounds stated at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.16853 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehmer%27s_totient_problem AT VERIFICATION TIME; reproducing omega >= 15 is a regression test, not a result. Unreviewed preprints claiming resolution never count.

partial_wins.statement: omega(N) >= 16: a rigorous, exhaustive computer proof, independently reimplemented by the verifier with identical branch-closure reasons on every branch, using exact rational arithmetic for every product p/(p-1) bound.

Certified N > 10^30: a rigorous, exhaustive, independently reimplemented computer proof that any Lehmer number exceeds 10^30 (certifying Pinch's uncertified claim), or a strictly larger bound, with a published branch log.

targets.verification_method: The verifier first reproduces Cohen-Hagis omega >= 14 and Renze's omega >= 15 as regressions. It then independently reimplements the branch-and-bound over increasing prime tuples using the Lehmer constraints (N odd and squarefree, p_i does not divide p_j - 1, and the condition on prod p/(p-1) with exact rationals) and diffs the branch-closure logs. For a counterexample: factor n, compute phi(n) exactly, and check divisibility.
angles: Branch-and-bound over increasing prime tuples in the style of Cohen-Hagis/Renze (N odd, squarefree, p_i not dividing p_j - 1, exact-rational bounds on prod p/(p-1)), parallelized on the 10 cores, aiming at a reproducible full branch log for omega = 15 -> 16.
Combine with Carmichael structure: any Lehmer number is a Carmichael number with extra constraints. Use Pinch's Carmichael tables to test structural conjectures quickly (sanity, not proof).
Use p-adic overflow constraints (as in the 2025 preprint) but derive them rigorously and check every claimed lemma symbolically.
pitfalls: Unreviewed preprints claiming resolution.
Floating-point products of p/(p-1) in branch bounds; use exact rationals.
Confusing Lehmer's totient problem with Lehmer's Mahler-measure problem.
ω ≥ 15 / N > 10^26 is already known (Renze), and Pinch claims N > 10^30.
arXiv 2003.13055 (Agama) is not a usable branch-and-bound method. Do not build on it.

targets.name: Prove Lychrel numbers exist in a new base (mechanical template-closure proof)
targets.statement: A Lychrel number in base b never reaches a palindrome under reverse-and-add. No base-10 Lychrel number is proven (196 iterated past a billion digits, Feb 2015). Existence is proven in bases 11, 17, 20, 26 and all powers of 2 (Wikipedia; base 2 example 10110). A 2023 paper, 'On the Construction of Some Lychrel Numbers', works in bases 3-10 with emphasis on base 4 (already a power of 2) and base 10, and appears to construct candidates rather than proofs; its novelty impact is unconfirmed. Target: a rigorous, mechanically checked proof for a base b not of the form 2^k and not in {11, 17, 20, 26}.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only with: (1) a start n and templates T_1..T_k (digit strings with integer-parameter repeated blocks); (2) a proof of closure under reverse-and-add for ALL parameter values that is either formalized (Lean/Coq, no sorry) or reduced to a finite mechanical check. Acceptable reductions are a finite automaton or transducer argument, or an explicit symbolic carry computation in which every parameter-dependent block is shown to produce a constant digit/carry run, together with brute force over all parameters below the threshold; (3) a proof that no template string is a palindrome; (4) a demonstration that n's orbit enters the template set; (5) a base b not in {2^k, 11, 17, 20, 26} and not listed as proven on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lychrel_number AT VERIFICATION TIME, plus a novelty search (Wikipedia references, OEIS, arXiv, the 2023 construction paper if obtainable). If step (2) only covers parameters up to some P, report 'VERIFIED FOR PARAMETERS <= P, GENERAL CASE UNPROVEN' with no claim. Any step needing 'by inspection' fails unless formalized. A base-10 proof would be a moonshot-level event.

partial_wins.statement: VERIFIED PROOF, NOVELTY UNCONFIRMED: a proof meeting conditions (1)-(4) in full (all parameters, mechanically checked) for a base b not in {2^k, 11, 17, 20, 26}, where the novelty search cannot rule out prior work (e.g. the 2023 paper could not be obtained).

Audit of the 2023 construction paper: obtain 'On the Construction of Some Lychrel Numbers' and run one of its constructions for a base in 3-10 other than 4 and 8 through this target's mechanical checker, ending either in a full all-parameter proof or in an explicit instance (concrete digit string) where the claimed template closure or non-palindromicity fails.

targets.verification_method: The verifier reimplements reverse-and-add on templates symbolically: digits are run-length blocks with symbolic lengths and the carry is tracked block by block. It must show each symbolic block emits a uniform output run with a uniform outgoing carry. Separately it brute-forces every parameter tuple up to max(threshold, 200). Non-palindromicity is checked symbolically by comparing mirrored block structure. The orbit of n is simulated 1e5 steps and each iterate is matched to a template with a regex. Lean/Coq proofs are built in a clean project with an axiom audit.
angles: Automate the search: simulate orbits in base b for many n, compress each iterate with run-length encoding, and detect eventually periodic run-length 'shapes' (as in the base-2 proof for 10110). A shape cycle of period 2-4 with linearly growing blocks is a proof candidate.

Treat reverse-and-add as a finite-state transducer on paired digit streams (outside-in) with carry states. Search for a regular language L closed under the transducer and disjoint from palindromes, using automaton learning (L*) seeded by simulation traces.

Prioritize bases b ≡ 2 mod 3 or b = 2^k ± small and other bases close to the proven ones (11, 17, 20, 26). Look for the arithmetic property that made those bases work and generalize it to a family theorem.
For base 10, prove a weaker statement: e.g., a positive-density set of orbit iterates of 196 lies in a regular language with no palindromes. Checkable but not a Lychrel proof, so not claimed.
Split run-length templates by block-length parity up front; carry behavior that depends on parity is the most common hidden gap.
pitfalls: Mistaking 'not palindrome after 10^9 steps' for a proof.
The closure check verified only for small block lengths (needs an argument for all lengths).
Prior art: some bases may already be done in the 2023 paper or hobbyist sites (Walker, Van Landingham).
Carry-boundary edge cases where block length 0 or 1 behaves differently.
Base 4, 8 and 16 are powers of 2 and already proven, so they do not count.
Run-length templates whose block lengths grow but whose carry behavior depends on block-length parity need a case split, which is easy to miss.

targets.name: 3x3 magic square with >= 7 square entries (second example) or nine squares
targets.statement: Does a 3x3 magic square of nine distinct perfect squares exist? Only one fully magic 3x3 square of distinct positive integers with 7 square entries is known: Bremner (1999), [[373^2,289^2,565^2],[360721,425^2,23^2],[205^2,527^2,222121]] with magic sum 541875. (Sallows' 1997 8-square square has a failing diagonal and is not fully magic.) Christian Boyer offers prizes for a second 7-square example or for a 9-square example. Rome-Yamagishi (2024) settled all n >= 4. Searches: Buell (center up to 25e24), Boyer (~2.5e27); Wikipedia: any solution has entries > 10^14. A Sept 2026 GitHub project (Kepler71) handled 11 sections by 2-descent/Chabauty, left the (11,4) and (15,8) parameter pairs unresolved, and states the problem is not solved.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED if the agent gives a 3x3 matrix of nine distinct positive integers with all 8 line sums equal (exact integer arithmetic), and either (a) at least 7 entries are perfect squares (math.isqrt) and the square is NOT equivalent to Bremner's square [[373^2,289^2,565^2],[360721,425^2,23^2],[205^2,527^2,222121]] (magic sum 541875), nor to any other 7-square fully magic square listed on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_square_of_squares or Boyer's prize pages at verification time; equivalence is tested under the 8 dihedral symmetries after dividing by the largest square common factor; or (b) all 9 entries are distinct squares (prize-level). Semi-magic squares, repeated entries, and zero or negative entries never count.

partial_wins.statement: Kepler71 open sections: a complete, machine-reproducible determination (rank and generators with a PARI/Magma-checkable certificate, plus descent or Chabauty output) of the rational points relevant to 7-square squares on the (11,4) or (15,8) section that the Kepler71 repo left unresolved, ending either in a new 7-square square or in a proof that the section yields none beyond known ones.

New placement pattern: a machine-reproducible proof that an explicit infinite family/section for a 7-of-9 placement pattern not treated in Kepler71's 11 sections or Bremner's work contains no fully magic 7-square square (or exhibits one), with all rank/descent computations rerunnable by the verifier.

targets.verification_method: Exact integer check of the 8 line sums, distinctness, positivity and isqrt squareness. Normalize by the square part of the gcd and compare all 8 symmetries against the hard-coded Bremner square (already verified magic with sum 541875). For partial wins, rerun the rank/descent computations in PARI (cypari2) or Magma from the stated curve equations and check that the section matches the Kepler71 parametrization.
angles: Use the parametrization: a 3x3 magic square with center e has entries e ± x, e ± y, e ± (x+y), e ± (x-y). With squares, this is a system of arithmetic progressions of three squares (congruent-number curves). Search for 7-square configurations as rational points on a specific genus-1 fibration, using point addition on each fiber instead of brute force.

Avoid the 11 sections already treated in the Kepler71 repo; the (11,4) and (15,8) parameter pairs are the unresolved ones. Target the other 7-of-9 placement patterns (which two cells are non-square) and compute ranks of the corresponding elliptic fibers with pari (pip cypari2) to find rank ≥ 1 fibers with small-height points.

Use Bremner's original method (rational points on a quartic surface) to generate infinitely many 7-square candidates in a family, then check distinctness/positivity. Most 'new' finds are scalings, so normalize aggressively.
Use a modular sieve over center values with residue-class precomputation (mod 2^k, 3, 5, 7, 13) to prune 9-square configurations, as a sanity-limited search, not a frontier push.
pitfalls: Scalings or symmetries of the known Bremner/Sallows square count as the same square.
Semi-magic (diagonals failing) or repeated entries (Parker Square) do not count.
Negative or zero entries do not count.
Floating-point square tests.
Sallows' 1997 square has a failing diagonal and is NOT the 7-square magic square. Only Bremner's is fully magic.
Kepler71 handled 11 sections. The (11,4) and (15,8) parameter pairs were left unresolved there, and those are the only sections with a fresh angle.

targets.name: New small-Mahler-measure polynomials / Salem numbers beyond the proven-complete ranges
targets.statement: Mossinghoff's Mahler-Measure-Database (updated 2026-07-18) lists known primitive irreducible noncyclotomic integer polynomials with Mahler measure < 1.3 up to degree 200 (AllSmallMeasures_200.txt), the smallest known measure for each even degree up to 200 (BestByDegree_200.txt) and Salem numbers < 49/37 (SalemList.txt). Mossinghoff-Rhin-Wu (Exp. Math. 2008) made the M<1.3 list complete through degree 44 and proved the per-degree minimum for every even degree <= 54; above those degrees the lists are heuristic. Target: a polynomial that belongs in these lists above the complete ranges but is missing, or that beats a BestByDegree entry above degree 54. Lehmer's question (is 1.17628... the smallest measure > 1?) remains open.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED requires an explicit integer polynomial P that is irreducible over Q (sympy factor_list), primitive in the database's sense (check the README definition; at minimum not of the form Q(x^k), k>=2), and noncyclotomic, with M(P) certified by interval arithmetic (python-flint arb/acb root isolation) or by two independent methods agreeing to 30 digits. It must also satisfy one of the following, judged against the database files freshly downloaded from https://github.com/mossinghoff/Mahler-Measure-Database AT VERIFICATION TIME: (i) 46 <= deg P <= 200, M(P) < 1.3, and P is absent from AllSmallMeasures_200.txt after canonicalization (P(x), P(-x), the reciprocal, and sign); (ii) 56 <= deg P <= 200 and M(P) STRICTLY BELOW (direction: min) the BestByDegree_200.txt entry for that degree; (iii) a Salem number < 49/37 absent from SalemList.txt with degree above the completeness range stated in the file header. Any 'new' polynomial of degree <= 44 with M<1.3, or any improvement at degree <= 54, is automatically classed as a BUG and is not claimed. Littlewood maximal-measure claims do not count.

partial_wins.statement: Certified completeness extension: an exhaustive enumeration, independently reimplemented by the verifier, that reproduces the published complete M<1.3 list through degree 44 as a regression and then certifies the complete list of M<1.3 polynomials at degree 46 (one degree past the Mossinghoff-Rhin-Wu range), provided the database README/headers do not already claim completeness there at verification time.

Certified minimality extension: a rigorous, independently reproduced proof that the BestByDegree_200.txt entry for degree 56 is the minimal measure among noncyclotomic polynomials of that degree (extending the proven range past 54), provided no such result is stated in the database or the literature at verification time.

targets.verification_method: Re-parse the coefficients, factor over QQ, and isolate roots with python-flint acb_poly at >= 300 bits, checking that the root count outside the unit circle matches. Compute M(P) as a certified interval. Canonicalize and diff against freshly downloaded database files, and reject immediately if deg <= 44 (or <= 54 for BestByDegree). For Salem claims: compute the trace polynomial and use Sturm sequences to certify that all but one of its real roots lie in (-2,2). For partial wins, rerun the enumeration with independent code and diff the resulting lists.
angles: Search at high degree (100-200), where the lists are certainly non-exhaustive. Use products/compositions of known small-measure polynomials with Chebyshev-type substitutions (P(x^k), P(x+1/x) lifts), then do local coefficient hill-climbing on the trace polynomial.

Use Coxeter-element constructions: characteristic polynomials of Coxeter transformations of star-shaped graphs T_{p,q,r} give Salem numbers (McMullen). Systematically enumerate graph families and other tree shapes and test against SalemList.
Integer-linear-programming root-separator method (Sac-Epee style) restricted to new degree windows, with the 10 Mac cores in parallel.
Interlacing construction: Salem numbers arise from pairs of interlacing cyclotomic polynomials (McKee-Smyth). Enumerate interlacing pairs of products of cyclotomics up to degree ~120.
Restrict every search to degree >= 46 (>= 56 for per-degree records); the lower ranges are proven complete.
pitfalls: Floating-point root finding near the unit circle misclassifies roots; use high precision or certified methods.
Forgetting canonicalization (reciprocal, x->-x) makes a known polynomial look new.
Reducible polynomials with cyclotomic factors have the same measure as their noncyclotomic factor and are not new.
The database files may contain range/completeness notes. Read them before claiming novelty.
Degree ≤44 (M<1.3) and degree ≤54 (per-degree minimum) are proven complete, so a 'new' entry there is a canonicalization or precision bug.
The LargeLittlewood list stops at degree 30 and is likely exhaustive. Drop the Littlewood angle.
Substitution x -> x^k preserves Mahler measure, so P(x^k) of a listed P is not a new primitive entry.

targets.name: Perfect cuboid (perfect Euler brick)
targets.statement: Is there a rectangular box with integer edges a, b, c such that the three face diagonals and the space diagonal are all integers? Exhaustive searches require smallest edge > 5e11, odd edge > 2.5e13 and space diagonal > 9e15 (R. D. Matson, 2015-01-18, per Wikipedia Euler_brick). de Grey-Gibbs-Helm (Geombinatorics 33(3), 2024) gave an elliptic-curve search approach. Peschmann (arXiv 2604.28072, 2026-04-30) proves non-existence on 1,072 explicit fibers with maximum parameter < 100. Many arXiv 'no perfect cuboid' claims (e.g. 2206.06160) are not accepted proofs.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for explicit positive integers a, b, c with a^2+b^2, b^2+c^2, a^2+c^2 and a^2+b^2+c^2 all perfect squares (math.isqrt check), or for a non-existence proof formalized in Lean without sorry and with a clean axiom audit. Body/face/edge cuboids (one diagonal irrational) never count.

partial_wins.statement: New excluded family: a rigorous non-existence proof for an explicit infinite family not covered by arXiv 2604.28072's 1,072 fibers (e.g. fibers with parameter >= 100, or a whole elliptic fibration of the de Grey-Gibbs-Helm reformulation), with every rank/descent computation rerunnable by the verifier in PARI or Magma and the written argument checked line by line (Lean preferred).

Search frontier: an independently reproducible exhaustive search raising one of Matson's bounds (smallest edge, odd edge, or space diagonal) strictly above the largest published bound for that quantity at verification time, with hashed logs and a coverage argument the verifier audits while rerunning sampled windows with independent code.

targets.verification_method: Exact isqrt checks for a solution. For proofs, a Lean build plus axiom audit. For partial wins, rerun of computer-algebra steps or sampled search windows with independent code.
angles: Use the de Grey-Gibbs-Helm elliptic-curve reformulation: Euler bricks correspond to points on a family of elliptic curves, and perfection is a further square condition. Search fibers by rank (cypari2) rather than by edge size, concentrating on fibers not among the 1,072 handled in arXiv 2604.28072.

Apply modular-form / Galois-representation obstructions: the perfect-cuboid surface is a known algebraic surface of general type. Look for a Brauer-Manin-type or étale descent obstruction on specific families.

Use the known parity/divisibility constraints (one edge odd, divisibility by 3, 4, 5, 11, 16, 19 etc.) to build a CRT-structured search that only visits admissible residue classes beyond 2.5e13 for the odd edge, as a sanity-bounded experiment.
pitfalls: Crank 'proofs' of non-existence are common on arXiv and ResearchGate.
Body/face/edge cuboids (one diagonal irrational) are near-misses, not solutions.
Floating-point square tests.

targets.name: Perfect triangle: integer sides, rational medians, integer area
targets.statement: Is there a triangle with rational sides, all three medians rational, and rational area (a Heron triangle with three rational medians)? It is conjectured that none exists. Buchholz-Rathbun showed infinitely many Heron triangles with two rational medians, and Hone (2024) gave explicit formulas linking these to Somos sequences and elliptic curves. 'No perfect triangle is isosceles' is proven.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for an explicit triangle with positive integer sides a, b, c satisfying the strict triangle inequality such that 2b^2 + 2c^2 - a^2, 2a^2 + 2c^2 - b^2 and 2a^2 + 2b^2 - c^2 are all perfect squares (so all three medians are rational) and 16*Area^2 = (a+b+c)(-a+b+c)(a-b+c)(a+b-c) is a perfect square. Rescalings and degenerate triangles never count.

partial_wins.statement: Non-existence on a new subfamily: a proof that no perfect triangle lies in an explicit infinite subfamily (e.g. a one-parameter family with a fixed angle, or a fiber of Buchholz's two-median elliptic family) not already treated in arXiv 1910.06888, Buchholz-Rathbun or Hone 2024, with every rank/descent/Chabauty computation rerunnable in PARI or Magma by the verifier and the written argument checked line by line.

New two-median family: an explicit infinite family of Heron triangles with two rational medians plus an additional rational quantity (e.g. a rational angle bisector), verified symbolically, and shown not to be a rescaling or reparametrization of the Buchholz-Rathbun or Hone families; reported without claim unless an independent expert-style check confirms novelty.

targets.verification_method: Exact integer arithmetic with isqrt on four quantities, under 1 second. For partial wins, symbolic verification of the family identities (sympy) and rerunning of the arithmetic-geometry computations.
angles: Work on Buchholz's one-parameter family of elliptic curves for two-rational-median Heron triangles. The third-median condition defines a further double cover. Search the base for parameters where the cover's fiber has rank ≥ 1, using cypari2 ellrank, instead of searching triangles directly.
Use Hone's Somos-sequence formula to generate the two-median family to enormous height cheaply, then sieve the third-median square condition mod many primes before any big-integer test.
Prove non-existence on a specific infinite subfamily (e.g., triangles with one angle fixed, cf. arXiv 1910.06888) by Chabauty or descent. This is a checkable partial result.
pitfalls: Confusing 'integer medians' with 'rational medians' (scaling by 2).
Degenerate triangles.
Families that are just rescalings of known two-median triangles.

targets.name: Ideal Prouhet-Tarry-Escott solution of size 11 or 13
targets.statement: Find two disjoint multisets A, B of n integers with sum a^k = sum b^k for k = 1..n-1 (an ideal PTE solution) for n = 11 or n = 13 (or any n ≥ 13). Ideal solutions over Z are known only for n ≤ 10 and n = 12. Status: Wikipedia lists n = 11 and n >= 13 as having no known ideal solution; the n = 12 example is Kuosa-Meyrignac-Chen Shuwen (1999). Coppersmith-Mossinghoff-Scheinerman-VanderKam (arXiv 2304.11254, 2023): no symmetric ideal solution for n = 11 with height <= 3500, n = 13 with height <= 2000, n = 15 with height <= 1100; they found n = 11 symmetric solutions over real quadratic fields. arXiv 2606.07735 (June 2026) treats only degree-3 symmetry questions.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED for explicit integer multisets A, B with |A| = |B| = n where n = 11 or n >= 13 is listed as having no known ideal solution on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prouhet%E2%80%93Tarry%E2%80%93Escott_problem AT VERIFICATION TIME, A and B disjoint as multisets (so the effective size after cancellation is still n), and sum a^k = sum b^k exactly for every k = 1..n-1. Solutions over Gaussian, Eisenstein or real-quadratic integers, and non-ideal solutions (degree < n-1), do not count.

partial_wins.statement: Symmetric n = 11 frontier: an exhaustive search, independently reimplemented by the verifier, proving no symmetric ideal n = 11 solution with height up to a bound strictly greater than 3500 (CMSV 2023) or the largest published bound at verification time.
Symmetric n = 13 frontier: as in p1 for n = 13, with height bound strictly greater than 2000 (CMSV 2023) or the largest published bound at verification time.

targets.verification_method: Python big integers: check sizes, check that the multisets are disjoint (Counter intersection empty), and compare power sums for k = 1..n-1. Equivalence to known solutions is irrelevant because none exist for these n. Under 1 second. For search-extension partial wins, the verifier reimplements the CMSV-style mod-p obstruction search, reruns it (or sampled height ranges plus the full obstruction tables), and compares the surviving-candidate lists.
angles: Non-symmetric solutions: CMSV searched only symmetric (B = -A) solutions for odd n. Search non-symmetric n = 11 configurations with their local-solution and CRT-lifting method (required prime divisors of the constant C_n).
Push the symmetric n = 11 search past height 3500 with their mod-p obstruction method plus more primes (29, 31, 37) and the 10 cores. Height 6000-8000 is a concrete frontier.
Lattice approach: fix 9 of the 11 values and solve for the remaining two via the quadratic resolvent. CMSV found near-misses with irrational pairs; search nearby for rational ones with LLL.
Build from n = 12 and n = 10 solutions using Frolov/Tarry transformations (A ∪ (B+d), B ∪ (A+d)), and look for cancellation that drops the size.
pitfalls: Non-ideal solutions (degree k < n-1) are plentiful and do not count.
Solutions with common elements in A and B have smaller effective size after cancellation.
Solutions over quadratic fields (like CMSV's α, β examples) are not integer solutions.
Floating-point power sums.

targets.name: Rational distance problem for the unit square (four-distance problem)
targets.statement: Is there a point (x, y) in the plane with rational distances to all four vertices of the unit square? Points on a diagonal, midline or edge are proven impossible (Yang Ji, arXiv 2105.05250), along with some prime-related cases. An unreviewed 2026 GitHub project (Mulatram-UwU, AI agent with human GPG-signing) claims an exhaustive search ruling out common denominators Q <= 5e10 (headline 2e10), with Lean checks of the reduction and search logic, and states it is not a solution.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for explicit rationals x, y (exact fractions) such that x^2+y^2, (x-1)^2+y^2, x^2+(y-1)^2 and (x-1)^2+(y-1)^2 are all squares of rationals: each value in lowest terms has a perfect-square numerator and denominator, checked with fractions.Fraction and math.isqrt. Three-distance points never count.

partial_wins.statement: New impossible family: a complete proof that no point on an explicit infinite rational curve (e.g. a line through the center with a fixed non-axis, non-diagonal slope t, or a whole one-parameter family of such lines) has rational distances to all four vertices, beyond the diagonal/midline/edge cases of arXiv 2105.05250, with all genus/rank/Chabauty computations rerunnable by the verifier and the written argument checked line by line (Lean preferred).

New local obstruction: an extension of the congruence condition of arXiv 1904.12097 to additional primes, with a complete proof and a brute-force check over residues that the verifier reruns, ruling out a stated positive proportion of height-bounded candidates not excluded by the published condition.

targets.verification_method: Python fractions.Fraction exact computation and isqrt square tests on reduced numerator/denominator. For partial wins, line-by-line proof check plus rerun of all computer-algebra steps.
angles: Three-distance solutions form a known parametrized surface (infinitely many points rational to three vertices). Parametrize it via a K3/elliptic fibration and search for fibers where the fourth distance condition gives an elliptic curve of positive rank, which is far more efficient than denominator scanning.

Use symmetry: impose the point on a rational line through the center with slope t (not the diagonals/midlines already excluded). Each t gives a curve. Compute genus and use Chabauty on low-genus cases to prove impossibility families.
Use local-global obstructions: extend the 2019 congruence condition (arXiv 1904.12097) to more primes to rule out larger fractions of height-bounded candidates.
pitfalls: Only three of four distances rational: infinitely many such points are known.
Floating-point near-misses.
Trusting the unreviewed 5e10 bound as established fact.

targets.name: Equal sums of sixth powers: 6.1.5 / 6.1.6 (Euler conjecture k=6) and 6.2.2
targets.statement: No sixth power is known to be a sum of six or fewer positive sixth powers (Euler's sum-of-powers conjecture is unresolved for k >= 6; the smallest known 6.1.n has n = 7). No nontrivial solution to a^6 + b^6 = c^6 + d^6 (6.2.2) is known, and none to 6.2.3 or 6.2.4. Search frontiers: 6.2.2 none with sum < 7.25e26 (Ekl 1996); 6.1.5/6.1.6 none with final term <= 730,000 (Resta-Meyrignac, Math. Comp. 72 (2003)); concentrated 6.1.5 subcase none for f <= 4.3e6 (ESOP6, 2026-09-04, self-graded evidence B, production logs not kept, unreviewed).
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for explicit positive integers satisfying the stated equation exactly (Python big integers), nontrivial (not a permutation identity, no zero terms, no cancelling equal terms across the sides): any solution of 6.2.2, 6.2.3 or 6.2.4, or any solution of 6.1.n with n <= 6, provided no such solution is listed on MathWorld or Wikipedia at verification time. Extending search bounds is NOT a claim-level result.

partial_wins.statement: 6.2.2 frontier extension: an exhaustive search, independently reimplemented by the verifier on randomly chosen windows with identical per-window candidate counts and hashed full logs, proving no nontrivial 6.2.2 solution with sum below a bound strictly greater than 7.25e26 (or the largest published bound found at verification time), using the square-coordinate fibration on u^3+v^3=w^3+t^3.

6.1.5 general-case extension: an exhaustive search of the FULL 6.1.5 equation (not only ESOP6's concentrated subcase) proving no solution with final term up to a bound strictly greater than 730,000 (or the largest published general bound at verification time), with logs kept and independently spot-reproduced as in p1.

targets.verification_method: Exact big-integer evaluation of both sides and a check for trivial solutions, under 1 second.
