For search-extension partial wins, the verifier reimplements the search kernel, reruns randomly sampled windows, compares per-window counts and log hashes, and audits the covering argument that the windows exhaust the claimed range.
angles: 6.2.2 via squares: (a^2, b^2, c^2, d^2) is a point on the cubic surface u^3+v^3 = w^3+t^3 with all coordinates squares. Enumerate taxicab-structured solutions of u^3+v^3=w^3+t^3 (Z[omega] factorization) and test squareness, instead of scanning sixth powers directly.

Use modular constraints: sixth powers mod 7, 9, 13, 19, 37 and 2^k lie in tiny residue sets. Build a multi-modulus filter (like ESOP6's 'concentrated case') for an un-searched configuration (exemptions split across two terms) rather than repeating theirs.

Use Elkies' lattice method for x^6 = sum of 5 or 6 sixth powers: for fixed residue patterns, reduce to finding small vectors near a projective variety; use LLL in Python (fpylll pip) to find small solutions in regions far beyond brute-force bounds.
pitfalls: Repeating ESOP6's concentrated-case brute force (no new idea).
Trivial solutions (permutations, zero terms).
Confusing 6.3.3, which has infinitely many solutions, with the open cases.
The suggested 6.2.2 reduction is garbled. The right fibration is (a^2,b^2,c^2,d^2) on the cubic surface u^3+v^3=w^3+t^3 with all coordinates squares, which is a Taxicab-structured search.
ESOP6's bound is self-graded B evidence, so do not treat it as a certified frontier.

targets.name: Sums of three cubes: k = 114, 390, 627, 633, 732, 921, 975, and a fourth representation of 3
targets.statement: Find integers x, y, z with x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = k for an open k < 1000 (114, 390, 627, 633, 732, 921, 975 per Wikipedia, edited 2026-09-12), or a fourth representation of 3 beyond (1,1,1), (4,4,-5) and Booker-Sutherland's 2019 solution. Epoch AI lists k = 114 and the new representation of 3 as FrontierMath open problems. Booker-Sutherland used Charity Engine with |z| <= 1e16 range bounds. Also open: primitive representations of k = 192, 375 and 600 (Wikipedia).
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only for explicit integers with x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = k exactly in Python big integers, where k is listed as open on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sums_of_three_cubes AT VERIFICATION TIME, or for k = 3 a triple not equal to any permutation of the representations listed there. Any claimed solution for k = 4 or 5 mod 9 is an error. Nothing else counts as full success.

partial_wins.statement: Primitive representation: integers x, y, z with gcd(x,y,z) = 1 and x^3+y^3+z^3 = k for k = 192, 375 or 600, provided Wikipedia still lists that k as having no known primitive solution at verification time (non-primitive scalings of solutions for k/8 or k/27 do not count).

Certified search extension: for one open k, an exhaustive search with a published, independently reimplementable algorithm proving no solution in a region strictly larger than the largest region reported searched for that k at verification time (Booker-Sutherland's |z| <= 1e16 as context), with hashed logs; the verifier reruns randomly sampled sub-ranges and audits the coverage argument.

targets.verification_method: Big-integer arithmetic, under 1 second. Compare against Wikipedia's open list and the known k = 3 triples. For p1, check gcd = 1 and Wikipedia's primitive-solution note. For p2, rerun sampled sub-ranges with independent code and audit coverage.
angles: Do NOT brute force (Charity Engine already covered |z| ≤ 1e16). Look instead for a structured family: search for polynomial or rational parametric curves on x^3+y^3+z^3 = k of low degree for these specific k, which would give infinitely many solutions. This is a genuinely new idea if it exists.

Use the Heath-Brown density heuristic to estimate where the smallest solution likely lies for each k, then pick the k with the smallest expected |z| and do a congruence-restricted (mod 9, 7, 13, 27 cubic residue) search around the Booker algorithm's blind spots, if any were documented.

Use arithmetic geometry: for the cubic surface, look for rational points via Brauer-Manin-free fibrations into conics or genus-1 curves (fix x + y = d dividing k - z^3). Search d over smooth numbers with large prime-power structure.
pitfalls: Repeating Booker-Sutherland's search with fewer resources.
Sign/permutation duplicates for k = 3.
Reported solutions for k ≡ 4, 5 mod 9 are impossible, so the computation is wrong.

k=192, 375 and 600 have no known PRIMITIVE solution (Wikipedia). A primitive representation for these would also be new, but a non-primitive one, such as a scaling of a solution for k/8 or k/27, is not.

targets.name: Improve the upper bound on Taxicab(7) (and higher taxicab bounds)
targets.statement: Ta(n) is the smallest positive integer expressible as a sum of two positive cubes in n distinct ways. Ta(1)..Ta(6) are known; Ta(6) = 24153319581254312065344. Ta(7) is unknown. The best known upper bound is Ta(7) <= 24885189317885898975235988544 (~2.49e28; Boyer 2006, OEIS A011541), which equals 101^3 * Ta(6), a pure scaling construction. Boyer's 2008 JIS paper (Article 08.1.6) gives upper bounds up to Ta(19) and for Cabtaxi(10..30). Target: a smaller N with 7 representations.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED if the agent gives an integer N with at least 7 pairwise-distinct unordered pairs {a,b} of POSITIVE integers satisfying a^3+b^3 = N exactly, and N is STRICTLY SMALLER (direction: min) than the best Ta(7) upper bound shown at https://oeis.org/A011541 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxicab_number AT VERIFICATION TIME (24885189317885898975235988544 on 2026-10-03, context only), compared as exact digit strings. Finding such N proves only an upper bound, never the value of Ta(7). Weaker results are partial wins.

partial_wins.statement: Higher taxicab bound: for some 8 <= n <= 19, an integer N with at least n distinct unordered positive-cube pairs a^3+b^3 = N, strictly smaller than Boyer's bound for Ta(n) in JIS 11 (2008) Article 08.1.6 AND than any smaller bound for Ta(n) found on OEIS A011541 or Wikipedia at verification time (exact digit-string comparison).

Cabtaxi bound: for some 10 <= n <= 30, an integer N with at least n distinct representations as a sum of two cubes of integers (negative or zero allowed, as in the Cabtaxi definition), strictly smaller than the Cabtaxi(n) bound in Boyer's 2008 JIS tables and than any later value found on OEIS or Wikipedia at verification time.

targets.verification_method: Python big integers: compute each a^3+b^3 (or signed cubes for Cabtaxi), check all equal N, check pairs are distinct as unordered pairs with the right sign rules, and compare N to the exact bound strings copied at verification time from OEIS A011541 / Wikipedia / Boyer's JIS tables. Seconds.
angles: Exploit the norm-form structure: a^3+b^3 = (a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2). The representation count is governed by factorizations in Z[omega]. Build N as products of many split primes p ≡ 1 mod 3 with small exponents, then solve for representations via the divisor d = a+b and the quadratic for a,b. This searches multiplicatively structured N instead of scanning.

Rational-point approach: representations of N correspond to rational points on the elliptic curve x^3+y^3=N. Pick cube-free kernels N0 whose curve has rank ≥ 2 and many small-height points, then scale by a common denominator cubed. Choose the denominator by an integer-program over point combinations to minimize the scale.
Generalize Boyer's 'multiply Ta(6) by c^3' trick: search small cube multipliers c^3 times numbers with 5-6 representations whose prime structure adds representations, instead of only scaling Ta(6).
Meet-in-the-middle over d = a+b dividing N: for each candidate N (smooth in split primes), enumerate divisors d with d^3/4 ≤ N ≤ d^3 and test discriminant squareness. Parallelize across 10 cores.
For the partial wins, compare against Boyer's 2008 JIS tables, not Wikipedia (which stops at Ta(12)): higher-n bounds are where scaling constructions may be weakest.
pitfalls: Counting (a,b) and (b,a) as distinct, or allowing zero/negative cubes (that is the Cabtaxi variant).
Comparing against a misremembered bound. Use the exact OEIS string.
A claim of 'Ta(7) found' without exhaustive minimality proof is only an upper bound.
Wikipedia lists only Ta(7)..Ta(12). Use Boyer's JIS tables for higher n, or a 'new' bound may already be beaten.
OEIS attribution (Wilson v, 2012) is the date of an edit, not the discovery.

targets.name: CVRPLIB VRPTW (Gehring-Homberger, DIMACS truncated-distance objective): beat an open best-known solution
targets.statement: CVRPLIB re-hosts the 300 Gehring-Homberger VRPTW instances (200-1000 customers) since May 2026 under the DIMACS-2022 convention: single objective = total travel distance with each edge length truncated to one decimal (floor(10*d)/10), and travel times equal to those truncated distances; no vehicle-minimization hierarchy. Live on 2026-10-08: 193 of the 300 instances are Opt = no (all 200-customer instances are Opt = yes; most 400-1000 ones are open). The Updates page shows 23 new BKSs between Sept 26 and Sept 28 2026, all from one practitioner (Tobias Linke), on C1_10_*, R1_10_*, RC1_*, R1_6_2, RC1_4_9, RC2_10_8, including a 0.2 improvement on RC1_8_1 one day after his own previous value, so the table still has slack. Find a feasible solution with truncated-distance total strictly below the listed UB for any Homberger instance with Opt = no.
targets.success_criterion: A solution file in CVRPLIB format ('Route #k: c1 c2 ...' with customer ids exactly as in the Solomon-format instance file, depot = 0) for one Gehring-Homberger instance (names C1_/C2_/R1_/R2_/RC1_/RC2_ with _2_, _4_, _6_, _8_ or _10_ middle part) whose Opt column reads 'no' in the All Instances table at https://galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib/index.php/en/instances, such that a standalone checker written from the Solomon format definition that (a) reads the instance (VEHICLE NUMBER and CAPACITY, then one line per customer: id x y demand ready due service), (b) computes per-edge distance d = floor(10 * euclid + 1e-9) / 10 (DIMACS truncation) and uses the same truncated value as travel time, (c) verifies each customer served exactly once, every route load <= CAPACITY, number of routes <= VEHICLE NUMBER, and time windows respected with arrival = max(departure_prev + d, ready) <= due at every customer and return to the depot by the depot's due time, service time added after arrival, and (d) sums the truncated edge lengths over every route including the depot legs, reports a total (to one decimal) strictly less than the UB for that instance in the All Instances table and consistent with the Updates log at https://galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib/index.php/en/updates, both re-fetched live immediately before claiming. Before any claim the checker must accept the posted BKS files of C1_10_10 (instance id 685), RC1_8_1 (id 656) and R1_10_3 (id 698) as feasible and reproduce 39815.6, 29946.1 and 44673.3 exactly (verified by the vetter 2026-10-08; with double-precision travel times the posted RC1_8_1 and R1_10_3 files violate a time window by < 0.1, so truncated travel times are the only convention under which the table is self-consistent). The solution file, checker and table snapshot are saved together. Nothing is submitted to CVRPLIB; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: Improve the SINTEF hierarchical BKS (strictly fewer vehicles, or equal vehicles and strictly smaller double-precision distance by at least 0.01 after 2-decimal rounding) for any Gehring-Homberger 600/800/1000 instance listed at https://www.sintef.no/projectweb/top/vrptw/homberger-benchmark/<600|800|1000>-customers/ (rows: instance, vehicles, distance, reference, date; solution files linked per row), checked by the same route checker in hierarchical mode (double-precision distances and travel times) after reproducing the posted SINTEF solution file's vehicle count and distance (e.g. c1_10_2 -> 90 / 42222.96). SINTEF's table is re-fetched live at claim time. Separate objective from the headline; never mix the two.

A solution for an open Homberger instance whose truncated-distance total equals the live CVRPLIB UB exactly but whose undirected edge set differs from the posted BKS file in at least 10% of edges (edge-set comparison by the same checker); independently checkable from the two files.

Strict CVRPLIB UB improvement (headline checker and re-fetch rule) on any C2_/R2_/RC2_ instance with Opt = no; recorded separately because, apart from RC2_10_8, the long-horizon classes were not touched in the Sept 2026 wave, so slack there is independent evidence.

targets.verification_method: Instance and BKS files via https://galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib/index.php/en/download/instance/<id> and .../download/bks/<id> (ids in the table HTML; 685 = C1_10_10, 656 = RC1_8_1, 698 = R1_10_3). The checker must first reproduce the posted BKS values and accept them as feasible under truncated distances and truncated travel times (C1_10_10: truncation 39,815.6; nearest-integer gives 39,775.0 and exact gives 39,851.34, so the convention is unambiguous). Then check the claimed solution. Minutes. Re-fetch the All Instances table with plain curl -L and parse the instance's <tr> (UB cell '$39{,}815.60$', Opt cell).
angles: Run PyVRP / HGS-VRPTW (open source, built for the DIMACS truncated objective) and other open VRPTW HGS/ALNS codes with long time limits and many seeds, seeded from the posted BKS; most CVRPLIB VRPTW values are converted SINTEF hierarchical solutions, which were never optimised for distance-only, so distance-only search from them has real slack.

Target instances whose BKS moved most recently by a single practitioner (RC1_8_1 moved twice in two days), and instances whose CVRPLIB UB equals a converted SINTEF hierarchical solution with a high vehicle count (distance-only can use more vehicles up to VEHICLE NUMBER).
Exploit the truncation: moves whose exact delta is slightly positive but truncated delta is negative are improvements under this objective.
Exact polishing of 2-4 neighbouring routes with a CP-SAT / set-partitioning model using truncated distances.
pitfalls: Two tables, two objectives: SINTEF (hierarchical, vehicles first, double precision, 2 decimals) vs CVRPLIB (distance only, truncated to 1 decimal, truncated travel times). A solution beating one is not a win against the other; the headline criterion is CVRPLIB only.

Truncation must be applied per edge (floor(10*d)/10), not to the total, and the SAME truncated value is the travel time; using double-precision travel times rejects posted BKSs (RC1_8_1, R1_10_3) and using truncated distance with untruncated time is a mixed convention that matches nothing.
Vehicle limit: the instance's VEHICLE NUMBER (250 for 1000-customer files, 200 for 800) is an upper bound; a solution with more routes is infeasible even though the objective ignores vehicle count.
Re-fetch the All Instances table and the Updates page immediately before claiming; values moved on three consecutive days in Sept 2026.
Do not treat Solomon 100-customer instances or the 200-customer Homberger instances (all Opt = yes on CVRPLIB) as targets.

targets.name: CVRPLIB: beat a best-known solution on an open X, XL or Arnold-XXL CVRP instance
targets.statement: CVRPLIB (galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib) lists, for every CVRP instance, the best known upper bound (UB) and whether it is proven optimal (Opt column). Live on 2026-10-08: 39 of the 100 Uchoa X instances are Opt = no, all 100 XL instances (XL-n1048-k237 .. XL-n10001-k1570, Queiroga et al. 2026 challenge set) are Opt = no, and all 10 Arnold-Gendreau-Sorensen XXL instances (Leuven1/2, Antwerp1/2, Ghent1/2, Brussels1/2, Flanders1/2; 3,000-30,000 customers) are Opt = no. The Updates page shows BKSs still falling in Sept 2026, often by a single unit (XL-n7193-k1683 2,958,155 -> 2,958,154 on Sept 23; Antwerp1 477,261 -> 477,260 on Sept 12; X-n536-k96, X-n716-k35, X-n979-k58 on Sept 20; 70 XL instances on Sept 11). Find a feasible solution with total cost strictly below the listed UB for any instance whose Opt column reads 'no'.
targets.success_criterion: A solution file in CVRPLIB format ('Route #k: c1 c2 ...' lines with 0-based customer ids, customer c = node c+1 of the .vrp NODE_COORD_SECTION, node 1 = depot, each route implicitly starts and ends at the depot; number of routes unrestricted) for one instance whose Opt column reads 'no' in the All Instances table at https://galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib/index.php/en/instances (plain curl -L; the table is one HTML <tr> per instance with columns Instance, |C|, |K|, Q, UB, Opt), such that a standalone checker written from the TSPLIB/CVRPLIB format definition that (a) parses the .vrp file (NODE_COORD_SECTION, DEMAND_SECTION, CAPACITY), (b) verifies every customer 2..n appears exactly once across all routes, (c) verifies every route load <= CAPACITY, and (d) sums EUC_2D edge lengths each rounded to the nearest integer (TSPLIB nint, int(d+0.5)) over depot->c1->...->ck->depot, reports an integer total strictly less than the UB shown for that instance in the All Instances table AND consistent with the Updates log at https://galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib/index.php/en/updates, both re-fetched live immediately before claiming. Before any claim the same checker must reproduce the posted BKS file costs exactly: X-n1001-k43 (instance id 257) -> 72346, Antwerp1 (id 258) -> 477260, XL-n9571-k55 (id 377) -> 106342 (all three verified by the vetter on 2026-10-08). Instance and BKS files: https://galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib/index.php/en/download/instance/<id> and .../download/bks/<id>; ids are in the table HTML (href download/instance/<id>). The solution file, the checker, and the fetched table snapshot are saved together. Nothing is submitted to CVRPLIB by the agent; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: A solution for an open X instance (Opt = no) whose checker cost equals the live UB exactly but whose undirected edge set differs from the posted BKS file's edge set in at least 10% of edges (edge-set comparison by the same checker); an alternative optimum-candidate, independently checkable from the two files.

Same as above for any XL instance with n >= 5,000: checker cost equal to the live UB with >= 10% edge-set difference from the posted BKS file. (A plain tie is not a partial win because the BKS files are downloadable.)

Strict UB improvement on any of the 10 Arnold-Gendreau-Sorensen XXL instances (Leuven1/2, Antwerp1/2, Ghent1/2, Brussels1/2, Flanders1/2), same checker and same re-fetch rule; recorded separately because these are the least saturated (last moved Sept 12 2026 by a single submitter, by 1 unit on Antwerp1).

targets.verification_method: Skeptic downloads the .vrp via https://galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib/index.php/en/download/instance/<id> and the posted BKS via .../download/bks/<id>, runs the standalone Python checker (nint per edge, 0-based customers, depot = node 1, load <= CAPACITY, every customer exactly once) on the posted BKS first: it must reproduce the table UB exactly (257 -> 72346, 258 -> 477260, 377 -> 106342). Then runs it on the claimed solution file: feasible and strictly smaller integer cost. Re-fetches https://galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib/index.php/en/instances with plain curl -L and parses the instance's <tr> (UB cell like '$72{,}346.00$', Opt cell 'yes'/'no'). Minutes on any machine. Optionally also pastes into the site's checker page (https://galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib/index.php/en/bks_challenge/checker); that is not required and nothing is submitted.
angles: Run open-source HGS-CVRP (Vidal 2022, C++) and FILO2 (Accorsi & Vigo, built for 10k+ customers) with long time limits and many seeds on the XXL and largest XL instances; seed from the posted BKS and apply SWAP*/relocate/2-opt* polishing with ruin-and-recreate restarts.

Target instances whose BKS moved most recently by a single unit from a single submitter (Antwerp1, Flanders1/2, XL-n7193-k1683) since one-unit movement signals slack; also instances with very long routes (large Q) where per-route TSP optimality via LKH-3 plus inter-route exchanges can shave units.
Decompose XL/XXL instances geographically (barycenter clustering / route-based partitions), optimize subproblems with HGS to near-optimality, then re-merge and run global local search.

Exact polishing: fix most routes, extract 3-5 neighboring routes, solve the resulting small CVRP exactly (CP-SAT or a set-partitioning MIP over enumerated routes); any strict improvement of the subproblem is a strict global improvement.
Exploit the integer-rounded objective: search for moves whose unrounded delta is slightly positive but rounded delta is negative (rounding slack), which continuous-metric local search ignores.
pitfalls: Distance convention: X, XL and AGS instances use EUC_2D with nearest-integer rounding per edge; unrounded X-n1001-k43 BKS is 72386.96, rounded is 72346. The checker must reproduce 72346 / 477260 / 106342 on the posted files before any claim.
Customer ids: solution files are 0-based (depot excluded) while .vrp nodes are 1-based with node 1 = depot; an off-by-one makes an infeasible route look feasible.

Fleet size: the k in X-nNNN-kK and XL-nNNN-kK is the fleet used by the BKS, not a hard limit in the CVRPLIB convention; AGS rows show '—' for |K|. The checker does not restrict route count, but report the route count alongside the cost.
The table value must be re-fetched at claim time: X, XL and XXL UBs changed several times in Sept 2026; a 'win' against a value cached at scout time may already be stale.
Do not count XML100 instances (all optimal), instances with Opt = 'yes' (61 X instances), or the XLTW VRPTW set (not released) as targets.
The /index.php/en/ root URL redirects (301) to /index.php/en/instances; always use the /instances URL and plain curl -L.

targets.name: Job-shop scheduling: lower the makespan upper bound on an open Taillard / Demirkol / SWV / YN / ABZ instance (Optimizizer tables)
targets.statement: Oleg Shylo's Optimizizer pages maintain the live best known lower and upper bounds, with the UB solution sequence, for the classical JSP benchmarks. Live on 2026-10-08: 20 Taillard instances (Ta18, Ta22, Ta23, Ta25-27, Ta29, Ta30, Ta32, Ta33, Ta40-44, Ta46-50), 49 Demirkol DMU instances and 10 Extra instances (Abz08, Swv06-Swv10, Yn01-Yn04) have LB < UB. UBs and LBs moved in 2024-2026 (UBs by HTSFP2024, HUSTLLG2026, OptalCP2026, EVALDIVERSIFY; LBs by RL2024, YMRL2025/2026), so the tables are a live frontier. Find a feasible schedule with makespan strictly below the listed UB for any instance with LB < UB.
targets.success_criterion: A schedule for one instance listed with LB < UB on https://optimizizer.com/TA.php, https://optimizizer.com/DMU.php or https://optimizizer.com/Extra.php, given as per-machine job sequences in Optimizizer's own 'sol' format (one line per machine in instance machine order 0..m-1, each line the n job ids 0..n-1 in processing order), such that a standalone checker written from the OR-Library/JSPLIB instance format (first line 'n m', then one line per job of (machine, time) pairs, 0-based machines) builds the semi-active schedule from the job routings plus the machine sequences (longest path in the disjunctive graph; must be acyclic), independently computes the makespan, and reports a value strictly less than the UB shown in that table, re-fetched live immediately before claiming. The checker must first reproduce the listed UB from the table's own 'sol' sequence for that instance (e.g. https://optimizizer.com/solution.php?name=ta41&UB=2006&problemclass=ta -> 2006 from the JSPLIB ta41 file; verified by the vetter 2026-10-08). The schedule file, checker, instance file (with sha256) and table snapshot are saved together. Nothing is submitted to Optimizizer; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: Close an instance with gap <= 3 (live: Ta33 1790/1791, Ta18 1393/1396) by a reproducible proof that no schedule with makespan <= UB-1 exists (CP-SAT / OptalCP run with logged seed, model file and a wall time a skeptic can repeat in under 1 hour on this 10-core Mac); counts only after the verifier re-runs it successfully.

Strict UB improvement on any open Dmu41-Dmu80 (cscmax) instance on https://optimizizer.com/DMU.php; these have the largest LB-UB gaps (e.g. Dmu41_cscmax_20_15_10 3130/3248, Dmu46_cscmax_20_20_6 3740/4035) so they are the most likely to be slack; same checker and re-fetch rule.
Strict UB improvement on Swv06-Swv10, Yn01-Yn04 or Abz08 on https://optimizizer.com/Extra.php, checked by the same standalone checker and re-fetch rule.

targets.verification_method: Instance data: Taillard ta01-ta80, swv, yn, abz in OR-Library/JSPLIB format from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tamy0612/JSPLIB/master/instances/<name> (lines starting with '#' are comments); Demirkol instances from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thomasWeise/jsspInstancesAndResults/master/data-raw/instance-data/demirkol/<rcmax|cscmax>_J_M_k.txt, where Optimizizer's DmuNN_<rcmax|cscmax>_J_M_k maps to <rcmax|cscmax>_J_M_k.txt (same 'n m' + (machine,time)-pair format). The skeptic runs the Python checker on (1) the Optimizizer 'sol' sequence (solution.php?name=<name>&UB=<ub>&problemclass=<ta|dmu|extra>) to confirm it yields the table UB, then (2) the claimed schedule. Seconds of compute. Re-fetch the table page with plain curl and parse the instance's <tr> (LB and UB are the leading integers of cells 3 and 4).
angles: Tabu search with N7/N6 neighborhoods and path relinking (Nowicki-Smutnicki i-TSAB, Zhang et al. TS/SA) seeded from the posted UB sequence, run for hours with many restarts on 10 cores; most historical UB improvements came from exactly this with more wall time.

Large-neighborhood search with CP-SAT: fix all but a window of ~30-40% of operations (time-window or machine-subset neighborhoods) and solve the subproblem to optimality repeatedly (LNS/CP hybrids produced the 2024-2026 improvements).
Target the instances with the largest relative gap (Ta50 1837/1923, Ta41 1912/2006, Dmu cscmax instances with 3-7% gaps, Swv07 1523/1595): the UB is far from the LB so there may be real slack.

Run OR-Tools CP-SAT with the full model, 10 workers, hint = posted UB schedule, for several hours on 30x20 and 50x20 instances; OptalCP2026 lowered several DMU UBs with a CP solver, so CP-SAT may lower one directly.
Exploit a new 2026 LB (YMRL2026) landing within a few units of the UB: run a targeted satisfiability search for makespan = UB-1 with strong symmetry breaking.
pitfalls: Instance format confusion: Taillard's original files list the times matrix and machines matrix separately (machines 1-based) whereas the OR-Library/JSPLIB format interleaves (machine, time) pairs 0-based. The checker must reproduce the posted UB from the posted sequence before any claim.

Optimizizer 'sol' pages are machine sequences (m lines of n job ids), not start times; the checker must build the schedule from scratch and detect cycles. Checking only job-order feasibility or reading makespan from the attacker's own simulator is not enough.

Several instances were improved in 2026 (HUSTLLG2026 on Ta26, Ta32, Ta44, Ta46 and many DMU; OptalCP2026 on DMU); re-fetch the specific table page immediately before claiming, and compare against UB not LB.
Claiming a closed instance (LB = UB after a CP run) is only a partial win if the skeptic can repeat the run; a solver log alone is not a certificate.
Do not use the GitHub REST API (api.github.com) for instance listings; it rate-limits unauthenticated calls (403 seen 2026-10-08). Use the raw.githubusercontent.com file URLs.

targets.name: MIPLIB 2017: improve the best known objective of an open collection instance
targets.statement: MIPLIB 2017 tags 212 collection instances as 'open' (no proven optimal solution); the tag page lists each instance's best known objective (marked *), or 'NA' for the 6 open instances with no known feasible solution (datt256, nucorsav, neos-3603137-hoteo, neos-3355323-arnon, supportcase30, fhnw-binpack4-58). Instance pages record every improved solution with submitter and date; improvements still arrive from individuals using local search and ML-guided heuristics (ex1010-pi: 236 Rothberg 2020 -> 234 Hattori Jan 2023 -> 233 Davletshin Oct 2023). The .solu file was last revised Sep 24 2026 (v37). Find a feasible solution with a strictly better objective (in the instance's OBJSENSE) than the listed best known objective for any open instance.
targets.success_criterion: A .sol file (MIPLIB format: 'varname value' lines in the original variable space of the posted .mps.gz) for one instance whose Status column is 'open' on https://miplib.zib.de/tag_open.html (one HTML <tr> per instance: Instance, Status, ..., Objective, Tags), that the MIPLIB solution checker (the checker/ directory of https://miplib.zib.de/downloads/miplib2017-testscript-v1.0.4.zip, built locally against GMP and zlib; usage 'solchecker model.mps.gz sol.sol 1e-6 1e-6') reports as feasible for the current https://miplib.zib.de/WebData/instances/<name>.mps.gz with 'Check SOL: Integrality 1 Constraints 1' at linear and integrality tolerance 1e-6, and whose objective, recomputed by the checker from the MPS objective row (including any objective offset/RHS and the OBJSENSE section; min unless the MPS says MAX), is strictly better than the objective shown for that instance on the open tag page AND on https://miplib.zib.de/instance_details_<name>.html, both re-fetched live immediately before claiming; the improvement must exceed 1e-6 * max(1, |objective|). The checker must first reproduce the posted best solution's objective for that instance (e.g. tokyometro solution 4 -> 8263.1, verified by the vetter 2026-10-08). The .sol file, checker build, instance sha256 and page snapshots are saved together. Nothing is submitted to MIPLIB; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: A checker-validated feasible solution (tolerance 1e-6) for an open instance whose Objective cell reads 'NA' on the tag page and which is '=unkn=' in the current .solu file at claim time (live 2026-10-08: datt256, nucorsav, neos-3603137-hoteo, neos-3355323-arnon, supportcase30, fhnw-binpack4-58); non-trivial because these defeated the solvers used to build MIPLIB.

A checker-validated feasible solution for an open instance whose objective ties the listed best known objective within 1e-6 * max(1,|obj|) and whose integer-variable assignment differs from every solution posted on that instance's page in at least 1% of the integer variables (checked mechanically from the downloaded .sol.gz files); an alternative optimum-candidate, independently checkable.

Prove optimality of an open instance (dual bound equal to the best known objective within 1e-6) with an open-source solver run that the skeptic can repeat in under 1 hour on this Mac from the saved model and parameters, or a certificate (VIPR / exact SCIP) that checks mechanically.

targets.verification_method: Unzip https://miplib.zib.de/downloads/miplib2017-testscript-v1.0.4.zip, 'make' in checker/ (on macOS: make CXXFLAGS="-O2 -I/opt/homebrew/include" LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/lib" with Homebrew gmp; builds in seconds, verified 2026-10-08). Download https://miplib.zib.de/WebData/instances/<name>.mps.gz and the current best solution https://miplib.zib.de/downloads/solutions/<name>/<k>/<name>.sol.gz linked from the instance page; run 'solchecker <name>.mps.gz <posted>.sol 1e-6 1e-6' and confirm it reproduces the listed objective, then run it on the claimed .sol. Minutes. Objective must be taken from the checker's recomputation, not from the file's '=obj=' comment. Re-fetch tag_open.html and the instance page with plain curl and parse the Status and Objective cells.
angles: Pick open instances with modest size and a combinatorial structure that has a strong dedicated local search: set covering / set partitioning (ex1010-pi 25k binaries, improved three times by 3-flip local search), binpacking, scheduling; run the specialised heuristic for hours seeded from the posted best solution.

Solution-polishing: fix most integer variables at the posted BKS, free a neighbourhood (random, constraint-based or objective-guided), solve the sub-MIP with HiGHS/SCIP/CP-SAT to optimality, iterate (RINS/LNS style) with 10 parallel workers.
Instances whose latest improvement is by an individual in 2023 or later signal slack; instances with integer objectives and small coefficient ranges are safest against tolerance games.

For the 'NA' instances, try feasibility-first approaches: CP-SAT on the pure-integer ones, feasibility pump with many restarts, and problem-specific constructive heuristics after reading the instance's description page.
pitfalls: Tolerance games: a 'better' objective obtained by exploiting feasibility slack (fractional integer variables within tolerance, constraint violations near tolerance) is not a win; require 1e-6 and an improvement well above tolerance; prefer instances with integer objectives.

OBJSENSE and offset: some MPS files declare MAX or carry an objective constant; reading 'min' by default or ignoring the RHS of the objective row flips or shifts the comparison. Use the checker's recomputed objective.

Status drift: the 'open' tag is updated as instances are solved; re-fetch both the tag page and the instance page at claim time. An 'improvement' on an instance that has become closed indicates a checker bug.
Instance file version: use the .mps.gz currently linked from the instance page, not a cached copy from another library with the same name.

Presolved variants: the solution must be in the original variable space of the posted .mps.gz; the checker reports 'unexpected variable' for anything else (two harmless '#' comment lines appear in CPLEX-written .sol files).
https://miplib.zib.de/downloads/solchecker.zip does not exist (it returns the HTML home page); the checker lives inside the testscript archive.

targets.name: PSPLIB J120 (single-mode RCPSP): lower a best known heuristic makespan on an unproven instance
targets.statement: PSPLIB (TU Munich) maintains best known heuristic upper bounds (HRS file) and proven lower bounds for the single-mode RCPSP sets. Live on 2026-10-08 the J120 merged JSON reports 600 instances, 89 proven optimal and 511 unproven; only 184 of the 600 carry a lower bound (95 unproven instances have LB < UB listed, 12 of them with UB - LB = 1), the other 416 have no LB at all. The HRS data carries per-instance author and date: 27 J120 bounds were lowered in 2024 by M. Vanhoucke and J. Coelho (18 on 2024-09-23), 17 in May-Aug 2026 by E. Goncharov (e.g. j12011_4 -> 194, j12016_9 -> 203, j12031_1 -> 196), and solution upload was re-enabled on 2026-05-06, so the table is live. Heuristic schedules are not published (only makespans), so ties cannot be copied. Find a precedence- and resource-feasible schedule with makespan strictly below the listed upper_bound for any instance with is_proven_optimal = false.
targets.success_criterion: A start-time vector (one integer start time per activity 1..n+2, dummies included) for one J120 instance whose entry in https://www.om-db.wi.tum.de/psplib/download_merged.php?set=j120&mode=sm has is_proven_optimal = false, such that a standalone checker written from the PSPLIB .sm format definition (PRECEDENCE RELATIONS successors, REQUESTS/DURATIONS durations and per-resource demands, RESOURCEAVAILABILITIES for the 4 renewable resources R1-R4) verifies every finish-to-start precedence (start_succ >= start_pred + dur_pred, zero lags), verifies for every integer period [t, t+1) over the whole horizon and for every resource that the summed demand of activities active in that period (start <= t < start + duration) does not exceed capacity, and reports the finish time of the sink (activity n+2) strictly less than the upper_bound for that (parameter, instance) in the merged JSON AND the Makespan in https://www.om-db.wi.tum.de/psplib/download_solution.php?set=j120&mode=sm&type=hrs, both re-fetched live immediately before claiming. The instance file must be the one from https://www.om-db.wi.tum.de/psplib/download_dataset.php?set=j120&mode=sm&format=zip (j120<param>_<inst>.sm; sha256 recorded). The checker must first (a) accept a serial-SGS schedule it generates itself and (b) reject a deliberately broken schedule (one precedence violated, one resource overload). The schedule, checker, instance sha256 and both fetched tables are saved together. Nothing is uploaded to PSPLIB; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: Same criterion on any J60 or J90 instance with is_proven_optimal = false in https://www.om-db.wi.tum.de/psplib/download_merged.php?set=j60&mode=sm or set=j90 (live: 98 and 105 unproven); counted as partial because these sets are smaller and more heavily searched.

Close an unproven J120 instance whose JSON entry has upper_bound - lower_bound = 1 (12 such instances live) by a reproducible CP-SAT / OR-Tools proof that makespan = upper_bound - 1 is infeasible, with saved model, parameters and seed, repeatable by the skeptic in under 1 hour on this Mac; counts only after the verifier re-runs it.

Checker-validated schedules attaining the current upper_bound on at least 10 distinct J120 instances whose upper_bound_date is in 2024 or later (45 such instances live: 27 Vanhoucke-Coelho 2024, 1 Goncharov 2024, 17 Goncharov 2026); non-trivial because PSPLIB publishes only makespans for heuristic bounds, so these schedules cannot be downloaded.

targets.verification_method: Instance archive: https://www.om-db.wi.tum.de/psplib/download_dataset.php?set=j120&mode=sm&format=zip (600 .sm files). Bounds: download_merged.php?set=j120&mode=sm (JSON with keys instance_set, meta, summary, solutions[]) and the HRS/LB text files from download_solution.php?set=j120&mode=sm&type=hrs|lb. Python checker builds the resource-usage profile from the start times and compares against capacities period by period for all four resources, checks all precedences, and reports the sink finish time. Seconds. Re-fetch the JSON and HRS file with plain curl.
angles: CP-SAT with interval variables and cumulative constraints, 10 workers, hours per instance, hinted by a good GA/SGS schedule; lazy-clause-generation CP produced most J120 UB improvements of the 2010s and 17 UBs still moved in 2026, so a long CP-SAT run on the never-improved-since-1998 instances is a real shot.

Hybrid GA / iterated forward-backward improvement with activity-list representation and massive restarts (the Vanhoucke-Coelho 2024 method family); target instances whose UB is from 1997-1998 (231 of 600) with high network complexity and tight resources (parameter sets 6-10, 16-20, 26-30 etc., where RS is small).
LNS over the critical path: fix all activities outside a time window, re-solve the window exactly with CP-SAT, slide the window.
Use the 12 gap-1 instances for the closing partial win: CP-SAT with energetic reasoning and precedence-based symmetry breaking at makespan = UB-1.
pitfalls: Makespan definition: finish time of the sink (dummy activity n+2) with dummies of zero duration; off-by-one from counting periods [t, t+1) incorrectly produces false 1-unit 'improvements'.
Resource check must be per period over the whole horizon for all 4 renewable resources, not a per-activity or average check; precedence is finish-to-start with no lags in the single-mode .sm format.
Only instances with is_proven_optimal = false count; 416 instances have no lower_bound key at all, so do not filter on LB < UB. Beating a proven-optimal UB is impossible and signals a checker bug.
Use PSPLIB's own j120 .sm files (download_dataset.php), not regenerated ProGen instances with the same names from other sites; parameters differ.

Re-fetch the merged JSON and HRS file immediately before claiming; uploads were re-enabled in May 2026 and 17 bounds landed in May-Aug 2026 without a news post. upper_bound_date formats differ ('Mon Sep 23 11:12:00 2024' vs '[2026-05-17 13:37:56]'); do not rely on date parsing.

targets.name: SINTEF Li & Lim PDPTW benchmark: hierarchically beat a best-known solution on a 600/800/1000-task instance
targets.statement: SINTEF's Transportation Optimization Portal maintains the best known solutions for the Li & Lim pickup-and-delivery-with-time-windows benchmark with a hierarchical objective: minimize vehicles, then total distance (double precision, reported to 2 decimals); detailed solution files checked by SINTEF's own checker are linked for every entry. Live on 2026-10-08 the 600/800/1000-task tables (58 real instances per size at 1000: lrc2_10_8 and lrc2_10_9 were never defined by Li & Lim and have no instance file) are dominated by entries from 2019-2021 (SCR, HW, SB) and Jan 2024 (NVIDIA), i.e. far fewer contributors than VRPTW, and none of the entries carries an optimality mark except a few 2003 '*' rows. Find a feasible solution that is hierarchically better (fewer vehicles, or equal vehicles and strictly smaller distance) than the listed BKS for any 600, 800 or 1000-task instance.
targets.success_criterion: A solution file in SINTEF's posted format ('Route k : id id ...' lines, task ids as in the instance file, depot = 0) for one Li & Lim instance with 600, 800 or 1000 tasks, such that a standalone checker written from the instance format (first line 'vehicles capacity speed'; then one line per node: id x y demand ready due service pickup-partner delivery-partner, with the depot as node 0) that (a) verifies every task served exactly once, (b) verifies each pickup and its delivery are in the same route with the pickup first, (c) verifies the running load never exceeds capacity and never goes negative along each route, (d) verifies time windows with double-precision Euclidean travel times, arrival = max(departure_prev + d, ready) <= due at every task and return to the depot by its due time, service time added after arrival, and (e) computes total distance in double precision, reports either strictly fewer vehicles (routes) than the table entry, or the same number of vehicles and a distance that is strictly smaller than the listed value by at least 0.01 after rounding to 2 decimals, where the table entry is the one on https://www.sintef.no/projectweb/top/pdptw/li-lim-benchmark/<600|800|1000>-customers/ re-fetched live immediately before claiming. The checker must first reproduce the posted BKS solution file's vehicle count and distance for that instance (e.g. lc1_10_2 file -> 94 / 44548.51, verified by the vetter 2026-10-08). The solution file, checker, instance file (sha256 from the SINTEF zip) and page snapshot are saved together. Nothing is submitted to SINTEF; the write-up goes to the human.

partial_wins.statement: Hierarchical improvement, by the identical checker and re-fetch rule, on any 400-task instance at https://www.sintef.no/projectweb/top/pdptw/li-lim-benchmark/400-customers/ (instances from pdp_400.zip); counted as partial because the smaller instances have been searched more exhaustively.

Hierarchical improvement, by the identical checker and re-fetch rule, on any 200-task instance at https://www.sintef.no/projectweb/top/pdptw/li-lim-benchmark/200-customers/ that is not marked optimal ('*') in its row (instances from pdp_200.zip).

A checker-validated solution for a 1000-task instance with the BKS vehicle count and a distance within 0.01 of the listed value whose undirected edge set differs from the posted BKS solution file in at least 10% of edges (edge-set comparison by the same checker); an alternative optimum-candidate, independently checkable from the two files.

targets.verification_method: Instances: https://www.sintef.no/contentassets/1338af68996841d3922bc8e87adc430c/pdptw1000.zip (58 files, LC1_10_1.txt ...), pdptw800.zip, pdp_600.zip, pdp_400.zip, pdp_200.zip, all linked from https://www.sintef.no/projectweb/top/pdptw/li-lim-benchmark/ (pdp_1000.zip is the same 58 instances). Posted BKS solution files are linked from each table row (e.g. https://www.sintef.no/contentassets/4787adf42512493986a16420bb6d1ca9/lc1_10_2.94_44548.51.txt). The skeptic runs the Python checker on the posted file (must reproduce vehicles and distance to 2 decimals and report zero violations), then on the claimed file. Minutes. Re-fetch the size page with plain curl and parse the instance's <tr>.
angles: Adaptive large neighbourhood search with pair-aware removal/insertion (Ropke-Pisinger style) plus route-minimisation (ejection chains / squeeze), seeded from the posted BKS and run for hours with many seeds on 10 cores; most 2019-2021 entries came from exactly such methods with more wall time.

Equal-vehicle distance polishing: fix the route set, optimise 2-3 neighbouring routes exactly with a CP-SAT model with precedence and time windows; any strict improvement is a strict global improvement.

Target instances whose entry is oldest (2019 SB / 2019 SCR rows) or with high vehicle counts relative to a capacity-based lower bound (sum of demands / capacity), where vehicle reduction may be possible.
Reuse VRPTW machinery: a PDPTW solution with pickup-before-delivery is a VRPTW solution with extra precedence constraints, so HGS-style crossover with repair is applicable.
pitfalls: Hierarchical objective: a shorter-distance solution using one more vehicle is worse, not better; and a solution with fewer vehicles must still be feasible.
Precedence and pairing: pickup and delivery must be in the same route with pickup first; load must be checked along the route (it rises and falls), not as a route total.
Rounding: the table shows 2 decimals; a difference below 0.01 is not a win; reproduce the posted BKS file's value first.

Instance size: Li & Lim '1000-task' instances have slightly more than the nominal number of tasks (e.g. LC1_10_2 has 1046); use the file's actual task list and the depot's time window / capacity from the file.
lrc2_10_8 and lrc2_10_9 do not exist (no instance file; SINTEF says Li & Lim never supplied them). A 'first solution' for them is impossible and must never be counted.
Dates in the table are free-form ('19-Dec-21', '19-Des-21', '2001'); do not parse dates to decide openness, use only the vehicles/distance cells.

targets.name: Lennard-Jones clusters: lower a putative global minimum in the Cambridge Cluster Database / Doye tables (N = 3..150, 310..1000)
targets.statement: The Cambridge Cluster Database (mirrored on Doye's site) lists putative global minima of LJ_N (energy in units of the pair well depth, 6 decimals) with point files: N = 3..150 (tables.150.html, LJ.tar), N = 310..561 (LJ310-561.html, incorporating Barron 537-548, Takeuchi 506/521/537-541, Huang-Lai-Xu 326/533/536) and N = 562..1000 (LJ562-1000.html, Xiang-Cheng-Cai-Shao 2004 plus 580 by Huang-Lai-Xu). The N = 151..309 and 1001..1610 tables were hosted at Shao's Nankai site, which no longer resolves (2026-10-08). Pages last modified 2025-03-04 (server move); the CCD invites improvements by email. Decades of global-optimization benchmarking make N <= 150 near-certainly optimal, but N = 310..1000 were set by one 2004 lattice-construction method and only a handful of N have been revisited (DLS-TPIO improved 533, 536; Barron 537-548, 664, 813). Moonshot-ish within a harvest frame: realistic targets are N in 310..1000.
targets.success_criterion: Success means Cartesian coordinates (>= 16 digits) for N atoms, N listed on one of the three live Doye/CCD LJ table pages, such that E* = sum_{i<j} 4(r^-12 - r^-6) computed in mpmath at 30 digits is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the table energy for N re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-5 (the tables carry 6 decimals; genuine new minima differ by >= 1e-3 historically), AND the configuration is a certified local minimum (mpmath or quad-precision Newton to gradient norm < 1e-15, Hessian positive semidefinite with exactly 6 zero modes), AND polishing the table's own point file for N with the same routine gives E_table_polished - E* >= 1e-5 (distinct basin), AND an arXiv/Google Scholar check finds no published lower value for that N (Barron's page https://academicos.azc.uam.mx/cbr/LennardJones/nw537-548.htm and the 2013 DLS-TPIO paper are known sources already folded into the table).

partial_wins.statement: A certified lower energy (same local-minimum and distinct-basin rules) for some N in 151..309 or 1001..1100 than a SPECIFIC published value that the skeptic can fetch (DOI or arXiv id plus page/table reference, the value quoted to the paper's precision); the CCD has no live table for these N (the Shao/Nankai host chinfo.nankai.edu.cn does not resolve, checked 2026-10-08), so this is reported as 'literature frontier', not a table record, and a claim without a fetchable published comparator is not a win.

A certified improvement to an (N, rho) row that exists on the live CCD Morse-cluster table (https://doye.chem.ox.ac.uk/jon/structures/Morse/tables.html), same local-minimum and distinct-basin rules with margin 1e-5, reported together with the best literature value found for that (N, rho) (the CCD Morse table is known to lag the literature).

Reproduction audit: re-polish every table point file for N = 310..1000 in double precision and report any N where the posted coordinates relax to an energy lower than the posted value by > 1e-5 (under-converged table row) or do not match the posted value within 1e-5.

targets.verification_method: Checker (< 15 minutes for N <= 1000): curl the live table page and parse the energy for N (multi-column HTML; pairs 'N energy'); load the claimed coordinates; mpmath mp.dps = 30 (or numpy float128 then mpmath for the final sum) compute E* with E = 4 sum (r^-12 - r^-6); Newton/BFGS polish in high precision and confirm E* stable to 1e-12 and gradient < 1e-15; eigen-decompose the 3N x 3N Hessian in double and assert exactly 6 zero modes and no negative eigenvalues; download the table point file (LJ310-561/<N>.TXT, LJ562-1000/<N>.TXT, or LJ.tar for N <= 150; all checked live 2026-10-08), polish it identically, assert its energy exceeds E* by >= 1e-5. For N = 664 and 813 also assert E* < Barron's -4596.1978 / -5712.2517 by >= 1e-5.
angles: N = 562..1000 came from a single 2004 lattice-construction + GA pipeline (Xiang et al.) and only N = 580, 664, 813 have since been improved; run dynamic lattice searching (DLS) with two-phase local search plus surface-interior operations from the posted structures, focusing on N just below Mackay/anti-Mackay shell completions (e.g. 561, 923) where decahedral or fcc competitors win (as at 38, 75-77, 98, 102-104).

Structural-competition scan: for each N in 310..1000 build the best icosahedral, decahedral (Marks), fcc truncated-octahedral, and Leary-tetrahedral candidates by filling/removing surface sites greedily, relax, and compare; the 2004 table only explored lattice-based icosahedral/decahedral families.
Polish-and-audit first (p3): relaxing all posted point files in double precision is cheap and may reveal under-converged rows (the CCD Thomson tables had such rows); then target those N.

Known table-vs-literature gap (checked 2026-10-08): Barron's 2010 page claims LJ664 = -4596.1978 and LJ813 = -5712.2517, while the live Doye 562-1000 table still shows -4596.197078 and -5712.249964. Reproducing Barron there is NOT novel; the bar for N = 664 and 813 is Barron's value. Use the same trick (icosahedral 'IC no center' and 'ID' variants of the posted structure) on neighbouring N where nobody has looked.
pitfalls: Literature beats the table for N = 664 and 813 (Barron 2010, not folded into the live Doye table). A 'record' at those N that does not also beat Barron's values fails NOVELTY; always compare against the published value, not just the table.

Units: energies are in pair well-depth units with sigma = 1 (E = 4 sum (r^-12 - r^-6)); a different reduced form (e.g. epsilon=1 with minimum at r=1, E = sum (r^-12 - 2 r^-6)) gives different numbers for the same structure.
Any 'improvement' under 1e-5 is numerical; historically new LJ minima differ by 1e-3 or more.
A polished posted structure giving a lower number than the posted value is an under-converged row, not a new minimum (distinct-basin test is mandatory).
The 151..309 and 1001+ tables are offline (Shao's site); claims there cannot be table records.
Emailing the CCD maintainers is an outbound message needing explicit permission from the human.

targets.name: Packomania: equal circles in a circle (cci), beat a per-N record radius
targets.statement: Packomania's 'circles in a circle' table (cci) lists the best known radius r(N) of N equal circles packed in the unit circle for every N = 1..2600 plus selected larger N up to 5000 (2735 rows). Only N <= 13 and N = 19 are proven; everything else is a putative record. Last table update 25-Dec-2024 (Basurto/Gurin/Odriozola/Specht); earlier waves by Lai-Hao et al. (2023-2024) and Zhou-He-Zheng-Li (2023). The cci category does NOT appear in Packomania's pending-requests list of 2026-10-08, so the live table is the actual frontier for this container. Per-N values are machine-readable (txt/radius.txt, 30 decimals) and per-N coordinates are at cci/txt/cci<N>.txt (30 decimals).
targets.success_criterion: Success means a file of N centers (x_i, y_i) for one N listed in https://packomania.com/cci/txt/radius.txt such that the FEASIBLE radius r* := min( min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, 1 - max_i |c_i| ), computed in mpmath at 50 digits directly from the submitted coordinates (no tolerance), is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the 30-decimal radius for that N re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-11, AND the configuration is not isometric to the posted cci<N>.txt one (sorted distance multisets differ), AND N does not appear in a History-of-updates line on the live cci.html newer than the one the scout fetched. QUEUE RULE (Packomania, checked 2026-10-08): the N must NOT lie inside any range listed for this category on https://packomania.com/pending-requests.html re-fetched at verification time; a value that is already in Packomania's queue does not count as ours. The 26-Sep-2026 'Moki & Julio *many* 4666 candidates' bundle is category-unspecified and cannot be resolved; the verdict must state this caveat and the N must be re-checked against the live table once that bundle disappears from the pending list. Packomania coordinate files are CENTERED (container centre at the origin: circle/sphere radius 1, square side 1 in [-1/2,1/2]^2, cube edge 1 in [-1/2,1/2]^3). No submission (email) is ever made; the claim is for the verified construction only.

partial_wins.statement: A configuration for some N in 1..2600 whose feasible radius r* equals the live table value to within 1e-11 but is certified non-isometric to the posted cci<N>.txt (different sorted distance multiset AND different contact graph, mpmath at 50 digits): a second optimum; not a record.
A certified improvement for one of the gap values N > 2600 that the table lists (e.g. N = 4495, 5000), where the record is a lattice-like seed by Specht rather than an optimized packing.

A certified improvement in the sibling regular-hexagon table chx (N <= 1261, 12-decimal https://packomania.com/chx/txt/radius.txt, so margin 1e-10) using the same mpmath feasible-radius rule, for an N not covered by any chx entry on the live pending-requests page (on 2026-10-08 chx N = 55 and 89 are queued).

targets.verification_method: Independent checker (< 2 minutes): (1) curl the live https://packomania.com/cci/txt/radius.txt and parse row N. (2) Load the claimed centers; mpmath mp.dps=50; r* = min(min pair distance / 2, 1 - max |c_i|). (3) Assert r* - r_table >= 1e-11. (4) Download cci/txt/cci<N>.txt, recompute its r (must reproduce the table to 1e-20; parser sanity) and compare sorted distance multisets. (5) Re-fetch cci<N>.html, the cci.html History of updates and pending-requests.html; apply the queue rule. (6) Compare the contact graph against txt/contacts.txt.
angles: Target N in 1000..2600: 2121 of 2735 rows are Specht's own (txt/author.txt), and the 2023-2024 Lai-Hao / Zhou-He / Basurto waves stopped near N = 1000, so the large-N rows have had far less competition. Use the N=1000..2600 coordinates as seeds and run perturb-and-repack (remove k circles, re-insert at largest holes, then re-jam).

Hexagonal-core templates: take the chx (hexagon) hex-number packings, cut a circular window and relax the boundary layer; Cantrell's bound rows ('now meet Cantrell's bound') show where the frontier is already tight, so skip those N.

Monotonic basin-hopping on a smooth penalty (sum of squared overlaps + squared protrusion) with L-BFGS, then an exact jamming step: solve the KKT system of the active contact set with mpmath to polish r to 30+ digits before comparing.
Rattler exploitation: rows with many 'loose' circles (txt/loose.txt) have slack; move rattlers to open up a boundary contact and re-inflate.
pitfalls: Direction and normalization: cci fixes the container radius at 1 and maximizes r; some literature reports the container radius for unit circles (ratio = 1/r). Compare r to r, never ratio to r.
Double-precision 'records' of +1e-13 are noise. The 1e-11 margin on the mpmath feasible radius is mandatory; a configuration with tiny overlaps that 'rounds' to a record is a false positive.

Stale-table trap: Packomania has a queue of over 5,000 pending candidates (2026-10-08). cci is not in the queue today, but re-check pending-requests.html and the per-N page immediately before claiming.
Known-literature trap: an improvement may already be published (Lai-Hao 2024, Basurto 2024) but not yet uploaded; search arXiv for the N before claiming.
Submitting to Packomania is by email (an outbound message on the human's behalf) and is asked not to happen in October 2026; claim the verified construction, not a submission.

targets.name: Packomania: equal circles in a square (csq), beat a per-N record radius
targets.statement: Packomania's 'circles in a square' table (csq) lists the best known radius r(N) of N equal circles in the unit square for N = 1..1000 and selected N up to 10000 (3150 rows, 12-decimal radius.txt, per-N coordinates at csq/txt/csq<N>.txt). Proven optimal only for N <= 30 and a few special N (36 etc.). Last update 10-Sep-2026 (two candidates N = 3000 and 9996 by ZeroThesis); the big 2022 wave by Lai-Hao-Xiao-Glover improved ~250 values of N in 106..400. IMPORTANT: the pending-requests page (2026-10-08) lists 557 csq candidates in 401..1000 and 250 in 1015..9996 (Zeeshan Tariq, Sept 2026) that are not yet processed, so the live table for N > 400 is probably about to move.
targets.success_criterion: Success means N centers for one N listed in https://packomania.com/csq/txt/radius.txt such that the FEASIBLE radius r* := min( min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, 1/2 - max_i max(|x_i|,|y_i|) ) for the centered unit square [-1/2,1/2]^2, computed in mpmath at 50 digits with no tolerance, is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the live 12-decimal txt/radius.txt value for that N re-fetched immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-10, AND the configuration is not isometric to the posted csq<N>.txt one (sorted distance multisets differ), AND N is outside every csq range on the live pending-requests page (on 2026-10-08: 401..1000 and 1015..9996 are queued, so only N <= 400 and N = 1001..1014 can be claimed until the queue is processed; queued N is partial win p1). QUEUE RULE (Packomania, checked 2026-10-08): the N must NOT lie inside any range listed for this category on https://packomania.com/pending-requests.html re-fetched at verification time; a value that is already in Packomania's queue does not count as ours. The 26-Sep-2026 'Moki & Julio *many* 4666 candidates' bundle is category-unspecified and cannot be resolved; the verdict must state this caveat and the N must be re-checked against the live table once that bundle disappears from the pending list. Packomania coordinate files are CENTERED (container centre at the origin: circle/sphere radius 1, square side 1 in [-1/2,1/2]^2, cube edge 1 in [-1/2,1/2]^3). No submission (email) is ever made; the claim is for the verified construction only.

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement (same mpmath rule, margin 1e-10) for an N inside a csq pending-queue range: real but not novelty-safe; record the value and re-check against the live table when Packomania processes the queue.

A certified improvement to a sibling 2D equal-circle Packomania table that exists live (csc semicircle, crt triangle, ccq circles-in-circle-quarter) for an N OUTSIDE every pending-queue range for that category (on 2026-10-08 csc 41..250, crt 54..299, ccq 57..600 are queued), same mpmath rule against that table's live txt/radius.txt with margin 1e-10 for 12-decimal files and 1e-11 for 30-decimal files.
A second distinct optimal configuration for a proven-optimal N (N <= 30), i.e. equal r* to 1e-11 but non-isometric to the posted coordinates, verified by contact-graph non-isomorphism.

targets.verification_method: Checker (< 2 minutes): curl https://packomania.com/csq/txt/radius.txt live (tab-separated N, r), parse row N; load claimed centers; mpmath mp.dps=50; r* = min(half the minimum pairwise distance, 1/2 - max_i max(|x_i|,|y_i|)); assert r* - r_table >= 1e-10. Download csq/txt/csq<N>.txt, recompute its r (parser sanity) and compare sorted distance multisets. Re-fetch csq<N>.html, the csq.html History of updates and pending-requests.html; apply the queue rule. Report r* to 20 digits.
angles: Work in 106..400 where the 2022 Lai-Hao wave set most rows: their algorithm was a single method; try a different family (event-driven Lubachevsky-Stillinger compression from random starts, then KKT polishing) and look for N where the table's contact count is low relative to 2N+1.

Exploit density dips: txt/records.txt lists the density-record N (e.g. 188, 194, ...); the N just after a density-record often sits in a bad basin (e.g. a record packing minus circles, with freed rattlers). Attack N = record+1..record+3 with rattler-driven re-packing.
Shifted-lattice families: for N near k^2 or k(k+1) try square/hexagonal hybrids with one or two skew rows, then optimize the skew angle continuously.
Use the per-N coordinate files as seeds and run large-neighbourhood search: remove 5-10% of circles, re-insert at the largest empty circles (Voronoi vertices), re-jam, accept if r improves.
pitfalls: Queue-stale table: 807 csq candidates are pending (N > 400). A 'record' for N in those ranges may already be in Specht's inbox; the criterion forces N <= 400 or an explicit queue check.

12-decimal table: an apparent improvement in the 12th decimal can be the table's own rounding (Packomania truncates to 12 decimals on csq); require the 1e-11 margin against the exact posted value and prefer re-deriving the table radius from the posted coordinates (csq<N>.txt) in mpmath.
Coordinate convention: Packomania files are centered at the origin with side length 1 (coordinates in [-0.5, 0.5]); do not test containment against [0, 1] without shifting.
Submission is by email and asked to pause in October 2026; do not count a submission as a claim.

targets.name: Packomania: equal 4D/5D/6D hyperspheres in a hypersphere (hsp4, hsp5, hsp6), beat a per-N record radius
targets.statement: Packomania Section 4 lists the best known radius r(N) of N equal d-dimensional balls packed in the unit d-ball for d = 4 (N = 2..300), d = 5 (N = 2..300) and d = 6 (N = 2..259), with 12-decimal txt/radius.txt files and per-N coordinates inside txt/hsp<d>_coords.tar.gz (files hsp<d>-<N>.txt: first line radius, then N rows of d coordinates, 12 decimals). Last updates: hsp4 06-Jul-2025, hsp5 01-Aug-2025, hsp6 31-Jul-2025. Author files show these tables were built almost single-handedly by Specht (hsp4: 247/299 rows Specht, 30 Sloane-Hardin-Smith, 11 Mackay; hsp5: 263/299 Specht; hsp6: 258/258 Specht). None of hsp4/5/6 appears in the pending-requests list (2026-10-08), and no competing group has touched them, so these are the least-contested per-N packing tables on Packomania.
targets.success_criterion: Success means N centers in R^d (d in {4,5,6}) for one N listed in the live https://packomania.com/hsp<d>/txt/radius.txt such that the FEASIBLE radius r* := min( min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, 1 - max_i |c_i| ) (unit container ball centred at the origin), computed in mpmath at 50 digits directly from the submitted coordinates with no tolerance, is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than that file's 12-decimal value for N re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-10 (the table carries 12 decimals; 1e-10 is 200x its rounding), AND the configuration is not isometric to the posted hsp<d>-<N>.txt configuration (sorted pairwise-distance multisets differ by more than 1e-8 somewhere), AND (d, N) does not appear in a History-of-updates entry on the live hsp<d>.html newer than the one the scout fetched. QUEUE RULE (Packomania, checked 2026-10-08): the N must NOT lie inside any range listed for this category on https://packomania.com/pending-requests.html re-fetched at verification time; a value that is already in Packomania's queue does not count as ours. The 26-Sep-2026 'Moki & Julio *many* 4666 candidates' bundle is category-unspecified and cannot be resolved; the verdict must state this caveat and the N must be re-checked against the live table once that bundle disappears from the pending list. No submission (email) is ever made; the claim is for the verified construction only.

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement for a row attributed to 'unknown' or 'A. L. Mackay' in txt/author.txt (hsp4), i.e. a row seeded from classical constructions rather than optimized.

An extension row: a certified packing for N = 301..310 (d = 4 or 5) or N = 260..270 (d = 6) that beats the obvious baseline of (best r(N-1) packing plus one ball at the largest cavity, re-jammed), reported with r* to 20 digits; not a record, but new data for an N the table does not list.

A certified contact-graph audit: for every listed N, re-derive r from the coordinates in the tarball and report any N where the posted coordinates do not achieve the posted 12-decimal radius (data-integrity finding).

targets.verification_method: Checker (< 2 minutes): curl the live hsp<d>/txt/radius.txt and parse row N; load the claimed centers; mpmath mp.dps=50; r* = min(half the minimum pairwise distance, 1 - maximum norm); assert r* - r_table >= 1e-10. Download txt/hsp<d>_coords.tar.gz (all three exist, checked 2026-10-08) and read hsp<d>-<N>.txt; recompute its r the same way (parser sanity: must reproduce the table to 1e-11) and compare sorted distance multisets to rule out an isometric copy. Re-fetch hsp<d>.html (History of updates) and pending-requests.html and apply the queue rule. Report r* to 20 digits.
angles: Single-author tables are the softest: run a completely different optimizer than Specht's (event-driven LS compression in d dimensions from random starts, 10 cores x hundreds of restarts per N) over all N = 50..300; expect many small gains in 12-digit tables.

Lattice shells: in 4D the D4 lattice (24-cell kissing) and in 6D the E6 lattice give dense shell structures; take shells around a center, cut to N, and relax; compare with txt/records.txt (density-record N) to find N where the table is NOT already a lattice shell.

Kissing-configuration seeds: a central ball with a 24-ball (4D) or 40-ball (5D) or 72-ball (6D) shell plus a partial second shell is a natural template for N near 25, 41, 73 and N near the second-shell completions; the table's density-record lists hint at which are already found.

Large-neighbourhood search on the posted coordinates: delete the 5 balls with the largest free volume (compute via random probing), re-insert at the deepest holes, re-jam; polish the active-contact KKT system with mpmath.
pitfalls: 12-decimal table: compare against the exact posted value with a 1e-11 margin; an improvement of 3e-12 is indistinguishable from the table's own rounding.
Container convention: unit container ball (radius 1, centered at origin); the 'ratio' column is 1/r, not the objective.
A new packing isometric to the posted one (rotated/reflected) with the same r is not a record; the checker compares distance multisets.
Email submission needs explicit permission from the human and Packomania asks for no submissions in October 2026; claim the verified configuration only.
Tables are 12-decimal: polishing the posted coordinates to high precision can gain up to ~1e-12 from rounding alone; that is why the margin is 1e-10 and the non-isometry test is mandatory.

targets.name: Packomania: equal spheres in a cube (scu), beat a per-N record radius
targets.statement: Packomania's 'spheres in a cube' table (scu) lists the best known radius r(N) of N equal spheres in the unit cube, complete for N = 1..1000 plus lattice rows up to N = 1024192 (1134 rows; txt/radius.txt at 30 decimals; per-N coordinates scu/txt/scu<N>.txt). Proven only for N <= 10 and a few more. The table is being revised right now: 04-Oct-2026 Specht posted 2022 Lai-Hao-Xiao-Glover candidates for ~60 values of N and wrote 'This table needs a revision!'; 05-Oct-2026 Yuan Gao (Harvard) set ~80 records in 202..576; 06-Oct and 08-Oct-2026 Lu Peng set ~185 records across 102..946. Author file: Goldberg (1971) still holds 263 rows, Cantrell 233, Specht 241, meaning hundreds of rows are 1970s-2012 constructions. scu is NOT in the pending-requests list of 2026-10-08 (but a 'many: 4666 candidates' bundle from Moki & Julio of 26-Sep-2026 is unspecified).
targets.success_criterion: Success means N centers in R^3 for one N listed in https://packomania.com/scu/txt/radius.txt such that the FEASIBLE radius r* := min( min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, 1/2 - max_i max(|x_i|,|y_i|,|z_i|) ) for the cube [-1/2, 1/2]^3, computed in mpmath at 50 digits with no tolerance, is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the live txt/radius.txt value (30 decimals) for that N re-fetched immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-11, AND the configuration is not isometric to the posted scu<N>.txt configuration (sorted distance multisets differ), AND N does not appear in a History-of-updates line on the live scu.html newer than the one the scout fetched (the table was rewritten on 04, 05, 06 and 08 Oct 2026 from private communications outside the public queue, so a same-day re-fetch is mandatory). QUEUE RULE (Packomania, checked 2026-10-08): the N must NOT lie inside any range listed for this category on https://packomania.com/pending-requests.html re-fetched at verification time; a value that is already in Packomania's queue does not count as ours. The 26-Sep-2026 'Moki & Julio *many* 4666 candidates' bundle is category-unspecified and cannot be resolved; the verdict must state this caveat and the N must be re-checked against the live table once that bundle disappears from the pending list. Packomania coordinate files are CENTERED (container centre at the origin: circle/sphere radius 1, square side 1 in [-1/2,1/2]^2, cube edge 1 in [-1/2,1/2]^3). No submission (email) is ever made; the claim is for the verified construction only.

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement (same rule) for an N whose live author (txt/author.txt) is 'Michael Goldberg' or 'Hugo Pfoertner' or 'Dave Boll' (pre-2000 hand constructions), i.e. a row nobody has optimized by computer; counted as a record if it passes the criterion, else as a near-miss with r* within 1e-6.

A certified improvement to the sibling 'spheres in a sphere' table (ssp, last update 26-Sep-2024, 1156 rows, 12-decimal txt/radius.txt) using the same mpmath feasible-radius rule against https://packomania.com/ssp/txt/radius.txt (container radius 1), margin 1e-10 because that file has only 12 decimals, same queue rule for category ssp.

Reproduction milestone: re-derive from scu<N>.txt the 30-decimal table radius for all N <= 1000 and report any N where the posted coordinates do NOT achieve the posted radius (a data-integrity finding, which Deeter-style audits have found in other tables).

targets.verification_method: Checker (< 2 minutes): curl https://packomania.com/scu/txt/radius.txt live; load the claimed N centers; mpmath mp.dps=50; r* = min(half minimum pairwise distance, 1/2 - max_i max(|x_i|,|y_i|,|z_i|)); assert r* - r_table >= 1e-11. Download scu/txt/scu<N>.txt, recompute its r (must reproduce the table to 1e-20; parser sanity) and compare sorted distance multisets. Re-fetch scu.html History of updates and pending-requests.html and apply the queue rule. Report r* to 25 digits and the contact graph.
angles: Read txt/author.txt live and attack only rows still attributed to Goldberg/Pfoertner/Boll/Schaer (hundreds of N in 100..1000): these are decades-old constructions and the Oct-2026 waves by Gao and Peng show large gains are still routine there.

Lattice-cut plus relax: cut fcc/hcp/bcc and 'layered square' lattices by the cube at many orientations and offsets, pick the best N-subsets, then inflate with an event-driven (Lubachevsky-Stillinger) compression and polish the active contacts with mpmath Newton.
Peng/Gao ran N = 102..946; try the complementary N they did not touch (check the History of updates lists) and the rows between record clusters.

Monotonic basin-hopping with a smooth overlap penalty; perturbation = remove the 3-5 'loosest' spheres (txt/loose.txt gives rattler counts) and re-insert at the largest cavities found by a Delaunay-based hole search.
Rows N = 385..395 (and other runs) share one identical radius with ref [24]: they are a larger packing with spheres removed, so any genuine optimization of the smaller N beats them.
pitfalls: The table is being rewritten daily (04-08 Oct 2026). A value fetched by the scout at 04:20 can be beaten by Packomania's own update before the verifier runs; re-fetch radius.txt immediately before claiming.
Cube convention: coordinates are centered (edge length 1, [-1/2, 1/2]^3); testing against [0,1]^3 produces false protrusion or false feasibility.
Noise in the 30th decimal is not a record; the 1e-11 margin on the mpmath feasible radius is mandatory.
Unspecified 'many' bundle (4666 candidates, Moki & Julio) might contain scu; a record may be scooped in the queue, so the novelty skeptic must check pending-requests.html and the per-N page.
Email submission requires explicit permission from the human and is asked to pause in October 2026.

targets.name: Spherical codes (Tammes problem and higher dimensions): beat an entry in Cohn's spherical-codes.org table
targets.statement: Henry Cohn's table at spherical-codes.org lists the best known spherical codes (maximize the minimal angle between N unit vectors) for dimensions 3..32 (plus one entry each in 52 and 64) and N up to 1024: 16,446 entries on the HTML index (checked 2026-10-08), each with the cosine of the minimal angle to 12 decimals, a coordinates file /data/<d>/<N> (16-17 digits per coordinate, one point per line), references, a '*' (HTML entity *) after N for proven-optimal cases, and in 11,996 entries the per-row reference text 'needs more optimization' (dims 4..32; none in dim 3), meaning the posted code has not converged. A plain CSV is at /plain (16,356 rows: d,N,cos[,minimal polynomial]; it carries NO star marks and no labels). Dimension 3 is the Tammes problem (/plain lists N = 7..1024; proven only for small N and N = 24). The table is actively maintained (entries dated 'Henry Cohn, 2026', 'Antoine Jay, 2026'; Numaro records cited). Sloane's original tables (neilsloane.com/packings) return HTTP 403 to curl and are superseded. EinsteinArena's Tammes N=50 leaderboard (checked 2026-10-08) tops out at 0.51347176 rad, consistent with the table's cos 0.868173209127 (= 0.5134721 rad); never use that leaderboard as a record source.
targets.success_criterion: Success means N vectors in R^d for a (d, N) row present in the live https://spherical-codes.org/plain, coordinates given to >= 20 digits, such that after normalizing each vector to unit length in mpmath at 50 digits the maximum pairwise inner product c* (cosine of the minimal angle) is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the table's 12-decimal cosine for (d, N) re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-10, AND on the live HTML index https://spherical-codes.org/ the (d, N) row has NO '*' (proven optimal) mark AND does NOT contain the text 'needs more optimization' (improving an entry the table itself flags as unconverged is partial win p2, never a claim), AND the row is not superseded by a newer arXiv result for the same (d, N) (search arXiv for 'spherical code' / 'Tammes' and N), AND the result is not a kissing-number configuration (if 9 <= d <= 23 and c* <= 0.5 the claim belongs to the bank target kissing-number-low-dim and is not counted here). Uploading to /upload-code is an external submission and is never done without explicit permission from the human; the claim is for the verified code.

partial_wins.statement: A certified improvement (same rule, margin 1e-10, no star, no 'needs more optimization' label) in dimension 3 (Tammes problem) for an N listed in /plain; 3D entries carry no 'needs more optimization' label, so this is the hardest sub-case.

A batch of at least 20 certified improvements (margin 1e-10 each) to rows labeled 'needs more optimization' in one dimension d in 4..32, delivered as one file set with the largest improvement reported; these rows are flagged unconverged by the table, so the batch is a partial win, never a claim.

An exact-angle certificate for an unstarred, unlabeled row that has no minimal polynomial listed: a configuration whose minimal-angle cosine is shown (mpmath findpoly/PSLQ at 60 digits, confirmed at 100 digits) to be an algebraic number matching the table value to 1e-12, with the contact structure verified rigid; adds a polynomial the table lacks.

targets.verification_method: Checker (< 5 minutes per entry): curl https://spherical-codes.org/plain and parse the (d,N) row (CSV: d,N,cos). curl https://spherical-codes.org/ and locate the row via its link href="/data/<d>/<N>": assert no '*' follows the link and the row's reference cell does not contain 'needs more optimization'. Load the claimed vectors; mpmath mp.dps=50; normalize; compute all N(N-1)/2 inner products; c* = max. Assert c_table - c* >= 1e-10. Also curl /data/<d>/<N> and compute the posted code's c (must reproduce the table to 1e-11; parser sanity). Report c* to 20 digits and the minimal angle in degrees.
angles: Harvest the 11,995 'needs more optimization' entries: for each (d, N) download /data/<d>/<N>, run a smooth-max (log-sum-exp of inner products with increasing sharpness) L-BFGS descent followed by an active-set SLSQP on the true min-angle objective, then mpmath polish; 10 cores can sweep thousands of entries in hours. Prioritize dims 5..12 where N is moderate and gains are typically 1e-6..1e-3.

Structured codes: for d = 4..8 use orbits of finite reflection groups (W(F4), W(E6), W(E7), W(E8)) and their subgroups; union-of-orbits codes with one continuous parameter per orbit often beat unstructured numerical codes at N near 100..1024.
Lifting/projection: good codes in dimension d+1 projected or sliced to d, and codes in d lifted by adding a small coordinate, give fresh basins; also antipodal doubling (N -> 2N) of a good code in d.

3D Tammes (p1): seed with Hars' N <= 60 point sets and Deeter-style symmetric (D_n, T, O, I subgroup) starts, run 10^5 restarts per N in 60..150, polish active contacts to 30 digits; the 2025 N = 60 gain (6e-9) shows tiny improvements still exist.
pitfalls: Direction: the table lists the COSINE of the minimal angle; smaller cosine = larger angle = better.
Normalization: vectors must be exactly unit length in mpmath before computing inner products.
