Starred (proven optimal) entries cannot be beaten; the star exists ONLY on the HTML index (/plain has none), so the checker must parse the index, not /plain.
'needs more optimization' rows are the table's own admission of an unconverged entry; beating one is p2, not a record.
Kissing-number overlap: configurations with c* <= 0.5 in dims 9..23 belong to kissing-number-low-dim.
EinsteinArena leaderboards have had verifier exploits; never cite a leaderboard without recomputing from coordinates.
Literature scooping: re-fetch /plain and search arXiv immediately before claiming; uploading to /upload-code needs explicit permission from the human.

targets.name: Thomson problem: lower the best known Coulomb energy for some N (Deeter / Cambridge Cluster Database / Riesz s=1 tables)
targets.statement: Minimize E(N) = sum_{i<j} 1/|x_i - x_j| for N unit-charge points on the unit sphere. Live tables: (1) Wayne Deeter's table (deetour.net/oppp/thomson/, last modified 2026-10-05) with 13-significant-digit energies and point files e.<N>.txt (12 decimals) for N = 4..523, which already corrects several Cambridge entries (e.g. N = 263, 360, 377, 380-382); (2) the Cambridge Cluster Database Thomson tables (Wales-Ulker 2006, N = 10..400 plus magic N up to 972; Wales-McKay-Altschuler 2009, N = 400..4352 step 10 plus magic N) with 7-decimal energies and xyz files (9 significant digits); (3) the CCD 'Riesz energy database' s = 1 (53 configurations, N = 512..9913, updated 2026-09-20, 18-digit point files); (4) Wikipedia's table (N <= 470); (5) EinsteinArena's N = 282 leaderboard (37147.294418, AlphaEvolve = Deeter's value). Tables disagree in places (CCD Riesz N = 512: 124673.9055677 vs Deeter 124673.8412508), so the record for an N is the MINIMUM over all live tables. Lai-Hao (ESWA 2024) improved N = 360; 2025-2026 arXiv work (2506.08398, 2512.12416) maps landscapes without new minima. Only N <= 6 and N = 12 are proven (a 2026 claim for N = 7 is unverified).
targets.success_criterion: Success means N points on the unit sphere (coordinates to >= 20 digits) for some N <= 1500 listed in at least one live table, such that E* computed in mpmath at 30 digits from the normalized coordinates is STRICTLY LOWER (direction: min) than the minimum energy for that N over ALL of: Deeter's table (https://deetour.net/oppp/thomson/, N = 4..523), CCD Thomson/table.html, CCD Thomson2/table.html, the CCD Riesz s=1 table (site/s_1/index.html), the Wikipedia table and (for N = 282) EinsteinArena, each re-fetched live immediately before claiming, by at least 1e-6 in absolute energy, AND the configuration is a certified strict local minimum (mpmath tangent-space Newton to gradient norm < 1e-20, all 2N-3 non-rotational tangent Hessian eigenvalues > 0), AND it is a different basin from every posted table configuration for that N: polishing each table's own point file (Deeter e.<N>.txt, CCD xyz/<N>.xyz, Riesz dat/points_<N>_1.dat) with the same routine must give an energy higher than E* by >= 1e-6. N > 1500 (Riesz rows up to 9913) cannot be Hessian-certified in under an hour and is partial win p3 only.

partial_wins.statement: A table-integrity finding: an N where a live table's posted energy is not reproduced by its own posted coordinates after mpmath polishing by more than 1e-6 (Deeter documents such cases for CCD N = 263, 377, 380, 381), reported with both energies to 12 digits.

A certified improvement for the logarithmic potential (sum of -log|x_i - x_j|) or Riesz s = 2 for some N <= 500 against the Lai-Hao 2024 ESWA values, if the scout can fetch that paper's table; same local-minimum and distinct-basin rules.

A certified improvement in the CCD Riesz s = 1 table (N = 512..9913) for N > 1500 or beating only that table: same mpmath energy, gradient norm < 1e-15 and a Lanczos/ARPACK smallest tangent-Hessian eigenvalue > 0 in double precision instead of the full eigendecomposition; reported as an improvement of that table only.

targets.verification_method: Checker (< 10 minutes for N <= 1500): (1) curl all live tables and take the minimum for N. (2) Normalize the claimed points in mpmath (mp.dps = 30), compute E* exactly. (3) Tangent-space Newton in mpmath until gradient norm < 1e-20; confirm E* changes by < 1e-12; build the 3N x 3N Hessian in double, project out rotations, assert 2N-3 positive eigenvalues. (4) Download every table's point file for N and polish identically; assert each E_table_polished - E* >= 1e-6. (5) Assert E_table_min - E* >= 1e-6. Report all energies to 12 digits.
angles: Attack N = 400..523 where Deeter's table is newest and CCD only has every 10th N: use Deeter's own method (basin hopping with symmetric seeds from his 'roundest polyhedra' lists) plus Lai-Hao-style population crossover of Voronoi-defect patterns (scars). Deeter himself found new minima at 360 and 382 this way.

Defect-motif engineering: for N near icosadeltahedral magic numbers (10h^2+10hk+10k^2+2) move the 12 disclinations into scar chains and re-relax; N = 520..523 and the Riesz rows 532..548 are far from magic and likely under-explored.

CCD Riesz s = 1 rows for N = 512..972 duplicate Deeter/CCD Thomson values in several cases but are HIGHER for N = 512 (124673.9056 vs 124673.8413); check every N in both tables and polish the Riesz point files, since under-converged rows are easy targets for p3.

Use the 2025 landscape result (number of local minima grows exponentially faster than thought) to justify massive restarts: 10 cores x 10^4 L-BFGS descents per N for N = 150..300 with symmetry-seeded starts (C2, C3, D2, D3, D5 orbits), then mpmath polish.
pitfalls: Under-converged table values: a posted energy can exceed the true minimum of its own basin by 1e-7..1e-4 (Deeter's audit of CCD). Polishing the posted coordinates and getting a lower number is NOT a new minimum; the distinct-basin test is mandatory.
Precision: CCD tables carry 7 decimals and xyz files 9 significant digits; always compute from coordinates in mpmath, never trust a printed value to more digits than it has.
Multiple tables: the record is the minimum over all live tables (Deeter, CCD x2, Riesz s=1, Wikipedia, EinsteinArena); beating only the CCD value is not a record.
Saddle points masquerading as minima: an L-BFGS stop with gradient 1e-8 can be a saddle; require positive tangent Hessian.
EinsteinArena shows a verifier-exploit leader on the sibling Tammes page; never take a leaderboard number without recomputing from coordinates.

targets.name: AlphaEvolve-family analytic constants: autocorrelation inequalities and Erdos minimum overlap
targets.statement: Improve any of these constants with an explicit step function. (i) C_1a, the Sidon (first) autocorrelation constant (upper bound via a nonnegative f minimizing max(f*f)/(∫f)^2 with the repo normalization; Tao's constants/1a.md). (ii) The Erdos minimum overlap constant C_1b, which is equivalent to Erdos problem #36 (Haugland 2016, arXiv:1609.08000; Tao's constants/1b.md); upper bound via a step function f with f+g=1. (iii) The second autocorrelation constant C_2 (lower bound via ||f*f||_2^2 / (||f*f||_1 ||f*f||_inf)). (iv) The third autocorrelation constant C_3 (upper bound; EinsteinArena 'third autocorrelation inequality'; not the GHR sum-difference constant C_3a). As of 2026-10-03: MILO (arXiv:2609.38349, 29 Sep 2026) claims Erdos overlap 0.3808586 -> 0.3808568, C_1a 1.50274365 -> 1.50274360 and C_3 1.45081 -> 1.44889; the live arena first-autocorrelation leader is AgentDiscover 1.50274353; C_2 >= 0.963588 (arena, ClaudeExplorer). Lower-bound side: Erdos >= 0.379005 (White 2022) is the established bound on Tao's 1b page; for C_1a, 1.2802 (Ivanisvili-Xie 2026) is the verified entry on Tao's 1a page and 1.292 (Piterbarg-Bajaj-Vincent 2026) is listed there as unverified. arXiv:2606.31182 (Kim-Pilanci, Jun 2026) claims C_1a >= 1.2937 and Erdos >= 0.37912 with interval-arithmetic dual certificates; these are claims, not yet listed on Tao's pages or checked here. Improvements now land at the 1e-7 to 1e-8 level among many competing agents.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an exact rational step function (data file) whose exactly computed functional (no FFT floating-point scores) is STRICTLY BETTER in that constant's direction (min for Erdos overlap, C_1a and C_3; max for C_2) than the BEST value at verification time over: the live EinsteinArena leaderboard for that problem (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/first-autocorrelation-inequality, https://einsteinarena.com/problems/erdos-min-overlap, https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, https://einsteinarena.com/problems/third-autocorrelation-inequality), Tao's live pages (https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/blob/main/constants/1a.md and 1b.md), arXiv:2609.38349 (MILO) and any newer arXiv claim, by at least 1e-6 absolute in the correct normalization (arena display may be halved; calibrate on published data first). Wherever a record holder's function is published (arena submissions, the Together AI repo, AlphaEvolve problem pages, links on Tao's pages), the verifier recomputes its UNROUNDED value with the same exact evaluator and compares against that, never against a rounded display; a record whose function is not published (e.g. MILO's) is used at its printed value. Context on 2026-10-03: C_3 bar 1.44889, Erdos 0.3808568, C_1a 1.50274353, C_2 0.963588. Dual-side lower-bound improvements count only with a rigorous interval-arithmetic or exact certificate.

partial_wins.statement: A rigorous dual-side record: a lower bound C_1a > 1.2937 or Erdos minimum overlap > 0.37912, strictly above the best lower bound found at verification time, counting the verified entries on Tao's 1a/1b pages (1.2802 IX2026; 0.379005 White 2022), the unverified 1.292 (PBV2026) and the claimed bounds of arXiv:2606.31182, with an interval-arithmetic or exact certificate the skeptic re-runs.

A sub-threshold exact record: an exact rational step function that beats the best live value for one constant by less than 1e-6, with the improvement certified in exact rational arithmetic in the arena's normalization (strict, not a floating-point tie).

An exactly certified improvement (direction: min) of a discrete minimum-overlap value M(n) on the live page https://www.neutreeko.net/mop/index.htm for some n where that page lists only a bound (not a proven optimum), with the partition of {1..2n} given explicitly and the overlap recomputed exactly over all shifts.

targets.verification_method: First recompute the current record holders' UNROUNDED values from their published functions (arena submissions, Together AI repo, AlphaEvolve problem pages, TTT data) with the same exact evaluator used for the candidate, to fix the normalisation and the true record digits. Use exact arithmetic with fractions or integers after scaling. The autoconvolution of a step function on a uniform grid is piecewise linear with knots at grid points, so its max is attained at a knot: compute the discrete convolution of the integer heights exactly. For C_2, integrate the piecewise-linear f*f squared exactly per interval (quadratic, so closed form). For the Erdos overlap, the correlation of step functions is piecewise linear, so check all breakpoints exactly and verify f+g=1, 0<=f<=1, and ∫f=1. Calibrate by re-deriving a published value (e.g. AlphaEvolve's 1.5053 or TTT's 1.50287 data) in the same normalization. EinsteinArena's display uses a halved scale (e.g. 0.75143 vs 1.50287). For a discrete M(n) claim, recompute max over shifts k of |A ∩ (B+k)| exactly and compare with the live neutreeko page.
angles: Do LP/QP alternation. For a fixed active set of near-maximal autoconvolution knots, the problem in f is an LP after normalizing ∫f=1. Iterate active-set LP (scipy HiGHS) at grid sizes 10^4-10^5, which is more principled than gradient methods.
Use multiscale upsampling with Nesterov or Adam on a log-sum-exp smoothed max, annealing the temperature, then an exact LP polish.
Exploit the 'block-oscillation' and asymmetry structure noted by arena agents. Parametrize f as a smooth envelope times a high-frequency comb and optimize envelope parameters.

Pursue the dual side for a partial win: improved lower bounds for C_1a (verified 1.2802, Ivanisvili-Xie 2026; unverified 1.292, PBV2026; claimed 1.2937, arXiv:2606.31182) via Fourier/SDP certificates. These are verifiable as rigorous inequalities with interval arithmetic.

Warm-start from the published SimpleTES/TogetherAI/AlphaEvolve step functions (EinsteinArena repo, AlphaEvolve problem page). Refine by sequential linear programming: linearise the bilinear term around the current f, minimise the max over the active breakpoints with a trust region, and repeat.
Progressive upsampling (N = 1k to 50k steps) with FFT-based subgradients on the max (bundle or prox-linear methods), then rationalise and re-certify exactly.
Structural priors from Haugland: near-optimal f is mostly 0/1 with thin transition zones. Parametrise the transition profiles with few parameters and optimise globally (CMA-ES), then polish with LP.
For the lower bound: White's Fourier/SDP approach. Raise the truncation order or add new valid inequalities and solve the SDP with a certificate (rational rounding).
Warm-start from the published Together AI / TTT-Discover / AlphaEvolve step functions and refine with sequential LP, minimising the max over active breakpoints under a trust region.
Upsample (N = 600 to 50k steps) with FFT subgradients and a prox-linear or bundle method, then rationalise and re-certify exactly.
Equalisation heuristic: optimal f should make f*f nearly flat on a large plateau. Solve for f that makes f*f equal a target plateau via Newton on the step heights.
Try structured families (sums of power-law spikes near ±1/4 plus smooth bulk) and polish them with the LP.
pitfalls: Normalization mismatches between AlphaEvolve, Tao's repo and EinsteinArena (factor 2, support [-1/4,1/4] vs [0,1]).
FFT round-off makes scores look better by around 1e-9. Use exact certification only.
There are dozens of agents on these leaderboards and improvements are in the 6th decimal. Re-fetch the leaderboard right before claiming.
The direction of the bound (upper vs lower) differs per problem.
Paper claims (MILO) may use different normalizations from the arena. Calibrate on its published data before comparing.
The third autocorrelation bar jumped from 1.4508 to 1.4489 in Sep 2026. Old baselines will cause false claims.
Normalisation mismatch between the discrete M(n)/n and continuous scalings ([-1,1] versus [0,2]).
Evaluating the sup only on a grid rather than at all breakpoints.
Claiming improvements at the 1e-7 level from float arithmetic.
Forgetting that g = 1 - f >= 0 requires f <= 1.
Records move monthly, so re-check the repo on the day.
Comparing against the rounded 0.380868 rather than the record's exact value.
Records changed four times in about a year; re-fetch 1b.md on the day.
Support/normalisation mismatch ([-1/4,1/4] versus [0,1] or [-1/2,1/2] conventions).
Evaluating the max on a grid instead of at all breakpoints.
Float-level 'improvements' below 1e-7.
Comparing against the rounded 1.502862.
The third autocorrelation constant C_3 here is NOT the GHR sum-difference constant C_3a (Tao's constants/3a.md, bank entry ghr-sum-difference-c3a). Never compare values across them.
Tao's 1a/1b pages lag the arena and MILO (1.502862 and 0.380868 on 2026-10-03). Using them as the bar would claim results that are already beaten.
Lower-bound provenance: White 2022 (0.379005) and IX2026 (1.2802) are verified; PBV2026 (1.292) is asterisked as unverified on Tao's page; arXiv:2606.31182's 1.2937 and 0.37912 are claims.

targets.name: Larger cap sets in F_3^7 (beat 236) or F_3^8 (beat 512)
targets.statement: A cap set in F_3^n contains no three distinct points on a line (equivalently, no x,y,z distinct with x+y+z=0). Exact maxima are known through n=6 (112). For n=7, 236 <= r(7) <= 288: the lower bound is Calderbank-Fishburn and the upper bound is Thackeray (2022, no 289-cap). For n=8, the best known is 512 (FunSearch 2023, matched by X-evolve 2025).
targets.success_criterion: Success means a set S of distinct vectors in {0,1,2}^n (n = 7 or 8) such that for every pair of distinct x,y in S, the third point -(x+y) mod 3 is not in S, verified exhaustively, with |S| STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the best known cap size for that n at verification time (OEIS A090245, Wikipedia 'Cap set', fresh arXiv search; context on 2026-10-03: 236 for n=7, 512 for n=8). For n=7, |S| must be <= 288 (Thackeray's bound); larger means a bug.

partial_wins.statement: A cap in F_3^9 or F_3^10, verified exhaustively, strictly larger than the best published cap for that dimension at verification time (Edel's tables, FunSearch, X-evolve, OEIS, fresh arXiv search).

An explicit admissible set (or other mechanically checkable ingredient) giving a cap-set capacity lower bound strictly above the live value at https://teorth.github.io/optimizationproblems/constants/4a.html, with the bound formula recomputed independently.
An upper bound r(7) <= 287, delivered as a DRAT (or similarly checkable) proof that the skeptic verifies with drat-trim.

targets.verification_method: Encode the vectors as base-3 integers in a set. For all pairs, compute the third point and check membership: about |S|^2/2 = 130k checks, instant. Check distinctness, coordinate ranges, and the dimension.
angles: Search caps that are unions of orbits under a prescribed subgroup of AGL(n,3) (e.g. Singer-like cyclic groups on F_{3^7}, or coordinate-permutation groups of order 7 or 14). Solve max independent orbit selection exactly with CP-SAT.
Extend Edel's product/doubling-type constructions: pair a large cap in F_3^a with one in F_3^b under twisted gluing rules, and search the twists.
Use an SAT/ILP with symmetry breaking in n=7 seeking 237, starting from the 236-cap and asking for any 'swap k out, k+1 in' move with k <= 6.
Use priority-function evolution (FunSearch style) with a better scoring function, e.g. counting future-blocking lines, run for hours on 10 cores.
pitfalls: Collinearity in F_3^n means x+y+z = 0 (mod 3) for distinct points, not affine collinearity over R.
Projective vs affine caps are different problems with different tables.
236 has stood since the 1990s-2004 despite FunSearch and X-evolve, so expect failure.

targets.name: Binary (or small-q) linear codes beating codetables.de lower bounds
targets.statement: For given [n,k] over GF(q), codetables.de (Grassl) records the best known lower and upper bounds on the maximum minimum distance d. A linear code with d larger than the tabulated lower bound is a new record. Binary tables cover n <= 256.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a k x n generator matrix over GF(q) with these properties. (1) Rank is exactly k over GF(q), computed independently. (2) The exact minimum distance d is computed by full enumeration of all q^k - 1 nonzero codewords when feasible (2^k <= ~2^32), or, for large k (or large k with small n-k, via the dual and MacWilliams identities), by two independent exact minimum-distance implementations that agree; never by sampling. (3) d is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the lower bound in the live http://www.codetables.de/ cell for (q,n,k) at verification time, and at most the upper bound. (4) The code is not one of the 7 LinCodeEvolve codes (arXiv:2609.37056) or a code derived from them, and no newer arXiv claim already reaches that d.

partial_wins.statement: A quantum-code record: an explicit stabilizer code [[n,k,d]] (symplectic self-orthogonality checked exactly, minimum distance computed exactly) whose d is strictly greater than the lower bound in the live codetables.de quantum-code table for that (n,k).

An improved upper bound: a re-checkable certificate (exact rational LP dual certificate, or an exhaustive non-existence classification with code the skeptic re-runs) proving that no [n,k,d] code over GF(q) exists for d equal to the live codetables.de upper bound, thereby lowering it.

targets.verification_method: Use an independent script. Compute rank by Gaussian elimination over GF(2) with numpy uint8 or bitset ints. For k <= 32, compute weights with a Gray-code walk over all codewords using XOR of packed rows (2^k * n/64 ops; k=22 takes seconds). For larger k, use two independent minimum-distance implementations (e.g. a custom Brouwer-Zimmermann plus pip 'galois' or 'ldpc' style tools) and require agreement. Look up the live table cell at codetables.de/BKLC/... for (n,k) and confirm the strict improvement. Then check arXiv for newer claims.
angles: Search quasi-cyclic and quasi-twisted codes of index 2-6. Each code is defined by a few circulant first rows, so the search space is small and the codes have a good chance of structure. Use the circulant to prune minimum-distance computation (only one codeword per cyclic orbit needs checking).
Run Construction X/XX on any new QC code, plus puncturing, shortening and extending, to propagate one win to several neighboring table cells.
Look at ternary/quaternary tables (q=3,4,5) in moderate n, which have historically received less AI attention than binary.
Use an evolutionary search over generator programs, not matrices (LinCodeEvolve style). Mutate small Python code that emits QC first rows, with the exact minimum-distance checker as the fitness.
Use Gray-code minimum-distance evaluation with early abort. Stop as soon as a codeword of weight below the target is found, which makes rejection cheap.
pitfalls: Floating-point or int8 overflow in the GF(2) arithmetic. Use bit operations.
A d computed only on a random sample of codewords proves nothing.
Rank deficiency: the code is then really [n,k'] with k' < k.
Comparing against a stale snapshot. The LinCodeEvolve results may already be incorporated, so re-check the live cell.
When k is large but n-k is small, use the dual and MacWilliams identities, or require two independent minimum-distance implementations. Never sample.

targets.name: Binary constant-weight codes A(n,d,w): new lower bounds in Brouwer's table
targets.statement: A(n,d,w) is the maximum number of binary words of length n and weight w with pairwise Hamming distance >= d. Brouwer's tables (d = 4..18, n up to 28 in the main tables and further for some) list best known lower and upper bounds. A code larger than the tabulated lower bound is a new record. Active as of 2026-10-03. Lysenstoen (arXiv:2607.19550, Jul 2026; values polished further in Brouwer's table) and Echols (arXiv:2608.13906, Aug 2026, 124 improved cells via tabu search). Lower bounds are still being pushed. Brouwer's live cells already carry polished Lysenstoen values (e.g. A(23,6,10) >= 2992, A(23,6,11) >= 3588, A(24,6,8) >= 1859, A(24,6,10) >= 4237), larger than the arXiv abstract's numbers.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit list of M distinct binary vectors of length n, each with Hamming weight exactly w, with all pairwise distances >= d (d even), where M is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the lower bound shown at verification time in the (n,d,w) cell of https://aeb.win.tue.nl/codes/Andw.html (also checking the mirror cell A(n,d,n-w)), and also strictly greater than any value for that cell in arXiv:2608.13906 (Echols, 124 improved cells), arXiv:2607.19550 (Lysenstoen) or any newer arXiv paper. M must not exceed the tabulated upper bound; exceeding it means a bug.

partial_wins.statement: A first explicit certificate: for a cell whose live lower bound has no surviving explicit code listing (a bare 1990-era citation), an explicit code of size equal to the tabulated lower bound, verified exactly. The skeptic confirms on the live page and in arXiv:2607.19550 / 2608.13906 that no explicit code for that cell is already published.

An improved upper bound: an exact rational dual certificate (Delsarte LP or Schrijver-type SDP, verified in rational arithmetic) proving A(n,d,w) <= U for U strictly below the live tabulated upper bound for some cell.

targets.verification_method: Use an independent script. Store the words as Python ints and assert popcount == w for each, all distinct, and popcount(x ^ y) >= d for all pairs: M^2/2 popcounts, vectorized in numpy (uint64) or with bitset blocks. Re-fetch aeb.win.tue.nl/codes/Andw.html at check time and read the cell. Also check the equivalent cell under complement symmetry, A(n,d,w) = A(n,d,n-w). Claim only if the strict improvement holds.
angles: Build codes from group orbits. Choose a group G acting on coordinates (cyclic of order n or n-1, PSL(2,q) on q+1 points, affine groups) and take the code as a union of G-orbits of weight-w words. Find a maximum compatible orbit set by max-weight clique search on the orbit graph (networkx or a custom bitset B&B). Few orbits make exact search feasible.
Use Lysenstoen's split-coordinate decomposition. Fix half of the coordinates to a known good code and optimize the complementary half with CP-SAT.
Look for cells where the lower bound is a bare citation to 1990 Brouwer-Shearer-Sloane-Smith with no surviving code listing, and reconstruct then beat them.
Use partitioning constructions: (u|u+v)-style, or partition-and-combine from codes with weights w1 + w2 = w on split coordinates. Sweep all splits automatically.
Run large-scale local search (e.g. 1-opt add/remove with tabu) on the conflict graph restricted to a random G-invariant subspace.
Auditor note: Echols' seeded bit-swap tabu search just swept 124 cells, so prefer group-orbit / structured constructions over plain local search, and target cells that paper did not improve.
pitfalls: Brouwer's table uses even d. Odd d reduces to d+1, so check the convention.
Equivalent cells: A(n,d,w) = A(n,d,n-w), so make sure the improved cell is not already beaten in its mirror.
The table moved from win.tue.nl/~aeb to aeb.win.tue.nl, so read the live page.
arXiv abstracts can lag Brouwer's table (polished values are larger), so always read the live cell.
Echols' 124 improvements may not all be reflected in the table yet, so check arXiv:2608.13906's tables too.

targets.name: Covering designs C(v,k,t): beat a repository entry
targets.statement: A (v,k,t) covering design is a collection of k-subsets (blocks) of a v-set such that every t-subset lies in at least one block. C(v,k,t) is the minimum number of blocks. The repository tables list the best known upper bounds for v <= 99, k <= 25, t <= 8. A design with fewer blocks than the current table entry for any listed (v,k,t) is a new record that can be submitted directly. The dmgordo/LJCR GitHub repository states it is the permanent data location for the La Jolla Covering Repository (the old website is going away), but its covering data file was last committed 2022-12-19; the live LJCR page is https://dmgordon.org/covering-designs/ (site last updated 2026-09-03), which points to coveringrepository.com for more recent improvements, and Zenodo v1.1 (2026-04-08) is a snapshot. coveringrepository.com imported Gordon's data through March 2026 and also hosts lottery-wheel (v,k,t,m) tables. Hobbyist repositories may hold claimed records not yet merged into any table. Example: the thebrockchain/covering-designs README claims C(28,13,4) <= 53 (7 Aug 2026; LJCR data: 54, Fadlaoui 2008) and C(32,13,4) <= 95 (8 Aug 2026; LJCR data: 96, Fadlaoui 2009). The README says Dan Gordon checked the (28,13,4) design with his own code; this was not confirmed on dmgordon.org on 2026-10-03, and coveringrepository.com could not be fetched from here. Both are unverified hobbyist claims.
targets.success_criterion: Success means b blocks, each a k-subset of a v-set (no repeated points), covering every t-subset (checked exhaustively), where b is STRICTLY SMALLER (direction: min) than EVERY one of the following, each re-fetched at verification time: the live coveringrepository.com plain (v,k,t) value (m=t section, https://coveringrepository.com/), the live LJCR value (https://dmgordon.org/covering-designs/), and the dmgordo/LJCR GitHub/Zenodo value. It must also beat any value found by grepping GitHub/arXiv for that (v,k,t) over the last 6 months, including unverified hobbyist claims (e.g. thebrockchain/covering-designs: C(28,13,4) <= 53, C(32,13,4) <= 95). If a live table cannot be fetched, the claim is 'PENDING TABLE CHECK', not a record. Parameters must be within v <= 99, k <= 25, t <= 8, and b must be at least the Schonheim bound L(v,k,t); going below it means a bug. Same-day claim only if C(v,t) <= 5e9, so the exhaustive coverage check runs on a laptop; larger cases are logged as 'PENDING chunked exhaustive check' and claimed only after that full check completes.

partial_wins.statement: A lottery-design record: an explicit (v,k,t,m) lottery covering (every m-subset of the v-set meets some block in at least t points, checked exhaustively) with strictly fewer blocks than the live coveringrepository.com lottery-table value for those parameters and any value found on GitHub/arXiv for them.

A new exact lower bound: a certified proof that C(v,k,t) is strictly larger than both the Schonheim bound and every lower bound listed for that cell in the live repositories or literature, for some in-range (v,k,t), delivered as a re-checkable certificate (a DRAT proof checked with drat-trim, or an exact ILP infeasibility certificate re-verified by an independent solver).

targets.verification_method: The verifier writes an independent checker. Parse blocks, assert each has exactly k distinct elements in range, and enumerate all t-subsets (or use a bitmask coverage array indexed by combinadic rank) to confirm each is covered. Compute the Schonheim bound recursively. Fetch the live values from coveringrepository.com, dmgordon.org/covering-designs and the LJCR GitHub/Zenodo data, and grep GitHub/arXiv for recent claims on the same (v,k,t). Claim only if b is below every one of those values, C(v,t) <= 5e9 (otherwise PENDING), and the solver's file hash matches the checked file. For huge C(v,t) (above 1e9), use a streaming check over blocks with a bitset of t-subsets and chunk it if memory is tight.
angles: Look for soft entries first. Scrape the table for (v,k,t) whose record comes from old generic methods (greedy, 'combining', Turan-type constructions) or that have not changed in 15+ years, especially large k with t=4..5. The Aug 2026 wins were exactly (28,13,4) and (32,13,4).

Use automorphism prescription. Fix a group G (cyclic Z_v, Z_{v-1} plus a fixed point, PSL(2,q), AGL(1,q)), so the design is a union of G-orbits of k-sets. Solve the orbit set-cover exactly with OR-Tools CP-SAT or an ILP (pip install ortools). This is the Kramer-Mesner trick applied to coverings.
Use Nurmela-Ostergard simulated annealing with incremental uncovered-t-set counts, started from the current record minus one block, so the search is to repair a small number of uncovered t-sets.

Use recursive constructions with fresh ingredients. A new record at (v,k,t) often propagates to (v+1,k,t), (v,k+1,t) and so on through standard combining constructions. After any single win, sweep its neighbors.
Use a lottery-wheel style local search: swap one element of one block and accept if uncovered count does not increase (tabu). This is cheap and parallelizes over 10 cores with different seeds.
Auditor note: AI/hobbyist sweeps began in Aug 2026, so prioritise cells whose record is old and not near the (28,13,4)/(32,13,4) neighbourhood that has just been picked over.

Simulated annealing or tabu search over block sets, with the cost equal to the number of uncovered t-sets and incremental delta updates (Nurmela-Östergård style). Target triples where the LJCR value has the largest ratio to the Schönheim bound.

Prescribed automorphism groups: require the design to be a union of orbits under Z_v, Z_{v-1}+fixed point, PSL(2,q) or AGL(1,q). The search becomes a small set-cover over orbits, which can be solved exactly with OR-tools CP-SAT (pip install ortools).

Recursive constructions: combine record coverings for (v1,k1,t1) and (v2,k2,t2) through the standard C(v1+v2,k,t) <= sum over i of C(v1,k1,i)*C(v2,k-k1,t-i)-type product constructions. Scan all splits of every table entry automatically. The 2026 improvements at large v suggest these are under-explored.

FunSearch/AlphaEvolve-style loop: have an LLM write construction programs (for example, greedy covering with learned priority functions over finite-field structure), score them by block count, and evolve the programs.
Take a record design and do local surgery: delete 1-3 blocks, then repair the uncovered t-sets with an exact ILP over all k-sets that cover at least one of them.

Before searching, merge LJCR and coveringrepository.com into one live-min table and rank entries by ratio to the Schoenheim bound; only target entries where both sources agree on the value (no recent Acerbi improvement).
pitfalls: Comparing against a stale table. The live LJCR page is https://dmgordon.org/covering-designs/ (updated 2026-09-03); the dmgordo/LJCR GitHub data (last commit 2022-12-19) and Zenodo v1.1 (2026-04-08) are snapshots; the old ljcr.dmgordo.org host did not respond on 2026-10-03; coveringrepository.com has newer improvements. Check all of them.
Off-by-one: the table's v counts points, so check the point labeling (0- vs 1-based) and that no block repeats a point.
Parameters outside the repository's listed range do not count as a record.
Coverings with multiplicity (lambda > 1) or (v,k,t,m) lottery coverings are different tables, so do not mix them up.
coveringrepository.com mixes lottery (v,k,t,m) coverings with plain (v,k,t) designs, so read the right table.
Independent hobbyist repos (e.g. thebrockchain) may hold claimed records not yet merged into any table. Treat them as values to beat, even when unverified.
The table may have been updated after the searcher last read it. Always re-fetch it.
Confusing covering designs with packing designs, or with lotto designs C(v,k,t,m).
Off-by-one errors in v when points are 1-indexed.
Duplicate blocks inflate the apparent coverage but not the count. Count unique blocks.
A result below the Schönheim bound means the checker is wrong, not that the search succeeded.
LJCR is no longer the most up-to-date source; coveringrepository.com has newer improvements. Beating only LJCR is not a record.
coveringrepository.com also hosts lotto (v,k,t,m) designs. Make sure the comparison uses the (v,k,t) section with m=t.
Lottery-wheel hobbyists optimize the small-v entries intensely. Expect wins only at large v, k and t, where verification is costly.

targets.name: Erdos #757: (4,5)-set with Sidon density below 4/7
targets.statement: Let c* be the largest constant such that every (4,5)-set A of reals (every 4-element subset determines at least five distinct values among its six pairwise absolute differences) of size n contains a Sidon subset of size >= c* n. Ma-Tang (arXiv:2602.23282) give 9/17 (about 0.5294) <= c* <= 4/7 (about 0.5714); the 4/7 witness is A = {0,136,200,243,246,249,272,286,298,323,400,528,596,1056} (|A|=14, max Sidon subset 8, independently re-checked by the auditor on 2026-10-03). The bank research attributes to Ma-Tang the identity c* = inf_n f(n)/n (f(n) = min over (4,5)-sets of size n of the largest Sidon subset); the auditor flags that this attribution, or the blow-up lemma (a disjoint generic union of dilated copies stays (4,5) and its Sidon number adds), must be confirmed in the paper before a finite witness is read as a new upper bound on c*. Given that, ONE finite (4,5)-set with s/|A| < 4/7 improves the upper bound; e.g. |A|=16 with s=9, |A|=18 with s=10, |A|=23 with s=13, |A|=25 with s=14.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a finite set A of distinct integers with all of the following. (1) Every 4-subset has at least 5 distinct absolute differences, checked exhaustively. (2) The exact maximum Sidon subset size s(A) is certified by two independent exact methods (bitmask branch-and-bound and an ILP that forbids every a+b=c+d, including a=b, i.e. 3-APs). (3) The ratio s/|A|, compared in fractions.Fraction, is STRICTLY SMALLER (direction: min) than the best upper bound on c* shown at verification time at https://www.erdosproblems.com/757, on the EinsteinArena 'Sidon Subsets of (4,5)-Sets' leaderboard and in any newer arXiv paper (context: 4/7 on 2026-10-03; a ratio exactly equal to the live best is not a success). (4) s/|A| >= 9/17; a ratio below 9/17 contradicts a theorem and means a bug, never a claim. (5) The verifier confirms in arXiv:2602.23282 the lemma that a finite witness bounds c* (the blow-up lemma or the inf-formula), or else re-derives it. (6) The checker reproduces s=8 on the Ma-Tang 14-set as a calibration test.

partial_wins.statement: A new extremal witness: a (4,5)-set A with |A| NOT a multiple of 14 (e.g. |A| = 21 with s = 12) whose certified exact maximum Sidon subset gives s/|A| exactly equal to the live best ratio (4/7 on 2026-10-03), verified by the same two-method pipeline. Disjoint unions of dilated copies of the Ma-Tang 14-set only reach multiples of 14, so this is a structurally new extremal example.

A frozen abstract target: an explicit 3-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices that satisfies every structural property arXiv:2602.23282 proves for 3-AP hypergraphs of (4,5)-sets (linear, F7-free, at most n-2 edges, and any further listed condition, each checked by script against the paper), with exact independence number alpha(H) and alpha(H)/n strictly below the live best ratio. The skeptic must confirm that the paper does not already exhibit or exclude such an H.

targets.verification_method: Use an independent script. (a) Run the C(n,4) (4,5) check. (b) Compute the exact max Sidon subset by exhaustive bitmask search for n <= 26, or with B&B plus a pulp/CBC ILP (all 3-AP and a+b=c+d constraints) and require agreement. (c) Calibrate on {0,136,200,243,246,249,272,286,298,323,400,528,596,1056}, which must give (4,5)=True and s=8. (d) Do the rational comparison. (e) Check the live arena and erdosproblems page.
angles: Use the hypergraph view. For (4,5)-sets, the Sidon number equals the independence number of the 3-AP hypergraph H(A), which Ma-Tang show is linear and F7-free with m <= n-2 edges. Search over abstract linear 3-uniform hypergraphs with small independence ratio that satisfy those constraints, then realize them as integer sets with an ILP or SMT over integer coordinates.
Glue copies of the 14-element witness along shared elements, or overlay two dilated copies so that APs share points. Look for configurations where the extra shared vertices push alpha(H)/n below 4/7.

Simulated annealing over integer sets in [0, 5000]. Score = max Sidon size / n plus a penalty for (4,5) violations. Do incremental (4,5) checking with difference-multiset counters and exact Sidon computation via fast bitset branch-and-bound.

Since c* = inf f(n)/n, aim at n in {16,18,23,25,30} and the s values that would beat 4/7. Use the Henning-Yeo transversal bound (17 tau <= 5n + 3m) to see which (n,m) are even possible before searching.
Use AP-rich seeds: unions of short APs with carefully perturbed common differences, Sidon-like scaffolds (Singer sets) with planted 3-APs, and the Ma-Tang base set as a seed for local moves.

Before searching, use the Henning-Yeo transversal bound and Ma-Tang's structural constraints to list which (n, m, s) are combinatorially possible, and then target only those n (auditor note: Ma-Tang presumably searched small n themselves).
pitfalls: Getting the definition wrong. The erdosproblems summary paraphrases it confusingly. Use the Ma-Tang definition exactly: 6 absolute differences, at least 5 distinct.
Floating-point reals. Use integers only, so equality of differences is exact.
Counting Sidon too loosely. Sidon must also forbid a+a=b+c (3-APs), and that is the key obstruction here.
A heuristic max-independent-set gives only a lower bound on s, which can understate s and fake a win. The maximum must be certified exactly.
Ratio below 9/17 means a bug (contradicts a theorem).
EinsteinArena now hosts this problem, so check the leaderboard right before claiming. An arena entry may beat 4/7 without an arXiv paper.
A ratio s/n < 4/7 but with s/n not a new infimum relative to arena submissions is not a record.

targets.name: Erich Friedman Packing Center: beat a listed packing
targets.statement: Friedman's Packing Center lists best known packings of n congruent shapes (circles, squares, triangles, pentagons, hexagons, octagons and others) into containers of various shapes. Mostly the goal is the smallest container for n unit shapes, or the largest shapes for a unit container. Several pages were updated in Sep-Oct 2026, including AI-team records (Numaro, Jul 2026, unequal-circle total-radius records) and new proofs (Vu-Le, Sep 2026). Submissions are by email, with sizes to 5 decimals; extensions of existing categories are accepted up to n=50. Many categories show updates dated 30 Sep - 3 Oct 2026, so multiple agents sweep the pages daily. Submission is by email, which is an outbound message on the human's behalf and requires explicit permission from the human.
targets.success_criterion: Success means explicit placements (centers plus rotation angles) for n shapes that meet all of the following. (1) Pairwise interiors are disjoint and every shape lies inside the container, certified rigorously by interval arithmetic or exact rational/algebraic computation. (2) The objective is STRICTLY BETTER, in the page's own direction (smaller container, or larger shape/total radius), than the value on the specific live Friedman page re-fetched immediately before verification, by at least 1e-5 at Friedman's 5-decimal precision. (3) The category and n are listed on the page, or n <= 50 for an extension of an existing category. The claim is for the verified construction; emailing Friedman needs explicit permission from the human.

partial_wins.statement: A Packomania record: a circles-in-square or circles-in-circle packing, rigorously certified, whose objective strictly beats the live Packomania value for that n at its listed precision.

An EinsteinArena sum-of-radii record: a circle packing for one of the EinsteinArena AlphaEvolve-style sum-of-radii problems, with containment and non-overlap certified in interval or exact arithmetic, whose exactly computed score strictly beats the live arena leaderboard best.

targets.verification_method: Use an independent checker. Represent polygons by exact vertices after applying the rotation with rational approximations to cos/sin, or bound them with interval arithmetic. Test pairwise overlap with the separating axis theorem in interval arithmetic, requiring positive separation or exact touching certified. Check containment of every vertex (and for circles, the center distance to each container edge >= r). Compute the objective and compare with the page value.
angles: Avoid circles-in-squares and circles-in-circles (Packomania-saturated). Target odd shape/container pairs (pentagons in triangles, octagons in squares, triangles in pentagons) where the record is an old hand construction.

Use penalty-method optimization with a contracting container (minimize container scale plus a squared overlap penalty from SAT-based penetration depth), with L-BFGS and random restarts across 10 cores.
Use a 'jamming plus rattler removal' pipeline: compress a random packing (Lubachevsky-Stillinger event-driven for circles, a rigid-body MD analogue for polygons), then optimize the rotation angles.
Transfer lattice cuts. Cut good periodic packings of the shape with the container and locally repair boundary pieces.
pitfalls: Comparing in the wrong direction. Some pages minimize container side, others maximize total radius or perimeter.
Numerical 'touching' that is actually a tiny overlap. Require rigorous certification.
Circle packing pages are heavily optimized already. The AlphaEvolve sum-of-radii benchmarks are separate EinsteinArena problems.
Pages are being updated daily (Sep 30 - Oct 3 2026), so re-fetch the specific page immediately before claiming.
Submitting to Friedman is an email on the human's behalf and needs explicit permission. Claim the verified construction, not the submission.

targets.name: Hadamard maximal determinant: new record determinants for orders n not divisible by 4
targets.statement: For each order n not divisible by 4, find an n x n {+1,-1} matrix with |det| larger than the best known value. Many records come from Orrick's MaxDet database (pre-2012, now reachable only through the Wayback archive). Butbaia ... Gukov (arXiv:2608.22518 v3, 1 Oct 2026) improved n = 51 and the n = 3 mod 4 orders 103-119 with two-circulant-block constructions; the Math-AI-Caltech/hadamard-maxdet repo holds exact det values with prev fields from the archived database, and EinsteinArena lists 'Hadamard Maximal Determinant (order 51)'. For many orders the Barba bound (n = 1 mod 4) or the Ehlich-Wojtas bound (n = 2 mod 4) is attained (e.g. n = 25, 26, 30, 41, 42, 50), so those records are proven maximal and closed. The research pass claimed maximality is certified for all n <= 22; the auditor could not verify this, so read it from the archive. Live targets are orders whose record is strictly below the residue-class bound, notably n = 3 mod 4 in 55..99 and n = 1, 2 mod 4 above 22 not touched by learning methods.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit n x n +-1 matrix whose exact integer |det| (Bareiss on Python ints, cross-checked with sympy) is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the max, at verification time, of: the archived MaxDet value (Wayback copy referenced by Math-AI-Caltech), the arXiv:2608.22518 / Math-AI-Caltech CSV value, the EinsteinArena order-51 leaderboard, and any newer arXiv value. It must not exceed the residue-class upper bound (Barba for n = 1 mod 4, Ehlich-Wojtas for n = 2 mod 4, or the Ehlich n = 3 mod 4 bound in the form valid for that n range). The order must be one where the previous record was strictly below that bound.

partial_wins.statement: A maximality certificate: for some order n >= 23 whose record is strictly below its residue-class bound, a re-runnable exhaustive proof (e.g. Gram-matrix enumeration with exact arithmetic and logged case splits that the skeptic re-runs) that the current record determinant is maximal, after confirming no such proof is published.

A frozen Gram target: for an order n whose record is below its bound, an explicit symmetric positive-definite integer matrix G with diagonal n, off-diagonal entries obeying the parity/congruence conditions of Gram matrices of +-1 matrices of that order, det G strictly greater than the square of the live record, and passing the rational (Hasse-Minkowski) equivalence test to n*I, all checked exactly; plus at least n-2 rows of a +-1 matrix realising the leading principal block of G.

targets.verification_method: Compute |det| with fraction-free Bareiss elimination on Python ints (exact), cross-checked with sympy Matrix(...).det(method='bareiss'). Note that det is divisible by 2^(n-1), so report |det|/2^(n-1) as an integer and compare it exactly to the record value. Confirm all entries are +-1. Also compute the bound for the residue class and confirm det <= bound. Pull the record from the Orrick archive or the Math-AI-Caltech CSVs (the *_prev columns give old benchmarks).
primary_sources: http://www.indiana.edu/~maxdet (Orrick archive, referenced by the 2026 paper; not opened this session)
angles: For n = 2 mod 4, use two-circulant D-optimal style constructions: two +-1 sequences whose periodic autocorrelations sum to a constant. Search these by SAT/compression methods (Djokovic-Kotsireas compression), which is far smaller than the general space.

For n = 3 mod 4, use Ehlich's block structure, where the Gram matrix ideally decomposes into 7 or so blocks. Search circulant-block matrices whose Gram matrix matches a near-Ehlich target, as in 2608.22518, but for the untouched orders 55..99.

For n = 1 mod 4, border a Hadamard or conference-type matrix, or use two-circulant sequences with periodic autocorrelation sum 1 (Barba-type). Brute-force the 'remove a row/col and add one' perturbations from Hadamard matrices of order n-1 and n+3.
Do simulated annealing on det with rank-1 update formulas (Sherman-Morrison), so a single sign flip costs O(n^2), and run many seeds per order in parallel.
Use a Gram-matrix-first search: pick a good positive-definite integer Gram target G with large det, then solve for a +-1 decomposition X X^T = G by backtracking.
First compute the residue-class bound for every order 23..119 and drop orders where the record already equals it (auditor: those are closed); rank the rest by record/bound ratio.
pitfalls: Using floating-point det from numpy.linalg.det. Never use it for certification (n ~ 100 loses precision).
Normalization confusion between det, det/2^(n-1), and ratio-to-bound. Compare exact integers.
The Orrick database is archived and partly pre-2012. Check 2608.22518 and any later arXiv for the newest values.
Order 51 and 103-119 were just improved, so beating them requires beating 2608.22518's matrices.
Orders where the Barba or Ehlich-Wojtas bound is already attained are closed. Exceeding the bound there means a bug, and matching it is not a record.
The Ehlich n = 3 mod 4 bound has different block counts for different n ranges (the 7-block form only for n >= 63), so use the correct form.
The original indiana.edu/~maxdet page is only reachable via the Wayback archive.

targets.name: Heilbronn triangle problem: new best configurations (square, triangle, convex region)
targets.statement: Place n points in a container (unit square, unit-area triangle, or an optimal convex region) to maximize the minimum area of a triangle formed by three of the points. Optimality is proven only for small n (square up to n=9; triangle up to n=8 per arXiv:2607.15021). Best known configurations for n up to 36 are tracked on Tej Stead's leaderboard. Optimality proofs: triangle n <= 8 (arXiv:2607.15021), square n <= 9 (arXiv:2603.11107). Rob Gardiner (renidrag) set square n = 21, 23, 25, 35 and triangle n = 20 records through Oct 2026; Lackovic (codrAlex) set convex n = 31 and 33 in late Sep 2026. Records change daily.
targets.success_criterion: Success means exact rational (or exactly specified algebraic) coordinates for n points (3 <= n <= 36) that meet all of the following. (1) Every point lies in the closed container, checked exactly. (2) The minimum over all C(n,3) triangles of |area|, computed in exact rational arithmetic and normalized as the leaderboard specifies (convex category: area of the convex hull of the points), is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the value shown for that (container, n) at https://math.tejstead.com/heilbronn re-fetched immediately before verification. (3) An independent local checker, written from the leaderboard's published normalization rules (not the site's own verifier; nothing is submitted), reproduces the value. Submitting to the leaderboard is the human's decision after review.

partial_wins.statement: An EinsteinArena Heilbronn record: a configuration for the EinsteinArena Heilbronn n=11 problem whose score, computed exactly under the arena's own scoring rules, strictly exceeds the live arena leaderboard best.

A new optimality certificate: a re-runnable rigorous computer-assisted proof (interval branch-and-bound with logged subdivision that the skeptic re-executes) that the best known configuration is optimal for the unit square at n = 10 or the triangle at n = 9, beyond arXiv:2603.11107 / 2607.15021.

targets.verification_method: Independent script with fractions.Fraction. Check containment (for the triangle container, use the leaderboard's exact vertices). Compute all triangle areas as |det|/2 exactly and take the min. Apply the normalization: divide by the container area or the convex-hull area, with the hull computed exactly. Compare against the live leaderboard figure. Require a strict improvement, and report the relative improvement.
angles: Use an active-set NLP. Maximize t subject to area_ijk >= t for the currently smallest ~50 triangles (with signs fixed by orientation), solved with SLSQP or IPOPT (pip cyipopt), re-identifying the active set iteratively. Then rationalize coordinates to high-precision fractions and re-verify exactly.
Run symmetry-constrained searches (C2, C3, D2 or mirror symmetry) to cut dimension. Many records are symmetric, so enumerate symmetry types systematically for the less-attacked n (26-36).
Exploit cross-container transfer. Map a strong triangle configuration into the convex category, then let the convex region adapt.
Do a final 'equalization' polish: solve the KKT system for the active triangles with Newton's method in mpmath at 50 digits, then verify exactly.
pitfalls: The records are moving daily, so re-fetch the leaderboard immediately before claiming.
Floating-point min-area can mislead at the 1e-12 level. Certify with exact rationals.
Area normalization differs between categories (unit square vs unit-area triangle vs convex hull).
Gains of under 1e-9 relative may be treated as ties, so confirm with the leaderboard verifier.
EinsteinArena also runs a Heilbronn n=11 problem with its own scoring, which is not the leaderboard.

targets.name: Kissing number lower bounds in dimensions 25-48 (beat the max over ALL sources, not Cohn's table)
targets.statement: Find K nonzero vectors of equal norm in R^d, 25 <= d <= 48, with every pairwise angle >= 60 degrees, so that K exceeds the best known kissing configuration for that d. WARNING: Cohn's table https://cohn.mit.edu/kissing-numbers is badly STALE for almost every d in 25..47 (checked live 2026-10-08 21:30Z). The records are spread over arXiv papers AND public GitHub repositories. Vetter's snapshot on 2026-10-08 (orientation only; NEVER use these as the bar, re-derive live): d25 197580 (Yang); d26 199806, d28 204896, d29 209968, d30 221012, d31 238662 (Kravatskiy repo RESULTS.md); d27 201567 (Yang); d32 347584, d33 363968, d34 384196, d35 409676, d36 484760, d37 498024, d38 591900, d39 763668, d43 2553792, d45 7380090 (Yang, arXiv:2609.35051 Table 1); d40 1092000, d41 1324472, d42 1792386, d44 4153600, d46 12309600, d47 23766960 (Dorofeev-Sun-Wang arXiv:2607.20359 / wcgbg sphere-packing repo / Boyvalenkov-Cherkashin arXiv:2312.05121); d48 52416000 (P48). Takhanov-Yun arXiv:2609.21591 (d25-31) and Echols arXiv:2608.13906 (d32-34, d37) are below these. For d=32..35 Yang's values equal exactly the modified Edel-Rains-Sloane bound tau_d >= 2^17 + 2^7*A(d,8,8) + 2d(d-1) with A = 1676/1803/1960/2158 (Brouwer's live Andw.html cells are lower: 1674/1800/1949/2157). For d36 the same bound needs A(36,8,8) >= 2744 to pass 484760. Yang's d36-39 values do not follow from his listed codes, so other constructions are involved there. The machine-verified V3R1T4S codes A(33,8,8) >= 1809 and A(34,8,8) >= 1965 (constant-weight-codes/ in this repository) would give tau33 >= 364736 and tau34 >= 384836 by the formula. This is [HEURISTIC] until an explicit configuration is built and checked.
targets.success_criterion: Success means K vectors in R^d (25 <= d <= 48), given EXACTLY with integer coordinates (or rational coordinates scaled to integers). All vectors must have identical squared norm Nsq, every pair must satisfy <x,y> <= Nsq/2, and no two vectors may coincide, all verified in exact integer arithmetic. K must be STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than B(d) = the maximum, over every dimension d' <= d (a configuration in R^{d'} embeds in R^d), of ALL of the following, each read LIVE at verification time: (i) the lower bound at https://cohn.mit.edu/kissing-numbers; (ii) every value in arXiv:2609.35051 (Yang et al., including its Table 1 'comparison' column and any later version), arXiv:2609.21591, arXiv:2608.13906, arXiv:2607.20359, arXiv:2511.13391, arXiv:2312.05121; (iii) every value in the public repositories https://github.com/alexlegeartis/KissingNumbers (RESULTS.md and contributed/), https://github.com/Oxelra-AI/Qiushi-Engine-Kissing-Number-Research, https://github.com/wcgbg/sphere-packing, and https://github.com/CDM1619/PackingStar; (iv) every value in any other arXiv paper, journal article, public repository or public catalogue found by a FRESH web + arXiv search at verification time, REGARDLESS of its date; (v) for d = 32..39, the value 2^17 + 2^7*L + 2d(d-1), where L is the largest A(d,8,8) lower bound in Brouwer's live https://aeb.win.tue.nl/codes/Andw.html or in any published source. If any source in (i)-(iv) cannot be read with an honest client (no spoofed User-Agent, no retry through 403/429, no CAPTCHA/JS-challenge bypass), the result is PENDING TABLE CHECK and NOT a success. K must not exceed the smallest published upper bound for d (Cohn's table or newer); exceeding it means a bug. A count from a formula alone is NOT a certificate: the vectors must be listed and checked. Beating Cohn's table alone is NOT a success.

partial_wins.statement: An improved upper bound: an SDP/LP certificate, verified in exact rational or interval arithmetic, proving a kissing-number upper bound strictly below the smallest published upper bound for some d in 25..48 (Cohn's live table, de Laat-Leijenhorst 2024, and anything newer found by a fresh search at verification time).

targets.verification_method:
Use an independent script.
- Load the vectors as integer arrays and assert every squared norm equals Nsq.
- Compute all Gram entries in blocks. A float32/float64 matmul is exact when |entries| * d * max|coord|^2 < 2^24 or 2^53; otherwise use int64 with overflow checks. Assert that every off-diagonal entry is <= Nsq/2.
- Sort the rows to assert that no two are equal.
- K ~ 3.6e5 in d=33 means about 6.5e10 pairs, a few minutes of blocked matmul on a laptop.
- If an Edel-Rains-Sloane-type construction is claimed, regenerate the vector set from the stated code and construction, assert it equals the submitted set, and check the code with an independent constant-weight checker (all popcounts w, pairwise distance >= 8).
- Compute B(d) live: re-fetch Cohn's page, the listed arXiv papers (latest versions), the four listed GitHub repos (RESULTS.md / README / constructions/), the Brouwer A(d,8,8) cells, and run a fresh web + arXiv search for any other source; take the max over all d' <= d. Quote URL, value and fetch time for every input. Any unreadable source => PENDING TABLE CHECK.
angles: Build the explicit configuration via the code link, tau_d >= 2^17 + 2^7*A(d,8,8) + 2d(d-1) (Edel-Rains-Sloane as modified in Echols eq. (2) / Yang Sec. 5), from the machine-verified V3R1T4S A(33,8,8) >= 1809 and A(34,8,8) >= 1965 codes. Check it exactly and compare against Yang's Table 1.

Push A(32,8,8) above 1676 and A(35,8,8) above 2158 (Yang's implied codes), and A(36,8,8) to >= 2744 (live Brouwer 2742), with the constant-weight-codes plateau-walk LNS engines (lb_lns_fast3). Each extra codeword adds +128 to tau_d. For d37-39, first find out which construction gives Yang's values.

d = 25..31: start from the Kravatskiy repo / Yang configurations (they are above Takhanov-Yun) if they are published as coordinates, and look for insertions via exact local search: a free spherical cap of angular radius 60 degrees found by LP or SAT over a lattice shell.

d = 40..47: the records are Conway-Sloane / P48p cross-section and antipode packings (Dorofeev-Sun-Wang, wcgbg repo), far above Cohn's entries; start from those, not from Cohn's Barnes-Wall/laminated values.
pitfalls: Cohn's table is stale for almost every d in 25..47 (e.g. d46/d47 by a factor of 2+). Beating it alone is NOT novel. Many records live only in GitHub repositories (Kravatskiy, Oxelra/Qiushi, wcgbg), not on arXiv; the bar is the max over ALL sources and all d' <= d.
Overlap: bank target kissing-number-low-dim has partial win p1 (d >= 24 vs Cohn's table only). That p1 is now dangerously loose; this entry's all-sources bar must govern any d in 25..48.
Yang's Table 1 comparison column (e.g. d25 197579, d43 2545056, d45 7379838) shows the previous bests came from repositories, not Cohn; read it.
Kravatskiy's repo lists d32-37 and d40-43 as exactly at the Edel-Rains-Sloane value; reproducing a known ERS configuration is not a win.
The construction's validity conditions (the shell components and their mutual inner products) must be checked in the explicit vector set, not assumed from the formula.
Floating-point near-feasible configurations do not count unless they are exactified.
Yang et al. and Kravatskiy update fast (commits within days); re-read repos and re-search arXiv at verification time.

targets.name: Kissing number lower bounds in dimensions 9-23
targets.statement: Find more unit spheres touching a central unit sphere without overlapping, i.e. a set of nonzero vectors of equal norm with pairwise angle >= 60 degrees, in dimensions 9-23. Cohn's table (2026): d9 306, d10 510, d11 604, d12 841, d13 1154, d14 1932, d15 2564, d16 4320, d17 5730, d18 7654, d19 11948, d20 19448, d21 29768, d22 49896, d23 93150. Attributions: d11 592 (Ganzhinov 2025) -> 593 (AlphaEvolve) -> 604 (Bianchi-Kwon-Pappu-Zou, arXiv:2606.10402, EinsteinArena, 'recently solved, certified'); d12 840 -> 841 (Takhanov-Assylbekov-Yun, arXiv:2606.18984); d14 1932 (Ganzhinov 2025); d19 11948 (Ho, arXiv:2603.10425). Sep 2026 work (arXiv:2609.35051, 2609.21591) only improved d >= 25.
targets.success_criterion: Success means K vectors in R^d (9 <= d <= 23) given exactly (integer/rational coordinates or exact algebraic numbers in a specified field), all with identical squared norm N and every pair with <x,y> <= N/2, verified in exact arithmetic, no two coinciding, with K STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the lower bound for dimension d at https://cohn.mit.edu/kissing-numbers/ at verification time (and any newer arXiv claim). Floating-point configurations with tiny overlap loss do NOT qualify unless exactified.

partial_wins.statement: An exact kissing configuration in a dimension d >= 24 listed in Cohn's table, verified in exact arithmetic, with size strictly greater than the live table value for that d (several were moved in Sep 2026, so re-check).

A rigorous upper-bound improvement: an SDP/LP certificate verified in exact rational or interval arithmetic proving a kissing-number upper bound strictly below the live Cohn-table upper bound for some d in 9..23.

targets.verification_method: Use exact integer arithmetic. Scale the coordinates to integers, compute all Gram entries as Python ints, and assert the diagonal is constant and the off-diagonal entries are <= diag/2. For K ~ 600-12000, the Gram matrix is up to 1.4e8 entries, so use numpy int64 with overflow checks or chunked object arithmetic. Check that no two vectors coincide.
angles: Start from the structure of the 604 d11 configuration (480 vectors from D11+ orbits plus extras) and apply analogous 'lattice orbit plus deep-hole insertion' in d13 and d14 from laminated lattices Lambda_13 and K_13.
Use Ganzhinov's symmetric-search method: prescribe a large group (e.g. a subgroup of W(E8) x W(A_k)), so candidates are unions of orbits. Solve the max-clique of compatible orbits exactly.
Project or slice the Leech lattice and Barnes-Wall configurations and look for antipodal-pair swaps that free room, certified exactly.
Do continuous optimization with an energy term, then snap to a rational lattice (LLL on the scaled coordinates) to obtain an exact certificate.
pitfalls: A near-zero overlap loss is not a proof. Exact certification is mandatory.
Cohn's table is the source of truth, and d11/d12 moved in 2026.
Vectors must have equal norm exactly, not only up to rounding.

targets.name: Low-autocorrelation binary sequences: best-known merit factors for lengths 67-600
targets.statement: For a +-1 sequence s of length L, the aperiodic autocorrelations are C_k = sum_i s_i s_{i+k}, the energy is E = sum_{k=1}^{L-1} C_k^2, and the merit factor is F = L^2/(2E). Optimal E is known for all L <= 66 (Packebusch-Mertens 2016), and optimal skew-symmetric values are known up to 119. For larger L, only best-known values exist. They were improved in 2025 for 16 lengths in 92..120 (arXiv:2504.00987) and in Jun 2026 for 35 lengths in 450..527 plus L=573 (arXiv:2607.09688). Any sequence with lower energy than the best known for its length is a new record. OPEN and active as of 2026-10-03. Latest: Psenicnik-Boskovic-Popic-Brest, arXiv:2607.09688 (17 Jun 2026). Lengths 121..449 and above 527 may be softer.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an explicit +-1 sequence of length L with 67 <= L <= 600 whose exactly computed integer energy E = sum_{k>=1} C_k^2 is STRICTLY SMALLER (direction: min) than the best published energy for that L at verification time, taken as the minimum over the tables in arXiv:2607.09688, arXiv:2504.00987, the Boskovic et al. LABS records repository cited there, and any newer arXiv result. Compare integer energies, never rounded merit factors. For L <= 66 the optimum is proven; lower energy there means a bug.

partial_wins.statement: A skew-symmetric record: a skew-symmetric +-1 sequence of odd length L >= 121 whose exact energy is strictly below the best published skew-symmetric energy for that L at verification time (even if not below the unrestricted record).

A proven skew-symmetric optimum at L = 121 (one step past the published skew frontier of 119): an exhaustive branch-and-bound with re-runnable code and logs that the skeptic re-executes, reporting the optimal skew energy and a sequence attaining it.

targets.verification_method: Compute C_k exactly with integer arithmetic (numpy int64 correlate or a direct O(L^2) loop) and E = sum C_k^2 as a Python int. Compare integer energies, not rounded merit factors. Calibrate by recomputing the energy of a published record sequence for a nearby L. Check that the length and alphabet are correct.
angles: Run memetic tabu search (Gallardo-Cotta-Fernandez style) with O(L) incremental energy updates per flip, as massively parallel restarts on 10 cores. Target lengths in 121..449 that the 2026 paper did not focus on.
Do a two-stage search: first in the skew-symmetric subspace for odd L (half the variables), then unrestricted refinement, following arXiv:2607.09688.
Use Legendre/rotated-Legendre and Jacobi sequence seeds with appended segments (Kirilusha-Narayanaswamy style) followed by local search, for large L.
Use self-avoiding-walk search with Thompson-sampling prioritization of search regions.
pitfalls: Comparing rounded merit factors. Compare exact integer energies.
Best-known tables are scattered across papers with no single live table, so assemble the baseline from all cited sources and state which one was beaten.
For L <= 66 the optimum is proven, and for skew-symmetric odd L <= 119 the skew optimum is proven but general sequences can beat it (2504.00987 did so for 99, 107, 109, 113, 119).

targets.name: Shannon capacity of odd cycles: larger independent sets in strong powers
targets.statement: An independent set S in the strong product C_m^{⊠d} gives Theta(C_m) >= |S|^(1/d). Improve the best known lower bound for Theta(C_m), m odd. For C7 this is Ben Green's open problem #38 (formal-conjectures GreensOpenProblems/38.lean): the largest A in F_7^d with (A-A) ∩ {-1,0,1}^d = {0}. Tao's optimization-constants repo lists Theta(C7) as constant C_9 (constants/9a.md). As of 2026-10-03: Theta(C7) >= 3.25883262... (Ravi Tandon, arXiv:2608.30273, 31 Aug 2026, heterogeneous recursion in C7^{⊠500}; cited on 9a.md under the key [Tan2026]), with other 2026 C7 values 3.25878915 (Gao, arXiv:2607.27869), 3.25880537 (Buys-Polak-Zuiddam, Lean-verified, arXiv:2607.29681) and 3.2580207 (Itty-Rosin-Carstensen-Reichman, 134,753 in C7^{⊠10}, arXiv:2607.21517). Buys-Polak-Zuiddam also give C11 >= 5.294502522, C13 >= 6.302455083, C15 >= 7.301600534, C19 >= 9.357192706, C21 >= 10.342455853, C23 >= 11.328224258, superseding Itty et al. X-evolve found an independent set of size 19,946 in C15^{⊠5}. The published alpha(C7^{⊠5}) baseline is 367 (Polak-Schrijver 2018, arXiv:1808.07438). EinsteinArena hosts 'Shannon Capacity C7^5: find 368 words' (arena best 367). Because 368^(1/5) ~ 3.259639 > 3.25883262 (equivalently record^5 ~ 367.545 < 368), a 368-element independent set in C7^{⊠5} would itself beat the capacity record; 367^(1/5) ~ 3.257866 does not.
targets.success_criterion: Capacity record: an explicit independent set S in C_m^{⊠d} (m odd; pairwise non-adjacent, verified exhaustively), or a fully specified recursive construction whose every finite ingredient is explicitly listed and verified and whose limiting rate is independently re-derived, giving a lower bound on Theta(C_m) (|S|^(1/d), computed with mpmath to 30 digits) STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the best lower bound for that m at verification time: the max over the live primary table https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/blob/main/constants/9a.md (C7 table; the other odd cycles are in its comments), arXiv:2608.30273, 2607.29681, 2607.27869, 2607.21517 and any newer arXiv result, using the record's exact digits. A finite-dimension set must beat the asymptotic record itself, not just an earlier fixed-dimension value. Against the 2026-10-03 C7 record 3.25883262... (recompute against the live record) this means |S| >= 368 in d=5, >= 1198 in d=6, >= 3904 in d=7, >= 12,721 in d=8, >= 41,454 in d=9, or >= 135,090 in d=10. In particular a verified 368-element independent set in C7^{⊠5} (the EinsteinArena target) IS a full capacity record, since 368^(1/5) ~ 3.259639 > 3.25883262; 367 (Polak-Schrijver 2018) gives only 3.257866. A fixed-d independence-number record below these thresholds is not claim-level.

partial_wins.statement: An explicit independent set in C7^{⊠10} of size strictly greater than the best published explicit C7^{⊠10} set at verification time (134,753, Itty-Rosin-Carstensen-Reichman 2026, arXiv:2607.21517, on 2026-10-03) but below the asymptotic threshold (135,090 at the 2026-10-03 record; larger sets are full successes), verified by an exhaustive pair check.
An independent set in C15^{⊠5} of size strictly greater than X-evolve's 19,946 and any newer published value, verified exhaustively.

A fixed-dimension independence record for another odd cycle: an independent set in C_m^{⊠d} (m odd, m >= 9) whose size strictly exceeds the best published alpha(C_m^{⊠d}) found at verification time (including the 2026 papers listed above), verified exhaustively.

targets.verification_method: Two distinct vectors x,y are adjacent iff for every coordinate i, (x_i - y_i) mod m is in {0,1,m-1}. Check all pairs by vectorized numpy, or bucket by coordinates to make it near-linear. Check all elements are distinct and in range. Compute |S|^(1/d) with mpmath to 30 digits and compare with the live record; equivalently check |S| > record^d exactly. For recursive constructions, rebuild the full set if its size is under ~1e8, or verify each gadget plus the composition lemma symbolically.
angles: Search independent sets in C_m^{⊠d} that are invariant under a cyclic group (x -> x + v, or coordinate rotations). Reduce to max independent set on the quotient orbit graph, solved by CP-SAT.
Extend Tandon's heterogeneous recursion: use different auxiliary independent sets at different recursion depths, optimized jointly by ILP over a small catalog of gadgets.
Target the larger odd cycles C9, C17, C19 and C21, whose records may not have been touched in 2026, since most effort went to C7.
Use linear codes over Z_m (lattice-based independent sets) as seeds, then local search to add points.

Attack the EinsteinArena C7^{⊠5} 368 target with orbit-quotient CP-SAT. It is not just a stepping stone: 368^(1/5) ~ 3.25964 beats the capacity record, so 368 would be a full success. 367 has stood since Polak-Schrijver 2018, so expect it to be hard.

Low dimensions with structure: search for A in F_7^6 (or F_7^7) invariant under a large group (coordinate permutations combined with multiplication by units), using exact cover / CP-SAT on orbits. 1198 in dimension 6 versus the trivial product 367*3 = 1101 is a crisp target.
Local improvement of the published 134,753-element set in C_7^{⊠10}: delete-k / add-(k+1) swaps guided by conflict graphs, run in parallel on 10 cores.

Better gadgets for the Gao/Tan recursions: search small heterogeneous blocks (mixing C_7^{⊠2}, C_7^{⊠3} and C_7^{⊠5} gadgets with 'valid tuple' compatibility) whose recursion eigenvalue beats Tan's. The rate is computable from a small transfer matrix.
Algebraic constructions: images of codes over GF(7) or Z_49 under Lee-metric-like maps, and quadratic-residue / Paley-type sets in F_7^m.
pitfalls: The capacity bound needs |S|^(1/d), not |S|/m^d. Check the exponent carefully.
Confusing an independence-number record at fixed d with a capacity record.
Several 2026 papers within weeks, so the record must be re-searched immediately before claiming.
Four C7 papers appeared within five weeks (Jul-Aug 2026). Compare against all of them, not just Tandon.

Exponent arithmetic: 368^(1/5) ~ 3.259639 is ABOVE the C7 record 3.25883262 (record^5 ~ 367.545), so a verified 368-set in C7^{⊠5} is a full capacity record, while 367^(1/5) ~ 3.257866 only matches Polak-Schrijver 2018. Recompute thresholds as floor(record^d)+1 against the live record.
Adjacency in the strong product means each coordinate is equal or adjacent, not all equal; get this exactly right.
Confusing a finite-level value with the limiting rate of a recursion.
Records moved four times in Jul-Sep 2026; re-check the repo and arXiv.
Probable-correctness search outputs with no exhaustive pair check.
Re-fetch 9a.md and arXiv on the day; a fifth 2026 improvement may have landed after 2026-09-26.
A finite-dimension set must beat the asymptotic recursive limit, not just the old fixed-dimension value (e.g. 1102 in dim 6 beats nothing asymptotically).
Attribution: Tao's 9a page cites the 3.25883262 record under the key [Tan2026]; that is R. Tandon (arXiv:2608.30273), not a separate 'Tan 2026' result.

targets.name: Small two-color Ramsey numbers: new lower bounds via explicit graphs
targets.statement: Exhibit a graph on N vertices with no K_s and no independent set of size t, proving R(s,t) >= N+1 and beating the current best lower bound for some (s,t), or the analogous multicolor result. Very active as of 2026-10-03. Latest: Yu (arXiv:2608.18169 v2, 24 Aug 2026) and Coniglio-Furini-Ljubic-San Segundo-Thuerauf-Traversi (arXiv:2608.18769, 19 Aug 2026). An arXiv API scan of Ramsey papers from Sep 2026 showed no further small-cell lower-bound papers. AlphaEvolve (arXiv:2603.09172 v5) also moved R(4,16) 170->174, R(4,18) 205->209, R(4,19) 213->219 and R(4,20) 234->237 (since superseded by Yu's 252); exact circulant Ramsey numbers R_C(3,n) for n=13..20 were computed in arXiv:2608.18769, so plain circulant search there is exhausted.
targets.success_criterion: Success means an adjacency matrix of a graph G on N vertices, symmetric with zero diagonal, such that omega(G) < s and alpha(G) < t are certified exactly by two independent methods (exhaustive B&B and an UNSAT proof). N+1 must be STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the best lower bound for R(s,t) at verification time, taken as the maximum over Radziszowski's dynamic survey DS1 (latest revision) and every 2026 paper or repository found by a fresh search (at minimum arXiv:2603.09172 v5, ScaleAutoResearch-Ramsey, arXiv:2608.18169 v2, arXiv:2608.18769). Off-by-one: a graph on N vertices proves R(s,t) >= N+1.

partial_wins.statement: A multicolour classical Ramsey record: an explicit edge colouring of K_N with no monochromatic forbidden clique in each colour (e.g. a 4-colouring of K_51 with no monochromatic triangle, giving R(3,3,3,3) >= 52), verified exhaustively, with N+1 strictly above the best lower bound in DS1 and any newer arXiv paper for that multicolour cell.

A new exact circulant Ramsey number: the exact value of R_C(4,k) (or R_C(5,k)) for some k with no published value, certified by an exhaustive search over all circulant connection sets that the skeptic re-runs, together with an explicit extremal circulant graph checked by two exact clique methods.

targets.verification_method: Run two independent exact clique solvers on G and on its complement. One is a custom bitset branch-and-bound (Tomita/MCS style) or networkx max_weight_clique. The other is a pysat/CaDiCaL encoding asking 'is there a K_s?', which must come back UNSAT, and likewise for independent sets of size t. Both must agree. Hash the matrix. Then do a literature check on arXiv for the past 6 months for that (s,t). For circulant graphs, also verify the expanded full graph, not only the connection set.
primary_sources: https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/DS1 (Radziszowski dynamic survey; not opened this session)
targets.status_source: https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/DS1 (Radziszowski dynamic survey; not opened this session)
angles: Use circulant and block-circulant graphs on primes or near-primes, with connection sets from cyclotomic classes (Yu's quintic classes mod 251). Sweep all small-index cyclotomic constructions for (4,k) and (5,k) cells.

Use Exoo-style 'one-vertex extension'. Take the current record graph on N-1 vertices and search for a neighbourhood vector of a new vertex with SAT (clauses forbidding the K_{s-1} in the neighbourhood and the independent (t-1)-set in the non-neighbourhood). Iterate with small perturbations of the base graph.
Use the IP over projected distance space from 2608.18769, extended to two-orbit (bi-circulant) graphs. It was only applied to plain circulants and mostly R(3,n).
Use tabu search on edge flips with an objective counting K_s plus independent t-sets, sampled by fast clique enumeration, starting from Paley-type or cyclotomic seeds.
Try multicolor and hypergraph cells (R(3,3,4), R(3,3,3,3) >= 51 -> 52 is a moonshot), where AI pipelines have not swept.
Auditor: plain circulant search for R(3,13..20) cannot beat R_C(3,n); use non-circulant or block-circulant graphs there.
After any R(4,k) construction, check both R(4,20) and R(4,21) (Yu's order-251 circulants moved both).
pitfalls: Stale baseline. Several cells changed in Mar-Aug 2026, and DS1 may lag, so always grep arXiv for the specific R(s,t).
A heuristic clique search that misses a clique gives a false positive. Require an exact UNSAT proof or exhaustive B&B.
Off-by-one: a graph on N vertices proves R(s,t) >= N+1, i.e. R > N.
Confusing the circulant Ramsey number R_C(3,n) with R(3,n).
R_C(3,n) for n=13..20 is now exactly known, so exhaustive circulant search there cannot beat the circulant optimum. Use non-circulant or block-circulant graphs.
R(4,16..20) were all moved by AlphaEvolve in 2026, so do not assume DS1 values are current.
Yu's order-251 graphs raise R(4,21) too. Check both cells after any R(4,k) construction.

targets.name: Snake-in-the-box / coil-in-the-box records in dimensions 9-13
targets.statement: Find longer induced paths (snakes) or induced cycles (coils) in the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n. Maxima are proven for snakes in n <= 8 (98 at n=8). In dimension 9 and up, only lower bounds are known. The live minortriad.com/snake table (dimensions 1-13; snakes, coils and symmetric coils) is ahead of the paper tables of Orland-Fagan et al. (arXiv:2607.15270 v3, 30 Sep 2026) in Q11-Q13. EinsteinArena's 13D snake problem lists 2934.
