targets.success_criterion: Success means a valid induced path (snake) or induced cycle (coil) in Q_n, 9 <= n <= 13, verified exhaustively (single-bit steps, distinct vertices, popcount(v_i ^ v_j) >= 2 for non-consecutive pairs, closing edge induced for coils), whose edge length is STRICTLY GREATER (direction: max) than the maximum, at verification time, of: the live primary table https://www.minortriad.com/snake/, the Math-AI-Caltech/Snake-in-the-Box README 'subsequent bounds by others' lists (https://github.com/Math-AI-Caltech/Snake-in-the-Box), the latest arXiv:2607.15270 version, the EinsteinArena value (13D snake) and any newer source from a fresh search, for that dimension and type (context on 2026-10-03: snakes Q9-Q13 191/379/750/1480/2938, coils 192/374/740/1468/2930). The verifier's checker must reproduce the exact length of at least one downloaded record file of the same n and type (length-convention calibration); without that calibration the claim is not a record.

partial_wins.statement: A symmetric-coil record: a coil in Q_n (9 <= n <= 13) that is invariant under the symmetry required by the minortriad symmetric-coil table, verified exhaustively, whose length strictly exceeds the live minortriad symmetric-coil value for that n (context: Q9 186, Q10 370, Q11 730, Q12 1434, Q13 2830).

A Q14 record: a snake or coil in Q14, verified exhaustively, strictly longer than every Q14 value published at verification time (arXiv:2607.15270 v3 tables, EinsteinArena, Math-AI-Caltech repo); counts only if such a published value exists for comparison.

An equal-record snake or coil: length equal to the live record (as defined in the success criterion) for that n and type, 9 <= n <= 13, verified exhaustively, and inequivalent under hypercube automorphisms (coordinate permutations and translations) and reversal (plus cyclic rotation for coils) to every record file published in the Math-AI-Caltech repository and the arXiv:2607.15270 data at verification time, checked by comparing canonical relabelled transition sequences.

targets.verification_method: Use an independent O(L^2) bit check, or O(L*n) with a hash set of vertices plus a check that each vertex's n neighbours contain at most 2 path members (1 for endpoints), all at the right positions. Confirm the length convention against the table by re-verifying a known record snake from the Math-AI-Caltech repo.
angles: Target coils and symmetric coils, which may be less heavily attacked than snakes in 2026. Convert snakepit ideas to cycles.
Splice from lower dimensions. Combine two record snakes in Q_{n-1} with a 1-bit lift and search the junction region exhaustively with SAT (pysat) on a small window.

Do window re-optimization. Take a record snake, cut out a segment of 30-60 vertices, and solve 'longest induced path between the fixed endpoints avoiding the rest's closed neighbourhood' exactly with CP-SAT. Repeat at all offsets.
Use symmetry prescription. Require invariance under a hypercube automorphism of order 2-4 (a coordinate permutation composed with XOR), which shrinks the space as in symmetric coil records.
Run Monte-Carlo beam search with a learned 'remaining free volume' heuristic: the count of vertices with no path neighbour.

Tail re-growth: take record snakes, cut the last 10-30% and regrow exhaustively with a bitset DFS plus a dead-vertex pruning bound. Use all 100+ inequivalent 190-snakes from the paper's repository as seeds for n=9.
Lift record (n-1) snakes and coils into Q_n through doubling constructions with permutation 'spreads', then local-repair with SAT (pysat with cadical) on a window of the sequence.
Nested Monte Carlo or limited-discrepancy search with a learned priority, comparing with the Beam Anchor idea from 2607.15270.
Exploit the 'snakepit' idea from the paper: pack disjoint snakes, then splice them through short bridges found by exact search.
Symmetric snakes: require the snake to be invariant under a hypercube automorphism of order 2 or 4. This halves the search, and many records are near-symmetric.
pitfalls: Length conventions: edges vs vertices, and whether a coil counts edges in the cycle. Calibrate on a known record.
Snakes vs coils vs symmetric coils are separate tables.
Values for Q10-Q13 come from 2607.15270's tables. Confirm the live minortriad value before claiming.
Paper tables lag the minortriad table. In Q11-Q13 minortriad is already 2-14 edges longer (snakes +4/+4/+14, coils +6/+2/+14).
Length conventions differ between sources (vertices vs edges, closed vs open).
Records changed in July-September 2026. Read the latest arXiv version and the repository.
A path that is only distance-preserving (no chords checked) is not induced.
The README 'subsequent bounds' already beat the paper at n=11, 12 and 13. Do not use the paper table alone.
Coil records may have moved after publication, so search for the newest values before claiming a coil.
Older bank copies list stale values (snake Q13 2934; coils Q11 734, Q12 1466, Q13 2916). The live values on 2026-10-03 were snake Q13 2938 and coils 740/1468/2930.

targets.name: Sorting networks: fewer comparators than the best known for n = 16..32
targets.statement: S(n) is the minimum number of comparators in a network that sorts every input on n channels. Optimality is proven only for n <= 12 (size) and for n <= 17 (depth). For n=16, the best known size is 60, which has stood since Green in 1969. For n=17..32, the best known sizes from Dobbelaere's SorterHunter table are: 17: 71, 18: 77, 19: 85, 20: 91, 21: 99, 22: 106, 23: 114, 24: 120, 25: 130, 26: 138, 27: 147, 28: 155, 29: 164, 30: 172, 31: 180, 32: 185. Best known depths: n = 13-16: 9 (optimal), 17: 10 (optimal), 18-20: 11, 21-24: 12, 25-28: 13 (27 and 28 lowered from 14 to 13 by Chengu Wang, arXiv:2511.04107), 29-32: 14. The table also records Pareto (size, depth) pairs. Any network with fewer comparators than listed for some n, with smaller depth than the best listed depth, or with a (size, depth) pair not dominated by a listed pair, is a record. OPEN as of 2026-10-03. Dobbelaere's page was last updated 7 Nov 2025, with Chengu Wang's depth-13 networks for 27 and 28 channels (arXiv:2511.04107). An arXiv API scan found no 2026 size records. EinsteinArena lists 'Sorting Network (16 inputs): under 60 comparators' as a new problem with no score yet. Dobbelaere's extended page covers n = 2..64 with (size, depth) pairs.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a list of comparators (i,j), 0 <= i < j < n, standard min-to-i form, with 13 <= n <= 32, that sorts all 2^n binary inputs (0-1 principle), checked exhaustively, and that is STRICTLY BETTER (direction: min for both size and depth) than the live Dobbelaere table at https://bertdobbelaere.github.io/sorting_networks_extended.html at verification time in at least one of these ways: (a) its comparator count is strictly smaller than the table's smallest size for that n; (b) its depth (greedy layering) is strictly smaller than the table's best depth for that n, at any size; or (c) its (size, depth) pair is not dominated by any pair listed for that n, i.e. no listed (s', d') has s' <= size and d' <= depth. For n=16 it must also beat the live EinsteinArena leaderboard, and it must beat any newer arXiv/GitHub claim (context on 2026-10-03: n=16 size 60, n=32 size 185; best depths 9 for n=13-16, 10 for 17, 13 for 25-28, 14 for 29-32). A network below a proven lower bound listed on the page for 13 <= n <= 32 (the min size or min depth bound columns, e.g. depth below 9 for n=13-16 or below 10 for n=17) means a bug, not a record. n <= 12 sizes are proven optimal; a smaller network there means a bug.

partial_wins.statement: A Pareto (size, depth) improvement for some n in 33..64 on Dobbelaere's extended table at verification time, verified exhaustively by the 0-1 principle (bit-sliced over 2^n inputs, or by an exact prefix/output-set method the skeptic re-runs).

A new optimal-size proof: a SAT-based proof, with a DRAT certificate checked by drat-trim, that no sorting network on n channels (13 <= n <= 16) has fewer comparators than a given bound strictly above the best published lower bound for that n.

targets.verification_method: Use an independent C or numpy bit-sliced simulator. Represent the 2^n inputs as n bit-vectors across 64-bit words. Each comparator (i,j) does a_i, a_j = a_i & a_j, a_i | a_j. At the end, check that each channel row is monotone (sorted output means every input word maps to a pattern 0..01..1, i.e. a_k <= a_{k+1} bitwise). For n=32 that is 2^32 inputs times about 185 comparators over 64-bit words, which takes minutes in C. Compute depth by greedy ASAP layering. Calibrate on a Dobbelaere network for the same n.
angles: Run SorterHunter-style evolutionary search with a prescribed prefix (e.g. a Green-type filter or reflection-symmetric first layers) and stochastic suffix completion. Target n=21..30 where the table cites only SorterHunter.
Do symmetric (reflection-invariant) network search, which halves the variables. Many records are symmetric.

Use SAT for the last layers: fix the first k layers from a good prefix, compute the set of reachable unsorted outputs (much smaller than 2^n), and ask a SAT solver for the minimum completion (Bundala-Ehlers/Codish technique).
For n=16 below 60 (moonshot), use prefix-optimization with exact SAT completion over the outputs remaining after a 4-layer Green filter.
Get depth records via Wang's 2025 technique, extended to n=29..32 or n=33..40.
SorterHunter-style evolution (prefix plus greedy completion), seeded with the newest Wang25 depth-13 networks, while targeting a size reduction at fixed depth.

Symmetric (reflection-invariant) networks: Wang's depth-13 networks were reflection-symmetric. Enforce symmetry to halve the search, and combine high-quality 16- and 12-channel prefixes as in 2511.04107.

SAT-based suffix optimization: fix the first d layers, compute the set of unsorted outputs that remain, and solve the minimal-size suffix exactly with CaDiCaL plus subsumption-based pruning (the Codish-style 'prefix + SAT' approach).
Target n values where the size-depth Pareto front has visible gaps relative to neighbouring n (interpolate from n-1 and n+1 records).
pitfalls: Testing only random permutations is not a proof. Use the exhaustive 0-1 principle.
Comparator orientation: reversed comparators (i > j) are non-standard networks and are not accepted.
n <= 12 sizes are proven optimal, so beating them means a bug.
The Dobbelaere page has not been updated since Nov 2025, so also grep arXiv/GitHub and the EinsteinArena leaderboard for newer claims.
Testing random inputs instead of all 2^n binary vectors. Only the exhaustive 0-1 check is a proof.
Miscounting depth when comparators in one layer share a channel.
Comparing against an old copy of the page. Re-fetch it at verification time.
Comparators with i>j (reverse comparators) make the network non-standard. Normalize or reject them.
Depth is proven optimal for n <= 17 (9 for 13-16, 10 for 17), and the page lists size and depth lower bounds for every n. A result below a listed lower bound is a checker bug, not a record.
A (size, depth) pair that ties a listed pair, or is dominated by one, is not a record. Check every listed pair for that n, not only the smallest-size one.

targets.name: Shorter superpermutations for n=7 (below 5905) or n=8 (below 46204)
targets.statement: Find a string over {1..n} containing all n! permutations as contiguous substrings that is shorter than the best known. For n=7 the record is 5905 (Teodorescu, 17 Aug 2026) with lower bound 5884. For n=8 it is 46204 (Uku Raudvere, 26 Jul 2026). For n=9 it is 408965 and for n=10 it is 4037046 (Echols, Jul 2026, GPT-5.6-Sol), and Raudvere also posted n=11..13.
targets.success_criterion: Success means a string over the alphabet {1..n} (n in 7..10) in which all n! permutations occur as length-n substrings, verified exhaustively, whose length is STRICTLY SMALLER (direction: min) than the best length at verification time on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superpermutation and the superpermutators group (context on 2026-10-03: 5905 for n=7, 46204 for n=8, 408965 for n=9, 4037046 for n=10). For n=7 the length must also be >= 5884; anything shorter means a bug.

partial_wins.statement: A superpermutation for n in 11..13, verified exhaustively, strictly shorter than Raudvere's live record for that n (context: 43,948,807 / 522,910,088 / 6,749,568,009).

A lower bound for n=7 strictly above 5884, delivered as a re-runnable computer-assisted proof (exact ILP or exhaustive search with certificate) that the skeptic re-executes, after confirming no stronger lower bound is published.

targets.verification_method: Slide a window of length n and add each window that is a permutation (n distinct symbols) to a set. Assert the set size is n!, the alphabet is exactly {1..n}, and the length is below the record. For n=10 the string is ~4M characters, which is trivial to check.
angles: For n=8, apply the Egan/Houston kernel method with the newer 2026 tricks Raudvere used. Search palindromic kernels of higher weight and use the 2-cycle graph cover with a cheaper ATSP solve (LKH via pip 'lkh' or elkai) on the 7!-node 'cycle graph'.

Treat it as ATSP on the permutation graph with edge weights 1..n and use an exact or near-exact solver on reduced quotient graphs (by symmetry). For n=7, solve on the 5040-node graph with elkai/LKH and many restarts, exploiting symmetry to restrict the search.
Lift a better n=7 solution through the Williams/Egan-style constructions to n=8 and beyond, which gives cascading improvements.
Look for a structural insight in Teodorescu's 5905: identify which 'weight-3 or weight-4 edges' it saves and generalize.
pitfalls: Counting a window with repeated symbols as a permutation.
Alphabet/length off-by-one.
The n=7 record changed in Aug 2026 and n=8 in Jul 2026. Always re-check the superpermutators group.
Raudvere's n=11-13 lengths (43,948,807; 522,910,088; 6,749,568,009) are also live baselines if one lifts constructions upward.

targets.name: Precovery of known asteroids in public ZTF / Pan-STARRS / DECam images, extending the observed arc
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (cutouts are ~1-10 MB each; orbit propagation is seconds; the limiting step is choosing objects whose back-propagated positions fall in archive coverage; MPCORB.DAT is 319 MB, NEA.txt is small)
targets.statement: For a known minor planet (MPCORB / NEA.txt / JPL SBDB), find and measure its image in public archival survey frames (ZTF science images via IRSA IBE, Pan-STARRS1 cutouts via ps1images, DECam via the NOIRLab SIA service) at an epoch EARLIER than the object's first observation recorded by JPL SBDB (orbit.first_obs) / MPC (MPCORB arc column; the object's full observation record via the MPC get-obs API, which answers a GET request carrying a JSON body {"desigs":[...],"output_format":["OBS80"]}, or the MPCAT-OBS NumObs/UnnObs files), such that the detection lies inside the back-propagated orbit covariance, its astrometry has residuals consistent with the orbit (< 2 arcsec, after refitting the orbit with the new point), and the source is absent from the static sky (not in Gaia DR3 / PS1 catalogs at that position and absent in other-epoch frames). No MPC submission is made; the claim is 'precovery detection, verified against the current orbit'. arXiv:2510.07588 (Oct 2025) ran an automated version on ZTF for ~3,000 NEAs, so novelty requires the specific epoch to be absent from the object's MPC observation record.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle {object designation, JPL SBDB JSON (orbit, covariance, first_obs) as fetched, the MPC observation record for the object as fetched (get-obs API OBS80 output or the MPCAT-OBS extract), archival image identifiers and download URLs, cutout FITS for every frame used, source detections with centroid and RA/Dec/uncertainty, predicted position and 3-sigma error ellipse from back-propagation (code saved), refit orbit residuals including the new points, static-sky check} such that: (1) the image epoch precedes JPL SBDB orbit.first_obs for that object (https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.api?sstr=<designation>, re-fetched live immediately before claiming) by at least one apparition (> 60 days), and the MPC observation record for the object (get-obs API, re-fetched live) contains no observation within 1 day of that epoch; (2) >= 2 detections of the object in distinct frames (same night separated by >= 20 min, or different nights), each inside the propagated 3-sigma ellipse, with the measured motion vector between them consistent with the predicted rate and direction within 3 sigma; (3) the residual of each detection against the a-priori orbit is inside the 3-sigma ellipse AND the refit orbit residual at the new epochs is < 2 arcsec (< 1 arcsec for PS1), with the refit changing the semi-major axis by less than its a-priori 3-sigma; (4) the predicted magnitude is within 1.5 mag of the measured one; (5) no static source is present at any detection position in another-epoch frame or in Gaia DR3/PS1 catalogs within 2 arcsec, and a SkyBoT cone search at each epoch shows no other known object within 30 arcsec. Claim is 'precovery detection, verified against the current orbit'; nothing is submitted to the MPC.

partial_wins.statement: For >= 10 objects, re-detect in public ZTF/PS1 frames observations that ARE in the MPC record (same epoch), recovering the recorded astrometry to < 1 arcsec; proves the image-retrieval and astrometry chain.
A single-frame detection satisfying (1),(3),(4),(5) with no second frame available: logged as 'unvetted single detection', never claimed.
Stretch tier: a fully verified precovery (all of (1)-(5)) that doubles an object's data arc (new arc >= 2x JPL data_arc) for an object with data_arc < 365 d; independently checkable against SBDB.

Stretch tier: a fully verified precovery (> 60 d earlier) for an object with n_obs_used < 50 in SBDB, where the added points reduce the semi-major-axis uncertainty by > 50% in the refit; the covariance before/after saved.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-fetches the SBDB JSON and the MPC get-obs record for the object, re-downloads the named cutouts from the saved URLs, re-measures the centroids with the saved script, re-propagates the orbit (saved code) to the frame epochs, and checks the ellipse, the motion vector and the residuals. Under one hour.
angles: Target recently discovered NEAs (NEA.txt entries with first-observation year 2025-2026 and arcs < 1 year) whose back-propagated 2018-2024 positions fall in ZTF's northern footprint; the 2510.07588 pipeline shows ~500 arc-doublings were possible, so plenty remain for objects discovered after their run.
Pan-STARRS1 (2010-2014 epochs, 3pi survey, r ~ 22) for objects discovered 2020+: a 10-year arc extension, with 1-arcsec-class astrometry.
DECam public frames (NOIRLab SIA) for southern objects that ZTF/PS1 cannot reach.
Synthetic tracking: shift-and-stack several ZTF frames from one night along the predicted motion to reach ~1 mag fainter than single frames.
Use SkyBoT cone searches to reject the case where another known object is at the predicted position.
pitfalls: Static stars, galaxies, hot pixels, cosmic rays and diffraction spikes at the predicted position: require the source to be absent in a different-epoch frame of the same field and in Gaia DR3/PS1 catalogs.

A detection at an epoch already in the MPC observation record (possibly reported by the archive's own team, e.g. the ZTF precovery pipeline of arXiv:2510.07588) is not an arc extension: check the full observation list for the object, not just SBDB first_obs, and re-fetch both right before claiming.

Error ellipses for short-arc objects can span degrees years back; a faint source somewhere inside a huge ellipse is likely a chance match - require a magnitude match and a refit residual < 2 arcsec, and prefer objects whose ellipse is < 1 arcmin.
Proper motion of the archival survey's astrometric reference frame (PS1 vs Gaia epochs) must be handled: all astrometry must be reduced to Gaia DR3 at the frame epoch.

The MPC db_search/show_object page does not list the observations themselves; use the get-obs API (GET with a JSON body; a POST returns 405) or the MPCAT-OBS files (NumObs.txt.gz 9.1 GB, UnnObs.txt.gz 0.46 GB, refreshed monthly) and save the response.
A single faint source inside a large ellipse with a refit that absorbs it is the classic false precovery: the main claim needs >= 2 frames with a consistent motion vector.

targets.name: New circumbinary transit candidate in a Kepler eclipsing binary (Villanova EB catalog)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (2878 EB light curves ~ 1.5 GB; the N-body stacking search is CPU-heavy, so restrict to detached EBs with morph < 0.5 and P_bin 5-60 d, ~ 700 systems)
targets.statement: Among the Kepler eclipsing binaries of the Villanova catalog (Kirk+2016, VizieR J/AJ/151/68, 2878 systems in the VizieR snapshot), find an additional transit-like signal (>= 3 events of variable duration/interval consistent with a circumbinary orbit, found directly or by a stacked detection using N-body-predicted transit windows as in the STANLEY algorithm) in a detached EB that is not one of the known Kepler circumbinary-planet systems (pscomppars cb_flag=1: Kepler-16, -34, -35, -38, -47, -64/PH1, -413, -453, -1647, -1661 by transit, plus Kepler-1660 and Kepler-451 by eclipse timing, as of 2026-10-08) and not a tertiary eclipse already in the Villanova catalog or in the Borkovits+2016 Kepler triples catalog (VizieR J/MNRAS/455/4136, 222 systems). As of a Jan 2025 presentation, the STANLEY survey of ~700 Windemuth-catalog EBs had found one unpublished additional planet, so a new candidate must be flagged for Windemuth membership. Absence checks are done by downloading whole ra/dec/id/ephemeris column lists with plain TAP/CSV requests (e.g. select+pl_name,hostname,ra,dec,cb_flag+from+pscomppars) and cross-matching LOCALLY; ADQL cone functions (contains/point/circle) in the Exoplanet Archive URL trigger a Cloudflare block and must not be used or retried. SIMBAD TAP cone queries are fine.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle {KIC, Villanova ephemeris, detrended light curve with primary/secondary eclipses masked, list of transit events (epoch, duration, depth), N-body/analytic circumbinary model with the binary parameters from the Villanova catalog (or Windemuth+2019) that reproduces every event's time and duration within errors, pixel-level centroid test on each event, null test, and the catalog files used} such that: (1) ABSENCE, re-fetched live immediately before claiming: the KIC position (3 arcsec) matches no pscomppars row (plain column download incl. cb_flag, matched locally) and no ExoFOP TOI/CTOI row, the KIC is not in VizieR J/MNRAS/455/4136 (Borkovits+2016 triples), and a SIMBAD TAP cone of 3 arcsec on the host returns no object whose otype is a planet or planet candidate (Pl, Pl?) or an eclipsing binary (EB*, EB?), which catches literature candidates that the Archive tables ingest with a lag; (2) >= 3 events, each individually > 5 sigma, with the dip on target in the pixel-level test; (3) the events are not periodic at the binary period or its harmonics and are not fit (delta-BIC > 10 in favour of the circumbinary model) by a strictly periodic third-body eclipse model, ruling out tertiary eclipses; (4) the circumbinary N-body model reproduces every event time and duration within errors; (5) null test: the same stacking search at >= 100 random trial orbits of the same planet period range yields no detection as significant as the claim; (6) implied radius < 2 RJup; (7) the host star id (TIC/KIC/EPIC/Gaia DR3) is not the host of any already-claimed (a confirmed result listed in this repository's RESULTS.md) claim under any other astronomy target of this bank, so the same signal is never counted twice across tess-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-k2-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-tess-single-transit-long-period-candidate / kepler-eb-circumbinary-transit-candidate. Claim is 'new circumbinary transit candidate'.

partial_wins.statement: Pipeline recovers, from raw Kepler light curves, the transits of at least 5 known Kepler circumbinary planets (Kepler-16b, 34b, 35b, 38b, 47b/c/d, 64b, 413b, 453b, 1647b, 1661b) with correct epochs and the variable durations predicted by the N-body model; saved as a table.

A new eclipse of a third body (depth and duration implying a stellar or brown-dwarf radius) in a Villanova EB not flagged as a triple in the catalog's ETV/tertiary columns or in the literature; checkable by the same bundle minus the planetary-radius condition.

A per-EB injection-recovery completeness map (transiting-planet radius x period) for >= 100 detached Villanova EBs with the agent's search, delivered as a CSV; non-trivial because such limits exist only for the ~700 Windemuth systems.
A two-event circumbinary-like signal passing (1),(3),(6) but with only 2 events: logged as unvetted (two events are always fit by both models), never claimed.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-downloads the KIC light curves from MAST, masks the eclipses with the saved Villanova ephemeris, confirms each listed event by re-fitting at the saved epoch, re-runs the saved N-body/analytic model to check it predicts the event times, and queries pscomppars + the Villanova page for the KIC. Under one hour. Also re-runs the Borkovits+2016 VizieR match, the SIMBAD cone and the random-orbit null test from the saved files.
angles: Detached EBs (morph < 0.5) with P_bin between 7 and 40 d that are NOT in the Windemuth+2019 ~700-system sample (so untouched by STANLEY): the Villanova catalog has ~1,500 more systems.
Stack transits at N-body-predicted windows over a grid of planet period and inclination (STANLEY-style) rather than fixed-period BLS, which fails for circumbinary transits of variable interval.
Use eclipse-timing variations in the Villanova ETV files as a prior for the planet period before stacking.
Look for lone, deep (> 1%) transit-like events outside eclipse in the ~1,000 long-period EBs where even one event is detectable at high significance.
Re-examine known Kepler CBP systems for a second, smaller transiting planet with the known planet's transits masked.
pitfalls: Tertiary stellar eclipses and eclipse-depth changes from binary precession or starspots produce aperiodic dips; a 'candidate' must have an implied radius < 2 RJup from the fit AND the Villanova ETV/tertiary flags checked.

Imperfect eclipse masking leaves residual dips at the binary period/harmonics that a stacking search will lock on to; require the events to be non-commensurate with P_bin and show the masked light curve.

The STANLEY team's unpublished 13th planet: a candidate in a Windemuth-catalog EB may already be known privately; the claim must say 'candidate not in public tables' and flag Windemuth membership explicitly.
Very low tractability: with ~14 known planets from 2878 EBs and automated surveys already run, a new detection is unlikely; do not relax any threshold to manufacture one.
Two events are always reproduced by a circumbinary model with free period/phase/inclination: the main claim needs >= 3 events; two-event signals are the unvetted partial win only.

targets.name: New vetted transit candidate in archival Kepler or K2 light curves (not in KOI/K2 candidate tables)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (do NOT fetch the full Kepler or K2 light-curve sets; restrict to a defined sub-sample under 200 GB, e.g. one K2 campaign (~20k targets, ~10 GB) or Kepler M dwarfs; pip install lightkurve transitleastsquares wotan triceratops astroquery)
targets.statement: Re-search public Kepler (Q1-Q17 DR25 PDCSAP) or K2 (campaigns 0-19) light curves at MAST with a modern detrending + TLS pipeline for a periodic transit whose host (KIC/EPIC and any Gaia DR3 source within 3 arcsec) is absent from the NASA Exoplanet Archive KOI cumulative table, the Q1-Q17 DR25 TCE table, the K2 planets-and-candidates table (k2pandc) and pscomppars, and from the TOI/CTOI tables for the same sky position; the candidate must pass the same vetting suite as the TESS target (odd/even, secondary, pixel-level centroid using the Kepler target pixel files, TRICERATOPS FPP < 0.5 / NFPP < 0.1, injection-recovery). Recent surveys (TFAW K2 reanalysis: 24 previously unpublished candidates; K2-OjOS) show the archive still contains unlisted candidates. Claims are 'new vetted candidate' only. Only PERIODIC signals with >= 3 transit events qualify; the host must not be a Villanova Kepler EB (those belong to kepler-eb-circumbinary-transit-candidate). Absence checks are done by downloading whole ra/dec/id/ephemeris column lists with plain TAP/CSV requests (e.g. select+pl_name,hostname,ra,dec,cb_flag+from+pscomppars) and cross-matching LOCALLY; ADQL cone functions (contains/point/circle) in the Exoplanet Archive URL trigger a Cloudflare block and must not be used or retried. SIMBAD TAP cone queries are fine.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle (as in tess-new-vetted-transit-candidate, with KIC/EPIC id, Gaia DR3 id, quarter/campaign list, MAST file URIs, null-test numbers and every catalog file used with its download timestamp) such that: (1) ABSENCE, re-fetched live immediately before claiming: the host id and every Gaia DR3 source within 3 arcsec are absent from the Archive cumulative, q1_q17_dr25_tce, k2pandc, pscomppars and toi tables (plain column downloads, matched locally by id and 3-arcsec position; a DR25 TCE with period within 0.1% and epoch within 0.05 d modulo the period counts as the same signal) and from the ExoFOP TOI/CTOI CSVs by position; a SIMBAD TAP cone of 3 arcsec on the host returns no object whose otype is a planet or planet candidate (Pl, Pl?) or an eclipsing binary (EB*, EB?), which catches literature candidates that the Archive tables ingest with a lag; a VizieR all-catalogue position search (https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/asu-tsv?-c=<RA>+<DEC>&-c.rs=3&-source=) is saved and shows no planet/candidate catalogue entry for the host; the KIC is not in the Villanova EB catalog (VizieR J/AJ/151/68); (2) >= 3 individual transit events; (3) odd/even < 3 sigma; (4) secondary < 3 sigma; (5) pixel-level test on the target pixel file shows the dip on the target; (6) TRICERATOPS FPP < 0.5 and NFPP < 0.1 (report the validation tier but do not claim it); (7) injection-recovery > 90% at the claimed depth/period through the same detrending; (8) null test: the identical search pipeline run on the flux-inverted light curve and on 20 phase-scrambled copies (transit windows shuffled) returns a maximum SDE/significance below the injection-calibrated detection threshold and below the claimed signal; the numbers are saved in the bundle; (9) for K2 the signal survives both a K2SFF/EVEREST-style systematics correction and a self-flat-field re-derivation (two independent detrendings); (10) the host star id (TIC/KIC/EPIC/Gaia DR3) is not the host of any already-claimed (a confirmed result listed in this repository's RESULTS.md) claim under any other astronomy target of this bank, so the same signal is never counted twice across tess-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-k2-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-tess-single-transit-long-period-candidate / kepler-eb-circumbinary-transit-candidate. Claims are 'new vetted candidate' only.

partial_wins.statement: Pipeline independently recovers, from MAST light curves alone, at least 10 of the TFAW-survey K2 candidates (period within 0.1%) and at least 20 KOI CANDIDATEs with koi_score > 0.9, plus rejects at least 10 koi_disposition FALSE POSITIVE KOIs flagged as EB; confusion matrix saved. Calibration gate.

An additional transit candidate (not in the Archive tables) in a system already hosting a KOI/K2 candidate, found after masking the known transits, passing all vetting steps; checkable exactly like the main criterion but with higher prior.
A signal passing absence + odd/even + secondary + injection-recovery but with TRICERATOPS 0.5 <= FPP < 0.9 or pixel test inconclusive: logged as 'unvetted', never claimed.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-downloads the named light-curve / target-pixel files from MAST, re-runs the saved detrending + TLS at the claimed period, recomputes the odd/even, secondary, and pixel-level statistics from saved inputs, re-runs TRICERATOPS from the saved star list, and re-runs the four Archive TAP absence queries plus a 3-arcsec cone on the KIC/EPIC coordinates. Under one hour. Also re-runs the SIMBAD cone, the VizieR position search and the null test from saved files; no ADQL cone functions to the Archive.
angles: K2 campaigns with the worst roll systematics (C0, C1, C10, C11) and overlapping campaigns (C5/C16/C18) where a two-campaign stitch doubles the baseline; K2-OjOS and TFAW found new candidates exactly there.
Kepler stars with koi_score between 0.1 and 0.5 or TCEs that failed the Robovetter on a single metric (e.g. 'model-shift' only): re-vet with the modern suite; the DR25 TCE table lists them.
Residual search in known KOI multi systems after masking all listed transits (stacking 4 years at a fixed trial period reaches ~100 ppm).
Low-mass hosts (Teff < 4000 K from the KIC/Gaia DR3) where the Kepler pipeline's stellar-radius priors were worst and the transit depth of small planets is largest.
Use the DR25 injected-planet completeness products as an external check on the pipeline's own injection-recovery.
pitfalls: A TCE or signal that is merely 'not yet a TOI' is not new if it already appears in the TOI, CTOI, KOI, K2 or Exoplanet Archive tables under any TIC/KIC/EPIC alias: cross-match by coordinates (3 arcsec) AND by TIC/KIC/EPIC/Gaia DR3 id, not by name alone.

Momentum-dump / scattered-light / reaction-wheel artifacts in TESS (every ~3-4 d at orbit perigee, sector edges) mimic single transits; require the dip to be absent in the background flux and present in the target aperture only.

Nearby eclipsing binaries diluted into the aperture produce flat-bottomed, equal-depth transits that pass odd/even: the centroid test and TRICERATOPS nearby-star scenarios (NFPP) are mandatory, not optional.
Detrending with too short a window (wotan/biweight < 3x transit duration) injects or erases shallow transits; the injection-recovery step must use the same detrending as the search.
Bootstrapped 'SDE > 7' from TLS/BLS is not a significance: compute the false-alarm level from transit-shaped injections on the same light curve with the same pipeline.

The DR25 TCE table contains ~34,000 threshold-crossing events; a signal present there is NOT new even if it never became a KOI - the absence check must include q1_q17_dr25_tce, and a match in period (within 0.1%) and epoch counts as the same signal.
K2 'candidates' in the literature (TFAW, K2-OjOS, Kruse 2019, Zink 2021) may be absent from k2pandc with a lag; a literature search by EPIC id (ADS/arXiv) is required in addition to the table check.
Exoplanet Archive TAP URLs containing contains(point(...),circle(...)) are blocked by Cloudflare (seen 2026-10-08): download the ra/dec columns and match locally; never retry through a 403.

K2 literature candidates (TFAW thesis at diposit.ub.edu, K2-OjOS, Kruse 2019, Zink 2021) are checked mechanically through SIMBAD otype Pl?/Pl and the VizieR position search, not by reading papers; an entry in either is not new.

targets.name: New single-/duo-transit long-period candidate in Kepler or TESS light curves
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (single-event search is cheap; the cost is downloading: use the tesscurl sector scripts for a defined bright sub-sample or Kepler PDCSAP for Teff < 6000 K dwarfs, well under 200 GB)
targets.statement: Find a single or double transit-like event (<= 2 events in all available data; duration >= 5 h; depth consistent with Rp < 2 RJup at the Gaia DR3 stellar radius, implying P > ~100 d) in public Kepler or TESS light curves of a star that is not a Villanova Kepler EB, that is not in the TOI/CTOI/KOI/TCE/k2pandc/pscomppars tables, not in the Kawahara & Masuda 2019 Kepler snow-line table (VizieR J/AJ/157/218), not among the Foreman-Mackey+2016 (arXiv:1607.08237) / Herman+2019 (arXiv:1901.01974, 18 KICs) Kepler long-period candidates, not among the four Kepler >342 d candidates of arXiv:2608.23425 (Aug 2026), not among the 85 TESS duotransits of Hawthorn+2024 (arXiv:2310.17268; all non-TOI ones were submitted as CTOIs) and not among the 88 TESS single-transit candidates of Salinas+2025 (arXiv:2502.07542). Must survive: single-event shape fit (limb-darkened transit vs. box vs. Gaussian, transit model preferred by delta-BIC > 10), no momentum-dump / sector-edge / scattered-light coincidence, pixel-level centroid test, no matching EB ephemeris within 2 arcmin, and an ingress/egress duration consistent with the stellar density. Absence checks are done by downloading whole ra/dec/id/ephemeris column lists with plain TAP/CSV requests (e.g. select+pl_name,hostname,ra,dec,cb_flag+from+pscomppars) and cross-matching LOCALLY; ADQL cone functions (contains/point/circle) in the Exoplanet Archive URL trigger a Cloudflare block and must not be used or retried. SIMBAD TAP cone queries are fine.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle {star id, Gaia DR3 id, light-curve file URIs, event epoch(s), duration, depth, transit-model vs box vs Gaussian fits with delta-BIC, per-pixel in/out-of-event difference image, momentum-dump/quality-flag timeline around the event, stellar density from Gaia DR3 vs density implied by the fit, (for duo-transits) the list of allowed period aliases, null-test numbers, and the literature exclusion lists as machine-extracted id lists with their source URLs} such that: (1) ABSENCE, re-fetched live immediately before claiming: the host id and all Gaia DR3 sources within 3 arcsec are absent from the ExoFOP TOI/CTOI CSVs and the Archive toi/cumulative/q1_q17_dr25_tce/k2pandc/pscomppars tables (plain column downloads matched locally), from VizieR J/AJ/157/218 (KIC match), from the KIC lists extracted from the ar5iv/arXiv HTML of 1607.08237 and 1901.01974 and the four candidates named in arXiv:2608.23425, from the TIC lists extracted from arXiv:2310.17268 (Table A1) and arXiv:2502.07542, and from the Villanova EB catalog (J/AJ/151/68); a SIMBAD TAP cone of 3 arcsec on the host returns no object whose otype is a planet or planet candidate (Pl, Pl?) or an eclipsing binary (EB*, EB?), which catches literature candidates that the Archive tables ingest with a lag; (2) <= 2 events in all public data for the star (a third event makes it a periodic candidate for the TESS or Kepler/K2 target instead); (3) transit model preferred by delta-BIC > 10 over both alternatives; (4) event not within 0.5 d of a momentum dump, safe mode or sector/quarter boundary, and no flux drop of similar depth in the background or in neighbouring apertures; (5) difference-image centroid on target; (6) implied Rp < 2 RJup and fitted density within 3x of the Gaia DR3 stellar density; (7) null test: the same single-event detector run on the flux-inverted light curve returns zero events passing (3)-(6); (8) the host star id (TIC/KIC/EPIC/Gaia DR3) is not the host of any already-claimed (a confirmed result listed in this repository's RESULTS.md) claim under any other astronomy target of this bank, so the same signal is never counted twice across tess-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-k2-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-tess-single-transit-long-period-candidate / kepler-eb-circumbinary-transit-candidate. Claim is 'new single-transit candidate'.

partial_wins.statement: The pipeline recovers, from raw MAST data, at least 10 of the Kawahara+2019 or Foreman-Mackey+2016 Kepler single-transit events (epoch within 0.05 d, depth within 20%) and at least 5 TESS duotransit candidates from Hawthorn+2024 that later became TOIs; results saved as a table.

For a known duo-transit TOI/CTOI with an ambiguous period, a new period determination (set of allowed aliases reduced by >= 50%) using additional public TESS sectors released since the candidate's listing, with the ephemeris and the sector data cited; checkable by re-folding.
An event passing absence, shape and quality-flag tests but with an inconclusive pixel-level test: logged as unvetted, not claimed.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-downloads the named light-curve and target-pixel files, re-fits the single event with the saved model code at the saved epoch (minutes), checks the quality flags and dump times from the FITS headers, reproduces the difference image, and re-runs the TAP/CSV absence checks plus a VizieR query on J/AJ/157/218. Under one hour. Also re-extracts the KIC/TIC exclusion lists from the saved arXiv HTML and re-runs the SIMBAD cone and the inverted-light-curve null test.
angles: TESS continuous-viewing-zone stars with 20+ sectors: duo- and tri-transits with P = 100-400 d now exist in the public data but the SPOC/QLP searches require >= 2 transits per sector-pair run, so many remain unlisted.
Kepler stars with 1-2 transits whose depth was below the Foreman-Mackey+2016 threshold (they searched only ~40,000 bright Sun-like stars): extend to Kp 15-16 and to M dwarfs.
Systems with a known inner KOI/TOI showing TTVs (arXiv:2608.23425 found its four candidates exactly there): mask the inner transits and run the single-event search on the residuals.
Use the stellar density consistency (Gaia DR3 radius + mass) as a built-in false-positive filter: an event whose duration implies a density off by > 3x is an EB or blend.
For every TESS single-transit candidate, query all later public sectors for a second event to turn a mono into a duo (period aliases).
pitfalls: Single dips coincident with TESS momentum dumps, orbit perigee ramps, Earth/Moon scattered light, or Kepler safe-mode/coarse-point recoveries are the dominant false positive; the quality-flag timeline must be in the bundle and the dip must not be present in the background pixels.
Long-period single transits from grazing EBs are V-shaped: a V-shaped single event with implied Rp > 2 RJup or a duration inconsistent with the Gaia DR3 stellar density is not a candidate.
Secular trends from starspots or flares (M dwarfs) detrended badly produce fake 'transits'; the bundle must show the raw and detrended curves and the detrending must be re-run by the skeptic.

Kawahara & Masuda 2019 (VizieR J/AJ/157/218), Foreman-Mackey+2016 (1607.08237), Herman+2019 (1901.01974), Hawthorn+2024 (85 duotransits, 2310.17268), Salinas+2025 (88 single transits, 2502.07542) and arXiv:2608.23425 already list hundreds of events: matching by KIC/TIC id AND by epoch is mandatory; a known event re-found with a different detrending is not new.
Exoplanet Archive TAP URLs containing contains(point(...),circle(...)) are blocked by Cloudflare (seen 2026-10-08): download the ra/dec columns and match locally; never retry through a 403.

targets.name: New periodic variable stars / eclipsing binaries absent from VSX, confirmed in two independent surveys
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (ZTF light curves are fetched per cone query, a few hundred KB each; TESScut 5x5-pixel cutouts are ~1 MB per sector; the CDS vsx.dat dump is 2.2 GB; Gaia and Chen+2020 catalogs are queried, not downloaded in full)
targets.statement: Discover periodic variable stars (eclipsing binaries, RR Lyrae, delta Scuti, rotational, etc.) that are absent from the AAVSO International Variable Star Index (VSX, > 2 million entries; live API at vsx.aavso.org and full dump at CDS B/vsx updated 2026-10-05) AND absent from the major machine catalogs that VSX has not fully ingested: Gaia DR3 vari_summary (11.75 million sources, incl. vari_eclipsing_binary 2.18 million), ASAS-SN variables, ZTF periodic variables Chen+2020 (VizieR J/ApJS/249/18), ATLAS variables Heinze+2018 (J/AJ/156/241), Catalina CRTS Drake+2014/2017 (J/ApJS/213/9, J/MNRAS/469/3688), WISE periodic variables Chen+2018 (J/ApJS/237/28), OGLE OCVS where in the OGLE footprint, TESS-EBs HLSP, and SIMBAD; with the period independently recovered (within 0.1% or an exact 2x alias) in two independent public data sets, e.g. ZTF DR23 light curves (IRSA) and TESS FFI light curves, or ZTF and Gaia DR3 epoch photometry. The AAVSO forum states that many millions of known-variable candidates await VSX ingestion, so the machine-catalog absence condition is what makes a find non-trivial.
targets.success_criterion: A batch of >= 10 objects, each with a saved bundle {Gaia DR3 source_id, RA/Dec, ZTF object ids and light-curve CSVs (IRSA URLs), second-survey light curve (TESS FFI cutout URL or Gaia epoch photometry), periodograms, period and uncertainty from each survey, folded curves, amplitude, classification, and every catalog response used with timestamps} such that for every object: (1) no VSX entry within 10 arcsec via the live api.list query at https://vsx.aavso.org/index.php?view=api.list (re-fetched live immediately before claiming; an error response counts as 'unknown', never as 'absent') and none in the CDS B/vsx dump; (2) no Gaia DR3 vari_summary source within 2 arcsec with any classification (Gaia TAP); (3) no ASAS-SN variable, no Chen+2020 ZTF periodic or suspected variable, no ATLAS (J/AJ/156/241), CRTS (J/ApJS/213/9, J/MNRAS/469/3688) or WISE (J/ApJS/237/28) variable, no OGLE OCVS entry (if inside the OGLE footprint), and no TESS-EBs entry within 10 arcsec; a SIMBAD TAP cone of 3 arcsec returns no object with a variable-star otype (V*, EB*, RR*, dS*, Ro*, Pu*, Er*, LP*, Mi* or their candidate forms); if the TESS Ten Thousand EB catalog (arXiv:2506.05631) machine-readable table is obtainable it is also checked and saved, and if it is not obtainable the TESS leg may not be used as a survey for EB-type candidates; (4) periods from the two surveys agree within 0.1% (or exactly 2x), each with bootstrap FAP < 1e-4, and the period is not within 1% of a sidereal-day alias (n/k day, k <= 4) unless the second survey is space-based; (5) amplitude > 5x the per-survey median scatter at that magnitude; (6) the TESS detection (if used) is not a blend: the signal is absent in neighbours within 1 arcmin that are brighter, or a pixel-level centroid shows it on target; (7) null test: the identical pipeline applied to 50 VSX 'constant'/non-variable comparison stars of similar magnitude yields zero objects passing (4)-(5), saved with the batch. Claim is 'new periodic variable, not in VSX or the listed catalogs'.

partial_wins.statement: Pipeline recovers, blind, the VSX period for at least 50 randomly drawn VSX EW/EA/RRAB/DSCT stars with ZTF coverage (within 0.1% or 2x alias) and reports its own false-alarm rate on 50 VSX 'constant' / non-variable comparison stars; saved as a table (calibration gate).
A batch of >= 20 objects satisfying (1)-(3) and (5) with a ZTF-only period at FAP < 1e-6 but no second-survey confirmation; logged as 'single-survey candidates', not claimed.

A table of >= 20 VSX entries imported from Gaia DR3 whose VSX period is a wrong alias (the AAVSO forum notes many are), with the correct period demonstrated in ZTF + a second survey; checkable by re-folding.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-runs the VSX api.list cone query, the Gaia TAP cone query, the SIMBAD cone, the VizieR matches (ASAS-SN/Chen+2020/ATLAS/CRTS/WISE/TESS-EBs, saved catalogs), re-downloads the ZTF light curve CSV from the IRSA URL in the bundle and the TESS cutout via TESScut, and re-computes the Lomb-Scargle/BLS period with the saved script for each of the >= 10 objects plus the 50 null-test stars. Under one hour for the batch.
angles: Sky regions where Gaia DR3 variability is incomplete (crowded low-latitude fields, |b| < 10 deg, and stars with few Gaia transits) but ZTF has > 200 epochs: run a Lomb-Scargle + BLS search on ZTF objects with high chi2 (ztf_objects_dr23 'chi'/'nobs' columns via Gator).
Faint end (ZTF r 18-20.5) below ASAS-SN's limit and below the Chen+2020 threshold, where VSX is emptiest.
Short-period (P < 0.2 d) EW/delta-Scuti systems whose Gaia DR3 period is an alias: cross-check with TESS 200-s FFI cutouts, which break ground-based aliases.

Use the TESS Ten Thousand '~900k unvetted targets with score > 0.9 and no known EB within 21 arcsec' list (arXiv:2506.05631) as a pre-filtered input and resolve each with ZTF (which has 21x finer pixels).
Automate a VSX-absence checker that queries api.list in batches with a 10-arcsec radius and caches results, to keep the AAVSO server load low (radius = 5 deg queries time out).
pitfalls: Absence from VSX alone is trivial: millions of Gaia DR3 / ZTF / ASAS-SN / ATLAS / CRTS / WISE / OGLE variables are not yet in VSX. A find must be absent from ALL listed machine catalogs and SIMBAD, otherwise it is a catalog cross-match exercise, not a discovery.
TESS 21-arcsec pixels: a periodic signal in a TESS cutout usually belongs to a brighter neighbour; without ZTF/Gaia confirmation on the same source it is a blend.

ZTF alias periods (1 d, 0.5 d, sidereal-day harmonics) and the ZTF 'catflags' bad-data flags produce fake periodicities; mask catflags and reject periods within 1% of n/k day aliases unless confirmed by TESS.
VSX name matching is not enough: match by position (10 arcsec) because VSX entries carry survey names (Gaia DR3, ZTF, ASASSN-V, KIC) not Gaia source_ids.
The api.list endpoint returns a PHP fatal error for large radii (5 deg timed out); the checker must use small cones and treat an error response as 'unknown', never as 'absent'.

The TESS Ten Thousand catalog (arXiv:2506.05631) had no VizieR/MAST machine-readable copy found on 2026-10-08; until one is saved in the bundle, TESS-based EB candidates cannot be declared absent from it.

targets.name: MOONSHOT - Planet Nine or a new extreme distant TNO candidate in public archival survey images
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (DECam frames are ~0.5-1 GB each; restrict to < 200 GB by selecting fields with >= 3 public epochs in the predicted Planet Nine region or ecliptic-latitude bands; shift-and-stack on 10 cores is feasible for a few square degrees per day)
targets.statement: Detect in public archival imaging (DECam frames via the NOIRLab SIA service, Pan-STARRS1 3pi cutouts, ZTF science images; optionally the IRAS/AKARI far-IR route of arXiv:2504.17288 / 2506.12854) a slow-moving source (< ~1 arcmin/yr for Planet Nine at 400-800 au; < 4 arcsec/hr for a > 100 au object) linked across >= 3 epochs on >= 2 nights with a bound heliocentric orbit fit (r > 100 au), that is absent from the MPC Distant.txt / TNO list / MPCORB.DAT and from JPL SBDB. Pan-STARRS1 DR2 (Brown & Batygin 2024), ZTF and DES have already excluded ~78% of the Brown & Batygin 2021 Planet Nine parameter space to V ~ 21.5, and Rubin LSST formally began its 10-year survey on 2026-06-29/30 (alerts since late Feb 2026), so this is a long-odds search of remaining faint/high-latitude/galactic-plane regions. No MPC submission is made; the claim is 'linked moving-object candidate not in any public orbit catalog'. Any 'new object' claim (main or partial) also requires absence from the MPC NEOCP/PCCP pages and from the MPC Isolated Tracklet File (itf.txt.gz, ~130 MB, refreshed daily) within 30 arcsec of each epoch position.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle {all frame identifiers and download URLs, cutouts at each epoch, source centroids with uncertainties, the linking solution (motion vector), a heliocentric orbit fit (saved code) with residuals < 0.5 arcsec, the implied r, a, e, i, and static-sky and known-object checks} such that: >= 3 detections on >= 2 distinct nights, consistent with a single bound orbit with r > 100 au, each detection > 5 sigma with no static source at that position in other-epoch frames or Gaia DR3/PS1 catalogs within 2 arcsec, no object within 30 arcsec of any epoch position in a SkyBoT cone search at that epoch, absence of any ITF tracklet (https://www.minorplanetcenter.net/iau/ITF/itf.txt.gz) and NEOCP/PCCP object within 30 arcsec of each epoch position, and absence from https://minorplanetcenter.net/iau/MPCORB/Distant.txt, https://minorplanetcenter.net/iau/lists/TNOs.html, https://minorplanetcenter.net/iau/MPCORB/MPCORB.DAT and JPL SBDB (all re-fetched live immediately before claiming). An agent may only claim 'candidate'; 'Planet Nine' is never claimed. Additionally the object (any epoch position within 30 arcsec) is not the subject of any already-claimed (a confirmed result listed in this repository's RESULTS.md) claim under any other astronomy target of this bank, so the same signal is never counted twice across tess-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-k2-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-tess-single-transit-long-period-candidate / kepler-eb-circumbinary-transit-candidate.

partial_wins.statement: Blind recovery, from public DECam/PS1 frames, of >= 3 known extreme TNOs (e.g. Sedna, 2012 VP113, 2015 TG387, Leleakuhonua) at the predicted positions with astrometry within 1 arcsec; proves the shift-and-stack / linking chain.

A linked >= 3-epoch, >= 2-night moving object with a bound orbit fit at r > 30 au absent from MPCORB/Distant.txt/SBDB (an ordinary new TNO candidate from archival data, as DEEP found 105 new TNOs in DECam data); same verification chain. The ITF and NEOCP/PCCP checks of the main criterion apply.

A reproducible sky-coverage and depth map (per field: epochs, limiting magnitude, motion-rate sensitivity) of the public DECam frames NOT included in the DES/PS1/ZTF Planet Nine exclusion analyses, delivered as a CSV with the frame lists; non-trivial because it defines the remaining search space.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-downloads the named frames/cutouts, re-measures the centroids, re-runs the saved orbit-fit code on the saved astrometry, runs SkyBoT at each epoch, and queries Distant.txt/TNOs/MPCORB and SBDB for any object within the error ellipse. Under one hour for a single candidate.
angles: Public DECam frames (non-DES programs) in the Brown & Batygin 2021 predicted sky region at high galactic latitude that were not part of the DES/PS1/ZTF exclusion analyses; shift-and-stack along the predicted motion range.
Galactic-plane crossing of the predicted orbit, where all optical searches are least complete; use difference imaging against a deep template.
The IRAS (1983) vs AKARI (2006-07) far-IR route: candidate pairs from arXiv:2504.17288 / 2506.12854 can be followed up in public optical archives at the predicted 2010-2025 positions.
Ordinary new TNO discovery as a realistic sub-goal (DEEP found 105 new TNOs in DECam data): the same pipeline, lower bar.
Use Gaia DR3 + PS1 as the static-sky mask to suppress the dominant false positives before linking.
pitfalls: Asteroids, Centaurs and known TNOs at the predicted position (SkyBoT must be run at every epoch) and spurious linkings of unrelated transients/artifacts across nights: require a single orbit fit with residuals < 0.5 arcsec and > 5 sigma detections.
Static faint galaxies and variable stars masquerading as slow movers between epochs years apart; require absence at the position in other-epoch frames and in PS1/Gaia catalogs.

Claims of a 'Planet Nine candidate' (e.g. the 2025 IRAS/AKARI pair) are routinely not confirmed; an agent may never upgrade 'candidate' to 'planet' and must state the excluded-parameter-space context.
Rubin LSST alerts (since 2026-06-30) and the MPC NEOCP/distant lists update daily; a candidate must be re-checked against the live MPC files on the day of the claim.
A tracklet already sitting in the MPC ITF or on the NEOCP/PCCP is not a new object: both are checked by position and epoch before any 'new' claim.

targets.name: New vetted transiting-planet candidate in public TESS light curves (not in TOI/CTOI/Archive)
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (one sector of 2-min SPOC light curves is ~20,000 files / ~40 GB; keep any sub-sample under 200 GB, e.g. Tmag < 12 M dwarfs or a single sector; pip install lightkurve transitleastsquares wotan triceratops astroquery into a virtual environment first)
targets.statement: Find a periodic transit signal in public TESS 2-min/20-s SPOC light curves or SPOC/QLP FFI light curves (MAST) whose host (TIC id, and any star within 3 arcsec) is absent from the live ExoFOP TOI and CTOI tables and from the NASA Exoplanet Archive toi/pscomppars tables, and that passes a fixed vetting suite: TLS/BLS detection with injection-recovery-calibrated significance, odd/even depth agreement, no secondary eclipse, in-transit centroid shift consistent with zero at pixel level (TESScut), TRICERATOPS FPP < 0.5 and NFPP < 0.1 ('likely planet' tier of Giacalone+2021), and no ephemeris match to any known EB (TESS-EBs HLSP, VSX) within 1 TESS pixel (21 arcsec). An agent may only claim 'new vetted candidate', never 'planet'. Only PERIODIC signals with >= 3 individual transit events in the analysed data qualify here; single or double events belong to kepler-tess-single-transit-long-period-candidate. Absence checks are done by downloading whole ra/dec/id/ephemeris column lists with plain TAP/CSV requests (e.g. select+pl_name,hostname,ra,dec,cb_flag+from+pscomppars) and cross-matching LOCALLY; ADQL cone functions (contains/point/circle) in the Exoplanet Archive URL trigger a Cloudflare block and must not be used or retried. SIMBAD TAP cone queries are fine.
targets.success_criterion: A saved bundle {TIC id, Gaia DR3 id, sector list, raw light-curve file URIs, detrended light curve, period/epoch/duration/depth, TLS result, odd-even and secondary-eclipse statistics, per-pixel/centroid test output, TRICERATOPS FPP+NFPP with the exact input files, injection-recovery completeness curve, null-test numbers, and every catalog file used for the absence checks with its download timestamp} such that: (1) ABSENCE, all re-fetched live immediately before claiming: the TIC id and every Gaia DR3 source within 3 arcsec are absent from the ExoFOP TOI CSV (https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/download_toi.php?sort=toi&output=csv, including its 'Previous CTOI' column) and CTOI CSV (https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/download_ctoi.php?sort=ctoi&output=csv, which carries Planet Hunters TESS and other community submissions), and from the Exoplanet Archive toi, pscomppars, k2pandc and cumulative tables (plain column downloads via TAP, matched locally by id and by 3-arcsec position); no entry of those tables, of the TESS-EBs HLSP, of Gaia DR3 vari_eclipsing_binary, or of VSX (api.list cone) within 2 arcmin shares the ephemeris (period within 0.1% or an exact 2x/0.5x alias AND epoch within 0.05 d modulo the period); a SIMBAD TAP cone of 3 arcsec on the host returns no object whose otype is a planet or planet candidate (Pl, Pl?) or an eclipsing binary (EB*, EB?), which catches literature candidates that the Archive tables ingest with a lag; and the signal does not match (same 2-arcmin + ephemeris rule) any SPOC TCE in the MAST tcestats lists (https://archive.stsci.edu/missions/tess/catalogs/tce/) - a TCE match is logged as the partial win tess-rediscovered-tce, never as new; (2) >= 3 individual transit events with the dip visible in the target aperture at each; (3) odd/even depth difference < 3 sigma; (4) secondary eclipse at phase 0.5 < 3 sigma and the depth is inconsistent with an EB at the TIC stellar radius; (5) TRICERATOPS FPP < 0.5 and NFPP < 0.1 (also report whether FPP < 0.015 and NFPP < 0.001, the validation tier, but validation is NOT claimed); (6) the signal is recovered in > 90% of >= 100 injections of the same depth/period/duration into the same light curve through the same detrending; (7) the centroid/pixel-level (TESScut difference-image) test shows the dip on the target; (8) null test: the identical search pipeline run on the flux-inverted light curve and on 20 phase-scrambled copies (transit windows shuffled) returns a maximum SDE/significance below the injection-calibrated detection threshold and below the claimed signal; the numbers are saved in the bundle; (9) the host star id (TIC/KIC/EPIC/Gaia DR3) is not the host of any already-claimed (a confirmed result listed in this repository's RESULTS.md) claim under any other astronomy target of this bank, so the same signal is never counted twice across tess-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-k2-new-vetted-transit-candidate / kepler-tess-single-transit-long-period-candidate / kepler-eb-circumbinary-transit-candidate. Claims are 'new vetted candidate' only, never 'planet'.

partial_wins.statement: Pipeline re-detects, from raw MAST light curves alone, at least 20 randomly chosen known TOIs with TFOPWG disposition PC/CP/KP (period within 0.1% and depth within 20%) and correctly rejects at least 10 TOIs with disposition FP (EB/NEB), with the confusion matrix saved; this is the calibration gate for any new claim.

A signal passing items (1)-(3),(5),(6) of the success criterion with TRICERATOPS either not run or 0.5 <= FPP < 0.9: an 'unvetted new candidate', logged with all artifacts, explicitly NOT claimed as vetted.

A per-target injection-recovery completeness map (period x depth grid, >= 400 injections) for a defined sample of >= 200 light curves, published as a CSV, showing the detection threshold of the pipeline; non-trivial because it sets the floor for all later claims.
A signal passing (2)-(8) whose only catalog match is a SPOC/QLP TCE that never became a TOI/CTOI: logged as 'rediscovered TCE, independently vetted' with the TCE id; not claimed as new.

targets.verification_method: Skeptic re-downloads the named light-curve files from MAST (URIs in the bundle), re-runs the saved detrending + TLS script at the claimed period (minutes), recomputes odd/even and secondary statistics from the saved phase-folded data, re-runs TRICERATOPS from the saved input files (tens of minutes with the saved star list), and re-fetches the TOI CSV, CTOI CSV and Archive TAP tables to confirm absence by TIC id and by a 3-arcsec cone match on the TIC RA/Dec. All under one hour on this Mac. The skeptic also re-runs the SIMBAD cone, the TCE-list match and the null test from the saved files. No ADQL cone functions are sent to the Exoplanet Archive.
angles: Search where the official pipelines are weakest: FFI-only targets with Tmag 12-14 in the QLP/SPOC-FFI HLSPs, single-sector M dwarfs, and targets near the TESS pixel-saturation limit, which the TOI process under-samples.

Multi-sector stitching of the 2-min light curves of a star observed in >= 10 sectors (continuous viewing zones) to reach depths ~200 ppm that single-sector searches miss; use wotan biweight with window = 3x the max duration.
Second-planet search: mask the known TOI transits in multi-TOI systems and re-run TLS on the residuals (TOI systems with one known candidate are the highest-prior place for an unlisted second one).
Build the vetting suite as a reusable CLI that takes a TIC id and period and emits the full bundle, then calibrate it on the ExoFOP CSV (PC vs FP dispositions) before searching.
Use the ExoFOP 'TESS Disposition'/'TFOPWG Disposition' columns to build the negative training set (NEB/EB/BEB) for the pipeline's rejection stage.
pitfalls: A TCE or signal that is merely 'not yet a TOI' is not new if it already appears in the TOI, CTOI, KOI, K2 or Exoplanet Archive tables under any TIC/KIC/EPIC alias: cross-match by coordinates (3 arcsec) AND by TIC/KIC/EPIC/Gaia DR3 id, not by name alone.

Momentum-dump / scattered-light / reaction-wheel artifacts in TESS (every ~3-4 d at orbit perigee, sector edges) mimic single transits; require the dip to be absent in the background flux and present in the target aperture only.

Nearby eclipsing binaries diluted into the aperture produce flat-bottomed, equal-depth transits that pass odd/even: the centroid test and TRICERATOPS nearby-star scenarios (NFPP) are mandatory, not optional.
Detrending with too short a window (wotan/biweight < 3x transit duration) injects or erases shallow transits; the injection-recovery step must use the same detrending as the search.
Bootstrapped 'SDE > 7' from TLS/BLS is not a significance: compute the false-alarm level from transit-shaped injections on the same light curve with the same pipeline.

ExoFOP TOI and CTOI tables are updated in batches (the Archive toi table shows latest toi_created 2026-08-27 and rowupdate 2026-10-01): a signal found today could already be queued; the claim must be re-checked against the live CSVs immediately before claiming, and any TIC that appears as a 'Previous CTOI' is not new.
Exoplanet Archive TAP URLs containing contains(point(...),circle(...)) are blocked by Cloudflare (seen 2026-10-08): download the ra/dec columns and match locally; never retry through a 403.
A SPOC TCE that the TOI team never promoted is NOT a new candidate: the MAST tcestats lists (132 sector files) must be matched by position and ephemeris.
Single and double transit events are out of scope here (they belong to the single-transit target); do not phase-fold two events and call the result periodic.

targets.name: The nine still-open 1918 ADFGVX radiograms (Childs collection, Lasry/Schmeh 2017 challenge)
targets.statement: In February 2017 George Lasry and Klaus Schmeh published 22 German ADFGVX radiograms (Nov-Dec 1918, J. Rives Childs collection) that resisted Lasry's large-scale break (Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker, Cryptologia 41(2), 2017). ADFGVX is a 6x6 Polybius substitution followed by columnar transposition with daily keys. Per the community repo github.com/0wwafa/adfgvx-1918 (Sept 2026), 12 are read (p.100, 105, 109, 132, 146, 164 (two partials), 171, 176, 187 (two parts), 215, 217) and 9 remain open; p.217 (keyword TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG) was credited to 'prinz' with GPT-6 Astra in Sept 2026 and independently verified by the swarm-ai-research group, though its key is dated 9 Dec 1918, twelve days after the message. The README does not list the nine open IDs; take them from the repo's docs/REPORT.md and messages.py. The repo's own two-edit exhaustive and beam searches have already failed on these nine. Decrypt any of the nine. Schmeh's Top-50 ranks unsolved ADFGVX cryptograms #46.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if ALL of the following hold. (0) The target ID appears as open in the repo's docs/REPORT.md on the day of the attempt. (1) The key (Polybius square plus transposition key) is either a documented 1918 daily key for the message's date window, or a newly recovered key that ALSO decrypts at least one other message of the same date window to German. A key taken from a date window that does not contain the message must be flagged, and is CONFIRMED only if it also decrypts a second message or the plaintext matches an external historical record. (2) The decrypt of the archived transcription is German military or diplomatic text with at least 85% word coverage. (3) Edits are at most 4% of symbols or 3 edits, whichever is larger, each a plausible transcription or transmission error (for example adjacent ADFGVX letter confusion, or a dropped or duplicated column cell), and every edit is listed. (4) Multiple-comparison control: the total hypothesis count (keys x edit-sets x column-offset variants) is reported, and the claimed German score exceeds the best score over the same search on wrong-key controls (all other known 1918 keys) and shuffled-ciphertext controls by a margin corresponding to p < 1e-6 after correction. (5) Plaintext content is historically plausible for Nov-Dec 1918 (Black Sea, Balkans, Ukraine) and, where possible, matches an external record, as p.217 matched HMS Canterbury's arrival at Sevastopol.

partial_wins.statement: CANDIDATE decrypt of one open message with a newly recovered key meeting criteria (0), (2), (3), (4) and (5), where no second message of the same date window is available to satisfy the cross-message part of (1).

For one open message, a key (documented or recovered) under which a contiguous stretch of at least 60% of the message decrypts to German at 85% coverage with every edit listed, beating the wrong-key and shuffled controls at p < 1e-6 after correction, even though the remainder does not decrypt.

targets.verification_method: Clone the repo and run verify.py to reproduce the 12 known decrypts. Re-derive the target ciphertext from Lasry et al. 2017 or Schmeh's #46 article where possible, and do not trust messages.py alone. Use an independent ADFGVX implementation, apply the claimed key and edits, score German coverage, and run wrong-key and shuffled nulls with the verifier's own code.

targets.name: Beale ciphers #1 (location) and #3 (names): book-cipher key-text search
targets.statement: Beale cipher #2 decodes with the Declaration of Independence (word n gives its initial letter). Ciphers #1 (about 520 numbers, max about 2906) and #3 (about 618 numbers) remain undeciphered. Either find the key text and numbering rule, or prove they are constructed nonsense. Gillogly found alphabetic runs ('abcdefghiijklmmnohpp') when B1 is decoded with the DoI, which is evidence of fabrication.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if ALL of the following hold. (1) A specific key text published before 1885 is identified, with exact edition or source, and a single deterministic numbering rule declared in advance (word-initial letter, a fixed treatment of hyphens and abbreviations, a fixed offset). (2) At least 90% of the numbers in B1 (or B3) decode under that rule to a continuous English text that is coherent and specific: B1 should describe a location, B3 should list names and residences. (3) The number of key texts times rule variants searched is reported, and the decode's English score beats the best decode over the same search applied to at least 1000 permuted copies of the cipher numbers (permutation p < 1e-6 after Bonferroni). (4) No per-number fudging beyond a declared error list of at most 3%. (5) The cipher must still be listed unsolved (Wikipedia list of ciphertexts, MTC3 Level X) at verification time. A hoax proof is NOT a confirmed solve; it is partial win p1.

partial_wins.statement: Rigorous hoax proof: a fully specified generative model of how B1 or B3 was produced (for example sequential selection from DoI word positions), with all competing genuine-book-cipher models declared before fitting, that explains the observed statistics with a likelihood ratio above 1e6 against every declared genuine model, and is a new quantitative result beyond Gillogly's runs, Nickell, and Wase's stylometry.

A specific pre-1885 key text (exact edition) and a single pre-declared numbering rule under which at least 300 consecutive numbers of B1 or B3 decode to coherent English, with at most 3% declared errors, and the decode beats the same search on 1000 permuted copies at p < 1e-6 after Bonferroni over all texts and rule variants searched.

targets.verification_method: Obtain the cipher numbers from the 1885 pamphlet transcription (Cipher Foundation) and cross-check them against a second transcription (GitHub cipher1.txt/cipher3.txt). Obtain the key text from an independent scan, word-index it with the declared rule using the verifier's own code, decode, score English, and rerun the permutation null.

targets.name: Chinese gold bar cryptograms (Shanghai, 1933)
targets.statement: Seven 'gold bars' allegedly issued to a General Wang in Shanghai (1933) carry Chinese text about a transaction over $300,000,000, unknown script, and 16 distinct Latin-letter cryptogram lines of 8-25 letters. Several lines are repeated across bars, e.g. SKCDKJCDJCYQSZKTZJPXPWIRN, MQOLCSJTLGAJOKBSSBOMUPCE, RHZVIYQIYSXVNQXQWIOVWPJO, FEWGDRHDDEEUMFFTEEMJXZR, HFXPCQYZVATXAWIZPVE, VIOHIKNNGUAB. Letter statistics are very flat. Determine what the lines encode.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if a single deterministic system and key (for example a period-appropriate polyalphabetic or commercial codebook) decodes ALL 16 lines (about 250 letters) into meaningful text (English, French, or romanized Chinese in Wade-Giles/Postal) that is coherent with the bars' Chinese inscriptions (amounts, bank, dates, names), with no per-line keys unless a documented indicator rule selects them. Alternatively, a decisive proof that the lines are produced by a specific identifiable generator, such as a published test-key or check-code scheme, where the generator reproduces all 16 lines exactly from bar data. The cryptograms must still be listed unsolved (Schmeh Top-50, IACR page) at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: A single identifiable generator (a published 1930s test-key, check-code or textbook scheme) that reproduces at least 4 distinct lines exactly from data on the bars, with the chance probability of that many exact reproductions under the searched generator space below 1e-6.

A single deterministic system and key, with no per-line keys, that decodes at least 4 distinct lines (at least 80 letters in total) into meaningful text coherent with the bars' Chinese inscriptions, while the same system on shuffled-letter lines yields nothing comparable.

targets.verification_method: Use the IACR transcription, cross-checked against the bar photos on the IACR page. Implement the claimed system, decode all lines, check consistency with the translated Chinese text, and run a shuffled-letter null.

targets.name: Remaining unbroken 1941 German Army Enigma messages (CryptoCellar list)
targets.statement: Six German Army 3-rotor Enigma I messages from 1941 on CryptoCellar remain unbroken: EHSTQ (22.06.1941, 52 cipher letters) and RXPSB (28.06, about 99) per g-army-messages.html (30 Sep 2026); KLJBO (03.07, 50), LXACA (05.07, 20), WEUWY (09.07, 48) and JBIYH (20.07, 55) per g-army-july-1941.html (28 Sep 2026; Batch A). The FMNGI break page states that WEUWY must have identical plaintext to another message of the same day, so a WEUWY break is key recovery only. Recover the full key (wheel order, Ringstellung, Stecker, Grundstellung, message key) and plaintext of any one. Recent breaks: ALQFI (28.08.1941) on 14 Jul 2026 via a matching SS-T message; MVUEH by Carter Leffen with GPT-6 Astra (14 Sep 2026); FMNGI by Jack Willis with Claude Opus 5 (final key search completed 20 Sep 2026); AWTZK and ZNLZT by John Woodhouse with Claude Opus 5.5 (26 Sep 2026; 9 and 11 garbles). The three September 1941 messages belong to the separate Ultimate Enigma Challenge target.
targets.success_criterion: Target message must still be shown unbroken on the live g-army-messages.html (EHSTQ, RXPSB) or g-army-july-1941.html (KLJBO, LXACA, WEUWY, JBIYH) at verification time; the 1941-msg-list-unbroken.html overview is stale and is never sufficient. CONFIRMED only if ALL of the following hold. (1) A complete Enigma I key: wheel order, UKW-B, Ringstellung, Stecker, Grundstellung, message key. (2) The indicator decrypts at the Grundstellung to exactly the message key used for the body. (3) The body decrypt of the live CryptoCellar transcription (Kenngruppe removed) is connected German with at least 80% of letters in words or abbreviations. The garble list is pre-declared (at most 15%), and an unfitted decrypt is reported alongside it. (4) For any message under 60 letters, at least one independent external check: the same daily key decrypts another message of that day; or the key matches a published key for that date and the SAME batch (Batch A for the July messages); or the plaintext matches an independently held text (same-day TS or NF copy). (5) The shuffled null is far below the claim. (6) LXACA (20 letters) needs an external key match. For WEUWY the plaintext is presumed known, so success means recovering a key that maps the archived ciphertext to that plaintext and passes (2). It is reported as 'key recovered', not 'new plaintext'.

partial_wins.statement: CANDIDATE break of EHSTQ, KLJBO or JBIYH (under 60 letters): a complete key satisfying criteria (1), (2), (3) and (5) on the live transcription, with the external check of criterion (4) still missing; reported as candidate, not confirmed.

RXPSB (about 99 letters): a complete key satisfying (1) and (2) whose unfitted body decrypt plus a garble list pre-declared at most 15% reaches at least 60% German coverage (below the 80% bar), with the shuffled-ciphertext null under the same solver budget never reaching 40%.

targets.verification_method: Use a known-good Enigma simulator with double-stepping, regression-tested on MVUEH, FMNGI and AWTZK using their published keys from the break pages. Re-extract ciphertext and indicators from g-army-messages.html or g-army-july-1941.html, NOT from the stale unbroken-overview page. Check indicator consistency and decrypt with and without the declared garbles. Before any claim, re-check the live July page and the main Army page for a new 'Broken' annotation. A daily-key cross-check against e-keys-july-1941.html is valid only for Batch B messages; the four July targets are Batch A.

targets.name: Unbroken German Army Truppenschlüssel (TS) hand-cipher messages, 1941 (CryptoCellar)
targets.statement: Frode Weierud's CryptoCellar (g-army-ts-messages.html, updated 27 Jul 2026) lists about 40 German Army Truppenschlüssel (TS) messages from June to September 1941. TS is a hand substitution cipher using two 5x5 squares (25-letter alphabet, J written as II), described in Ostwald and Weierud's Cryptologia article 'Modern Cryptanalysis of the Truppenschlüssel'. 11 are marked broken (10 on 22.01.2022, TUNYA on 26.01.2022); about 29 carry no 'Broken' marker, e.g. YSGSS (28.06.1941, 13 letters), FCVHR/HKMZI/FBOIQ (03.07; FBOIQ 38), KVLIG/SGOXX/UBYVQ/HFEYY/LICUD/DSZPZ/DEZPS/TKYKJ (04.07; TKYKJ 35), SSKFV/HOHOX (06.07), IABZV/EHNPZ/IASRZ (08.07; IASRZ appears twice, 90 and 52 letters), XWFEC (12.07), AFUVO (13.07, 14), DOLHA, CPUDN (32), NEUEM, LSSLG, CFQIB, VHRNE, ZUBZE, MZXNX, AAXYN, AOXST. The page publishes NO keys or plaintexts for the broken messages and attributes the failures to unfavourable plaintext, garbles or ciphering errors, and short messages. Break any one qualifying unbroken message: recover its key and plaintext. Context: TS plaintexts for 10-11 July 1941 were supplied privately by Olaf Ostwald (requested by Sean Harrington) for the Sept 2026 AWTZK/ZNLZT Enigma attack; none of the Sept 2026 breaks touched TS.
targets.success_criterion: Target message must still carry no 'Broken' marker on https://www.cryptocellar.org/bgac/g-army-ts-messages.html at verification time (otherwise the result is reported as a non-first re-break). CONFIRMED only if ALL of the following hold. (1) The full key (both 5x5 squares) and the exact TS procedure are given, with the procedure cited to Ostwald and Weierud's Cryptologia article 'Modern Cryptanalysis of the Truppenschlüssel' (section and page). (2) Deterministic decryption of the CryptoCellar transcription (re-extracted fresh) gives connected German military text, with at least 85% of letters inside German words or standard Wehrmacht abbreviations. (3) A garble list is declared BEFORE scoring: at most 8% of letters, each Morse-plausible, with red J positions treated as unknown symbols. (4) Length gate: only messages of at least 80 cipher letters qualify alone. A shorter message qualifies only if the SAME key also decrypts another same-date message to German meeting (2), AND the Cryptologia description confirms that same-day messages share a key. Messages under 40 letters are never CONFIRMED. (5) A shuffled-ciphertext null: 200 shuffles, same pipeline and budget, best score at least 5 SD below the claim. (6) Historical coherence with June to September 1941 traffic of the same net. A custodian 'Broken' marker counts as final external confirmation.
