partial_wins.statement: Blind garble-tolerance benchmark: the verifier enciphers 3 period-style German military texts of 60-100 letters with the TS procedure as implemented from the Cryptologia paper (validated on its worked example), using random squares and injecting about 8% Morse-plausible garbles; the solver, given only the ciphertexts, recovers at least 95% of the plaintext letters of all 3 within a declared compute budget.

A pair of 5x5 squares under which a contiguous run of at least 70 cipher letters of one unbroken message (at least 80 letters long) decrypts to German with at least 85% word/abbreviation coverage, with a garble list declared before scoring and the 200-shuffle null at least 5 SD below, even if the rest of the message exceeds the 8% garble cap.

Same-key evidence: one pair of squares decrypts two unbroken messages of the same date to German meeting criterion (2) on each, with the null at least 5 SD below on each; this counts as a partial win when the Cryptologia description does not confirm daily key sharing (so the full criterion's same-day clause cannot be invoked).

targets.verification_method: Implement TS from the Cryptologia paper's description and worked example. No broken keys are public, so validate the implementation by encrypting and decrypting the paper's own example, and if possible ask the custodian (a human action) for one broken key. Re-scrape the page with a script and assert each message's length against the page's stated length. Apply the claimed key and declared garbles, compute German coverage with a lexicon plus an abbreviation list, rerun the shuffled null with the verifier's own solver, and check same-day key consistency where it is used.

targets.name: D'Agapeyeff cipher (1939 textbook challenge)
targets.statement: A 395-digit challenge cipher from the first edition of Alexander D'Agapeyeff's 'Codes and Ciphers' (1939), dropped from later editions; the author reportedly later forgot how he made it. Read as digit pairs it gives 197 pairs plus one leftover digit (196 pairs if the trailing '000' padding is discarded), with 19 distinct pairs drawn almost entirely from rows 6-9 and columns 1-5, plus the anomalous '04' (from ...63630 47481...) and '00' (from the trailing '92000'). This suggests a Polybius-square stage. It has an unusually flat distribution and a low pairs IC. D'Agapeyeff described nulls inserted every third, fourth or fifth letter as one technique. Find the method and plaintext.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if ALL of the following hold. (0) The canonical input is the full 395-digit string from the MTC3 PDF; the treatment of the trailing '000' and of the irregular pair '04' is declared before searching, and counts toward the error budget in (2) if they are treated as slips. (1) The method is a single procedure from D'Agapeyeff's 1939 book, with page reference, using only techniques of the type it teaches (Polybius squares, keyword alphabets, columnar transposition, nulls at a fixed rule, Playfair-like digraphic substitution), fully specified with all keys and no rule changes mid-text. (2) It deterministically maps the ENTIRE ciphertext to grammatical English (or French/Russian if argued), with at least 95% of letters in words and at most 4 declared encipherment errors, each explainable as a single slip. (3) Key-space accounting: the bits in all keys combined must be below 0.6 x (decoded plaintext length x 3.2 bits). (4) The same pipeline on 500 shuffled versions of the ciphertext never yields comparable English. (5) The cipher is still listed unsolved on Wikipedia and MTC3 Level X (0 solvers) at verification time; unverified public claims (e.g. the Nov 2025 comment) do not count as prior solutions unless they meet (0)-(4).

partial_wins.statement: A single procedure from the 1939 book (page cited) with fully specified keys that decrypts at least 100 consecutive pairs to English with at least 95% word coverage and at most 2 declared slips, satisfies the key-bit bound (3) for that segment, and passes the 500-shuffle null on that segment.

Near-solve: a method and key meeting (0), (1), (3), (4) that decrypts the entire ciphertext to English with at least 95% word coverage but needs 5-8 declared single-slip errors (exceeding the 4-error budget).

targets.verification_method: Extract the digits from the MTC3 PDF with pdftotext and assert 395 digits. Apply the declared padding rule, implement the claimed method independently, decrypt, measure coverage, recompute key bits and run the 500-shuffle null.

targets.name: Henry Debosnys cryptograms (1882-83)
targets.statement: Henry Debosnys, executed in 1883 for murdering his wife in Essex County NY, left several enciphered documents and poems in a symbol script. One transcription counts 1,188 glyph instances of 425 glyph types; another treats glyphs as composed of subglyphs (possibly syllables). Nobody has decrypted a single word. It is #3 on Schmeh's Top-50.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if a single subglyph or glyph-to-sound/letter mapping, fixed across ALL documents, yields readable text in a natural language (French, English, Portuguese or Spanish, all plausible for Debosnys) over at least 300 consecutive glyph instances, with at least 85% word coverage. Any poem must keep plausible meter or rhyme, and a held-out document never used in fitting must decode with the same mapping. All decoding is against a transcription frozen with a SHA-256 hash BEFORE any fitting (Sektu's if obtainable, or a new one from Cipher Foundation scans, made blind to the solver), and the cryptograms must still be listed unsolved at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: A glyph or subglyph mapping fitted on one document that, frozen and applied to a held-out document of the hashed transcription, decodes at least 100 consecutive glyph instances to a natural language with at least 85% word coverage and beats a mapping-shuffle null at p < 1e-4.

Identification of a specific published 19th-century shorthand system (e.g. Duployé, Prévost-Delaunay, Pitman) whose direct transliteration, with the sign table taken from a cited manual and not fitted, yields readable text for at least 50 consecutive glyph instances of a held-out document, beating a sign-shuffle null at p < 1e-4.

targets.verification_method: First freeze a transcription with its SHA-256: either Sektu's, if obtainable, or a new one from Cipher Foundation scans made before any decipherment attempt and blind to the solver. Fit on one document, apply the frozen mapping to a held-out document, measure language coverage, and compare against a mapping-shuffle null.

targets.name: Dorabella cipher (Elgar, 1897)
targets.statement: An 87-character note of semicircle glyphs (24 distinct symbol types), sent by Edward Elgar to Dora Penny in July 1897. Transcribed by Schmeh as: ABCDE FGDHA IJKLJ MJJFB BJNGO GNIP / GJGFQ DHRSC JJCFN KGJIJ FTPKL QHHQI P / CPFUP CLUUN PCJFU KPNDB NPFDL ED. Modern MASC solvers that handle 87-letter English or Latin MASCs at about 98% succeed fail on it, which suggests it is not a plain monoalphabetic substitution. Find the method and plaintext.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if ALL of the following hold. (1) A method family is declared BEFORE searching, from systems Elgar is documented to have known (for example Elgar's own Pigpen-like cipher notes, Playfair, keyword substitution with transposition), with total key bits stated. (2) The method decrypts all 87 symbols to grammatical English with at most 2 exceptions. (3) Key bits are below 0.5 x 87 x 3.2 ≈ 140, or else an external corroboration such as the key written in Elgar's papers. (4) Across 1000 random 87-symbol strings with the same symbol-frequency profile, the same solver never achieves comparable fluency. The cipher must still show 0 solvers on MTC3 Level X at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: Archival corroboration: a citable document in Elgar's papers or correspondence (archive, shelfmark, scan) that gives a key, method or plaintext for the Dorabella note, which a skeptic can open and apply to the 87-symbol MTC3 transcription.

Over-budget candidate: a method family declared before searching and a key that decrypts all 87 symbols to grammatical English with at most 2 exceptions and passes the 1000-string frequency-matched null, but with key bits between 140 and 200 (failing only criterion (3)); reported as candidate, not confirmed.

targets.verification_method: Use Schmeh's MTC3 transcription and check it against the original image. Implement the method independently, decrypt, check grammar and word coverage, recompute key bits, and run the frequency-matched random-string null.

targets.name: Kryptos K4: recover the encryption METHOD (plaintext known only to Sanborn and archive owners)
targets.statement: K4 is the 97-letter final section of Jim Sanborn's Kryptos at CIA HQ (Wikipedia gives OBKRUOXOGHULBSOLIFBBWFLRVQQPRNGKSSOTWTQSJQSSEKZZWATJKLUDIAWINFBNYPVTTMZFPKWGDKZXTJCDIGKUHUAUEKCAR; verify the 97-character length). Sanborn's public clues fix positions 22-34 to EASTNORTHEAST and 64-74 to BERLINCLOCK (1-indexed). In Sept 2025 Jarett Kobek and Richard Byrne found the K4 plaintext in Smithsonian archive scraps. They do not intend to release it, and Sanborn says 'K4 has not been solved... discovered', with the method known only to Sanborn and Scheidt. RR Auction sold the full archive (plaintext, coding system, K5 materials) on 20 Nov 2025 for $962,500. The buyer, Paradigm, announced on 12 Jun 2026 a sealed SHA-256 plus Google Cloud KMS verification oracle that accepts K4 plaintext guesses for $1 each, without publishing plaintext or method. The open problem is the cryptanalytic method that maps the ciphertext to a plaintext consistent with all cribs. The oracle is reached through the CTF site and requires an account plus payment, so it is strictly a human-only action.
targets.success_criterion: CANDIDATE (not a confirmed result): one fully specified deterministic method with key bits ≤ 60 maps all 97 letters such that positions 22-34 = EASTNORTHEAST and 64-74 = BERLINCLOCK exactly, the remaining 73 letters reach ≥ 85% English word coverage, there are no per-position exceptions, AND the same method family run against 1000 random 97-letter strings never satisfies both cribs plus that coverage. CONFIRMED: only after the human submits the candidate to Paradigm's official K4 oracle and reports a positive verdict. Agents never create accounts, pay, or submit.

partial_wins.statement: CANDIDATE tier exactly as defined in the success criterion: one deterministic method with key bits at most 60, both cribs exact at positions 22-34 and 64-74, remaining 73 letters at least 85% English word coverage, no per-position exceptions, and the 1000-random-string null never satisfied.

Crib-only constraint hit: a single fully specified method with key bits at most 60 that reproduces all 24 crib letters at their exact positions, where the identical method-family search over 1000 random 97-letter strings never satisfies both cribs; reported as a structural finding, never as a plaintext claim.

targets.verification_method: Re-derive the ciphertext from the Wikipedia K4 string and assert 97 letters. Implement the method independently, decrypt, and assert the crib positions. Compute key bits and check that a 1000-run search of the same method family against random 97-letter strings cannot hit both cribs plus readable English. Final step: the human submits the plaintext to paradigm.xyz/kryptos-ctf and reports the oracle verdict.

targets.name: Cicada 3301 Liber Primus: unsolved runic pages
targets.statement: The Liber Primus (2014) is a runic book in Cicada's Gematria Primus (29 runes). Its early pages were decrypted (Vigenère with DIVINITY or FIRFUMFERENFE keys, Atbash/shift, and a totient-of-primes stream). The remaining pages, about 12,956 runes (56 of 58 LP2 pages by one count), are unsolved. Their statistical signature is near-uniform with strongly suppressed adjacent repeats (86 observed against 447 expected, i.e. 0.66-0.68% against 3.45%), and no periodicity. Recover any unsolved page.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if a deterministic, fully specified key or keystream rule decrypts at least one complete unsolved page section (at least 150 consecutive runes) into English (Cicada's archaic style acceptable) with at least 90% word coverage. The same rule family must also reproduce at least one already-solved section, and the claim must pass the Dukotah repo's verify_solution.py oracle after its --selftest succeeds. Running the rule on rune-shuffled pages must not give English. verify_solution.py is a community tool, so passing it is necessary but not sufficient: an independent re-implementation by the verifier must reproduce the decrypt. The target page must still be listed unsolved in the Dukotah repo at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: A deterministic, fully specified rule that decrypts 50-149 consecutive runes of an unsolved page to English with at least 90% word coverage, reproduces at least one already-solved section with the same rule family, and gives no English on rune-shuffled copies of that page.

A deterministic rule that decrypts at least 150 consecutive runes of an unsolved page to English with at least 90% word coverage, verified by an independent re-implementation and failing on shuffled pages, but whose rule family does not reproduce any already-solved section; reported as candidate.

targets.verification_method: Clone Dukotah/cicada3301, run verify_solution.py --selftest, then run it on the claimed key. Independently re-transcribe the target page from the byte-verified source images (SHA1 matches listed in the repo). Decrypt with the verifier's own Gematria Primus implementation and score English.

targets.name: MysteryTwister 'Double Column Transposition Reloaded' Parts 1-3 (0 solvers since 2013)
targets.statement: After George Lasry broke Schmeh's original Double Transposition Challenge in November 2013, Wacker, Esslinger and Schmeh published three harder Level III challenges that avoid the exploited weaknesses. Part 1: English plaintext, 613 letters, both keys 20-27 long and coprime, keys derived from English sentences; the answer is the first 34 plaintext letters. Part 2: two English texts interleaved word by word, keys 20-27, coprime and random; the answer is the first 37 letters. Part 3: German plaintext, 1006 letters, keys 27-34, coprime and random; the answer is the first 48 letters. MTC3 lists 0 solvers for each. These challenges were designed to defeat Lasry's published attack and have resisted the community, including Lasry, since 2013.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED for a Part if the claim gives two transposition keys whose lengths satisfy that Part's stated ranges and coprimality, plus the exact columnar convention (irregular grid, row-wise fill, read-out by key order, tie-breaking rule; for Part 1 the sentence-to-key convention, frozen before declaring success). Decrypting the ENTIRE canonical ciphertext (the MTC3 ciphertext .txt, cross-checked against the PDF: Part 1 = 613 letters, Part 3 = 1006 letters, Part 2 measured and asserted) must give fluent English (Parts 1 and 2; for Part 2 both interleaved texts must read correctly when de-interleaved) or German (Part 3), with at least 97% of letters inside dictionary words and no edits, and re-encrypting that plaintext with the same keys must reproduce the ciphertext exactly. First-solve status is judged against the live solver count on https://mysterytwister.org/challenges/level-3/ at verification time. Only the human may submit the first-N-letters answer to MTC3.

partial_wins.statement: Blind Part-3-parameter benchmark: the verifier double-transposes 3 German texts of 1006 letters with random coprime keys of lengths 27-34 (MTC3 convention); the solver, ciphertext-only, recovers both keys and the full plaintext of at least 2 of the 3 with exact round-trip.

Blind Part-1-parameter benchmark: the verifier double-transposes 3 English texts of 613 letters with coprime keys of lengths 20-27 derived from English sentences under a convention unknown to the solver; the solver recovers both keys and the full plaintext of at least 2 of the 3 with exact round-trip.

targets.verification_method: As written, plus assert extracted lengths of Part 1 = 613 and Part 3 = 1006 letters (Part 2 to be measured), using the MTC3 ciphertext .txt (e.g. /media/challenges/add/mtc3-wacker-08-DCTreloaded-01-ciphertext.txt) as the canonical source, cross-checked against the PDF. Only the human may submit the first-N-letters answer.

targets.name: MysteryTwister 'The Hutton Cipher – Part 5' (4,250-letter ciphertext-only, 0 solvers since 2023)
targets.statement: Eric Bond Hutton's 2018 pen-and-paper cipher: a repeating keyword K1 and a keyword-mixed alphabet from K2. For each letter, the shift is n = rank(K1[i mod |K1|]) + rank(current first letter of the alphabet). The plaintext letter is swapped with the letter n places to its right, and that letter is output, so the alphabet mutates every step. Part 5 is a ciphertext-only challenge with contemporary English plaintext, numerals spelled out, spaces and punctuation removed, and both keywords random strings under 10 letters. The ciphertext file hutton_ciphertext_5.txt holds 4,250 A-Z letters (4,272 bytes including 22 newlines) with IC 0.0385. Recover the plaintext and both keywords.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED if keywords K1 and K2 (each under 10 letters) are given such that the Hutton procedure exactly as specified in the PDF decrypts the ENTIRE 4,250-letter ciphertext to fluent contemporary English with ≥97% of letters in dictionary words and zero edits, and re-encryption with the same keys reproduces the ciphertext byte for byte. Key space is about 85 bits against about 13,000 bits of plaintext redundancy, so a fluent full decrypt is decisive. Final external confirmation comes when the human submits on MTC3. First-solve status is judged against the live solver count on https://mysterytwister.org/challenges/level-2/ at verification time. Only the human submits to MTC3.

partial_wins.statement: Reduced blind benchmark: the verifier enciphers 3 contemporary English texts of 4,250 letters with the Part 5 procedure (verified on the PDF example) under random keywords K1, K2 of fewer than 10 letters, disclosing only |K1| and |K2|; the solver recovers both keywords and the full plaintext of at least 2 of the 3, checked by exact re-encryption.
Full blind benchmark: as above but with keyword lengths undisclosed; the solver recovers both keywords and the full plaintext of at least 2 of the 3, ciphertext-only, checked by exact re-encryption.

targets.verification_method: Implement Hutton exactly per the PDF and check it reproduces the PDF example: MEETMEATTHEGREENMANATTHREE with FEDORA/JUPITER gives RSBIENXONGQYTMWQVWXWIOKXKU. An auditor implementation already round-trips this. Download the add.zip, strip newlines and assert 4,250 letters. Decrypt with the claimed keys, re-encrypt and diff, then run a dictionary-coverage check.

targets.name: MysteryTwister Spanish Strip Cipher Part 3 (Spanish Civil War telegram, 0 solvers)
targets.statement: An original Spanish Civil War telegram (summer or fall 1936), apparently encrypted with the Spanish Strip Cipher (SSC): a homophonic substitution where a keyword-derived, shifted random alphabet assigns each plaintext letter to a column of 3-5 two-digit homophones; the challenge hint allows an alphabet that includes LL and CH and may omit W. The ciphertext is 142 two-digit tokens with 55 distinct values (range 02-98). The plaintext is most likely Spanish, possibly Basque. MTC3 Level X (published 2014-03-27) lists 0 solvers.
targets.success_criterion: The challenge must still show 0 solvers on https://mysterytwister.org/challenges/level-x/ at verification time for a first-solve claim. CONFIRMED only if ALL of the following hold. (1) The homophone-to-letter key respects the SSC structure as the PDF hints allow it: 3-5 homophones per column; an ordered alphabet that may include LL and CH and may omit W; a keyword-derived random alphabet plus an initial shift, with the variant declared before searching. (2) All 142 tokens decrypt to coherent Spanish or Basque telegraphic text, with at least 90% of letters in words or telegram abbreviations and at most 3 declared garbles. (3) Key-entropy accounting: with 55 distinct homophones, a free mapping costs about 55 x log2(28) ≈ 264 bits, against roughly 142 x 3 ≈ 426 bits of plaintext redundancy. Free mappings are therefore marginal. A claim must either derive the mapping from a keyword-and-shift table structure (≤ about 100 bits) or pass (4) by a wide margin. (4) Null: 200 random token sequences matched on length and repeat profile never reach comparable fluency. (5) Content is plausible for summer or fall 1936.

partial_wins.statement: A structured key (keyword-derived alphabet plus shift plus table layout, at most about 100 bits, variant declared before searching) under which at least 100 consecutive tokens decrypt to Spanish or Basque telegraphic text with at least 90% coverage and at most 2 declared garbles, while 200 length- and repeat-profile-matched random token sequences never reach comparable fluency.

Blind benchmark: the verifier enciphers 3 period-style Spanish telegrams of 142 tokens under randomly drawn SSC variants within the PDF's allowed space (3-5 homophones per column, optional LL/CH, optional W); the solver recovers at least 95% of plaintext letters of at least 2 of the 3.

targets.verification_method: Extract the tokens with pdftotext from pages 9/10 of the PDF and assert 142 tokens and 55 distinct values. Check the structural constraints programmatically under the declared variant, then score with Spanish and Basque lexica and run the null.

targets.name: MysteryTwister 'Spirale Part 4' (hand 'OTP' cipher, 0 solvers)
targets.statement: Spirale is a hand cipher by Philippe Allard designed to resemble a one-time pad. Part 4 is ciphertext-only: a 485-letter A-Z ciphertext (ciphertext_Spirale-04.txt) under four NEW random keys of exactly 7 letters each (lenkey=7 in the reference code, about 131.6 bits in total). K1 and K2 generate alphabet permutations; K3 and K4 generate the long key through a lagged-Fibonacci-style recurrence X_n = X_{n-d} o X_{n-k} under a generalized operator. The official zip (mtc3-allard-04-spirale-04-add.zip) contains MTC3_Spirale_Description.pdf, the ciphertext and spirale.zip with the reference implementation Spirale2.1.3.py. The MTC3 answer is the first four words of the second sentence. MTC3 Level III lists 0 solvers (published 2015-08-23). Parts 1-3 keys are not published.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED if four 7-letter keys and a 485-letter plaintext are given such that the unmodified Spirale2.1.3.py from the official zip encrypts the plaintext to ciphertext_Spirale-04.txt byte for byte (after whitespace normalization), and the plaintext is fluent natural language with at least 97% dictionary coverage. The human may optionally submit the first four words of the second sentence to MTC3. First-solve status is judged against the live solver count on https://mysterytwister.org/challenges/level-3/ at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: Blind full-key benchmark: the verifier encrypts a fresh ~485-letter English text with Spirale2.1.3.py (default alphabet) under four random 7-letter keys; the solver, ciphertext-only, returns all four keys and the plaintext, and the unmodified reference script reproduces the ciphertext byte for byte.

Blind keystream benchmark: as above, but the verifier discloses K1 and K2; the solver recovers K3, K4 and the plaintext from ciphertext only, verified by exact re-encryption with the reference script.

targets.verification_method: Download mtc3-allard-04-spirale-04-add.zip, record its SHA-256, and unzip it along with the inner spirale.zip. Run 'python Spirale2.1.3.py -e K1 K2 K3 K4' on the claimed plaintext with the default alphabet and diff against ciphertext_Spirale-04.txt. Assert 485 letters. Run a language-coverage check.

targets.name: Noita Eye Messages (designed game cipher, developer-confirmed real)
targets.statement: Nine messages of eye glyphs in five orientations (5 East, 4 West) in the game Noita (2020). Read as trigrams in base 5, they give an 83-symbol alphabet with values 0-82 and no gaps. Known structure includes no immediately doubled trigrams, shared aligned sections and isomorphs across messages, and a distinct first character per message. The developers say the messages contain a real message. The leading model is a deck or group-autokey style polyalphabetic cipher over S_83. Recover the plaintext and method. The developers' 'real message' confirmation is older; wiki.gg (updated May 2026) shows no new developer statement.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if a single fully specified algorithm and key (or key-derivation rule) decrypts ALL nine messages from the community's standard trigram transcription into readable text in a natural language (English or Finnish most likely). Each message must have at least 90% of characters in dictionary words. The method must reproduce the observed isomorph alignments and the no-doubles property as consequences, and must not use per-message ad hoc tables. Decrypting with the same method on symbol-shuffled messages must give no readable text. The puzzle must still be listed unsolved on the community tracker at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: Frozen held-out structure prediction: a fully specified cipher family and key-update rule fitted on at most 8 of the 9 messages (fitting set and model hash committed before the held-out message is scored) that predicts specific symbol relations in the held-out message beyond the already-documented isomorphs and alignments, with those predictions holding at p < 1e-6 against a shuffled-message null.

A single fully specified algorithm and key that decrypts at least one complete message (from the standard trigram transcription) to a natural language with at least 90% dictionary-word coverage, reproduces the no-doubles property as a consequence, and gives no readable text on symbol-shuffled messages, even if it does not yet decrypt all nine.

targets.verification_method: Take the transcription from the wiki or community data files, re-derive the trigram values with the verifier's own parser from the glyph orientation data, implement the claimed algorithm, decrypt all 9, check language coverage, check the isomorph-explanation property, and run the shuffled null.

targets.name: Somerton Man (Tamam Shud) code: exact initialism source search
targets.statement: The pencilled code from the back of the Rubaiyat in the 1948 Somerton Man case reads: W(M?)RGOABABD / [struck] MLIAOI / WTBIMPANETP / MLIABO AIAQC / ITTMTSAMSTGAB, with an 'X' over one O. Abbott's group judged it most likely the initial letters of words, while Rehling (2014) suggested shorthand that is unrecoverable. The man was identified in 2022 as Carl 'Charles' Webb, but the code remains unbroken. The target: find the exact source text, if it is an initialism of a published text, or another deterministic decoding. Lines 1, 3, 4 and 5 total 44 letters (9 + 11 + 11 + 13).
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if the claim exhibits a text demonstrably published before December 1948, with exact edition, whose consecutive word initials reproduce at least 40 of the 44 letters of lines 1, 3, 4 and 5 in order, allowing only the documented M/W ambiguity plus at most 2 further mismatches, with each line mapping to a contiguous passage. In addition, the expected number of such matches in the searched corpus under a word-initial-frequency model must be below 1e-4 (report corpus size in word positions). Free-form 'phrase invention' (making up a sentence per letter) is never acceptable. If lines are matched to different passages, the chance expectation is computed per line and combined (product of per-line expectations times the number of passage combinations considered), and the combined expectation must be below 1e-4. M/W and crossed-out-line handling is declared before searching.

partial_wins.statement: One full line (line 3, 4 or 5; 11-13 letters) matched by the consecutive word initials of a single contiguous passage in a text demonstrably published before December 1948, with at most 1 mismatch, and a per-line chance expectation below 1e-4 over the reported corpus size in word positions.

Two different lines each matched (at most 2 mismatches each) by contiguous passages of the SAME pre-December-1948 work, with the combined chance expectation (per-line expectations multiplied, times the number of within-work position pairs considered) below 1e-4.

targets.verification_method: Obtain the source passage from an independent digitized copy (HathiTrust, Internet Archive, Trove). Compute word initials with a script and align them to the code with the allowed mismatches. Recompute the chance-match expectation from initial-letter frequencies and the stated corpus size.

targets.name: CryptoCellar 'Ultimate Enigma Challenge' (5 Sept 1941 messages, possibly non-standard machine)
targets.statement: Five messages with Enigma-style indicators but unusual operators, comments and very low radio frequencies: QTXMA and SZAEJ (29.09.1941) and BYQMZ, FKQLZ and XFEDT (30.09.1941). The ultimate-enigma.html page gives raw character counts including headers (280/129/308/198/226); the unbroken overview gives cipher letters for the 30.09 messages only (BYQMZ 167, FKQLZ 107, XFEDT 97); cipher-letter counts for QTXMA and SZAEJ are unverified. Weierud suspects a police network (Ordnungspolizei) and possibly a machine with different wheel wiring. Every attack since 2003-2004 has failed. Break any of them.
targets.success_criterion: CONFIRMED only if a fully specified machine (wiring of all wheels and reflector, stepping, plugboard) and ONE daily key decrypt at least TWO messages of the SAME date (two of BYQMZ, FKQLZ, XFEDT for 30.09, or QTXMA plus SZAEJ for 29.09) to German with at least 85% coverage. Garbles are pre-declared and at most 10%. Both indicators must decrypt consistently to their message keys. Any non-standard wiring must be a documented historical wiring or be derived once and then held fixed across both messages. Shuffled nulls are run per message. The messages must still be shown unbroken on https://www.cryptocellar.org/bgac/ultimate-enigma.html at verification time.

partial_wins.statement: Single-message machine break: a fully specified machine of documented historical wiring (e.g. Enigma I, Enigma G, Railway Enigma, Swiss K) and key under which one message of at least 97 cipher letters (BYQMZ, FKQLZ or XFEDT) has a consistent indicator and decrypts to German with at least 85% coverage, garbles pre-declared and at most 10%, and the shuffled null for that message far below the claim, without yet a second same-date message.

Single-message hand-cipher break: a fully specified hand system (e.g. Doppelkasten or a police transposition) and key that decrypts one of the 30.09 messages to German with at least 85% coverage, at most 10% pre-declared garbles, key bits below half the message's redundancy (message length x 3.2 bits / 2), and a per-message shuffled null far below the claim.

targets.verification_method: Re-extract the ciphertext from ultimate-enigma.html and separate header from cipher groups, asserting letter counts against the unbroken overview (167/107/97 for the 30.09 messages). Implement the machine independently, check the indicators and run the nulls.

targets.name: Cypro-Minoan: sign-inventory merges and Cypriot-syllabary value transfer tested on held-out inscriptions
targets.statement: Cypro-Minoan (Late Bronze Age Cyprus and Ugarit; about 250 objects; inventory estimates of 88 to 112 or more signs; Donnelly 2025 gives an integrated signary of 112 signs plus variants) is undeciphered. About 9-11 signs have plausible phonetic values via Linear A/B and the Iron Age Cypriot syllabary, but none of these is definitive. Two things are open. First, whether CM1/CM2/CM3 are one script or several; Corazza et al. (PLoS ONE 2022) used deep learning to argue for reclassification. Second, which variants are distinct signs. The task is a sign-merge and value-transfer hypothesis that makes checkable predictions on held-out inscriptions. There is no authoritative open machine-readable corpus (Olivier 2007 HoChyMin and Ferrara 2012-13 are print), so data entry is the binding constraint. Tamburini's CSA_OptMatcher (Frontiers in AI, 2025-05-30) has NOT been applied to Cypro-Minoan; its 86.3% figure is on the Cypriot Syllabary/Greek benchmark. Status as of 2026-10-03: Undeciphered as of 2026-10-03 (Donnelly 2025 monograph). CM1/2/3 classification is debated (Corazza et al. PLoS ONE 2022). No accepted phonetic values beyond plausible Cypriot and Linear A homomorph transfers.
targets.success_criterion: There are two possible outcomes. (A) A sign-merge set: fixed using at most 70% of inscriptions, then on the held-out inscriptions it must raise cross-inscription sequence recurrence (repeated sign-groups at least 3 long) by at least 25% over the raw signary. The null is a matched random merge set, and the gain must have p < 0.01. (B) A value transfer: Cypriot-syllabary values applied to CM homomorphs that produce at least 3 sign-groups which match independently attested Cypriot or Ugaritic personal names or toponyms from a list fixed in advance. The phonological-latitude-adjusted null (random value permutations) must give p < 0.01. Outcome (B) must also report how many matches random assignments produce. Both outcomes are subject to these conditions. Every inscription used must be transcribed from or checked against Olivier 2007 (HoChyMin) or Ferrara 2012-13, with sign IDs mapped to the Donnelly 2025 integrated signary; the hawkinsnick corpus cannot be the sole source. For (B), the name list (Ugaritic and Cypriot prosopography) and the phonological-equivalence rules are frozen and hashed before any reading is produced. Report the full null distribution of match counts from random value permutations. The p < 0.01 must survive Bonferroni correction over all sign-group lengths tried.

partial_wins.statement: Outcome (A) at a weaker threshold: a sign-merge set fixed on at most 70% of inscriptions (all transcribed from or checked against HoChyMin/Ferrara, sign IDs mapped to the Donnelly 2025 signary) that raises held-out cross-inscription recurrence of sign-groups of length at least 3 by at least 15% over the raw signary, with p < 0.01 against matched random merge sets.

Outcome (B) at a weaker threshold: Cypriot-syllabary (or CSA_OptMatcher-derived) values applied to CM homomorphs give at least 2 sign-groups matching a frozen, hashed list of independently attested Ugaritic or Cypriot personal names or toponyms under frozen phonological-equivalence rules, with p < 0.01 against random value permutations after Bonferroni correction over all sign-group lengths tried, and the full null distribution reported.

A sequence-only (no sign-shape features) classifier, frozen before evaluation, that separates CM1 from CM2 inscriptions on held-out inscriptions with label-permutation p < 0.01 after controlling for text length, a distributional result not reported by Corazza et al. 2022 or Donnelly 2025.

targets.verification_method: The verifier checks a random 10% of the claimed corpus against HoChyMin or Ferrara images, then recomputes recurrence (A) or name matches (B) and the nulls with its own seed. For (B) it builds its own name list from Ugaritic prosopography before seeing the matches.

targets.name: Cuneiform: identify unplaced transliterated fragments as witnesses of known compositions (electronic Babylonian Library)
targets.statement: The electronic Babylonian Library (LMU Munich) catalogs 328,411 fragments, of which 38,494 are transliterated (625,321 lines), per its public API statistics endpoint on 2026-10-03. Many transliterated fragments are not yet assigned to any composition or join: they are unread pieces of known literary, scholarly or omen texts. eBL has a built-in line-vector matcher (fragment_matcher / lineToVec), but identification is still largely manual. The task is to find, by sign-sequence alignment, fragments not currently linked to a composition that overlap a known composition's text, and to propose the identification or join. Status as of 2026-10-03: Ongoing, open-ended work as of 2026-10-03. ebl-api was last pushed 2026-10-01. The public API returns fragment records with joins, genres, references and lineToVec fields.
targets.success_criterion: At least 1 fragment must meet all of the following. (a) Its eBL record has no joins, no corpus-chapter manuscript link, and no reference or genre naming the matched composition. (b) It aligns to a specific composition witness (eBL corpus chapter or an Oracc edition) over at least 3 consecutive lines or at least 15 consecutive signs, with at most 10% sign mismatches after normalising sign readings. (c) The alignment score has p < 1e-4 against a null of the same fragment aligned to all corpus lines with line order shuffled, Bonferroni-corrected over all fragments searched. (d) The match is not returned in the top 10 of eBL's own fragment matcher for that fragment. (e) The matched lines are not a formula that recurs in at least 5 unrelated compositions. Claim as 'candidate identification', confirmed only when an Assyriologist or the eBL team accepts it. Fragment status (a) and the eBL matcher output (d) are re-checked live at verification time; an identification recorded in eBL or published before the claim voids it.

partial_wins.statement: A fragment meeting conditions (a), (c), (d) and (e) of the full criterion whose alignment to a specific composition witness covers 2 consecutive lines or 10-14 consecutive signs (below the full 3-line / 15-sign bar) with at most 10% sign mismatches after normalisation, at Bonferroni-corrected p < 1e-4 against the shuffled-line null.

A fragment meeting conditions (a), (b), (c) and (e) whose correct composition appears in eBL's own fragment-matcher top 10 but is not recorded anywhere in its eBL record (no join, corpus-chapter manuscript link, reference or genre naming it) and is not identified in the publications its record cites.

targets.verification_method: The verifier fetches the fragment and the composition text via the public eBL API (recording the timestamp), recomputes the alignment with independent code using a published sign-reading normalisation, reruns the shuffled-line null, queries eBL's matcher for that fragment, checks the fragment's joins/references/genres fields and the chapter manuscript list, and checks whether the matched lines are formulaic across the corpus.

targets.name: MOONSHOT: Indus script, sign values or meanings that predict held-out seals
targets.statement: Assign phonetic or logographic values to Indus signs in a way that yields consistent readings in a specific language and predicts unseen inscriptions. Status as of 2026-10-03: Unsolved. The USD 1M Tamil Nadu prize (announced January 2025) is unclaimed and has no formal submission portal. Many 2025-2026 claims (Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, cryptanalytic) are unaccepted. paragorth/Indus- (September 2026) shows that decipherment validators accept wrong keys. Its 2026-09-25 correction found that with more than about 150 signs, wrong keys beat the true key under every objective tested; only small syllabaries (about 80 signs) let correct keys win.
targets.success_criterion: All of these must hold. (1) A frozen sign-to-value table. (2) The paragorth validator plus a planted-key test on synthetic corpora matched to the Indus scale (at least 400 sign types, frequency distribution matched to M77, mean text length about 5, about 4,000 texts): the method ranks the true key first against 100 random and 100 adversarially optimized wrong keys in at least 90% of synthetic replicates. (3) On a verifier-chosen held-out set of seals, the readings produce lexicon matches in the target language beyond scrambled-sign controls with p < 0.001. (4) It predicts at least 5 field-symbol or object-type correlations that are confirmed on the held-out set.

partial_wins.statement: Indus-scale planted-key recovery alone: a frozen method that, on verifier-generated synthetic corpora with at least 400 sign types, M77-matched frequency distribution, mean text length about 5 and about 4,000 texts, ranks the true key first against 100 random and 100 adversarially optimized wrong keys in at least 90% of replicates (paragorth 2026 found no objective that does this above about 150 signs).

A method that passes p1 and whose frozen sign-to-value table, applied to a verifier-chosen held-out set of seals, yields lexicon matches in a named target language beyond scrambled-sign controls with p < 0.001.

targets.verification_method: The verifier runs the validators in paragorth/Indus- and the joyboseroy null suite, does the planted-key recovery on synthetic data, and computes the held-out statistics with its own seeds. Additionally, the verifier generates the scale-matched synthetic corpora itself with fresh seeds.

targets.name: Indus script: structural model trained on the 1977 corpus that predicts later-excavated inscriptions
targets.statement: The Indus script is undeciphered: about 4,000-5,600 texts, 400-700 signs, and very short inscriptions (about 5 signs on average). The open structural sub-problems are the sign function classes (numeral strokes, the frequent 'jar' terminal, fish-sign variants), whether texts split into reusable segments, and whether those segments are consistent across sites (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Lothal, Gulf/Mesopotamian seals). The task is a structural finding that is genuinely predictive. Mahadevan's 1977 concordance (M77) gives a natural time split: models fitted only on M77 can be tested on inscriptions published after 1977, held in the larger indus_website and ICIT corpora. Status as of 2026-10-03: Undeciphered as of 2026-10-03. The USD 1M Tamil Nadu prize (Jan 2025) is unclaimed, with no formal submission portal. 2026 decipherment claims (Zenodo, LLM-dictionary) are unaccepted. paragorth/Indus- (Sept 2026) shows that with more than about 150 signs, wrong keys beat true keys under every objective tested. arXiv 2608.02999 (Aug 2026) shows the standard statistics are non-specific.
targets.success_criterion: A concrete structural claim, for example 'sign class C marks segment-final position', 'segment S is a reusable unit', or 'stroke signs N1-N7 behave as a numeral system with classifier X'. It must be fitted only on M77 texts and frozen in a timestamped file. On the post-M77, non-duplicate held-out texts (deduplicated by object ID and exact sequence) it must predict a measurable property with paired-bootstrap p < 0.001 against BOTH (i) a tuned Kneser-Ney 3-gram trained on the same M77 data and (ii) a SIGIL-style non-linguistic synthetic control matched on unigram and length distribution. Example properties: masked-sign top-1 accuracy, held-out segment-boundary agreement with site-specific variants, or prediction of seal versus tablet object type from sequence. The effect must also replicate separately on at least 2 sites. A claim says 'structural finding', never 'decipherment'. Additionally: (a) Each held-out object has a documented first-publication source dated after 1977 (CISI volume or excavation report); objects without one are excluded. (b) Dedup by seal impression identity: sealings of the same seal count once (use paragorth's 386-identity directory where applicable). (c) The claim is not equivalent to any of paragorth's frozen predictions P1-P9 or Q1-Q14, or to published positional findings (Mahadevan 1977, Rao et al. 2009/2010, Yadav et al., Kriger & Hunt 2026). (d) The effect must beat both baselines on Mohenjo-daro and on Harappa separately.

partial_wins.statement: A frozen, M77-only structural claim that meets every condition of the full criterion (publication-dated post-1977 held-out set, seal-identity dedup, novelty vs paragorth P1-P9/Q1-Q14 and published positional findings, paired-bootstrap p < 0.001 against both the tuned Kneser-Ney 3-gram and the SIGIL-style synthetic control) on the pooled held-out set and on one of Mohenjo-daro or Harappa, but not yet on the other.

Field-symbol conditioning: a frozen M77-only model that predicts the field symbol (unicorn, bull, elephant, etc.) of deduplicated post-1977 held-out seals from the text's terminal segment with accuracy exceeding both the majority-motif baseline and a Kneser-Ney 3-gram-feature classifier trained on the same M77 data, paired-bootstrap p < 0.001, and not among paragorth's frozen predictions.

Ligature substitution: a frozen M77-only list of composite signs AB whose substitution rate for the bigram A B in parallel contexts of the held-out texts exceeds that of frequency-matched random composite/bigram pairs with permutation p < 0.001, not among paragorth's frozen predictions or published positional findings.

targets.verification_method: The verifier clones joyboseroy/indus_decipher (with the M77 CSV) and paragorth/Indus- (im77 plus the derived 5,369-object corpus) and rebuilds the time split independently. It dedups by sequence plus object ID and reruns the frozen model alongside its own KN 3-gram and synthetic control. It checks that no held-out sequence appears in the training data and that reading direction is correct (the joyboseroy repo documents a reversal bug). The p-values are recomputed with 10,000 bootstrap resamples. Additionally, the verifier rebuilds the split from publication metadata, not from corpus membership; confirms no held-out sequence or seal identity appears in training; and diffs the claim against the paragorth frozen prediction files (P1-P9, Q1-Q14).

targets.name: Isthmian (Epi-Olmec): reproducible language-family test and a check of the Justeson-Kaufman grid on texts it was not built from
targets.statement: In 1993, Justeson & Kaufman proposed a partial syllabic decipherment of the Isthmian script (La Mojarra Stela 1, the Tuxtla Statuette, Tres Zapotes C, the Teotihuacan-style mask) as Zoquean. Houston & Coe failed to apply it to the mask text, and Vonk (2020) argued that the corpus is too small for a unique decipherment and that a Huastecan reading fits equally well. Whether either hypothesis can be decided on the data is the open question. The corpus is about 700 tokens and about 160 sign types, and no open machine-readable transcription was confirmed. The chemvatho/isthmian-script repo (created 2025-12-22) reports preliminary log-evidence (PMZ -44.4 vs Huastecan -49.6) from hypothetical, not empirical, priors, and requires the author's prior permission for any use of its code or results. Status as of 2026-10-03: disputed and unresolved.
targets.success_criterion: Either (1) a Bayes factor of at least 20 for one family, robust to 3 segmentations and to priors varied over an order of magnitude, with priors derived from cited lexical data (not hand-set), after a calibration that recovers the correct family with BF at least 20 in at least 80% of trials on Maya or Cypriot data truncated to Isthmian size; or (2) a power analysis showing that for a whole stated class of distributional methods, calibration at Isthmian size (about 700 tokens, about 160 types) recovers the correct family in fewer than 50% of trials, while the same methods succeed at 5-10x the size. 'Our method was inconclusive' alone does not count.

partial_wins.statement: Calibration success: a fully specified pipeline with priors derived from cited lexical data recovers the correct language family with BF at least 20 in at least 80% of trials on Maya or Cypriot-syllabary data truncated to Isthmian size (about 700 tokens, about 160 types), robust to 3 segmentations, reimplemented independently of the licence-restricted repo.

Mask-text held-out test: the Justeson-Kaufman grid frozen from La Mojarra Stela 1 alone yields, on the Teotihuacan-style mask text, a count of Zoquean lexicon matches (lexicon and vowel-latitude rules frozen beforehand) above the 99th percentile of the same count for 1,000 random grids of the same size (p < 0.01).

targets.verification_method: The verifier independently implements the pipeline from the written description (not the licence-restricted repo code), rebuilds the Isthmian transcription from the Pérez de Lara & Justeson sign catalog, and reruns calibration and the robustness table.

targets.name: Khitan small script: phonetic values for unread graphemes from Chinese loanwords and titles
targets.statement: Khitan small script (Liao dynasty, about 470 encoded characters, Unicode 13.0) is partly read: many phonetic values come from Chinese loanwords and official titles in the Kane/Chinggeltei tradition. A number of graphemes still have no secure value, and Khitan-Chinese parallel-text methods are reported to be at an impasse. Khitan large script is much further behind: about 10% of roughly 2,245 characters are fully read. The task is to predict values for unread graphemes and test those predictions on held-out loanword occurrences. No open machine-readable corpus of Khitan small script texts with aligned Chinese parallels was confirmed (BabelStone has only some texts), and the novelty check practically requires the Chinese-language literature (Inner Mongolia University school, Aisin-Gioro Ulhicun and others). Status as of 2026-10-03: Partly deciphered. Encoding and standardization progressed (China's 2025 large-script encoding proposal) and readings appeared in 2025 (Korean Association for Mongolian Studies). No full decipherment.
targets.success_criterion: A value for a grapheme listed as unread in Kane 2009 (the BabelStone list). The value must come from a frozen procedure, for example constraint solving over clusters that transcribe known Chinese titles and names in dated epitaphs. When substituted, it must produce at least 3 readings of Chinese loanwords or names in held-out clusters (not used for inference) that match Liao-period Chinese pronunciations, and random value permutation must give p < 0.01. The value must also not already be in the literature after Kane 2009. Additionally: training and held-out clusters are listed with source inscription and line before solving; the Liao-period northern Chinese reconstruction is fixed beforehand. Claim only as 'candidate value, novelty not cleared against the Chinese-language literature' unless a Chinese-language search (CNKI titles and abstracts) is documented.

partial_wins.statement: Method calibration: the frozen constraint solver, run with one grapheme value that was published after Kane 2009 withheld (the value and its source named beforehand), recovers that value from training clusters alone and confirms it on at least 3 held-out clusters with Liao-period Chinese matches, random value permutation p < 0.01.

A frozen value for a grapheme listed as unread in Kane 2009 that yields at least 2 held-out Chinese loanword or name readings matching the pre-fixed Liao-period northern Chinese reconstruction, with random value permutation p < 0.01 and clusters listed with source inscription and line before solving (full criterion requires 3).

targets.verification_method: The verifier re-derives the cluster transcriptions from BabelStone Unicode texts and Kane's character list, reruns the solver on the training clusters, and checks each held-out match against a Middle or Liao Chinese reconstruction and the parallel Chinese epitaph text. Additionally, the verifier re-derives the clusters from BabelStone Unicode texts at a pinned date and checks each held-out match against the parallel Chinese epitaph text.

targets.name: Linear A: KU-RO totals and fraction-sign values reconciled by arithmetic
targets.statement: Linear A has about 1,400 inscriptions and about 7,400 sign tokens. Its whole-number decimal numerals are understood, and KU-RO / PO-TO-KU-RO are accepted as 'total' / 'grand total'. The fraction signs are the open part. Corazza, Ferrara, Montecchi, Tamburini & Valério (JAS 125, 2021, 105214) proposed J=1/2, E=1/4, F=1/8, B=1/5, D=1/6, K=1/10, L2=1/20, L3=1/30, L4=1/40, L6=1/60, with H and A at 1/32 or 1/36 (unresolved; H=1/16 also discussed). Their assumptions (additivity, no two representations of the same value) are contested, and several rare fraction signs and compound fractions are unresolved. Some KU-RO totals do not equal the sum of the listed items; only the fraction-dependent mismatches are in scope. The task is to find global fraction values or accounting rules (for example, a commodity category excluded from KU-RO, or a subtotal structure) that close more fraction-dependent totals without breaking those already closed. Scale warning: lineara.xyz has only 37 'KU-RO' and 2 'PO-TO-KU-RO' tokens, many damaged. Status as of 2026-10-03: Partly understood: integer numerals and KU-RO = 'total' are secure. Fraction values follow Corazza, Ferrara, Montecchi, Tamburini & Valério, JAS 125 (2021) 105214: J=1/2, E=1/4, F=1/8, B=1/5, D=1/6, K=1/10, L2=1/20, L3=1/30, L4=1/40, L6=1/60, with H/A = 1/32 or 1/36 unresolved and H=1/16 considered. These are leading but not settled. No 2025-2026 published fraction study was found. The 2026 Di Mino Semitic claims are unrelated and fail kbennett2000 controls.
targets.success_criterion: All of the following must hold. (1) Pre-register the list of KU-RO / PO-TO-KU-RO sections in which every item numeral, every fraction sign and the total are fully preserved: no bracketed or uncertain signs in lineara.xyz, and certain=true for the fraction signs in Navarre/SigLA. Classify each non-closing section as fraction-dependent (it contains a fraction sign whose value is unresolved or contested) or integer-only. Integer-only mismatches are out of scope. (2) The baseline is the best closure count over both H/A assignments of Corazza et al. 2021, or over any later published fraction table found at verification time; the new rule must be strictly better (more exact closures) than that baseline. (3) The new global fraction values or accounting rule (no per-tablet values, and integer readings may not be altered) is fitted leave-one-tablet-out. It must close at least 2 more fraction-dependent sections exactly than the baseline and open no new failures. (4) The exact permutation distribution over all same-size assignments from the pre-declared candidate value family gives p < 0.01; report the full distribution, given the small N. (5) The result is not in Bennett 1950, Schrijver (2014 and later), or Corazza et al. 2021 (including its rejected alternatives). An intermediate reportable result: a documented transcription disagreement (lineara.xyz vs SigLA vs GORILA) that explains a non-closure, verified on the GORILA image.

partial_wins.statement: A documented transcription disagreement (lineara.xyz vs SigLA vs GORILA) that explains a KU-RO / PO-TO-KU-RO non-closure: the reading verified on the GORILA photograph (or SigLA drawing) makes the section close exactly under the baseline values with no per-tablet fraction values, and the disagreement is not already recorded in the Navarre-AI defect log or the published literature.

An arithmetic discriminant for H/A: a pre-registered intact fraction-dependent KU-RO section (or set of sections) that closes exactly under exactly one of H/A = 1/32, 1/36 (or H = 1/16) and fails under the others, with the integer readings unaltered and image-checked, establishing a value that Corazza et al. 2021 leave unresolved.

A global fraction value or accounting rule, fitted leave-one-tablet-out, that closes at least 1 more pre-registered fraction-dependent section exactly than the best baseline, opens no new failures, is not in Bennett 1950, Schrijver (2014 and later) or Corazza et al. 2021 (including rejected alternatives), and lies in the top 5% of the exact permutation distribution over the pre-declared candidate value family (full distribution reported).

targets.verification_method: The verifier pins mwenge/lineara.xyz (commit hash) for integer numerals and Navarre-AI/linear-a (commit hash) for fraction-sign identity and certainty. It extracts KU-RO sections with an independent parser, computes item sums with fractions.Fraction under baseline (both H/A variants) and claim, and confirms the pre-registered section list and its fraction-dependence classification. It reruns leave-one-out and the exact permutation test, then checks every newly closing section against the GORILA photograph or the SigLA drawing for damage and sign identity.

targets.name: MOONSHOT: Linear A, identifying the Minoan language with predictive translations
targets.statement: Identify the language of Linear A and produce translations that predict unseen data. Phonetic values are approximately known via Linear B, but the language (Semitic, Luwian, Hurrian, Tyrsenian, isolate, or other) is unknown. Status as of 2026-10-03: Unsolved. The 2026 claims (Di Mino 'Ya Diktu', Tinitic Semitic, 508-entry lexicon, a September 2026 preprint) are unverified, and the independent check found that Hebrew-root matches are no better than scrambled controls. No accepted decipherment. kbennett2000/linear-a-check found that scrambled words match Hebrew roots nearly as well as real words for Di Mino's Sept 2026 preprint, holding across Hebrew, Ugaritic and invented root lists. Navarre-AI carries RILA Supplement 1 provenance on only 25 records.
targets.success_criterion: All of these must hold. (1) A lexicon and grammar frozen with a hash before testing; every gloss tested against logogram adjacency must have been derived without any logogram-context information, documented in the frozen lexicon's provenance. (2) On a held-out set chosen by a third-party seed as a 30% document split stratified by site (not just the 25 RILA records), the frozen grammar predicts morphology and logogram-consistent meanings. Example: words glossed as 'wine' precede the VIN logogram at least 80% of the time on held-out tablets. (3) Lexicon matches to the claimed language exceed all kbennett2000 cycle 6-8 controls (scrambled words, alternate root lists, invented roots, latitude count) with p < 0.001 after correcting for phonological latitude. (4) The translations of held-out accounting tablets are numerically coherent with KU-RO totals. Anything less is not a claim.

partial_wins.statement: A frozen lexicon of at least 3 commodity glosses derived without any logogram-context information (provenance documented) whose held-out logogram-adjacency predictions (e.g. 'wine' word precedes VIN) hold at least 80% of the time on the third-party-seeded, site-stratified 30% document split, with p < 0.001 against glosses permuted among the same words.

A frozen lexicon whose matches to a single named candidate language exceed every kbennett2000 cycle 6-8 control (scrambled words, alternate root lists, invented roots, latitude count) with p < 0.001 after phonological-latitude correction, on held-out documents.

targets.verification_method: The verifier runs the kbennett2000/linear-a-check-style staged tests on the frozen lexicon, checks the hash and timestamp, applies the grammar to held-out documents itself, and scores logogram consistency automatically. Additionally, the verifier checks the provenance of each gloss for logogram-context leakage.

targets.name: Linear A: pre-registered morphological alternations that predict held-out contexts
targets.statement: With Linear B phonetic values applied to Linear A homomorphs, Linear A words can be transliterated, but the language is unknown. Morphology is the open sub-problem. Candidate alternations have been discussed (initial A-/JA-, final -TE/-TI/-NA/-RE variation, libation-formula variants such as JA-SA-SA-RA-ME and A-SA-SA-RA-ME), but none has been shown to predict distribution. The task is to find affix or alternation rules whose presence predicts where a word occurs: its document type, its adjacency to a logogram (VIR/personnel versus commodity), its site, or libation-formula position. Data caveat: in Navarre-AI corpus.json (release 2026-09-18, 1,884 records) the 'words' field is present on only 666 records (SigLA-derived); other records' words come from lineara.xyz with different division conventions. Status as of 2026-10-03: Partly deciphered at the phonetic level; the language is unknown. The 2026 Di Mino 'Ya Diktu' Semitic grammar is unverified, and the adversarial replication kbennett2000/linear-a-check finds its root matches are no better than scrambled controls. The corpus infrastructure was updated in September 2026 (Navarre-AI release 2026-09-18).
targets.success_criterion: A frozen list of at most 10 alternation hypotheses is written before evaluation. Held-out data is every document from a whole site (for example, all Khania or all Zakros) or a random 30% of documents, chosen beforehand. At least one hypothesis must predict a held-out contextual variable with Bonferroni-corrected p < 0.001 (Fisher exact or permutation test over word-to-context assignments). Examples: 'words ending -RE precede personnel logograms', 'A-/JA- alternation tracks libation versus administrative support'. The effect must survive dropping the single most frequent word type. Hypotheses in the published literature that do not reach significance do not count. A published hypothesis reaching this significance for the first time does count, with that stated. Additionally: tokens come from a single declared word_source (SigLA or lineara.xyz), or the result must replicate in both; tokens containing uncertain or unidentified signs (e.g. 're?', '[?]') are excluded; the held-out split is by whole site or by document, never by token; and every hypothesis is checked for novelty against existing libation-formula studies (e.g. Davis 2014 on stone vessels).

partial_wins.statement: A frozen hypothesis (from a pre-registered list of at most 10) that, on the pre-declared held-out site or document split, under one declared word_source and excluding uncertain-sign tokens, predicts the held-out contextual variable at Bonferroni-corrected p < 0.01 (rather than the full bar of p < 0.001), survives dropping the most frequent word type, and has not previously reached that significance in the literature.

Onomastic cross-prediction: Linear A sign-groups that also occur as Linear B personal names or toponyms at Knossos (list frozen before evaluation) are adjacent to personnel logograms (VIR etc.) on held-out documents significantly more often than non-shared sign-groups of matched length and frequency (Fisher exact or permutation p < 0.001), surviving the drop of the most frequent type, with the effect not already published.

targets.verification_method: The verifier pins the Navarre-AI commit and filters by word_source. It rebuilds tokens, excludes uncertain signs, re-applies the frozen regexes, recomputes Fisher or permutation tests with Bonferroni correction over all frozen hypotheses, reruns with the most frequent type dropped, and checks the git timestamp order.

targets.name: Linear Elamite: values for the 4 undeciphered signs, and a predictive test of the 2022 grid
targets.statement: Desset et al. (2022) proposed a near-complete decipherment of Linear Elamite: 72 phonographic signs with allographs, 4 undeciphered infrequent signs, and 33 hapax legomena, from an inventory of 348 glyphs and about 51 inscriptions. Some Assyriologists accept it (Krebernik, Stolper, Steinkeller). Mäder disputes the claim of a purely phonographic system and argues that about 30% of signs are logograms. Two things remain open: the values of the 4 undeciphered signs, and an independent predictive test of the grid. Status as of 2026-10-03: Proposed near-complete decipherment (Desset et al. 2022), accepted by several Assyriologists but contested (Mäder: about 30% logograms). New corpus volume by Desset et al. (OrientLab Series Maior, Aug 2026). No source found resolving the 4 residual signs as of 2026-10-03, but the Aug 2026 volume has not been checked.
targets.success_criterion: (0) First confirm, from the Aug 2026 Desset, Tabibzadeh, Basello, Marcazzan & Colonna d'Istria volume (OrientLab Series Maior), that the target sign is still unassigned there. Then: for one of the 4 undeciphered signs, propose a CV value from the gaps in Desset's grid, written down before checking. The Elamite lexicon subset (Elamite cuneiform sources, Hinz & Koch) and the vowel-latitude rules are frozen and hashed before testing. The value must yield at least 2 independent readings in at least 2 distinct inscriptions not sharing a formula that match attested Elamite lexemes or onomastics in contexts consistent with those inscriptions' parallels. Every other free grid-gap value tried must give fewer matches, and a random-value null over all unfilled grid cells plus all filled cells (the sign could be an allograph of a known value) must give p < 0.01. A strong alternative outcome is a pre-registered test showing that Desset's grid (as updated in the 2026 volume) predicts, at above-chance rates (p < 0.01 against random grids), the readings of royal names or titles in an inscription that was not used in building the grid.

partial_wins.statement: An allograph identification: one of the 4 residual signs (confirmed unassigned in the 2026 volume) shown, by a frozen distributional test on contexts not used to propose it, to occupy the same positions as a specific filled-grid sign significantly more than any other filled sign (p < 0.01 under a frequency-matched permutation null over all grid cells), with the identification absent from Desset et al. 2022 and the 2026 volume.

A residual-sign value meeting all of the full criterion's conditions (frozen lexicon and vowel-latitude rules, at least 2 matches on 2 inscriptions not sharing a formula, beats every other free value) except that the all-cells random-value null gives p < 0.05 rather than p < 0.01.

targets.verification_method: The verifier fetches sign sequences from github.com/elamicon/elamicon (pinned commit) and the Balmer et al. 2020 OCLEI concordance, applies the 2022 grid as updated in the 2026 volume, checks each lexeme against Hinz & Koch, and recomputes the null over all grid cells.

targets.name: Meroitic: meanings for unknown words from distribution, validated on held-out known words
targets.statement: Meroitic (Kush, Sudan, about 300 BCE to 400 CE) is phonetically readable in both hieroglyphic and cursive forms. Much of its vocabulary and grammar is unknown, and there is no sizable bilingual. Otten & Anastasopoulos (ALP 2025) released the first machine-readable Meroitic corpus and ran embedding and cross-lingual alignment experiments with Late Egyptian. The open task is to assign semantic classes or meanings to unknown words in a way that is validated, not interpretive. The corpus, embeddings and code are public at github.com/Joshua-Otten/Meroitic-Corpus. The known-meaning gloss set from Rilly is not machine-readable and must be hand-built. Status as of 2026-10-03: Partly understood. Rilly links Meroitic to North Eastern Sudanic. Computational work began in 2025, and no 2026 breakthrough was found.
targets.success_criterion: Two steps are required. (1) Validation: on words with known meanings (titles, deities, kinship terms, toponyms from Rilly's lexicon), hide each word's gloss and predict its semantic class from distribution alone. Top-1 class accuracy must be at least 2x the majority-class baseline, with permutation p < 0.001. (2) Discovery: the same frozen model assigns a class to at least 3 currently unglossed words with posterior at least 0.9. At least one of these must be corroborated by an independent signal the model never saw: an Egyptian or Greek loanword etymology, a determinative, or co-occurrence with an iconographic context recorded in REM metadata. Interpretive translations without step 1 do not count. Additionally: the known-gloss set (word, class, citation) is frozen and hashed before any model is fit; classes are fixed beforehand (at most 8); leave-one-out excludes all inflected variants of the held-out word.

partial_wins.statement: Step (1) alone: on the frozen, hashed known-gloss set (at most 8 pre-fixed classes, citations to Rilly), leave-one-out with all inflected variants excluded, top-1 semantic-class accuracy from distribution alone is at least 2x the majority-class baseline with permutation p < 0.001.

Step (1) plus one discovery: the same frozen model assigns a class with posterior at least 0.9 to an unglossed word, and that class is corroborated by an independent signal the model never saw (Egyptian or Greek loanword etymology, a determinative, or iconographic context in REM metadata), with the corroboration not already published for that word.

targets.verification_method: The verifier clones Joshua-Otten/Meroitic-Corpus (pinned commit), rebuilds the frozen gloss set from cited Rilly pages, reruns leave-one-out with fresh seeds and the permutation test, and checks each corroboration source.

targets.name: Oracle bone script: identifications of undeciphered characters validated by held-out prediction
targets.compute_profile: laptop-hours (inference only; full method training needs GPU)
targets.statement: About 4,500 distinct Shang oracle-bone characters are known, and only about 1,600 are deciphered. The National Museum of Chinese Writing (Anyang) offers 100,000 yuan per deciphered character and 50,000 yuan for settling a disputed one, subject to sufficient evidence. AI methods (Open-Oracle, OracleFusion 2025, generative dictionary retrieval in April 2026 (arXiv 2604.09668), a GAN-based human-computer approach in Heritage Science 2026) propose candidates, but acceptance requires paleographic chains through bronze and seal forms plus context in inscriptions. The '~1,600 of ~4,500 deciphered' framing is from arXiv 2506.21101 (OracleFusion, ICCV 2025). Status as of 2026-10-03: Active AI work in 2025-2026 (OracleFusion ICCV 2025; generative dictionary retrieval arXiv 2604.09668, Apr 2026; GAN approach in Heritage Science 2026). The large majority of characters remain undeciphered (about 1,500-1,600 of about 4,500-4,600 read). The Anyang museum reward stands (100,000 yuan per character, expert-adjudicated).
targets.success_criterion: Both steps are required. (1) Method validation: the code first reproduces the best published top-10 accuracy on the unseen-character split of arXiv 2604.09668 (or a HUST-OBC / EVOBC time split) as listed at verification time (54.3% top-10 in 2604.09668 as of 2026-10-03), and the method is not significantly worse than that best value. (2) For at least 1 undeciphered character, a proposed modern equivalent with a complete paleographic chain (oracle bone to bronze to seal to clerical form, each link an attested form with source cited). Substituting the character must give grammatical readings in at least 5 different inscriptions with consistent syntactic role. A documented Chinese-language novelty search (Xiaoxuetang, CNKI, Anyang databases) shows the identification is unpublished. A claim may report only 'candidate identification', never 'deciphered', because acceptance takes expert review (the Anyang museum reward is expert-adjudicated). Retrieval hits on the dictionary alone are not identifications.

partial_wins.statement: On the exact unseen-character split of arXiv 2604.09668, after reproducing its baseline, a frozen method achieves top-10 accuracy strictly higher than the best value published for that split at verification time (54.3% as of 2026-10-03), with the improvement significant under paired bootstrap at p < 0.01.

On a HUST-OBC or EVOBC time split (characters whose decipherment was published after a stated cutoff are hidden), a frozen method ranks the accepted modern equivalent in its top 10 for a strictly larger fraction of hidden characters than the best published method on that split at verification time, paired bootstrap p < 0.01.

targets.verification_method: For (1), the verifier reruns the baseline and the claim on the stated split with fixed seeds and recomputes the bootstrap. For (2), the verifier checks each chain link in cited sources and reads the 5 inscriptions. This part is human and expert-dependent.

targets.name: Proto-Elamite: numeral-system and commodity assignments checked by tablet arithmetic
targets.statement: Proto-Elamite (Susa and the Iranian plateau, c. 3100-2900 BCE; about 1,400-1,700 tablets) is only partly deciphered. Its numerical systems (sexagesimal, bisexagesimal, decimal, capacity, etc., following Englund and Damerow) are mostly understood. Three things are still open. (a) The same numeral signs can be read in up to four systems, so the system meant on a given entry is ambiguous (Born, Monroe, Kelley & Sarkar 2025). (b) Most non-numeric signs (ideograms, 'header' signs, complex graphemes) have no known commodity or meaning. (c) Many tablets with a reverse-side total do not reconcile with their obverse entries under the current readings. The task is to find new, falsifiable assignments of the form 'sign X is counted in system Y', 'sign X denotes commodity class Z' or 'unit U = k x unit V' that the tablets' own arithmetic confirms. Status as of 2026-10-03: Partly deciphered (numerical systems largely understood); no accepted reading of ideograms as of 2026-10-03. Latest: Born et al. arXiv 2502.00090 v2 (2025-04-25); Monroe/Kelley/Born/Sarkar NEA 88(4) Dec 2025; Kelley, Cambridge Element (2026-07-18). Amateur repo MahmoodKhalil57/ProtoElamite (created 2026-06-17, 1,467 tablets, '9 falsifiable claims') is not peer-reviewed.
targets.success_criterion: All of the following must hold. (1) Before any evaluation, freeze in a timestamped, hashed file: (i) the rule, as a deterministic function of observable context only (numeral sign identity, accompanying ideogram/header sign, position, obverse/reverse), with a declared count k of free parameters; and (ii) a seeded 30% held-out split of P-numbers. Choosing the system per entry, or per tablet, to maximize balance is forbidden. (2) A tablet's total is identified only by the pre-registered layout convention (reverse-side numeral after the entries), never by which number equals the sum. (3) Eligible held-out tablets have an intact total and every entry intact (no [ ], #, ? or x in any numeral). Report N_eligible and the baseline count of unbalanced tablets first. (4) The baseline is the best of two readings: Born et al. 2025 v2 sign values plus their published disambiguation, and Englund-convention readings. The new rule must balance at least max(5, 15% of baseline-unbalanced eligible held-out tablets) more held-out tablets exactly (Fraction equality), and break at most 1 tablet the baseline balanced. (5) The gain has permutation p < 0.01 against 1,000 alternative rules with the same k and the same form. (6) A literature check of Born/Kelley/Monroe/Sarkar 2019-2025, NEA 2025, Kelley 2026 and Englund 2004 shows the rule is unpublished. Claim only as 'arithmetic-confirmed reading rule (candidate)'. Results that only improve classifier accuracy without arithmetic closure do not satisfy the full criterion.

partial_wins.statement: Cross-tablet record linkage: a pre-registered search finds at least one pair or set of Proto-Elamite tablets in which one tablet's layout-defined total (or its full entry list) equals exactly (Fraction equality) the sum of the layout-defined totals or entries of the other tablet(s) under the baseline readings, all numerals intact (no [ ], #, ? or x). The number of such exact links must exceed the 99th percentile of the same search run on 1,000 random re-pairings of tablets with matched entry-count and value distributions, and the links must be absent from Born/Kelley/Monroe/Sarkar 2019-2025, NEA 88(4) 2025, Kelley 2026 and Englund 2004.

A frozen, deterministic unit-ratio or system-assignment rule ('unit U = k x unit V', or 'numeral sign N under header/ideogram H is read in system S') with declared k free parameters, not published in the sources above, that balances at least 3 more eligible held-out tablets exactly than the best baseline (Born et al. 2025 v2 pipeline or Englund-convention readings), breaks none, and has permutation p < 0.05 against 1,000 same-form, same-k alternative rules. (Weaker than the full bar of max(5, 15%) and p < 0.01.)

A model or rule trained without the Born et al. 2025 v2 released numeral-disambiguation test set (no test items in training, checked by the verifier) that strictly exceeds the best accuracy published on that test set at verification time, with paired bootstrap p < 0.01 over test items.

targets.verification_method: The verifier obtains the ATF in one of two ways: (a) git-lfs clone of cdli-gh/data, checking the LFS oid sha256 of each file against the claim; or (b) the current CDLI framework export from cdli.earth with a recorded download date and hash. It filters period = Proto-Elamite and parses numerals with independent code using a published system table (Englund 2004 / Born v2 corrected decimal). It applies the frozen rule mechanically (no per-tablet choices) and recomputes per-tablet balance with fractions.Fraction under baseline and claim, recomputing N_eligible. It checks the split hash and timestamp, reruns the permutation null with a new seed and the same k, and spot-checks 5 newly balanced tablets against CDLI photos or RTI for damage.

targets.name: Rongorongo: graphemic inventory and new parallel passages found by alignment
targets.statement: Rongorongo (Rapa Nui) survives on about 26 wooden objects with roughly 15,000 glyphs. The only text segment with an accepted meaning is the lunar-calendar portion of the Mamari tablet (Barthel 1958; Guy 1990 interprets it as an intercalation canon). Two foundational problems are open. First, the true grapheme inventory: which of Barthel's roughly 600 codes are allographs or ligatures. Pozdniakov argued for about 52 basic glyphs. Second, the complete map of parallel passages across tablets. A 2025 study (Digital Scholarship in the Humanities) segmented texts I, Gv and T around sign 76 and argued that personal names are present. Radiocarbon work in 2024 dated one tablet to the 15th century, which supports independent invention. Recent work that sets the baseline: Korovina, LT4HALA 2026 (syllabic-substitution GA on CEIPP and rongopy transliterations); the ipezygj/rongorongo-catalogue-audit Zenodo preprint (Sept 2026), which shows that the choice of catalogue (CEIPP L=1,897 / CEIPP numeric L=633 / Horley basic L=125) moves conditional entropy about 4x more than the signal and ships parallels3.py, a table of scribes' substitutions; Sproat's automatic parallel detection (2003); Kudrjavtsev's parallels. The CEIPP Barthel transliteration is restricted to bona fide researchers; open routes are jgregoriods/rongopy and the ipezygj fetch_data.py. Status as of 2026-10-03: Undeciphered as of 2026-10-03; only the Mamari lunar-calendar section has an accepted interpretation. Latest scholarly items: DSH 2025 reassessment of I/Gv/T; Korovina LT4HALA 2026; Väätäinen catalogue audit (Zenodo, Sept 2026). 2026 Zenodo 'full decipherments' have no acceptance.
targets.success_criterion: (A) A new parallel passage between two different tablets, or two sections at least 2 lines apart: at least 10 aligned positions, with at most 2 mismatches, where any further substitution is allowed only if it is an allograph pair accepted by Barthel, Pozdniakov or Horley. Alignment p < 0.001 against glyph-shuffled tablets of the same composition, with Bonferroni correction over all tablet pairs searched.
